children.translated_text: Reference system:

NyS_ = <s>Nyāyasūtra</s>
NySBh_ = <s>Nyāyasūtrabhāṣya</s>

children.text:
pramāṇato 'rthapratipattau pravṛttisāmathyadirthavat pramāṇam|
pramāṇamantareṇa nārthapratipattiḥ|
nārthapratipattimantareṇa pravṛttisāmartham|
pramāṇena khalvayaṃ jñātārthamupalabhya tamīpsati va jihāsati vā|
tasyepsājihāsāprayuktasya samīhā pravṛttirityucyate|
sāmarthya punarasyāḥ phalenābhisambandhaḥ|
samīhamānasvamarthamabhīpsan jihāsan vā tamarthamāpnāti jahāti vā|
arthastu sukhaṃ sukhahetuśca|
so 'yaṃ pramāṇārtho 'parisaṃkhyeyaḥ, prāṇabhṛdbhedasyāparisaṃkhyetvāt|
children.translated_text: When an object is apprehended through a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), the <s>pramāṇa</s> is purposeful due to [its] capacity for activity. Without a <s>pramāṇa</s>, there is no apprehension of objects. Without the apprehension of objects, there is no capacity for activity. Indeed, this [person], having apprehended a known object through a <s>pramāṇa</s>, either desires it or wishes to avoid it. The endeavor of one impelled by desire and aversion is called <s>pravṛtti</s> (activity). The capacity of this [activity] is its connection with a result. One who endeavors, desiring or wishing to avoid a particular object, either attains or abandons that object. The object, moreover, is pleasure and the cause of pleasure. This purpose of the <s>pramāṇa</s> is innumerable, because the distinctions among living beings are innumerable.

children.text:
arthavati ca pramāṇe pramātā prameyaṃ pramitirityarthavanti bhavanti|
kasmāt ? anyatamāpāye 'rthasyānupapatteḥ/
children.translated_text: And when the <s>pramāṇa</s> is purposeful, the <s>pramātā</s> (knower), the <s>prameya</s> (knowable), and <s>pramiti</s> (resultant knowledge) become purposeful. Why? Because in the absence of any one [of these], the purpose would not be established.

children.text:
tatra yasyepsājihāsāprayuktasya pravṛttiḥ, sa pramātā|
sa yenārtha pramiṇoti vijānāti tatpramāṇam|
yo 'rthaḥ pramīyate
children.translated_text: There, the one whose activity is impelled by desire and aversion is the <s>pramātā</s> (knower). That by which he measures — that is, cognizes — an object is the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge). The object that is measured,
that is, cognized — that is the <s>prameya</s> (knowable).

children.text:
kiṃ punastatvam ? sataśca sadbhāvo 'sataścāsadbhāva iti|
satsaditi gṛhyamāṇaṃ yathābhūtamaviparītaṃ tatvaṃ bhavati|
asaccāsaditi gṛhyamāṇaṃ yathābhūtamaviparītaṃ tacvaṃ bhavati|
kathaṃ punaruttarasya pramāṇenopalabdhiriti ?
satyupalabhyamāne tadvadanupalabdheḥ pradīpavat|
yathā darśakena pradīpena dṛśye guhyamāṇe tadiva yanna gṛhyate tatrāsti/
children.translated_text: Now, what is <s>tattva</s> (reality)? The real existence of what exists and the non-existence of what does not exist — thus it is. What exists, being apprehended as existent, is <s>tattva</s> — as it truly is, without error. And what does not exist, being apprehended as non-existent, is <s>tattva</s> — as it truly is, without error. But how is there apprehension of the latter [i.e., non-existence] through a <s>pramāṇa</s>? When something [existing] is being apprehended, [non-existence is known] by the non-apprehension of what would be like it — like a lamp. Just as, when visible objects are illuminated by a revealing lamp, that which is not apprehended there [is known to be] absent.

children.text:
yadyabhaviṣyadidamiva vyajñāsyate vijñānābhāvānnāstīti|
tadevaṃ sataḥ prakāśakaṃ pramāṇamasadapi prakāśayatīti|
sacca khalu ṣoḍaśadhā vyūḍhamupadekṣyate|
tāsāṃ khalvāsāṃ sadvidhānām ---
children.translated_text: If it did not exist, it would be cognized as 'this does not exist, due to the absence of cognition.' Thus, the <s>pramāṇa</s> that illuminates what exists also illuminates what does not exist. And indeed, what exists has been arranged in sixteen categories, which will be taught. Of those categories —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.1: From the <s>tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality) of <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), <s>prameya</s> (objects of knowledge), <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt), <s>prayojana</s> (purpose), <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine), <s>avayava</s> (members of syllogism), <s>tarka</s> (reasoning), <s>nirṇaya</s> (ascertainment), <s>vāda</s> (debate), <s>jalpa</s> (wrangling), <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavilling), <s>hetvābhāsa</s> (fallacious reasons), <s>chala</s> (quibbling), <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinder), and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (points of defeat) — there is the attainment of <s>niḥśreyasa</s> (the highest good).

children.text:
nirdeśe yathāvacanaṃ vigrahaḥ|
cārthe dvandvaḥ samāsaḥ|
pramāṇādīnāṃ tatvamiti śaiṣikī ṣaṣṭhī|
tatvasya jñānaṃ niḥśreyasasyādhigama iti ca karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhyau|
ta etāvanto vidyamānārthāḥ|
eṣāmaviparītajñānārthamihopadeśaḥ|
so 'yamanavayavena tantrārtha uddiṣṭo veditavyaḥ/
children.translated_text: In the enumeration, the analysis follows the words as stated. The compound is a <s>dvandva</s> (copulative compound) in the sense of 'and.' The genitive in '<s>tattva</s> of <s>pramāṇa</s> and the rest' is a possessive genitive. 'Knowledge of <s>tattva</s>' and 'attainment of <s>niḥśreyasa</s>' — in both, the genitives are objective. These are the real categories enumerated. Their teaching here is for the purpose of correct knowledge of them. This summary of the system's meaning, stated concisely, should be understood.

children.text:
ātmādeḥ khalu prameyasya tatvajñānātriḥśreyasādhigamaḥ taccaiduttarasūtreṇānūdyate|
heyaṃ tasya nirvartakaṃ hānamātyantikaṃ tasyopāyo 'dhigantavya ityetāni khalu catvāryarthapadāni samyagbuddhvā niḥśreyasamadhigacchati/
children.translated_text: Indeed, from the <s>tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality) of <s>prameya</s> (knowable objects) beginning with <s>ātman</s> (self), there is the attainment of <s>niḥśreyasa</s> (the highest good) — and this is reiterated by the next <s>sūtra</s>. What is to be abandoned, its cause, the abandonment that is absolute, and the means to that [abandonment] — having correctly understood these four topics, one attains <s>niḥśreyasa</s>.

children.text:
tatra saśayādīnāṃ pṛthagvacanamarthakame saṃśayādayo hi yathāsambhavaṃ pramāṇeṣu prameyeṣu cāntarbhavanto na vyatiraccinta iti|
satyamevametat, imāstu catastro vidyāḥ pṛthakprasthānāḥ prāṇabhṛtāmanugrahāyopadiśyante, yāsāṃ
children.translated_text: Therein, the separate mention of <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt) and the rest — is it purposeless? For <s>saṃśaya</s> and the rest, being subsumed under <s>pramāṇas</s> and <s>prameyas</s> as appropriate, would not be distinguished [from them]. True, this is so; but these four sciences, having separate approaches, are taught for the benefit of living beings, of which

children.text:
caturrthāyamānvīkṣikī nyāyavidyā|
tasyāḥ pṛthakprasthānāḥ saṃśayādayaḥ padārthāḥ|
teṣā pṛthagvacanamantareṇādhyātmavidyāmātramiyaṃ syāt, yathopaniṣadaḥ|
tasmāt saṃśayādibhiḥ padārthaiḥ pṛthak prasthāpyate/
children.translated_text: the fourth is <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> (<s>Nyāya</s> science, the science of logical inquiry). <s>Saṃśaya</s> (doubt) and the other categories are its distinct subject matter. Without their separate mention, this [science] would be merely <s>adhyātmavidyā</s> (spiritual knowledge), like the <s>Upaniṣads</s>. Therefore, it is distinguished separately by the categories of <s>saṃśaya</s> and the rest.
Now, one does not engage in [inquiry] regarding an object that is unapprehended or already ascertained.
What then? Regarding an object that is doubted.
And thus it is said: ascertainment (<s>nirṇaya</s>) is the determination of an object through deliberation on thesis and counter-thesis.

children.text:
(1.1 . 41) iti|
vimarśaḥ saṃśayaḥ|
pakṣapratipakṣau nyāyapravṛttiḥ|
arthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇayastatvajñānamiti|
sa cāyaṃ kiṅkhiditi vastuvimarśamātramanavadhāraṇaṃ jñānaṃ saṃśayaḥ|
sa ca prameye 'ntabhavannevamartha pṛthagucyate iti/
children.translated_text: (1.1.41) Thus: deliberation is <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt). Thesis and counter-thesis constitute the operation of <s>Nyāya</s> (logical method). Determination of the object is <s>nirṇaya</s> (ascertainment), which is <s>tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality). And this <s>saṃśaya</s> is a cognition of mere deliberation about the nature of a thing — 'what is this?' — a non-ascertainment. And though subsumed under <s>prameya</s>, it is mentioned separately for this purpose.

children.text:
artha prayojanam, yena prayuktaḥ pravartate tat prayojanam, yamarthamabhopsan jihāsan vā karmārabhate|
tenānena sarve prāṇinaḥsarvāṇi karmāṇi sarvāśca vidyā vyāptāḥ|
tadāśrayaśca nyāyaḥ pravartate|
kaḥ nunarayaṃ nyāyaḥ? pramāṇairarthaparīkṣaṇam|
pratyakṣāgamāśritaṃ cānumanam|
sānvīkṣā|
pratyakṣāgamābhyāmīkṣitasyārthasyānvīkṣaṇamanvīkṣā|
tayā pravartata ityānvīkṣakī nyāyavidyā nyāyaśāstram|
yatpunaranumānaṃ pratyakṣāgamaviruddha nyāyābhāsaḥ sa iti/
children.translated_text: Now, <s>prayojana</s> (purpose): that impelled by which one acts is <s>prayojana</s> — the object desiring or wishing to avoid which one undertakes action. By this, all living beings, all actions, and all sciences are pervaded. And <s>Nyāya</s> (logical method) operates based on it. What then is this <s>Nyāya</s>? It is the examination of objects through <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge). And inference resting on perception and scripture — that is <s>anvīkṣā</s> (investigation). The re-examination of an object already examined through perception and scripture is <s>anvīkṣā</s>. That [science] which proceeds by this [method] is <s>ānvīkṣikī</s>, <s>Nyāya</s> science, the science of logic. But inference that contradicts perception and scripture is a <s>nyāyābhāsa</s> (semblance of reasoning) — thus it is.

children.text:
tatra vādajalpau saprayojanau, vitaṇḍā tu parikṣyate|
vitaṇḍayā pravatāmāno vaitaṇḍikaḥ|
sa prayojanamanuyukto yadi pratipadyate, so 'sya pakṣāḥ so 'sya siddhānta iti vaitaṇḍikatvaṃ jahāti|
atha na pratipadyate nāyaṃ laukiko na parīkṣaka ityāpadyate/
children.translated_text: Therein, <s>vāda</s> (debate) and <s>jalpa</s> (wrangling) have a purpose, but <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavilling) is to be examined. One who proceeds by <s>vitaṇḍā</s> is a <s>vaitaṇḍika</s> (caviller). If, when challenged about his purpose, he accepts [a position], then that becomes his thesis, that becomes his <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine) — and he abandons his status as a <s>vaitaṇḍika</s>. But if he does not accept, then the consequence follows that he is neither a worldly person nor an examiner.

children.text:
athāpi parapakṣapratiṣedhajñāpanaṃ prayojanaṃ bravīti, etadapi tādṛgeva|
yo jñāpayati, yo jānāti, yena jñāpayate, yacca jñāpyate-etacca pratipadyate cadi, tadā vaitaṇḍikatvaṃ jahāti|
atha na pratipadyate, parapakṣapratiṣedhajñāpanaṃ prayojanamityetadasya vākyamanarthakaṃ bhavati/
children.translated_text: Even if he says that his purpose is to make known the refutation of the opponent's thesis, this too is just the same. He who makes known, he who knows, that by which he makes known, and that which is made known — if he accepts all this, then he abandons his status as a <s>vaitaṇḍika</s>. But if he does not accept, then his statement 'my purpose is to make known the refutation of the opponent's thesis' becomes meaningless.

children.text:
vākyasamūhaśca sthāpanāhīno vitaṇḍā|
tasya yadyabhidheyaṃ pratipadhate so 'sya pakṣāḥ sthāpanīyo bhavati|
atha na pratipadyate pralāpamātramanarthakaṃ bhavati, vitaṇḍatvaṃ nivartata iti/
children.translated_text: And a collection of statements lacking establishment [of one's own position] is <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavilling). If he accepts what is to be expressed by it, that becomes his thesis to be established. But if he does not accept, it becomes mere babbling and is meaningless — and the status of <s>vitaṇḍā</s> is refuted.

children.text:
atha dṛṣṭāntaḥ|
pratyakṣaviṣayo 'rtho dṛṣṭāntaḥ, catra laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ darśanaṃ na vayāhanyate|
sa ca prameyam|
tasya pṛthagvacanaṃ ca|
tadāśrayāvanumānāgamau|
tasmin sati syātāmanumānāgamau, asati ca na syātām|
tadāśrayā nyāyapravṛttiḥ|
dṛṣṭāntavirodhena ca parapakṣapratiṣedho vacanīyo bhavati|
dṛṣṭānsamādhinā ca svapakṣaḥ sthāpanīyo bhavati|
nāstikaśca dṛṣṭāntamabhyupagacchan nāstikatvaṃ jahāti|
anabhyupagacchan kiṃsādhanaḥ paramupālabheta ?
niruktena ca dṛṣṭāntena śakyamabhidhātum,
children.translated_text: Now, <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example). An object that is a matter of perception is a <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>, regarding which the understanding of both ordinary people and examiners is not contradicted. And it is a <s>prameya</s> (knowable). And it is mentioned separately. Inference and scripture depend on it. When it exists, inference and scripture are possible; when it does not exist, they are not possible. The operation of <s>Nyāya</s> depends on it. The refutation of the opponent's thesis must be stated through contradiction with the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>. And one's own thesis must be established through agreement with the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>. And even a <s>nāstika</s> (denier), by accepting a <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>, abandons his status as a denier. Without accepting it, with what means would he criticize another? And by means of a defined <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>, it is possible to state:
An illustration (<s>udāharaṇa</s>) is a <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example) that possesses the property of the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved), due to similarity with the <s>sādhya</s>. (1.1.36)
Or the reverse, from dissimilarity. (1.1.37)

children.text:
iti
astyayamityabhyanujñāyamāno 'rthaḥ siddhāntaḥ|
sa ca prameyam|
tasya pṛthagvacanam, satsu siddhāntabhedeṣu vādajalpavitaṇḍāḥ pravartante, nātānyatheti/
children.translated_text: Thus: an object that is acknowledged as 'this exists thus' is a <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine). And it is a <s>prameya</s> (knowable). It is mentioned separately because <s>vāda</s> (debate), <s>jalpa</s> (wrangling), and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavilling) operate when there are distinctions among <s>siddhāntas</s>, and not otherwise.

children.text:
sādhanīyasyārthasya yāvati śabdasamūhe siddhiḥ parisamāpyate, tasya pañcāvayavāḥ pratijñādayaḥ samūhamapekṣyāvayavā ucyante|
teṣu pramāṇasamavāyaḥ|
āgamaḥ pratijñā, heturanumānam, udāharaṇaṃ pratyakṣame upamānamupanayaḥ, sarveṣāmekārthasamavāye sāmarthyapradarśanaṃ nigamanamiti|
tadāśrayā ca tatvavyavasthā|
te caite 'vayavāḥ
children.translated_text: The five members (<s>avayavas</s>) beginning with <s>pratijñā</s> (proposition) are called members in relation to the collection of words in which the establishment of the object to be proved is completed. In them there is the convergence of <s>pramāṇas</s>. Scripture is the <s>pratijñā</s> (proposition), the reason (<s>hetu</s>) is inference, the illustration (<s>udāharaṇa</s>) is perception, analogy (<s>upamāna</s>) is the application (<s>upanaya</s>), and the demonstration of the efficacy of all of these converging on a single object is the conclusion (<s>nigamana</s>). And the establishment of <s>tattva</s> (reality) depends on these. And these members,

children.text: śabdaviśeṣāḥ santaḥ prameye 'ntamūtā evamartha puthagracyanta iti/
children.translated_text: being specific words, though subsumed under <s>prameya</s>, are mentioned separately for this purpose.

children.text:
tarko na pramāṇasaṃguhāto, na pramāṇāntaram, pramāṇānāmanugrāhakastatvajñānāya kalpate|
tasyodāharam, kimidaṃ janma kṛtakena hetunā nirvartyate, āhosvidakṛtakena, athākasmikamiti ? evamavijñātatatve 'rthe kāraṇopapatyā
children.translated_text: <s>Tarka</s> (reasoning) is not included among the <s>pramāṇas</s>, nor is it a separate <s>pramāṇa</s>; it serves as an aid to the <s>pramāṇas</s> for the purpose of <s>tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality). An illustration of it: is this birth brought about by a created cause, or by an uncreated cause, or is it without any cause? Thus, when the reality of the object is unknown, through the fitness of causes,

children.text:
uhaḥ pravatāte-yadi kṛtakena hetunā nirvartyate, hetūcchedādupapanno 'yaṃ janmocchadaḥ|
athākṛtakena hetunā, tato henūcchedasyāśakyatvādanupapanno janmocchedaḥ|
athākāsmikam, ato 'kasmānnirvartyamānaṃ na punarnirvartsyatīti nivṛttikāraṇaṃ nopapadyate|
tena janmānuccheda iti|
etasmiṃstarkaviṣaye karmanimitaṃ janmeti pramāṇāni pravartamānāni
children.translated_text: reasoning proceeds: if [birth] is brought about by a created cause, then from the destruction of the cause, the cessation of birth is established. But if by an uncreated cause, then since the destruction of the cause is impossible, the cessation of birth is not established. And if [birth is] without any cause, then since what is produced without any cause would not cease to be produced again, a reason for cessation is not established. Therefore, there is no cessation of birth. In this domain of <s>tarka</s>, the <s>pramāṇas</s> operating [to establish] that birth is caused by <s>karma</s> (action)

children.text:
tarkeṇānugṛhyante|
tanvajñānaviṣayasya ca vibhāgāt tatvajñānāya kalpate tarka iti|
so 'yamitthamabhūtastarkaḥ pramāṇasahito vāde sādhanāyopālambhāya cārthasya bhavatītyevamartha pṛthagucyate prameyāntabhūto 'pīti/
children.translated_text: are aided by <s>tarka</s> (reasoning). And since it distinguishes the domain of non-knowledge, <s>tarka</s> serves for <s>tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality). This <s>tarka</s>, being of this nature, when combined with <s>pramāṇa</s>, serves in <s>vāda</s> (debate) for the establishment and the criticism of an object — and for this purpose it is mentioned separately, though subsumed under <s>prameya</s>.

children.text:
nirṇayastatvajñānaṃ pramāṇānāṃ phalam|
tadavasāno vādaḥ|
tasya pālanārtha jalpavitaṇḍe|
tāvetau tarkanirṇayau
children.translated_text: <s>Nirṇaya</s> (ascertainment) is <s>tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality), the fruit of the <s>pramāṇas</s>. <s>Vāda</s> (debate) culminates in it. <s>Jalpa</s> (wrangling) and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavilling) serve to protect it. These two — <s>tarka</s> and <s>nirṇaya</s> —

children.text:
lokayātrāṃ vahata iti|
so 'yaṃ nirṇayaḥ prameyāntarbhūta evamartha pṛthaguddiṣṭa iti/
children.translated_text: sustain the conduct of the world. This <s>nirṇaya</s>, though subsumed under <s>prameya</s>, is mentioned separately for this purpose.

children.text: vādaḥ khalu nānāpravaktṛkaḥ pratyadhikaraṇasādhano 'nyatarādhikaraṇanirṇayāvāsāno vākyasamūhaḥ pṛthaguddiṣṭa upalakṣaṇārtham, upalakṣitena vyavahārastatvajñānāya bhavatīti/
children.translated_text: <s>Vāda</s> (debate) is indeed a collection of statements having multiple speakers, establishing [arguments] against [each other's] positions, and culminating in the ascertainment of one of the positions. It is mentioned separately for the purpose of characterization — for when characterized, practice [of debate] leads to <s>tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality).

<s>Jalpa</s> (wrangling) and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavilling), being the two varieties of that [debate], serve for the protection and securing of the ascertainment of <s>tattva</s> (reality) — this has been stated.

children.text:
nigrahasthānabhyaḥ pṛthaguddiṣṭa hetvābhāsāḥ, vāde caudanīyā bhaviṣyantīti|
jalpavitaṇḍayostu nigrahasthānānīti/
children.translated_text: <s>Hetvābhāsas</s> (fallacious reasons) are mentioned separately from <s>nigrahasthānas</s> (points of defeat), because they will be cited in <s>vāda</s> (debate). But in <s>jalpa</s> (wrangling) and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavilling), they are [included under] <s>nigrahasthānas</s>.

children.text:
chalajātinigrahasthānānāṃ pṛthagupadeśa upalakṣaṇārthaḥ|
upalakṣitānāṃ svāvakye parivarjanaṃ chalajātinigrahasthānānāṃ paravākye paryanuyogaḥ|
jātestu pareṇapra yujyamāṇāyāḥ sulabhaḥ samādhiḥ, svayaṃ ca sukaraḥ prayoga iti/

children.translated_text: This <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> (science of logical inquiry), being analyzed through the categories beginning with <s>pramāṇa</s> —
is a lamp for all sciences, a means for all actions,
a foundation for all <s>dharmas</s> — so it is celebrated in the teaching of the sciences.

The separate teaching of <s>chala</s> (quibbling), <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinder), and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (points of defeat) is for the purpose of characterization. Having characterized them, one avoids <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> in one's own speech, and challenges them in the opponent's speech. Moreover, when <s>jāti</s> is employed by the opponent, its refutation is easy, and its own employment is also easy.

children.text:
tadidaṃ tatvajñānaṃ niḥśreyasādhigamaśca yathāvidyaṃ vedatavyam|
iha tvadhyātmavidyāyāmātmādijñānaṃ tatvajñānam/
niḥśreyasādhigamāpavargaprāptiriti//2//
children.translated_text: This <s>tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality) and the attainment of <s>niḥśreyasa</s> (the highest good) are to be understood according to their respective sciences. Here, however, in <s>adhyātmavidyā</s> (the science of the self), knowledge of <s>ātman</s> (self) and the rest is <s>tattvajñāna</s>. The attainment of <s>niḥśreyasa</s> is the obtaining of <s>apavarga</s> (final liberation). //2//

children.text: tat khalu vai niḥśreyasaṃ kiṃ tattvajñānānantarameva bhavati? netyucyate kiṃ tarhi? tattvajñānād--
children.translated_text: Now, does that <s>niḥśreyasa</s> (highest good) come about immediately after <s>tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality)? No, it is said. What then? From <s>tattvajñāna</s> —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.2: <s>Apavarga</s> (final liberation) results from the successive cessation of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), <s>janma</s> (birth), <s>pravṛtti</s> (activity), <s>doṣa</s> (faults), and <s>mithyājñāna</s> (false knowledge) — each [being removed] upon the removal of the one following it, [culminating in] the absence of what immediately follows.

children.text:
tatrātmādyapavargaparyante prameye mithyājñānamanekaprakārakaṃ vartate|
ātmani tāvannāstīti, anātmanyātmeti, duḥkhe sukhamiti, anitye nityamiti, atrāṇe trāṇamiti, sabhaye nirbhayamiti, jugupsite 'bhimatamiti, hātavye apratihātavyamiti, pravṛttau nāsti karma, nāsti karmaphalamiti, doṣeṣu nāyaṃ doṣanimittaḥ saṃsāra iti|
pretyabhāve nāsti janturjīvo vā sattva ātmā vā yaḥ preyāt pretya ca bhavediti, anamittaṃ janma, animitto janmoparama iti, ādimān pretyabhāvo 'nantaśceti, naimittikaḥ sannakarmaṃnimittaḥ pretyabhāva iti, dehendriyabuddhivedanāsantānocchedapratisandhānābhyāṃ nirātmakaḥ pretyabhāva iti|
apavarge bhīṣmaḥ khalvayaṃ sarvakāryoparamaḥ, sarvaviprayoge 'pavarge bahu bhadrakaṃ lupyataṃ iti kathaṃ buddhimān sarvasukhocchedamacaitanyamamumapavargaṃ rocayediti//
children.translated_text: There, regarding <s>prameya</s> (the knowable) ranging from <s>ātman</s> (self) to <s>apavarga</s> (liberation), <s>mithyājñāna</s> (false knowledge) of many kinds operates. Regarding the <s>ātman</s> first: 'it does not exist'; regarding the non-self: 'this is the self'; regarding suffering: 'this is pleasure'; regarding the impermanent: 'this is permanent'; regarding what offers no refuge: 'this is a refuge'; regarding what is fearful: 'this is without fear'; regarding what is loathsome: 'this is desirable'; regarding what is to be abandoned: 'this need not be abandoned'; regarding activity: 'there is no <s>karma</s> (action), there is no fruit of <s>karma</s>'; regarding the <s>doṣas</s> (faults): 'this <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of transmigration) is not caused by faults.' Regarding rebirth (<s>pretyabhāva</s>): 'there is no being, no living soul, no creature, no self that departs and exists after death'; 'birth is without cause, cessation of birth is without cause'; 'rebirth has a beginning but no end'; 'though caused, rebirth is not caused by <s>karma</s>'; 'rebirth is without a self due to the interruption and re-connection of the series of body, sense-organs, intellect, and sensation.' Regarding <s>apavarga</s> (liberation): 'frightful indeed is this cessation of all activity; in <s>apavarga</s>, where there is separation from everything, much that is good is lost — how would a wise person desire this <s>apavarga</s> that is the destruction of all pleasure and is devoid of consciousness?'

children.text:
etasmānmithyājñānādanukūleṣu rāgaḥ, pratikūleṣu ca dveṣaḥ|
rāgadveṣādhikārāccāsatyerṣyāsūyāmānalobhādayo doṣā bhavanti|
doṣaiḥ prayuktaḥ śarīreṇa pravartamāno hiṃsāsteyapratiṣiddhamaithunānyācarati|
vācā anṛtaparūṣasūcanāsambaddhāni|
manasā paradrohaṃ paradravyābhīpsāṃ nāstikyaṃ ceti|
seyaṃpāpātmikā pravṛttiradharmāya//
children.translated_text: From this false knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>), there arises attachment (<s>rāga</s>) towards agreeable [objects] and aversion (<s>dveṣa</s>) towards disagreeable [objects]. From the prevalence of attachment and aversion, faults (<s>doṣa</s>) such as falsehood, envy, malice, pride, greed, and the like arise. Impelled by [these] faults, one engages through the body in violence (<s>hiṃsā</s>), theft, and prohibited sexual intercourse; through speech in falsehood, harsh words, slander, and incoherent speech; through the mind in ill-will toward others, coveting others' property, and nihilism (<s>nāstikya</s>). This activity, whose nature is sinful, leads to <s>adharma</s> (demerit).

children.text:
atha śubhā, śarīreṇa dānaṃ paritrāṇaṃ paraciraṇaṃ ca|
vācā satyaṃ hitaṃ priyaṃ svādhyāyaṃ ceti|
manasā dayāmaspṛhāṃ śraddhāṃ ceti|
seyaṃ dharmāya|
atra pravattisādhanau dharmādharmauṃ pravṛttiśabdenoktau, yathānnasādhanāḥ prāṇāḥ, annaṃ vai prāṇinaḥ prāṇāḥ iti|
seyaṃ pravṛttiḥ kutsitasyābhipūjitasya ca janmanaḥ kāraṇam|
janma punaḥ śarīrendriyabuddhivedanānāṃ nikāyaviśiṣṭaḥ prādurbhāvaḥ|
tasmin sati duḥkham, tatpunaḥ pratikūlavedanīyaṃ bādhanā pīḍā tāpa iti|
ta hame mithyājñānādayo duḥkhāntā dharmā avicchedena pravartamānāḥ saṃsāra iti//
children.translated_text: Now the auspicious [activity]: through the body — giving (<s>dāna</s>), protection, and service to others; through speech — truth, beneficial words, pleasant words, and self-study (<s>svādhyāya</s>); through the mind — compassion (<s>dayā</s>), non-covetousness, and faith (<s>śraddhā</s>). This leads to <s>dharma</s> (merit). Here, <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, which are the means of activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>), are referred to by the word 'activity,' just as the vital breaths (<s>prāṇa</s>), which are the means of food, [are called] 'food' — as in 'food indeed is the life of living beings.' This activity is the cause of birth that is either despised or honored. Birth, moreover, is the manifestation of the body, sense-organs, intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), and sensations, distinguished according to specific bodily forms (<s>nikāya</s>). When that [birth] exists, there is suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>); and that [suffering] is what is experienced as disagreeable — affliction, distress, torment. These factors beginning with false knowledge and ending with suffering, proceeding without interruption, constitute <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of transmigration).

children.text:
yadā tu tattvajñānānmithyājñānamapaiti, tadā mithyājñānāye doṣā apayanti|
doṣāpāye pravṛttirapaiti, pravṛttyapāye janmāpaiti|
janmāpāye duḥkhamapaiti|
duḥkhāpāye cātyantiko 'pavargo niḥśreyasamiti//
children.translated_text: But when, through knowledge of reality (<s>tattvajñāna</s>), false knowledge departs, then with the departure of false knowledge, the faults depart. With the departure of faults, activity departs; with the departure of activity, birth departs; with the departure of birth, suffering departs. With the departure of suffering, there is absolute liberation (<s>apavarga</s>) — the supreme good (<s>niḥśreyasa</s>).

children.text:
tattvajñānaṃ tu khalu mithyājñānaviparyayeṇa vyākhyātam|
ātmani tāvat astīti|
anātmanyanātmeti|
evaṃ duḥkhe 'nitye 'trāṇe sabhaye jugupsite hātavye ca yathāviṣayaṃ veditavyam|
pravṛttau, asti karmāsti karmaphalamiti|
doṣeṣa, doṣanimitto 'yaṃ saṃsāra iti|
pretyabhāve khalu, asti janturjovaḥ sattva ātmā vā yaḥ preyāt pretya ca bhavediti|
nimittavajjanma nimittavān janmoparama iti, anādiḥ pretyabhāvo 'pavargānta iti, naimittikaḥ san pretyabhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: Knowledge of reality, indeed, has been explained as the opposite of false knowledge. Regarding the <s>ātman</s> (self), first: 'it exists.' Regarding what is not the self: '[it is] not the self.' Likewise, regarding suffering, [it should be known as] impermanent, without protection, fearful, disgusting, and to be abandoned — each according to its proper domain. Regarding activity: 'action exists, the fruit of action exists.' Regarding the faults: 'this <s>saṃsāra</s> is caused by faults.' Regarding the afterlife (<s>pretyabhāva</s>), indeed: 'there exists a being — a creature, a living entity, a self — who departs and, having departed, comes into being again.' Birth has a cause; the cessation of birth has a cause. The afterlife is beginningless and ends with liberation (<s>apavarga</s>). Being caused, the afterlife

children.text:
pravṛttinimittaṃ iti|
sātmkaḥ san dehendriyabuddhivedanāsantānocchedapratisandhānābhyāṃ pravartata iti|
apavarge, śāntaḥ
children.translated_text: is caused by activity. Being endowed with a self (<s>sātmaka</s>), it proceeds through the severance and reconnection of the continuum of body, sense-organs, intellect, and sensations. Regarding liberation (<s>apavarga</s>): it is peaceful;

children.text:
khalvayaṃ sarvaviprayogaḥ sarvoparamo 'pavargaḥ, bahu ca kṛcchraṃ ghora pāpakaṃ lupyata iti kathaṃ buddhimān sarvaduḥkhocchedaṃ sarvaduḥkhāsaṃvidamapavargaṃ na rocayediti|
tad yathā, madhuviṣasaṃpṛktamannamanādeyamiti|
evaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhānuṣaktamanādeyamiti//2//
children.translated_text: indeed, this complete separation from all, this total cessation, is <s>apavarga</s> (liberation); and much that is painful, terrible, and sinful is destroyed — so how would an intelligent person not delight in <s>apavarga</s>, which is the complete destruction of all suffering and the complete absence of awareness of all suffering? Just as food mixed with honey and poison is not to be accepted, so too pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) conjoined with suffering is not to be accepted. //2//

children.text:
trividhā cāsya śāstrasya pravṛttirūddeśo lakṣaṇaṃ parīkṣā ceti|
tatra nāmadheyena padārthamātrasyābhidhānamuddeśaḥ|
tatroddiṣṭasyātattvavyavacchedako dharmo lakṣaṇam|
lakṣitasya yathālakṣaṇamupapadyate na veti pramāṇairavadhāraṇaṃ parīkṣā|
tatroddiṣṭasya pravibhaktasya lakṣaṇamucyate, yathā pramāṇānāṃ prameyasya ca|
uddiṣṭasya lakṣitasya ca vibhāgavacanam, yathā chalasya---
vacanavighāto 'rthavikalpopapattyā chalam [1.1.3]
tat trividham [1.2.11]
iti//
children.translated_text: The procedure of this <s>śāstra</s> (science) is threefold: enumeration (<s>uddeśa</s>), definition (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>), and examination (<s>parīkṣā</s>). Of these, enumeration is the mere designation of a category by name. Therein, the definition is the property that distinguishes the enumerated [category] from what it is not. Examination is the ascertainment through <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) whether the defined [category] conforms to its definition or not. Therein, the definition of what has been enumerated and classified is stated — as in the case of the <s>pramāṇas</s> and <s>prameya</s> (objects of valid knowledge). The statement of division of what has been enumerated and defined — as in the case of <s>chala</s> (quibble): 'The frustration of [an opponent's] statement through a meaning different from the intended one is <s>chala</s>' [1.1.3], 'that is threefold' [1.2.11].
Now, the statement of division of what has been enumerated —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.3: Perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), inference (<s>anumāna</s>), analogy (<s>upamāna</s>), and verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>) are the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge). //

children.text:
akṣāsyākṣasya prativiṣayaṃ vṛttiḥ pratyakṣam|
vṛttistu sannikarṣo jñānaṃ vā|
yadā sannikarṣastadā jñānaṃ pramitiḥ, yadā jñānaṃ tadā hānopādānopekṣabuddhayaḥ phalam|
mitena liṅgena liṅgino 'rthasya paścānmānamanumānam|
upamānaṃ sāmīpyamānam, yathā gaurevaṃ gavaya iti|
sāmīpyaṃ tu sāmānyayogaḥ|
śabdaḥ śabdyate 'nenārtha ityabhidhīyate vijñāpyata iti//
children.translated_text: The functioning of each sense-organ (<s>akṣa</s>) with respect to its own object is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception). 'Functioning' means either contact (<s>sannikarṣa</s>) or cognition (<s>jñāna</s>). When it is contact, then cognition is the resultant knowledge (<s>pramiti</s>); when it is cognition, then the [practical] result is the judgments of rejection, acceptance, or indifference. <s>Anumāna</s> (inference) is the subsequent measurement of an object possessing a mark (<s>liṅgin</s>) through a measured mark (<s>liṅga</s>). <s>Upamāna</s> (analogy) is measurement by similarity — as in 'a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is like a cow.' Similarity, moreover, is the possession of common properties. <s>Śabda</s> (verbal testimony) is that by which a meaning is expressed — it is called 'signification' or 'communication.'

children.text:
upalabdhisādhānāni pramāṇānīti samākhyānirvacanasāmārthyād boddhavyam|
pramīyate 'neneti karaṇārthābhidhāno hi pramāṇaśabdaḥ|
tadviśeṣasamākhyāyā api tathaiva vyākhyānam//
children.translated_text: That the <s>pramāṇas</s> are the means of apprehension should be understood from the etymological force of the designation. For the word <s>pramāṇa</s> denotes the instrumental sense — 'that by which one measures.' The explanation of the specific designations [of each <s>pramāṇa</s>] is likewise.

children.text: kiṃ punaretāni pramāṇāni prameyamabhisaṃplavante, atha pratiprameyaṃ vyavatiṣṭhanta iti? ubhayathā darśanam/
children.translated_text: Now, do these <s>pramāṇas</s> converge upon [a single] object of knowledge (<s>prameya</s>), or do they each apply to separate objects? Both views are observed.
That the self (<s>ātman</s>) exists is known from the instruction of a reliable person (<s>āpta</s>). Here, inference [also applies]:
'Desire, aversion, effort, pleasure, pain, and cognition are the marks (<s>liṅga</s>) of the self' [1.1.10].
Perception [of the self] is available to one who practices <s>yoga</s> — born from <s>yogic samādhi</s> (meditative absorption),
'The self is perceptible from a special conjunction of the self, the inner self, and the mind' [<s>Vaiśeṣikasūtra</s> 6.1.11].

children.text:
agnirāptopadeśāt pratīyate amutrāgniriti/
pratyāsīdatā dhūmadarśanenānumīyate|
pratyāsannena
ca pratyakṣata upalabhyate|
vyavasthā punaḥ,
children.translated_text: Fire is known from the instruction of a reliable person — 'there is fire over there.' By one approaching, it is inferred through the perception of smoke. By one who has come near, it is perceived directly. The proper allocation [of <s>pramāṇas</s>], however, [is illustrated by]:
'One who desires heaven should perform the <s>Agnihotra</s>'

children.text:
iti|
laukikasya svarge na liṅgadarśanam, na pratyakṣam|
stanayitnuśabde śrūyamāṇe śabdahetoranumānam|
tatra na pratyakṣaṃ nāgamaḥ|
pāṇau ca pratyakṣata upalabhyamāne nānumānaṃ nāgama iti//
children.translated_text: — for an ordinary person, there is neither inferential evidence nor direct perception regarding heaven. When the sound of thunder is heard, there is inference from a sound-based cause; in that case, there is neither perception nor scripture. And when [something] is directly perceived in the hand, there is neither inference nor scripture.

children.text:
sā ceyaṃ pramitiḥ pratyakṣaparā|
jijñāsitamarthamāptopadeśāt pratipadyamāno liṅgadarśanenāpi bubhutsate|
liṅgadarśanenānumitaṃ ca pratyakṣato didṛkṣate|
pratyakṣata upalabdhe 'rthe jijñāsā nivartate|
pūrvoktamudāharaṇamagniriti/
children.translated_text: And this valid cognition (<s>pramiti</s>) ultimately depends on perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>). One who apprehends a desired object from the instruction of a reliable person also wishes to ascertain it through the observation of inferential marks. What has been inferred through the observation of marks, one also desires to see directly. When the object is directly perceived, inquiry ceases. The previously stated example of fire [illustrates this].

children.text: pramātuḥ pramātavye 'rthe pramāṇānāṃ saṃkaro 'bhisaṃplavaḥ, asakaro vyavastheti //3//
children.translated_text: The convergence of <s>pramāṇas</s> is the combined application of [multiple] <s>pramāṇas</s> to the knower's object of knowledge; their non-convergence is their proper allocation. //3//
Now, the statement of definitions of the classified [categories] —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.4: Perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>) is cognition that arises from the contact of a sense-organ with its object, that is non-verbal (<s>avyapadeśya</s>), non-erroneous (<s>avyabhicāri</s>), and of the nature of determinate judgment (<s>vyavasāyātmaka</s>). //

children.text:
indriyasyārthena sannikarṣādutpadyate yajjñānaṃ tat pratyakṣam|
na tarhi idānīmidaṃ bhavati ātmā manasā saṃyujyate, mana indriyeṇa, indriyamartheneti? nedaṃ kāraṇāvadhāraṇam--etāvatpratyakṣe kāraṇamiti, kiṃ tu viśiṣṭakāraṇavacanamiti/
yatpratyakṣajñānasya viśiṣṭakāraṇaṃ taducyate, yattu samānam anumānādijñānasya, na tannivartyata iti//
children.translated_text: The cognition that arises from the contact of a sense-organ with its object is perception. [Objection:] Is it not the case now that the self is conjoined with the mind, the mind with the sense-organ, and the sense-organ with the object? [Reply:] This is not a restriction of causes — meaning 'only this much is the cause of perception'; rather, it is a statement of the distinguishing cause. What is stated is the distinguishing cause of perceptual cognition; but what is common [also] to inferential and other cognitions is not thereby excluded.

children.text: manasastarhīndriyeṇa saṃyogo vaktavyaḥ? bhidyamānasya pratyakṣaśrajñānasya nāyaṃ bhidyata iti samānatvānnokta iti//
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Then should not the conjunction of the mind with the sense-organ also be stated? [Reply:] Since [the mind's conjunction] is not differentiated when perceptual cognition is differentiated [from other types] — i.e., because it is common [to all cognitions] — it is not stated.

children.text:
yāvadarthaṃ vai nāmadheyaśabdāstairarthasampratyayaḥ, arthasaṃpratyayācca vyavahāraḥ|
tatredamindriyārthasannikarṣādutpannamarthajñāna rūpam iti vā, rasa ityeva vā bhavati, rūparasaśabdāśca viṣayanāmadheyam|
tena vyapadiśyate jñānam--rūpamiti jānīte, rasa iti jānīte|
nāmagheyaśabdena vyapadiśyamānaṃ sat śābdaṃ prasajyate/
children.translated_text: Names are words sufficient for [conveying] their purpose; through them, comprehension of the meaning [arises], and from comprehension, practical activity. Here, this cognition of an object arising from the contact of a sense-organ with its object takes the form 'it is color' or 'it is taste,' and 'color,' 'taste,' etc., are names of sense-objects. Cognition is designated by these — 'he knows [it as] color,' 'he knows [it as] taste.' Being designated by a name-word, it would follow that [perception] is verbal (<s>śābda</s>).

children.text:
ata āha--avyapadeśyamiti|
yadidamanupayukte śabdārthasambandhe arthajñānam, na tat nāmadheyaśabdena vyapadiśyate, gṛhīte 'pi ca śabdārthasambandhe asyārthasyāyaṃ śabdo nāmadheyamiti|
yadā tu so 'rtho gṛhyate, tadā tatpūrvasmādarthajñānāt
children.translated_text: Therefore he says '<s>avyapadeśya</s>' (non-verbal). This cognition of an object, when the relation between word and meaning has not been employed, is not designated by a name-word; even when the relation between word and meaning has been grasped — 'this word is the name of this object' —

children.text:
na viśiṣyate, tat arthavijñānaṃ tādṛgeva bhavati|
tasya tvarthajñānasyānyaḥ samākhyāśabdo nāsti, yena pratīyamānaṃ
children.translated_text: when that object is [subsequently] apprehended, [the cognition] is not different from the prior cognition of the object; that cognition of the object is of exactly the same kind. But there is no other designating word for that cognition of the object by which, when [the object is] being cognized,

children.text:
vyavahārāya kalpet|
na cāpratīyamānena vyavahāraḥ|
tasmājjñeyasyārthasya saṃjñāśabdenetikaraṇayuktena nirddhiśyate--rūpamiti jñānam, rasa iti vā jñānamiti|
tadevamarthajñānakāle sa na samākhyāśabdo vyāpriyate, vyavahārakāle tu vyāpriyate|
tasmādaśābdam arthajñānamindriyārthasannikarṣotpannamiti//
children.translated_text: it could serve for practical activity. And without being cognized, there is no practical activity. Therefore, the cognition is indicated by the name-word of the object to be known, used in an instrumental sense — 'cognition of color,' or 'cognition of taste.' Thus, at the time of cognizing the object, that designating word does not function; but at the time of practical activity, it functions. Therefore, the cognition of an object arising from the contact of a sense-organ with its object is non-verbal.

children.text:
grīṣme marīcayo bhaumenoṣmaṇā saṃsṛṣṭāḥ spandamānā dūrasthasya cakṣuṣā sannikṛṣyante|
tatrendriyārthasannikarṣādudakamiti jñānamutpadyate|
tacca pratyakṣaṃ prasajyate ityata āha avyabhicārīti yadetasmiṃstadati
children.translated_text: In summer, mirages — trembling heat-waves mixed with terrestrial warmth — are brought into contact with the eye of a distant observer. There, from the contact of a sense-organ with its object, the cognition 'it is water' arises. And that would follow as being perception. Therefore he says '<s>avyabhicāri</s>' (non-erroneous): what [represents] that [thing] as being in that [place] —
that is erroneous (<s>vyabhicāri</s>); but what [represents] that [thing] as being that [thing itself], that is non-erroneous perception.

children.text:
dūrāccakṣuṣā hyayamarthaṃ paśyannāvadhārayati dhūma iti vā reṇuriti vā|
tadetadindriyārthasannikarṣotpannamanavadhāraṇajñānaṃ pratyakṣaṃ prasajyata ityata āha--vyavasāyātmakamiti|
na caitanmantavyam--ātmamanaḥ sannikarṣajamevānavadhāraṇajñānamiti|
kiṃ tarhi? cakṣuṣā hyayamarthaṃ paśyannāvadhārayati, yathā cendriyeṇa upalabdhamartha manasopalabhate, evamindriyeṇānavadhārayanmanasā nāvadhārayati|
yacca tadindriyānavadhāraṇapūrvakaṃ manasānavadhāraṇaṃ tadviśeṣāpekṣaṃ vimarśemātraṃ saṃśayaḥ, na pūrvamiti|
sarvatra ca pratyakṣaviṣaye jñāturindriyeṇa vyavasāyaḥ, paścānmanasānuvyavasāyaḥ, upahatendriyāṇāmanuvyavasāyābhāvāditi//
children.translated_text: For one seeing an object from afar with the eye does not ascertain whether it is smoke or dust. This cognition arising from the contact of a sense-organ with its object, being indeterminate, would follow as being perception. Therefore he says '<s>vyavasāyātmaka</s>' (of the nature of determinate judgment). And one should not think that indeterminate cognition is produced only from the conjunction of the self and mind. Why then? Because one seeing an object with the eye does not ascertain it; and just as the mind apprehends an object apprehended by a sense-organ, so too when [one] does not ascertain through the sense-organ, [one] does not ascertain through the mind either. And that indeterminate cognition preceded by sense-organ non-ascertainment, being dependent on distinguishing features, is mere deliberation — it is doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>), not prior [determinate cognition]. And in every case in the domain of perception, the knower first has determinate judgment (<s>vyavasāya</s>) through the sense-organ, and afterwards reflective judgment (<s>anuvyavasāya</s>) through the mind — since for those with impaired sense-organs, reflective judgment does not occur.

children.text:
ātmādiṣu sukhādiṣu ca pratyakṣalakṣaṇaṃ vaktavyam, anindriyārthasannikarṣajaṃ hi taditi|
indriyasya vai sato manasa indriyebhyaḥ pṛthagupadeśo dharmaṃbhedāt|
bhautikānīndriyāṇi niyataviṣayāṇi, saguṇānāṃ caiṣāmindriyabhāva iti|
manastvabhautikaṃ
children.translated_text: [Objection:] The definition of perception should be stated for the self (<s>ātman</s>) and for pleasure (<s>sukha</s>) and the like, since the cognition of these does not arise from contact of a sense-organ with an object. [Reply:] Indeed, the mind (<s>manas</s>) being a [kind of] sense-organ, it is taught separately from the [other] sense-organs because of a difference in properties. The [physical] sense-organs are material (<s>bhautika</s>) and have restricted objects; and their being sense-organs is [due to their being constituted] of [the material] qualities. But the mind is non-material (<s>abhautika</s>),

children.text:
sarvaviṣayaṃ ca, nāsya saguṇasyendriyabhāva iti|
sati cendriyārthasannikarṣe sannidhimasannidhi cāsya yugapajjñānānutpattikāraṇaṃ vakṣyāmaḥ(1/1/16) iti|
manasaścendriyābhāvānna vācyaṃ lakṣaṇāntaramiti/
children.translated_text: has all things as its objects, and its being a sense-organ is not [due to material] qualities. And we shall state [in NyS 1.1.16] that the presence or absence of the mind, when there is contact of a sense-organ with its object, is the cause of the non-simultaneous arising of cognitions. Since the mind is not excluded from being a sense-organ, no separate definition is needed.
And this should be understood from the accepted practice of other systems.
For it is a principle of systematic reasoning (<s>tantrayukti</s>) that what is accepted by another [school] and not rejected [by us] is [implicitly] approved.
Perception has been explained. // 4 //

children.text: NyS_1,1.5: atha tatpūrvakaṃ trividham anumānaṃ pūrvavaccheṣavatsāmānyato dṛṣṭaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.5: Now, inference (<s>anumāna</s>), which is preceded by that [perception], is threefold: <s>pūrvavat</s> (from cause to effect), <s>śeṣavat</s> (from effect to cause), and <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (based on general observation). //

children.text:
tatpūrvakamityanena liṅgaliṅginoḥ sambandhadarśanaṃ|
liṅgadarśanaṃ cābhisaṃbadhyate|
liṅgaliṅginoḥ saṃbaddhayordarśanena liṅgasmṛtirabhisaṃbadhyate|
smṛtyā liṅgadarśanena cāpratyakṣo 'rtho 'numīyate//
children.translated_text: By 'preceded by that' (<s>tatpūrvaka</s>), the perception of the relation between the mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and the possessor of the mark (<s>liṅgin</s>), and the [subsequent] perception of the mark, are connected. Through the perception of the mark and its possessor as related, the recollection of the mark is connected [to the inference]. Through recollection and the perception of the mark, an imperceptible object is inferred.

children.text:
pūrvavaditi--yatra kāraṇena kāryamanumīyate, yathā medhonnatyā bhaviṣyati vṛṣṭiriti|
śeṣavattat--yatra kāryeṇa kāraṇamanumīyate, pūrvodakaviparītamudakaṃ nādyāḥ pūrṇatvaṃ śīghratvaṃ dṛṣṭhvā strotaso 'numīyate bhūtā vṛṣṭiriti|
sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ--vrajyāpūrvakamanyatra dṛṣṭasyānyatra darśanamiti, tathā cādityasya, tasmāt astyapratyakṣāpyādityasya vrajyeti//
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrvavat</s> — where an effect is inferred from a cause: for example, 'it will rain,' from the rising of clouds. <s>Śeṣavat</s> — where a cause is inferred from an effect: seeing the water of a river reversed from its previous [flow], its fullness, and its swiftness, one infers from the current that 'rain has occurred.' <s>Sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (based on general observation) — the observation elsewhere of something previously seen moving elsewhere; so too with the sun; therefore, though imperceptible, the sun's movement exists.
Alternatively, <s>pūrvavat</s> means — where, of two things previously perceived together, the perception of one [leads to] the inference of the other which is not perceived; for example,

children.text:
dhūmenāgniriti|
śeṣavannāma pariśaṣaḥ, sa ca prasaktapratiṣedhe 'nyatrāprasaṅgācchiṣyamāṇe saṃpratyayaḥ, yathā sadanityamevamādinā dravyaguṇakarmaṇāmaviśeṣeṇa sāmānyaviśeṣasamavāyebhyo nirbhaktasya śabdasya, tasmin dravyaguṇakarmasaṃśaye, na dravyam, ekadravyatvāt, na karma, śabdāntarahetutvāt, yastu śiṣyate so 'yamiti śabdasya guṇatvapratipattiḥ|
sāmānyatodṛṣṭaṃ nāma--yatrāpratyakṣe liṅgaliṅginoḥ sambandhe kenacidarthena liṅgasya sāmānyādapratyakṣo liṅgī gamyate, yathecchādibhirātmā, icchādayoguṇāḥ, guṇāśca dravyasaṃsthānāḥ, tadyadeṣāṃ sthānaṃ sa ātmeti//
children.translated_text: [As in] 'fire from smoke.' The <s>śeṣavat</s> (based on the remainder) is indeed the residual [inference]. And it is the cognition of what remains when what is connected is excluded elsewhere because there is no connection — for example, when the word (<s>śabda</s>) has been separated from <s>sāmānya</s> (universality), <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularity), and <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) by [the rule] 'eternally existent' and similar [attributes applied] without distinction to <s>dravya</s> (substance), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), and <s>karma</s> (action), and when there is doubt whether <s>śabda</s> is substance, quality, or action — it is not substance, because it exists in a single substance; it is not action, because it is the cause of another word — thus what remains is [the conclusion] 'this is a quality'; this is the cognition of the quality-nature of <s>śabda</s>. The <s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s> (inference from general observation) is — where the relation between the <s>liṅga</s> (inferential sign) and <s>liṅgin</s> (the thing inferred) is not perceptible, and through some common feature of the sign, the imperceptible thing inferred is cognized — as the <s>Ātman</s> (self) [is inferred] from desire and the like; desire and so on are <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), and qualities reside in <s>dravya</s> (substance); that in which they reside is the <s>Ātman</s>.

children.text: vibhāgavacanādeva trividhamiti siddhe trividhavacanaṃ mahato mahāviṣayasya nyāyasya laghīyasā sūtreṇopadeśāt paraṃ
children.translated_text: Since the threefold [nature] is already established by the statement of division, the explicit mention of 'threefold' is for the sake of teaching the great <s>Nyāya</s> (logic), which has a vast subject-matter, by means of a more concise <s>sūtra</s>,

children.text:
vākyalāghavaṃ manyamānasyānyasmin vākyalāghave 'nādaraḥ|
tathā cāyamasyetthambhūtena vākyavikalpena pravṛttaḥ siddhānte chale śabdādiṣu ca bahulaṃ samācāraḥ śāstra iti//
children.translated_text: For one who values economy of expression, there is disregard for other instances of verbal economy. And thus, this practice — engaged through such varieties of verbal formulation — is frequently found in the <s>śāstra</s> (treatise), in <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine), <s>chala</s> (quibble), <s>śabda</s> and other [categories].
Why? Because it apprehends [objects of] the three times — things connected with the three times (past, present, and future) are grasped by inference.
It is inferred 'it will be,' 'it is,' and 'it was.'
And indeed what is non-existent is the past and the future. [End of NyS 1.1.5]
<s>Pratyakṣa</s> (perception) has only existing things as its object, while <s>anumāna</s> (inference) has both existing and non-existing things as its object.
[Section: NySBh 1.1.6]
Now, <s>upamāna</s> (comparison) —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.6: <s>Upamāna</s> (comparison) is the means of establishing what is to be proved through similarity with what is well-known.

children.text:
prajñātena sāmānyātprajñāpanīyasya prajñāpanamupamānamiti|
yathā gaurevaṃ gavaya iti|
kiṃ punaratropamānena kriyate? yadā khalvayaṃ gavā samānadharmaṃ pratidyate, tadā pratyakṣatastamarthaṃ pratipadyata iti|
samākhyāsambandhapratipattiḥ upamānārthaṃ ityāha|
yathā gaurevaṃ gavaya ityupamāne prayukte gavā samānadharmāṇam arthamindriyārthasaṃnikarṣādupalabhamāno 'sya gavayaśabdaḥ saṃjñeti saṃjñāsajñisambandhaṃ pratipadyata iti|
children.translated_text: When the <s>upamāna</s> 'a <s>gavaya</s> is like a cow' is employed, one who perceives an object having common properties with a cow through the contact of sense-organ and object, understands that the word '<s>gavaya</s>' is the name of this [animal] — thus one cognizes the relation between name (<s>saṃjñā</s>) and the named (<s>saṃjñin</s>).

children.text: yathā mudgastathā mūdgaparṇī yathā bhāṣastathā māṣapaṇītyupamāne prayukte upamānātsaṃjñāsaṃjñisambandhaṃ pratipadyamānastāmoṣadhī bhaiṣajyāya āharati|
children.translated_text: When the <s>upamāna</s> 'a <s>mūdgaparṇī</s> (plant) is like a <s>mudga</s> (mung bean)' or 'a <s>māṣaparṇī</s> (plant) is like a <s>māṣa</s> (black gram)' is employed, one who cognizes the relation between name and named from the <s>upamāna</s> gathers those herbs for medicinal purposes.
Thus, other domains of <s>upamāna</s> in the world are also to be investigated. [End of NyS 1.1.6]

The making-known of what is to be made known, through a recognized commonality, is <s>upamāna</s> — for example, 'a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) is like a cow.' Now, what does <s>upamāna</s> accomplish here? When this [animal] is recognized as having a common property with a cow, then one cognizes that object through direct perception. The cognition of the relation between name and named — this, he says, is the purpose of <s>upamāna</s>.
[Section: NySBh 1.1.7]
Now, <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.7: <s>Śabda</s> (verbal testimony) is the instruction of a reliable person (<s>āpta</s>).

children.text:
āptaḥ khalu sākṣātkṛtadharmā yathādṛṣṭasyārthasya cikhyāpayiṣayā prayukta upadeṣṭā|
sākṣātkaraṇamarthasyāptiḥ,
children.translated_text: A reliable person (<s>āpta</s>) is indeed one who has directly realized <s>dharma</s>, who is a teacher motivated by the desire to communicate an object as it has been seen. The direct realization of an object is <s>āpti</s>,
The defining characteristic is the same for <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers), <s>āryas</s> (noble ones), and <s>mlecchas</s> (foreigners).

children.text: tathā ca sarveṣāṃ vyavahārāḥ pravartanta iti|
children.translated_text: And accordingly, the transactions of all [these groups] proceed.
Thus, by these <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), the transactions of gods, humans, and animals are determined — and not otherwise. [End of NyS 1.1.7]
One who acts on the basis of that is an <s>āpta</s> (reliable person).
[Section: NySBh 1.1.8]
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.8: That [verbal testimony] is of two kinds, because [it relates to] objects that are seen and unseen.

children.text:
yasyeha dṛśyate 'rthaḥ sa dṛṣṭārthaḥ|
yasyāmutra pratīyata so 'dṛṣṭārthaḥ|
evamṛṣilaukikavākyānāṃ vibhāga iti|
kimarthaṃ punaridamucyate? sa na manyeta dṛṣṭārthaṃ evāptopadeśaḥ pramāṇam, arthasyāvadhāraṇādita, adṛṣṭārtho 'pi
children.translated_text: For what purpose is this stated? Lest one think that the instruction of a reliable person is a valid means of knowledge only with respect to seen objects, because the object can be ascertained [by other means] — [it is stated that] even with respect to unseen objects,
it is a valid means of knowledge, because the object [can be known] through inference.
Thus ends the <s>bhāṣya</s> (commentary) on the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge). [End of NyS 1.1.8]

That whose object is seen here [in this world] is <s>dṛṣṭārtha</s> (relating to the seen). That whose object is understood in the other [world] is <s>adṛṣṭārtha</s> (relating to the unseen). Thus is the division of the statements of <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers) and worldly persons.
[Section: NySBh 1.1.9]
Now, what is the class of objects to be known through these <s>pramāṇas</s>? This is stated —

<s>NyS</s> 1.1.9: The <s>prameya</s> (objects of valid knowledge) are: <s>ātman</s> (self), <s>śarīra</s> (body), <s>indriya</s> (sense-organs), <s>artha</s> (objects), <s>buddhi</s> (cognition), <s>manas</s> (mind), <s>pravṛtti</s> (activity), <s>doṣa</s> (defects), <s>pretyabhāva</s> (transmigration), <s>phala</s> (fruit), <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), and <s>apavarga</s> (liberation).

children.text:
tatrātmā sarvasya draṣṭā sarvasya bhoktā sarvajñaḥ sarvānubhāvī|
tasya bhogāyatanaṃ śarīram|
bhogasādhanānīndriyāṇi|
bhoktavyā indriyārthāḥ|
bhogo buddhiḥ|
sarvārthopalabdhau nendriyāṇi prabhavantīti sarvaviṣayamantaḥkaraṇa manaḥ|
śarīrendriyārthabuddhisukhaduḥkhasaṃvedanānāṃ nirvṛttikāraṇaṃ pravṛttiḥ, doṣaśca|
nāsyedaṃ śarīramapūrvamanuttaraṃ ca|
pūrvaśarīrāṇāmādirnāsti, uttareṣāmapavargo 'nta iti pretyabhāvaḥ|
samādhanasukhaduḥkhopabhogaḥ phalam|
duḥkhamiti nedamanukūlavedanīyasya sukhasya pratīteḥ pratyākhyānam|
kiṃ tarhi? janmana evedaṃ sasukhasādhanasya duḥkhānuṣaṅgāt duḥkhenāviprayogādvividhabādhanāyogād duḥkhamiti samādhibhāvanamupadiśyate|
samāhito bhāvayati,
children.translated_text: Among these, the <s>Ātman</s> (self) is the seer of all, the experiencer of all, the knower of all, the one who experiences everything. The body (<s>śarīra</s>) is the locus of its experience. The sense-organs (<s>indriyas</s>) are the instruments of experience. The sense-objects (<s>indriyārthas</s>) are what is to be experienced. Cognition (<s>buddhi</s>) is the experience [itself]. Since the sense-organs are not capable of apprehending all objects, the mind (<s>manas</s>) is the internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>) that has all [objects] as its domain. Activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) and defects (<s>doṣa</s>) are the productive cause of the arising of experiences of pleasure and pain through body, sense-organs, objects, and cognition. This body of his is neither without a predecessor nor without a successor. The beginninglessness of prior bodies and the end of future ones through <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) — this is <s>pretyabhāva</s> (transmigration). The experience of pleasure and pain resulting from meditative concentration is the fruit (<s>phala</s>). '<s>Duḥkha</s> (suffering)' — this is not a rejection of the perception of pleasure, which is experienced as agreeable. What then? Since birth itself, together with the means of pleasure, is accompanied by suffering, since there is no separation from suffering, since there is the inevitable experience of various afflictions — 'this is suffering' — thus meditation in <s>samādhi</s> (concentrated absorption) is taught. One who is concentrated contemplates;

children.text:
bhāvayannirvidyate, nirviṇṇasya vairāgyam, viraktasyāpavarga iti|
janmamaraṇaprabandhocchedaḥ sarvaduḥkhaprahāṇamapavarga iti//
children.translated_text: One who contemplates becomes disenchanted; for the disenchanted, there is dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>); for the dispassionate, there is <s>apavarga</s> (liberation). The cessation of the continuous series of births and deaths, the complete abandonment of all suffering — this is <s>apavarga</s> (liberation).

children.text: asya tu tattvajñānādapavargo mithyājñānātsaṃsāra ityata etadupadiṣṭaṃ viśeṣeṇeti //9//
children.translated_text: But from the true knowledge of these [twelve categories listed in the sūtra], there is <s>apavarga</s> (liberation); from false knowledge, there is <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) — therefore these have been taught specifically. [End of NyS 1.1.9]

There are also other <s>prameyas</s> (objects of knowledge): <s>dravya</s> (substance), <s>guṇa</s> (quality), <s>karma</s> (action), <s>sāmānya</s> (universality), <s>viśeṣa</s> (particularity), and <s>samavāya</s> (inherence) — and through their subdivisions, they are innumerable.
[Section: NySBh 1.1.10]

children.text:
tatrātmā tāvatpratyakṣato na gṛhyate|
sa kimāptopadeśamātrādeva pratipadyata iti? netyucte|
anumānācca pratipattavya iti|
katham?
children.translated_text: Among these, the <s>Ātman</s> (self) is first — it is not grasped through direct perception. Is it then known only through the instruction of a reliable person? No, it is said — it is also to be known through inference. How?
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.10: Desire, aversion, effort, pleasure, pain, and cognition are the inferential marks (<s>liṅga</s>) of the <s>Ātman</s> (self).

children.text:
yajjātīyasyārthasya sannikarṣātsukhamātmāpalabdhavān, tajjātīyameva arthaṃ paśyannupādātumicchati, seyamādātumicchā ekasyānekārthadarśino darśanapratisandhānādbhavati liṅgamātmanaḥ|
niyataviṣaye hi buddhibhedamātre na saṃbhavati, dehāntaravaditi|
ekamekasyānekārthadarśino darśanapratisandhānāt duḥkhahetau dveṣaḥ|
yajjātīyo 'syārthaḥ sukhahetuḥ prasiddhastajjātīyamartha paśyan ādātuṃ prayatate|
so 'yaṃ prayatna ekamanekārthadarśinaṃ darśanapratisandhātāram anteraṇa na syāt|
niyataviṣaye hi buddhibhedāmātre na saṃbhavati, dehāntaravaditi|
etena duḥkhahetau prayatno vyākhyātaḥ|
sukhaduḥkhasmṛtyā cāyaṃ tatsādhanamādadānaḥ sukhamupalabhate duḥkhamupalabhate, suḥkhaduḥkhe vedayate|
pūrvokta eva hetuḥ|
bubhutsamānaḥ khalvayaṃ vimṛśati kiṃ sviditi, vimṛśaṃśca jānīte idamiti, tadidaṃ jñānaṃ bubhutsāvimarśābhyāmabhinnakartṛkaṃ gṛhyamāṇamātmano liṅgam|
pūrvokta eva heturiti|
tatra dehāntaravaditi vibhajyate|
yathā anātmavādino dehāntareṣu niyataviṣayā buddhibhedā na pratisandhīyante, tathaikadehaviṣayā api na pratisandhīyeran, aviśeṣāt|
so 'yamekasattvasya samācāraḥ svayandṛṣṭasya smaraṇaṃ, nānyadṛṣṭasya, nādṛṣṭasyeti|
children.translated_text: This is the practice of a single being — the remembering of what one has seen oneself, not of what another has seen, not of what has not been seen.

children.text: evaṃ khalu nānāsattvānāṃ samācāro 'nyadṛṣṭamanyo na smaratīti|
children.translated_text: Thus is the practice of different beings — another does not remember what one [being] has seen.
Both of these [facts] cannot be established by one who denies the <s>Ātman</s> — thus it is proven that the <s>Ātman</s> exists. [End of NyS 1.1.10]

When the <s>Ātman</s> has experienced pleasure from contact with a particular kind of object, seeing the same kind of object again, it desires to obtain it. This desire to obtain is the inferential mark of the <s>Ātman</s>, arising from the recognition (<s>pratisandhāna</s>) of [past] perceptions of a single [self] that has seen many objects. For in merely distinct cognitions with fixed objects, this [desire] would not be possible — as in different bodies. In one single [self] that has seen many objects, aversion arises toward the cause of suffering from the recognition of [past] perceptions. When a particular kind of object is known to be the cause of pleasure, seeing such an object, one makes effort to obtain it. This effort would not exist without a single [self] that has seen many objects and connects [past] perceptions. For in merely distinct cognitions with fixed objects, this would not be possible — as in different bodies. By this, effort toward the cause of suffering is also explained. And this one, through the memory of pleasure and suffering, while obtaining the means thereof, experiences pleasure and experiences suffering — it experiences pleasure and suffering. The reason is the same as stated before. Moreover, this one, desiring to know, deliberates 'what is this?' and while deliberating, knows 'this is such' — this cognition, grasped as having the same agent as the desire-to-know and the deliberation, is the inferential mark of the <s>Ātman</s>. The reason is the same as stated before. Regarding this, 'as in different bodies' is analyzed: Just as, for those who deny the <s>Ātman</s>, cognitions with fixed objects in different bodies are not connected through recognition, so also cognitions pertaining to a single body would not be connected, since there is no difference [in the argument].
[Section: NySBh 1.1.11]
The locus of its [the Ātman's] experience —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.11: The body (<s>śarīra</s>) is the locus of effort (<s>ceṣṭā</s>), sense-organs (<s>indriya</s>), and objects (<s>artha</s>).

children.text: kathaṃ ceṣṭāśrayaḥ? īpsitaṃ jihāsitaṃ vārthamadhikṛtyepsājihāsāprayuktasya tadupāyānuṣṭhānalakṣaṇā samīhā ceṣṭā, sa yatra
children.translated_text: How is it the locus of effort? With respect to an object that is desired or to be avoided, the endeavor (<s>samīhā</s>) characterized by the performance of the means [to attain or avoid] — which is impelled by desire and avoidance — is effort (<s>ceṣṭā</s>); that in which
it abides is the body.

children.text: kathamindriyāśrayaḥ? yasyānugraheṇānugṛhītāni upaghāte na copahatāni svaviṣayeṣu sādhvasādhuṣu pravartante, sa eṣāmāśrayaḥ taccharīram|
children.translated_text: How is it the locus of the sense-organs? That by whose support the sense-organs, when supported, function in their respective objects — both good and bad — and when impaired, are [themselves] impaired, is their locus — that is the body.

children.text: kathamarthāśrayaḥ? yasminnāyatane indriyārthasannikarṣādutpannayoḥ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ pratisaṃvedanaṃ pravartate, sa eṣāmāśrayaḥ taccharīramiti //11//
children.translated_text: How is it the locus of objects? That substrate in which the experience of pleasure and pain, arising from the contact of sense-organs and objects, occurs — that is their locus, that is the body. [End of NyS 1.1.11]
[Section: NySBh 1.1.12]
Now, the instruments of experience —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.12: The sense-organs (<s>indriyas</s>) are smell, taste, sight, touch, and hearing, [arising] from the elements (<s>bhūtas</s>).

children.text:
jighratyaneneti ghrāṇaṃ gandhaṃ gṛhṇātīti|
rasayatyaneneti rasanaṃ rasaṃ gṛhṇātīti|
caṣṭe 'neneti cakṣū rūpaṃ paśyatīti|
tvaksthānamindriyaṃ tvak|
tadupacāraḥ sthānāditi|
śṛṇotyaneneti śrotraṃ śabdaṃ gṛhṇātīti|
evaṃ samākhyānirvacanasāmarthyādbodhyaṃ svaviṣayagrahaṇalakṣaṇānīndriyāṇīti|

children.translated_text: 'From the elements (<s>bhūtas</s>)' —
The restriction of [each sense-organ to its specific] object is [possible] because these have different material causes (<s>prakṛtis</s>), not because they have a single material cause.
And given the restriction of objects, the characteristic of apprehending one's own object is established. [End of NyS 1.1.12]

That by which one smells is the organ of smell (<s>ghrāṇa</s>) — it grasps odor. That by which one tastes is the organ of taste (<s>rasana</s>) — it grasps flavor. That by which one sees is the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) — it perceives form. The sense-organ located at the skin (<s>tvak</s>) is [the organ of] touch — that is a metonymy, [naming the organ] after its location. That by which one hears is the ear (<s>śrotra</s>) — it grasps sound. Thus, by the force of the etymological derivation of the names, it is to be understood that the sense-organs are characterized by the apprehension of their respective objects.
[Section: NySBh 1.1.13]
Now, what are the causes of the sense-organs?
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.13: The elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) are earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>), water (<s>āpas</s>), fire (<s>tejas</s>), air (<s>vāyu</s>), and space (<s>ākāśa</s>).

children.text: saṃjñāśabdaiḥ pṛthagupadeśo bhūtānāṃ vibhaktānāṃ suvacaṃ kāryaṃ bhaviṣyatīti //13//
children.translated_text: The separate teaching of the elements through their distinctive names [indicates that] their distinct functions will be easy to state. [End of NyS 1.1.13]
[Section: NySBh 1.1.14]
Now, these indeed —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.14: Odor, flavor, form, touch, and sound are the qualities of earth and the others respectively; they are their objects.

children.text: pṛthivyādīnāṃ yathāviniyogaṃ guṇā indriyāṇāṃ yathākramamarthā viṣayā iti //14//
children.translated_text: They are the qualities of earth and the others in their respective assignments, and the objects — the domains — of the sense-organs in their respective order. [End of NyS 1.1.14]
[Section: NySBh 1.1.15]

children.text: acetanasya karaṇasya buddherjānaṃ vṛttiḥ, cetanasyākarturūpalabdhiriti yuktiviruddhamarthaṃ pratyācakṣāṇaka ivedamāha---
children.translated_text: As if challenging the logically contradictory position that cognition is the function of the unconscious instrument, and apprehension is [the function] of the conscious but non-acting [self], he states this —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.15: <s>Buddhi</s> (cognition), <s>upalabdhi</s> (apprehension), and <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) are synonymous.
For then that [instrument] would be conscious.
And this one conscious entity is distinct from the aggregate of body and sense-organs.
This is the illumination of an additional meaning of the statement defining <s>prameya</s> (objects of knowledge), through the force of logical reasoning. [End of NyS 1.1.15]
Cognition cannot belong to an unconscious instrument;
[Section: NySBh 1.1.16]

Memory, inference, <s>āgama</s> (scripture), doubt, intuitive insight (<s>pratibhā</s>), dream-cognition, and apprehension — as well as perception of pleasure and the like, and desire and so on — are the inferential marks of the mind (<s>manas</s>). Among these, there is also this —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.16: The non-simultaneous arising of cognitions is the inferential mark of the mind (<s>manas</s>).

children.text: yugapacca khalu ghrāṇādīnāṃ gandhādīnāṃ ca sannikarṣeṣu satsu yugapajjñānāni notpadyante|
children.translated_text: And indeed, when the contacts of smell and other [sense-organs] with odor and other [objects] are simultaneously present, simultaneous cognitions do not arise.

children.text: tenānumīyate, asti tattadindriyasaṃyogi sahakāri nimittāntaramavyāpi, yasyāsannidhernotpadyate jñānam, sannidheścotpadyata iti|
children.translated_text: From this it is inferred: there exists another cooperating cause, connected with each sense-organ, which is non-pervasive — from whose absence cognition does not arise, and from whose presence it does arise.
For if the contact of sense-organ and object were the cause of cognition without depending on conjunction with the mind (<s>manas</s>), cognitions would arise simultaneously. [End of NyS 1.1.16]
Memory and the like, which are not caused by sense-organs, must be caused by another instrument.
[Section: NySBh 1.1.17]
Now, [the topic] that has come up in order —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.17: Activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>) is the initiation of speech, mind, and body.
By 'mind' (<s>manas</s>) here, <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is intended; <s>buddhi</s> is that by which one cognizes.

children.text: so 'yabhārambhaḥ śarīreṇa vācā manasā ca puṇyaḥ pāpaśca daśavidhaḥ|
children.translated_text: This initiation [of action] (<s>ārambha</s>), by body, speech, and mind — meritorious (<s>puṇya</s>) and sinful (<s>pāpa</s>) — is tenfold.
This is the commentary (<s>bhāṣya</s>) composed on the second sūtra. //17//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.18: The <s>doṣas</s> (faults) are characterized as that which causes activity (<s>pravartanā</s>).

children.text:
pravartanā---pravṛttihetutvam, jñātāraṃ hi rāgādayaḥ pravartayanti puṇye pāpe vā|
yatra mityājñānaṃ tatra rāgadveṣāviti|
pratyātmavedanīyā hīme doṣāḥ kasmāllakṣaṇato nidrdiśyanta iti? karmalakṣaṇāḥ khalu raktadviṣṭamūḍhāḥ, rakto hi tatkarma kurute yena karmaṇā sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ vā labhate, tathā dviṣṭastathā mūḍha iti|
children.translated_text: Since these <s>doṣas</s> are to be known by each individual for himself, why are they indicated by a defining characteristic? Indeed, those who are attached, averse, or deluded are characterized by their actions (<s>karma</s>); for the attached person performs that action by which he obtains pleasure or pain, and likewise the averse, and likewise the deluded.
The <s>doṣas</s> (faults) are <s>rāga</s> (attachment), <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion), and <s>moha</s> (delusion) —
were this stated [directly], much would remain unsaid. //18//

<s>Pravartanā</s> (impelling) means being the cause of activity (<s>pravṛtti</s>); for <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and the rest impel the knower toward what is meritorious or sinful. Where there is false knowledge (<s>mithyājñāna</s>), there arise <s>rāga</s> (attachment) and <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion).
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.19: Rebirth (<s>pretyabhāva</s>) is renewed birth (<s>punarutpatti</s>) after death.

children.text:
utpannasya kvacitsattvanikāye mṛtvā yā punarūtpattiḥ sa pretyabhāvaḥ|
utpannasya---sambaddhasya|
sambandhastu dehendriyabuddhivedanābhiḥ|
punarūtpattiḥ--- punardehādibhiḥ sambandhaḥ|
purarityabhyāsābhidhānam|
yatra kvacitprāṇabhṛnnikāye varttamānaḥ pūrvopāttān dehādīn jahāti tatpraiti|

children.translated_text: When, there or elsewhere, he takes up other bodies and the rest — that is his 'becoming' (<s>bhava</s>).
<s>Pretyabhāva</s> means rebirth (<s>punarjanma</s>) after death.
This continuous series of birth and death, beginningless, ending with <s>apavarga</s> (final liberation) — this should be understood as <s>pretyabhāva</s>. //19//

The renewed birth of one who has been born in some category of beings, after dying — that is <s>pretyabhāva</s> (the state after death). 'Of one who has been born' means one who has been connected. The connection is with body, sense-organs, intellect, and sensations. 'Renewed birth' means renewed connection with body and the rest. The word 'again' (<s>punar</s>) indicates repetition. One existing in some category of living beings, who abandons the previously assumed body and the rest — that one 'departs' (<s>praiti</s>).
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.20: The result (<s>phala</s>) is the object produced by activity and <s>doṣas</s> (faults).

children.text:
sukhaduḥkhasaṃvedanaṃ phalam|
sukhavipākaṃ karma duḥkhavipākaṃ ca|
tatpunardehendriyaviṣayabuddhiṣu satīṣu bhavatīti saha dehādibhiḥ phalamabhipratam|
children.translated_text: That [result] moreover occurs when body, sense-organs, objects, and intellect are present; thus the result is intended together with body and the rest.
For thus, the object produced by activity and <s>doṣas</s> — all of this constitutes the result.

children.text: tadetatphalamupāttamupāttaṃ heyam, tyaktaṃ tyaktamupādeyamiti nāsya hānopādānayorniṣṭhā paryavasānaṃ vāsti, sa khalvayaṃ phalasya hānopādānasrotatasohyate loka iti //20//
children.translated_text: This result, once acquired, is to be abandoned; once abandoned, is [again] to be acquired — and thus there is no final end or conclusion to its abandonment and acquisition. Indeed, this world is carried along in the current of the acquisition and abandonment of results. //20//
The result (<s>phala</s>) is the experience of pleasure and pain. <s>Karma</s> (action) has either a pleasurable or a painful maturation (<s>vipāka</s>).
Now this very [topic continues] —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.21: <s>Duḥkha</s> (suffering) is characterized by affliction (<s>bādhanā</s>).
<s>Bādhanā</s> means pain, torment, anguish.
That which is bound up with it, inseparable from it, existing without distinction from it — due to its conjunction with suffering, it is [called] <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering).

children.text: so 'yaṃ sarvaṃ duḥkhenānubaddhamiti paśyan duḥkhaṃ jihāsurjanmani duḥkhadarśī nirvidyate nirviṇṇo virajyate virakto vimucyate //21//
children.translated_text: One who sees thus — 'everything is bound up with suffering' — desiring to abandon suffering, seeing suffering in birth, becomes dispassionate; being dispassionate, becomes detached; being detached, becomes liberated. //21//

children.text: yatra tu niṣṭhā yatra tu paryavasānaṃ so 'yam---
children.translated_text: But where there is a final end, where there is a conclusion — that is this —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.22: Absolute release from that [suffering] is <s>apavarga</s> (final liberation).

children.text:
tena duḥkhena janmanā atyantaṃ vimuktirapavargaḥ|
katham? upāttasya janmano hānam, anyasya cānupādānam|
etāmavasthāmaparyantāmapavargaṃ vedayante 'pavargavidaḥ|
tadabhayamajaramamṛtyupadaṃ brahma kṣemaprāpitariti//
children.translated_text: Absolute liberation from that suffering and birth is <s>apavarga</s>. How? The cessation of the assumed birth, and the non-assumption of another. Those who know <s>apavarga</s> describe this state as unlimited [and call it] <s>apavarga</s>. That is the fearless, ageless, deathless station — <s>Brahman</s>, the one who brings [beings] to safety.

children.text:
nityaṃ sukhamātmano mahattvavat tattu mokṣe abhivyajyate, tenābhivyaktenātyantaṃ vimuktaḥ sukhī bhavatīti kecit manyante|
teṣāṃ pramāṇābhāvādanupapattiḥ|
na pratyakṣaṃ nānumānaṃ nāgamo vā vidyate, nityaṃ sukhamātmano mahattvavat tattu mokṣe 'bhivyajyata iti//
children.translated_text: Some think that eternal pleasure belongs to the <s>ātman</s> (self), like [its] greatness, and that it becomes manifest in <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation); by that manifested [pleasure], the absolutely liberated one becomes happy. Their [view] is untenable due to the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge). There is no perception, nor inference, nor scripture [to establish] that eternal pleasure belongs to the <s>ātman</s>, like [its] greatness, and that it becomes manifest in <s>mokṣa</s>.

children.text:
nityasyābhivyaktiḥ saṃvedanam, tasya hetuvacanam|
nityasya sukhasyābhivyaktiḥ saṃvedanam jñānamiti, tasya heturvācyo yatastadutpadyata iti//
children.translated_text: The manifestation of what is eternal is its being experienced (<s>saṃvedana</s>); the cause of that must be stated. The manifestation of eternal pleasure is its experience, its cognition — and the cause from which that arises must be stated.

children.text:
sukhavannityamiti cet? saṃsārasthasya muktenāviśeṣaḥ|
yathā muktaḥ sukhena tatsaṃvedanena ca sannityenopapannastathā
children.translated_text: If [it is argued:] 'It is eternal, like pleasure'? Then there would be no distinction between the one in <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration) and the liberated one. Just as the liberated one is endowed with eternal pleasure and its experience,
so too would the one in <s>saṃsāra</s> be — there would be no distinction, because both are eternal.

children.text:
abhyunujñāne ca dharmādharmaphalena sāhacaryaṃ yaugapadyaṃ gṛhyate|
yadidam utpattisthāneṣu dharmādharmaphalaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca saṃvedyate paryāyeṇa, tasya ca nityasaṃvedanasya ca sahabhāvo yaugapadyaṃ gṛhyeta, na sukhābhāvo nānabhivyaktirasti, ubhayasya nityatvāt/
children.translated_text: And if [this is] accepted, the co-existence and simultaneity with the results of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) would be apprehended. The pleasure and pain that are the results of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> are experienced in succession in the places of birth; the co-existence and simultaneity of that [successive experience] with eternal experience would be apprehended — [meaning] there is neither absence of pleasure nor non-manifestation, because both are eternal.

children.text:
anityatve hetuvacanam|
atha mokṣe nityasya sukhasya savedanamanityam? yatastadutpadyate sa heturvācyaḥ|
ātmamanaḥsaṃyogasya nimittāntarasahitasya hetutvam|
tasya sahakārinimittāntaravacanam|
ātmamanaḥsaṃyogo heturiti cet? evamapi tasya sahakāri nimittāntaraṃ vacanīyamiti//
children.translated_text: The cause must be stated for [pleasure's] impermanence. But is the experience of eternal pleasure in <s>mokṣa</s> impermanent? The cause from which it arises must be stated. The conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> (mind), together with another co-operative cause, is the cause. The co-operative cause of that must be stated. If the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> is the cause? Even so, its co-operative cause — the other condition — must be stated.

children.text:
dharmasya kāraṇavacanam|
yadi dharmo nimittāntaram? tasya heturvācyo yata utpadyata iti|
yogasamādhijasya kāryāvasāyavirodhātprakṣaye saṃvedanenivṛttiḥ|
yadi yogasamādhijo dharmo hetuḥ? tasya kāryāvasāyavipodhātprakṣaye saṃvedanam amatyantaṃ nivarteta//
children.translated_text: The cause of <s>dharma</s> must be stated. If <s>dharma</s> is the other condition? Its cause — that from which it arises — must be stated. Since [<s>dharma</s>] born of <s>yoga</s>-<s>samādhi</s> is contradicted by the cessation of its effects, upon its exhaustion the experience would cease. If <s>dharma</s> born of <s>yoga</s>-<s>samādhi</s> is the cause? Due to the contradiction with the cessation of its effects, upon its exhaustion, the experience would cease — but not absolutely.

children.text:
asaṃvedane cāvidyamānenāviśeṣaḥ|
yadi dharmakṣayātsaṃvedanoparamo nityaṃ sukhaṃ na saṃvedyate iti kiṃ vidyamānaṃ na saṃvedyate, athāvidyamānamiti nānumānaṃ viśiṣṭe 'satīti/
children.translated_text: And in the absence of experience, there would be no distinction from the non-existent. If, due to the exhaustion of <s>dharma</s>, the experience ceases and eternal pleasure is not experienced — is it existent but not experienced, or non-existent? There is no inference when the distinguishing [characteristic] is absent.
