children.text:
aprakṣayaśca dharmasya niranumānamutpattidharmakasyānityatvāt|
yogasamādhijo dharmo na kṣīyata iti nāstyanumānam|
utpattidharmakamanityamiti viparyayasya tvanumānam|
yasya tu saṃvedanoparamo nāsti tena saṃvedanaheturnitya ityanujñeyam//
children.translated_text: And the non-exhaustion of <s>dharma</s> is without inferential support, because what is subject to origination is impermanent. That <s>dharma</s> born of <s>yoga</s>-<s>samādhi</s> does not get exhausted — there is no inference for this. Rather, there is inference for the contrary: what is subject to origination is impermanent. But for that whose experience does not cease, the cause of experience must be acknowledged as eternal.

children.text:
nitye ca muktasaṃsārasthayoraviśeṣa ityuktam|
yathā muktasya nityaṃ sukhaṃ tatsaṃvedanahetuśca, saṃvedanasya tūparamo nāsti, kāraṇasya nityatvāt, tathā saṃsārasthasyāpīti|
evaṃ ca sati dharmādharmaphalena sukhaduḥkhasaṃvedanena sāhacaryaṃ gṛhyeteti//
children.translated_text: And when [the cause] is eternal, there would be no distinction between the liberated and the one in <s>saṃsāra</s> — as stated. Just as the liberated one has eternal pleasure and its cause of experience, and there is no cessation of experience because the cause is eternal — so too for the one in <s>saṃsāra</s>. And this being so, co-existence with the experience of pleasure and pain, the results of <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, would be apprehended.

children.text:
śarīrādisambandhaḥ pratibandhaheturiti cet? na, śarīrādīnāmupabhogārthatvāt, viparyayasya cānanumānāt|
syānmatam, saṃsārāvasthasya śarīrādisambandho nityasukhasaṃvedanahetoḥ pratibandhakaḥ, tenāviśeṣo nāstīti|
etaccāyuktam, śarīrādaya upabhogārthāste bhogapratibandhaṃ kariṣyantītya nupapannam |
na cāstyanumānamaśarīrasyātmano bhogaḥ kaścidastīti//
children.translated_text: If [it is argued:] 'Connection with body and the rest is the obstructing cause'? No, because body and the rest are for the purpose of enjoyment, and there is no inference for the contrary. One might think that the connection with body and the rest obstructs the cause of the experience of eternal pleasure for the one in <s>saṃsāra</s>, so there is no lack of distinction. But this is unjustified — body and the rest are for the purpose of enjoyment; that they would obstruct enjoyment is untenable. Nor is there any inference that the bodiless <s>ātman</s> has any enjoyment.

children.text:
iṣṭādhigamārthā pravṛttiriti cet? na, aniṣṭoparamārthatvāt|
idam anumānam, iṣṭādhigamārtho mokṣopadeśaḥ pravṛttiśca mumukṣūṇām, nobhayamanarthakamiti|
etaccāyuktam, aniṣṭoparamārtho mokṣopadeśaḥ, pravṛttiśca mumukṣūṇāmiti|
neṣṭamaniṣṭenānanubaddhaṃ sambhavatīti aniṣṭānubandhāt iṣṭamapyaniṣṭasampadyate, aniṣṭahānāya ca ghaṭamāna iṣṭamapi jahāti, vivekahānasyāśakyatvāditi//
children.translated_text: If [it is argued:] 'Activity is for the purpose of attaining what is desired'? No, because [liberation] is for the purpose of the cessation of what is undesired. This inference [runs]: the teaching of <s>mokṣa</s> and the activity of those seeking liberation are for the purpose of attaining what is desired — neither would be purposeless. But this is unjustified; the teaching of <s>mokṣa</s> and the activity of those seeking liberation are for the purpose of the cessation of what is undesired. What is desired cannot exist without being accompanied by what is undesired; because of its accompaniment by what is undesired, even what is desired becomes undesirable. And one striving for the removal of what is undesired abandons even what is desired, because separation [of the two] is impossible.

children.text:
dṛṣṭātikramaśca dehādiṣu tulyaḥ|
yathā dṛṣṭamanityaṃ sukhaṃ parityajya nityaṃ sukhaṃ kāmayate, evaṃ dehendriya buddhīranityā dṛṣṭā anikramya muktasya nityā dehendriyabuddhayaḥ kalpayitavyāḥ, sādhīyaścaivaṃ muktasya caikātmyaṃ kalpitaṃ bhavatīti//
children.translated_text: And the transgression of what is observed is the same regarding body and the rest. Just as one abandons observed impermanent pleasure and desires eternal pleasure, so too — having observed that body, sense-organs, and intellect are impermanent — eternal body, sense-organs, and intellect would have to be postulated for the liberated one; and thus a more extreme identity of the liberated one would be postulated.

children.text:
upapattivirūddhamiti cet? samānam|
dehādīnāṃ nityatvaṃ pramāṇavirūddhaṃ kalpayayitumaśakyamiti? samānam|
sukhasyāpi tarhi nityatvaṃ pramāṇavirūddhaṃ kalpayitumaśakyamiti//
children.translated_text: If [it is argued:] 'This contradicts reason'? The same [applies to your view]. [You say] the eternality of body and the rest cannot be postulated because it contradicts the <s>pramāṇas</s>? The same [applies]: the eternality of pleasure also cannot be postulated because it contradicts the <s>pramāṇas</s>.

children.text:
ātyantike ca saṃsāraduḥkhābhāve sukhavacanādāgame 'pi satyavirodhaḥ|
yadyapi kaścidāgamaḥ syāt muktasyātyantikaṃ sukhamiti? sukhaśabda ātyantike duḥkhābhāve prayukta ityevamupapadyate, dṛṣṭo hi duḥkhābhāve sukhaśabdaprayogo bahulaṃloka iti//
children.translated_text: And even if there is a scriptural statement of pleasure in the absolute absence of <s>saṃsāric</s> suffering, there is no real contradiction. Even if there is some scripture [saying] 'the liberated one has absolute pleasure' — the word 'pleasure' (<s>sukha</s>) is used for the absolute absence of suffering; this is how it is justified, for the use of the word 'pleasure' in the absence of suffering is commonly seen in the world.

children.text:
nityasukharāgasyāprahāṇe mokṣādhigamābhāvo rāgasya bandhanasamājñānāt|
yadyayaṃ mokṣe nityaṃ sukhamabhivyajyata iti nityasukharāgeṇa mokṣāyaghaṭamānā na mokṣamadhigacchet, nādhigantumarhatīti|
bandhanasamājñāto hi rāgaḥ|
na ca bandhane satyapi kaścinmukta ityupapadyata iti//
children.translated_text: If attachment to eternal pleasure is not abandoned, there is no attainment of <s>mokṣa</s>, because <s>rāga</s> (attachment) is acknowledged as bondage. If one [believes] that eternal pleasure becomes manifest in <s>mokṣa</s>, then one striving for <s>mokṣa</s> due to attachment to eternal pleasure would not attain <s>mokṣa</s>, and does not deserve to attain it. For <s>rāga</s> is acknowledged as bondage. And when bondage exists, no one can be called liberated — this is justified.

children.text: athāsya nityasukharāgaḥ prahīyate, tasminprahīṇe nāsya nityasukhārāgaḥ pratikūlo bhavati? yadyevam, muktasya nityaṃ sukhaṃ bhavati, athāpi na bhavati, nāsyobhayoḥ pakṣayormokṣādhigamo vikalpyata iti // 22 //
children.translated_text: But if one's attachment to eternal pleasure is abandoned — when that is abandoned, one's attachment to eternal pleasure does not become averse [to liberation]? If so, whether the liberated one has eternal pleasure or does not have it, the attainment of <s>mokṣa</s> is not contingent on either alternative. //22//
[There is] no aversion for one who has abandoned attachment to eternal pleasure.

children.text: sthānavata etarhi saṃśayasya lakṣaṇaṃ vācyamiti taducyate---
children.translated_text: Since doubt (<s>saṃśaya</s>) has a [legitimate] basis, its defining characteristic must be stated — so it is stated:

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.1.23: <s>Saṃśaya</s> (doubt) is a deliberation that looks for a distinguishing feature, [arising] from the apprehension of properties common [to multiple objects], from conflicting testimony, from the indeterminate status of perception and non-perception.

children.text:
samānadharmopapatterviśeṣāpekṣo vimarśaḥ saṃśaya iti|
sthāṇupurūṣayoḥ samānaṃ dharmamārohapariṇāhau paśyan pūrvadṛṣṭaṃ ca tayoviśeṣaṃ bubhutsamānaḥ kisvidityanyataraṃ nāvadhārayati, yat tadanavadhāraṇajñānaṃ sa saṃśayaḥ|
samānamanayordharmamupalabhe viśeṣamanyatarasya nopalabha ityeṣā buddhiḥ apekṣā|
sā saṃśayasya pravarttikā varttate|
tena viśeṣāpekṣo vimarśaḥ saṃśayaḥ//
children.translated_text: A deliberation that looks for a distinguishing feature, arising from the apprehension of common properties — that is <s>saṃśaya</s>. Seeing a property common to a post and a person — such as height and girth — and wishing to know the distinguishing feature previously observed between them, one does not ascertain either one, [thinking] 'What is it?' That cognition of non-ascertainment is <s>saṃśaya</s>. 'I apprehend a common property between them; I do not apprehend the distinguishing feature of either one' — this cognition is the expectation (<s>apekṣā</s>). That gives rise to <s>saṃśaya</s>. Therefore, a deliberation that looks for a distinguishing feature is <s>saṃśaya</s>.

children.text:
anekadharmopapatteriti|
samānajātoyamasamānajātīyaṃ cānekam|
tasyānekasya dharmopapatteḥ viśeṣasyobhayathā dṛṣṭatvāt|
samānajātīyebhyo 'samānajātīyebhyaścārthā viśiṣyante, gandhavattvātpṛthivyavādibhyaśca viśiṣyate, guṇakarmabhyaśca|
asti ca śabde vibhāgajanyatvaṃ viśeṣaḥ|
tasmin dravyaṃ guṇaḥ karma veti sandehaḥ, viśeṣasyobhayathā dṛṣṭatvāt|
kiṃ dravyasya sato guṇakamabhyo viśeṣaḥ, āhosvidaguṇasya sato dravyakarmabhyaḥ, atha
children.translated_text: 'From the apprehension of multiple properties' — [means properties that are] of the same class and of different classes, [which are] multiple. From the apprehension of a property of that multiple [set], because the distinguishing feature has been observed both ways. Things are distinguished from those of the same class and those of different classes; earth is distinguished from water and the rest by possessing odor, and also from qualities and actions. And in sound there is a distinguishing feature — being produced by disjunction. Regarding that, there is doubt: 'Is it a substance, a quality, or an action?' — because the distinguishing feature has been observed both ways. Is the distinguishing feature from qualities and actions when it is a substance?

children.text: karmaṇaḥ sato dravyaguṇebhya iti? viśeṣāpekṣā anyatamasya vyavasthāpakaṃ dharmaṃ nopalabha iti buddhiriti//
children.translated_text: Or from substances and actions when it is a quality? Or from substances and qualities when it is an action? The expectation of a distinguishing feature is the cognition: 'I do not apprehend the property that would establish either one.'

children.text:
vipratipatteriti|
vyāhatamekārthadarśanaṃ vipratipattiḥ, vyāghātaḥ virodho 'sahabhāva iti|
astyātmekaṃ darśanam nāstyātmetyaparam|
na ca sadbhāvāsadbhāvau sahaikatra sambhavataḥ|
na cānyatarasādhako heturūpalabhyate|
tatra tattvānavadhāraṇaṃ saṃśaya iti//
children.translated_text: 'From conflicting testimony' — conflicting testimony (<s>vipratipattiḥ</s>) is contradictory perception of a single object. Contradiction means opposition, incompatibility. One view is 'the <s>ātman</s> exists,' another is 'the <s>ātman</s> does not exist.' And existence and non-existence cannot co-exist in a single [subject]. And no reason establishing either one is apprehended. Therein, the non-ascertainment of the truth is <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt).

children.text:
upalabdhyavyavthātaḥ khalvapi|
saccodakamupalabhyate taḍāgādiṣu, marīciṣu cāvidyamānamudakamiti, ataḥ kkacidupasabhyamāne tattvavyavasthāpakasya pramāṇasyānupalabdheḥ kiṃ sadupalabhyate 'thāsaditi saṃśayo bhavati//
children.translated_text: Also from the indeterminate status of perception and non-perception. Water with movement is perceived in ponds and the like, and in mirages water is non-existent — therefore, when something is perceived somewhere, in the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s> that establishes the truth, there arises doubt: 'Is what is perceived existent or non-existent?'

children.text:
anupalabdhyavasthātaśca|
sacca nopalabhyate mūlakīlakodakādi, asaccānutpannaṃ nirūddhaṃ vā, tataḥ kkacidanupalabhyamāne, kiṃ sannopalabhyate utāsaditi saṃśayo bhavati|
viśeṣāpekṣo pūrvavat//
children.translated_text: And because of the state of non-apprehension — both what exists is not apprehended, such as roots, pegs, water and so forth, and what does not exist is either not yet arisen or has ceased; therefore, when something is not apprehended somewhere, there arises doubt: 'Is what exists not apprehended, or is it non-existent?' The specific consideration is as before. [End of NyS 1.1.23]

children.text: pūrvaḥ samāno 'nekaśca dharmo jñeyasthaḥ, upalabdhyanupalabdhī punarjñātṛsthe, etāvatā viśeṣeṇa punarvacanam|

children.translated_text: From the ascertainment of common properties, from the occurrence of common properties, the deliberation that depends on the recollection of specific differences — this is <s>vimarśa</s> (reflective consideration). [End of NyS 1.1.23]

The prior [consideration] is the same, and the multiple properties reside in the object of knowledge, while apprehension and non-apprehension reside in the knower — with this specific difference, the restatement is made.
[Section: NySBh 1.1.24]
The statement of the definition for those that have a [definite] occasion is the same [as before].
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.24: That purpose for which one undertakes [an action] is <s>prayojana</s> (purpose).

children.text:
yamarthamāptavyaṃ hātavyaṃ vā vyavasāya tadāptihānopāyamanutiṣṭhati, prayojanaṃ tadveditavyam, pravṛttihetutvāt/
imamarthamāpsyāmi hāsyāmi vetivyavasāyo 'rthasyādhikāraḥ, evaṃ vyavasīyamāno 'rtho 'dhikriyata iti//14//
children.translated_text: That purpose which one resolves to attain or abandon, and for the sake of which one follows the means of attainment or abandonment — that should be understood as <s>prayojana</s> (purpose), because it is the cause of activity. The resolution 'I shall attain this object' or 'I shall abandon it' is the <s>adhikāra</s> (undertaking) of the object; the object thus resolved upon is undertaken. [End of NyS 1.1.24]
[Section: NySBh 1.1.25]

children.text: NyS_1,1.25: laukikaparīkṣadāṇāṃ yasminn arthe buddhisāmyaṃ sa dṛṣṭāntaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 1.1.25: That object regarding which there is agreement in understanding among ordinary people and investigators is a <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example).

children.text: lokasāmānyamanatītāḥ laukikāḥ, naisargikaṃ vainayikaṃ buddhyatiśayam aprāptāḥ|

children.translated_text: Those opposed to them are <s>parīkṣakas</s> (investigators), who are capable of investigating objects through reasoning and <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge).

children.text: yathā yamarthaṃ laukikā budhyatante, tathā parīkṣakā api, so 'rtho dṛṣṭāntaḥ|
children.translated_text: That object which the ordinary people understand in the same way as the investigators — that is a <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example).

children.text: dṛṣṭāntavirodhena hi pratipakṣāḥ pratiṣeddhavyā bhavantīti, dṛṣṭāntasamādhitā na svapakṣāḥ sthāpanīyā bhavantīti, avayaveṣu codāharaṇāya kalpata iti //25//
children.translated_text: For opposing positions must be refuted by showing conflict with the example; one's own position need not be established by conformity with the example; and among the members [of a syllogism], it serves as <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration). [End of NyS 1.1.25]

Those who have not transcended common [understanding] of the world are <s>laukikas</s> (ordinary people) — they have not attained any superiority of understanding, whether natural or acquired through training.
[Section: NySBh 1.1.26]

children.text:
atha siddhāntaḥ|
idamitthambhūtañcetyabhyanujñāyamānamarthajātaṃ siddham siddhasya saṃsthitiḥ siddhāntaḥ|
saṃsthitiritthambhāvavyavasthā---dharmaniyamaḥ|
sa khalvayam---
children.translated_text: Now, <s>siddhānta</s> (established conclusion) — 'This is of such a nature' — the body of things accepted and acknowledged is <s>siddha</s> (established); the settled state of what is established is <s>siddhānta</s>. The settled state is the determination of the nature — the fixed rule of a property. And this is —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.26: The established conclusion of a system, a topic, a thesis, or an assumption is <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine).
The settled state of meaning connected with a topic is <s>adhikaraṇasaṃsthiti</s> (topical establishment).
<s>Abhyupagamasaṃsthiti</s> (assumptive establishment) is the acceptance of a meaning not yet fully ascertained.
For the purpose of investigating its specific nature, there is the <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s> (assumptive doctrine). [End of NyS 1.1.26]
The settled state of the meaning of a system is <s>tantrasaṃsthiti</s>. A <s>tantra</s> (system) is a treatise (<s>śāstra</s>) that teaches a body of interconnected meanings.
[Section: NySBh 1.1.27]
But due to the difference of systems, it is indeed fourfold —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.27: Because of the distinct natures of the established conclusions of all systems, of a particular system, of a topic, and of an assumption.
Among these, these four settled states are of distinct natures. [End of NyS 1.1.27]
[Section: NySBh 1.1.28]
Of those —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.28: A meaning that is accepted in a system and is not contradicted by any system is a <s>sarvatantrasiddhānta</s> (doctrine established in all systems).

children.text: yathā ghrāṇādīnīndriyāṇi, gandhādaya indriyārthāḥ, pṛthivyādīni bhūtāni, pramāṇairarthasya grahaṇamiti //28//
children.translated_text: For example: the sense-organs beginning with smell, the objects of the senses beginning with odor, the elements beginning with earth, and the apprehension of objects through <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge). [End of NyS 1.1.28]
[Section: NySBh 1.1.29]
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.29: What is established in one's own system but not established in another system is a <s>pratitantrasiddhānta</s> (doctrine of a particular system).

children.text: yathā nāsata atmalābhaḥ, na sata ātmahānam, niratiśayāścetanāḥ dehendriyamanaḥsaṃ viṣayeṣu tattatkāraṇeṣu ca viśeṣa iti sāṅkhcānām /
children.translated_text: For example, [the doctrines] of the <s>Sāṅkhyas</s>: there is no origination from non-existence, no destruction of what exists, conscious beings are unsurpassable, and there is a specific [connection] with the body, sense-organs, mind, and objects as their respective causes.

children.text: puruṣakarmādinimitto bhūtasargaḥ, karmahetavo doṣāḥ pravṛttiśca, svaguṇaviśiṣṭāścetanāḥ, asadutpadyate utpannaṃ nirudhyata iti yogānām //29//
children.translated_text: The creation of beings is caused by the <s>karma</s> (actions) of the individual (<s>puruṣa</s>); <s>doṣas</s> (defects) and activity are the causes of <s>karma</s>; conscious beings are distinguished by their own qualities; what does not exist comes into being, and what has arisen ceases — these are [the doctrines] of the <s>Yogas</s>. [End of NyS 1.1.29]
[Section: NySBh 1.1.30]
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.30: That whose establishment leads to the establishment of another topic is an <s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s> (topical doctrine).

children.text:
yasyārthasya siddhāvanye 'rthā anuṣajyante, na tairvinā so 'rthaḥ sidhyati te 'rthā yadadhiṣṭhānāḥ, so 'dhikaraṇasiddhāntaḥ|
yathā dehendriyavyatirikto jñātā darśanasparśanābhyāmekārthagrahaṇāditi|
atrānuṣaṅgiṇo 'rthā
indriyanānātvam, niyataviṣayāṇīndriyāṇi, svaviṣayagrahaṇaliṅgāni jñāturjñānasādhanāni, gandhādiguṇavyatiriktaṃ dravyam, guṇādhikaraṇamaniyataviṣayāścetanā iti|
pūrvārthasiddhāvete 'rthāḥ sidhyanti|
na tairvinā so 'rthaḥ sambhavatīti//30//
children.translated_text: When upon the establishment of a certain meaning, other meanings follow — and without those [supporting meanings], that meaning cannot be established, and those meanings are its foundation — that is an <s>adhikaraṇasiddhānta</s>. For example: 'The knower is distinct from the body and sense-organs, because one grasps a single object through both sight and touch.' Here the subsidiary meanings are: the plurality of sense-organs, that sense-organs have fixed objects, that sense-organs are instruments of knowledge for the knower characterized by grasping their own objects, that substance is distinct from qualities like odor and so forth, and that substance is the substrate of qualities while conscious beings have unfixed objects. Upon the establishment of the primary meaning, these meanings are established; and without them, that meaning is not possible. [End of NyS 1.1.30]
[Section: NySBh 1.1.31]
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.31: The investigation of the specific nature of that which is accepted without examination is an <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s> (assumptive doctrine).

children.text: yatra kiṃcidarthajātamaparīkṣitamabhyupagamyate, astu dravyaṃ śabdaḥ, sa tu nityo 'thānitya iti? dravyasya sato anityatā nityatā vā tadviśeṣaḥ parīkṣyate, so 'bhyupagamasiddhāntaḥ svabuddhyatiśayacikhyāpayiṣayā parabuddhyavajñānāya ca pravartata iti //31//
children.translated_text: When some body of meaning is accepted without examination — 'Let sound be a substance; but is it eternal or non-eternal?' — the specific nature of the existing substance, whether eternal or non-eternal, is investigated; that is the <s>abhyupagamasiddhānta</s>. It proceeds from the desire to display one's own intellectual superiority and from disregard for the understanding of the opponent. [End of NyS 1.1.31]
[Section: NySBh 1.1.32]
Now the members [of a syllogism] —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.32: <s>Pratijñā</s> (proposition), <s>hetu</s> (reason), <s>udāharaṇa</s> (example), <s>upanaya</s> (application), and <s>nigamana</s> (conclusion) are the members [of a syllogism].

children.text:
daśāvayavāneke nauyayikā vākye sañcakṣate jijñāsā saṃśayaḥ śakyaprāptiḥ prayojanaṃ saṃśayavyudāsa iti|
te kasmānnocyanta iti? tatrāpratīyamāne 'rthe pratyayārthasya pravartikā jijñāsā|
apratīyamānamarthaṃ kasmājjijñāsate? taṃ tattvato jñātaṃ hāsyāmi vopādāsya upekṣiṣye veti|
tā etā hānopādānopekṣābuddhayastattvajñānasyārthaḥ tadarthamayaṃ jijñāsate|
sā khalviyamasādhanam arthasyeti|
jijñāsādhikaṣṭhānaṃ saṃśayaśca vyāhatadharmopasaṅghātāt tatvajñāne pratyāsannaḥ|
vyāhatorhi dharmayoranyatarattattvaṃ bhavitumarhatīti|
sa pṛthagupadiṣṭo 'pyasādhanamarthasyeti|
pramātuḥ pramāṇāni prameyādhigamārthāni, sā śakyaprāptirna sādhakasya vākyasya bhāgena yujyate pratijñādivaditi|
prayojanaṃ tattvāvadhāraṇamarthasādhakasya vākyasya phalaṃ naikadeśa iti|
saṃśayavyudāsaḥ pratipakṣopavarṇanaṃ tatpratiṣedhena tattvajñānābhyanujñānārtham, na tvayaṃ sādhakavākyaikadeśa iti|
children.translated_text: Removal of doubt is the description of the opposing position, for the purpose of acknowledging true knowledge through its refutation — but this too is not a part of the probative statement.
However, in a discussion, the desire to know and the rest are competent because they assist in the determination of the meaning to be ascertained.

children.text: tattvārnthasādhakabhāvāttu pratijñādayaḥ sādhakavāṅkyasya bhāgā ekadeśā avayavā iti // 32 //
children.translated_text: But because of their nature as means of establishing truth, the proposition and the rest are parts, portions, and members of the probative statement. [End of NyS 1.1.32]

Some <s>Naiyāyikas</s> (logicians) state ten members of a sentence: desire to know, doubt, capacity to obtain, purpose, and removal of doubt. Why are they not mentioned? Among these, when the object is not [yet] understood, the desire to know impels one towards understanding the object. Why does one desire to know the object that is not understood? 'Having truly known it, I shall either abandon it, or adopt it, or disregard it.' These cognitions of abandonment, adoption, and disregard are the purpose of true knowledge; for the sake of that, one desires to know. But this [desire to know] is not a means of establishing the object. And doubt, which is the occasion for the desire to know, is close to true knowledge because of the conjunction of contradictory properties — for one of two contradictory properties must be the truth. Even though separately stated, it is not a means of establishing the object. The <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) of the knower are for the purpose of apprehending the object to be known; that capacity to obtain is not properly a part of the probative statement like the proposition and others. Purpose is the ascertainment of truth — the result of the probative statement, not a part of it.
[Section: NySBh 1.1.33]
Of those, as separately distinguished —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.33: The statement of what is to be proved is the <s>pratijñā</s> (proposition).

children.text: prajñāpanīyena dharmeṇa dharmiṇo viśiṣṭasya parigrahavacanaṃ pratijñā sādhyanirdeśaḥ|

children.translated_text: 'Sound is non-eternal.' [End of NyS 1.1.33]
The statement of acceptance of the subject (<s>dharmin</s>) qualified by the property to be established — that is the <s>pratijñā</s>, the statement of what is to be proved.
[Section: NySBh 1.1.34]
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.34: The means of proving what is to be proved through similarity with the example is the <s>hetu</s> (reason).

children.text: udāharaṇena sāmānyātsādhyasya dharmasya sādhanaṃ prajñāpanaṃ hetuḥ|
sādhye pratisandhāya dharmamudāharaṇe ca pratisandhāya tasya sādhanatāvacanaṃ hetuḥ|
children.translated_text: Connecting the property with what is to be proved and connecting it with the example, the statement of its capacity to prove — that is the <s>hetu</s>.
'Because of having the property of origination' —
that which has the property of origination has been observed to be non-eternal. [End of NyS 1.1.34]
The means of proving, the establishing of the property to be proved through commonality with the example — that is the <s>hetu</s> (reason).
[Section: NySBh 1.1.35]
Is this the entire definition of <s>hetu</s> (reason)? No, it is said. What then?
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.35: Likewise through dissimilarity.
And through dissimilarity with the example, the proving of what is to be proved is the <s>hetu</s> (reason).
How? Sound is non-eternal, because of having the property of origination.
That which does not have the property of origination has been observed to be eternal — the <s>ātman</s> (self) and the like. [End of NyS 1.1.35]
[Section: NySBh 1.1.36]
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.36: An example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) that possesses the property [to be proved] due to similarity with what is to be proved is the <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration).

children.text:
sādhyena sādharmyaṃ samānadharmatā|
sādhyasādharmyātkāraṇāttaddharmabhāvī dṛṣṭānta iti|
tasya dharmastaddharmaḥ|
tasyeti sādhyasya|
sādhyaṃ ca dvividham dharmiviśiṣṭo vā dharmaḥ śabdasyānityatvam, dharmaviśiṣṭo vā dharmī anityaḥ śabda iti|
ihottaraṃ tadgrahaṇena gṛhyata iti|
kasmāt? pṛthagdharmavacanāt|
tasya dharmastaddharmaḥ|
taddharmasya bhāvastaddharmabhāvaḥ|
sa yasmin dṛṣṭānte vartate sa dṛṣṭāntaḥ taddharmabhāvī|
yasmin dṛṣṭānte sādhyasādharmyādutpattidharmakatvāt sādhyasya dharmo 'nityatvaṃ bhavati sa dṛṣṭāntaḥ|
sādhyasādharmyādutpattidharmakatvāttaddharmabhāvī bhavati, sa codādaharaṇamiṣyate|
sthālyādi dravyamutpattidharmakamanityaṃ dṛṣṭāmiti|
tatra yudatpadyate tadutpattidharmakam|
tacca bhūtvā na bhavati, ātmānaṃ jahāti nirudhyata ityanityam|
evamutpattidharmakatvaṃ sādhanamanityatvaṃ sādhyam|
so 'yamekasmin dvayordharmayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvaḥ sādharmyād vyasthita upalabhyate|
children.translated_text: This relation of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> between the two properties in one [example] is apprehended as established through similarity.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭānta upalabhamānaḥ śabde 'pyanuminoti, śabdo 'pyutpattidharmakatvādanityaḥ sthālyādivaditi|
children.translated_text: One who apprehends this in the example infers it also for sound — 'Sound too is non-eternal because of having the property of origination, like a pot and the like.'
It is called <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration) because by it the relation of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> between the properties is illustrated. [End of NyS 1.1.36]

Similarity with what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>) means having a common property. Because of similarity with the <s>sādhya</s>, the example possesses that property. 'That property' means the property of the <s>sādhya</s>. The <s>sādhya</s> is twofold: either the property qualified by the subject — the non-eternality of sound — or the subject qualified by the property — 'sound is non-eternal.' Here the latter is grasped by the word 'that.' Why? Because of the separate mention of the property. 'That property' means the property of that [<s>sādhya</s>]; the existence of that property is <s>taddharmabhāva</s>. The example in which this obtains is the example that 'possesses that property.' The example in which, due to similarity with the <s>sādhya</s> — namely, having the property of origination — the property of the <s>sādhya</s>, non-eternality, exists — that is the example. Due to similarity with the <s>sādhya</s>, because of having the property of origination, it possesses that property — and that is accepted as the <s>udāharaṇa</s> (illustration). A substance such as a pot has the property of origination and is observed to be non-eternal. In that [example], what is produced has the property of origination, and it ceases to be after having been, abandons itself, ceases — thus it is non-eternal. In this way, having the property of origination is the means of proof (<s>sādhana</s>), and non-eternality is what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>).
[Section: NySBh 1.1.37]
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.37: Or, the reverse through the opposite [dissimilarity] [is also an illustration].

children.text:
dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇamiti prakṛtam |
sādhyavaidharmyādataddharmabhāvī ca dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇamiti |
anityaḥ śabda utpattidharmakatvāt anutpattidharmakaṃ nityamātmādi, so 'yamātmādirdṛṣṭāntaḥ sādhyavaidharmyādanutpattidharmakatvādataddharmabhāvī-yo 'sau sādhyasya dharmo 'nityatvaṃ sa tasmin na bhavatīti|
atrātmādau dṛṣṭānta utpattidharmakatvasyābhāvādanityatvaṃ na bhavatīti upalabhamānaḥ śabde vapiryayamanuminoti, utpattidharmakatvasya bhāvādanityaḥ śabda iti|
sādharmyoktasya hetoḥ sādhyasādharmyāt taddharmabhāvī dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇam|
vaidharmyoktasya hetoḥ sādhyavaidharmyādataddharmabhāvī dṛṣṭānta udāharaṇam|
pūrvasmin dṛṣṭānte yau tau dharmauṃ sādhyasādhanabhūtau paśyati sādhye 'pi tayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvamanuminoti|
uttarasmin dṛṣṭānte yayordharmayorekasyābhāvāditarasyābhāvaṃ paśyati tayorekatarasya bhāvāditarasya bhāvaṃ sādhye 'numinotīti|
children.translated_text: In the latter example, one who sees that the absence of one of the two properties [leads to] the absence of the other, infers the presence of the other from the presence of one of them in what is to be proved.
This does not hold in the case of pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsas</s>); therefore non-reasons are <s>hetvābhāsas</s> (fallacious reasons).

children.text: tadidaṃ hetūdāharaṇayoḥ sāmarthyaṃ paramasūkṣmaṃ duḥkhabodhaṃ paṇḍitarūpavedanīyamiti //37//
children.translated_text: This capacity of the reason and the example is supremely subtle, difficult to understand, and to be grasped by those of a learned disposition. [End of NyS 1.1.37]

It is understood that the example is the <s>udāharaṇa</s>. An example that does not possess that property due to dissimilarity with the <s>sādhya</s> is also an <s>udāharaṇa</s>. 'Sound is non-eternal, because of having the property of origination; that which does not have the property of origination is eternal — the <s>ātman</s> and the like.' This <s>ātman</s> and so forth is an example that, due to dissimilarity with the <s>sādhya</s>, because of not having the property of origination, does not possess that property — the property of the <s>sādhya</s>, non-eternality, does not exist in it. One who observes in this example of the <s>ātman</s> and the like that non-eternality does not exist because of the absence of the property of origination, infers the reverse for sound — 'Sound is non-eternal because of the presence of the property of origination.' For the reason stated through similarity, the example that possesses that property due to similarity with the <s>sādhya</s> is the <s>udāharaṇa</s>. For the reason stated through dissimilarity, the example that does not possess that property due to dissimilarity with the <s>sādhya</s> is the <s>udāharaṇa</s>. In the first example, one who sees the two properties as having the relation of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> infers their relation of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> also in what is to be proved.
[Section: NySBh 1.1.38]

children.text: NyS_1,1.38: udāharaṇāpekṣaḥ tathā iti upasaṃhāraḥ na tathā iti vā sādhyasya upanayaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 1.1.38: Dependent upon the <s>udāharaṇa</s> (example), the subsumption 'it is so' or 'it is not so' of the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) is <s>upanaya</s> (application).

children.text:
udāharaṇāpekṣa udāharaṇatantra udāharaṇavaśaḥ|
vaśaḥ sāmarthyam|
sādhyasādharmyayukte udāharaṇe sthālyādidravyamutpattidharmakamanityaṃ dṛṣṭam, tathā ca śabda utpattidharmaka iti sādhyasya śabdasyotpattidharmakatvamūpasaṃhriyate |
sādhyavaidharmyayuktaṃ punarudāharaṇe ātmādidravyamanutpattidharmakaṃ nityaṃ dṛṣṭam, na ca tathānutpattidharmakaḥ śabda iti, anutpattidharmakatvasyopasaṃhārapratiṣedhenotpattidharmakattvamupasaṃhriyate |
tadidamupasaṃhāradvetamudāharaṇadvaitādbhavati|
upasaṃhriyate aneneti copasaṃhāro veditavya iti//38//
children.translated_text: 'Dependent upon the <s>udāharaṇa</s>' means governed by the <s>udāharaṇa</s>, subject to the <s>udāharaṇa</s>. 'Subject to' means capacity. When the <s>udāharaṇa</s> is conjoined with the similarity to the <s>sādhya</s>, a substance such as a pot is seen to possess the property of being produced and to be non-eternal; and so too sound possesses the property of being produced — thus the property of being produced is subsumed under the <s>sādhya</s>, sound. When the <s>udāharaṇa</s> is conjoined with dissimilarity to the <s>sādhya</s>, a substance such as the self is seen to possess the property of not being produced and to be eternal; and sound does not so possess the property of not being produced — thus by the negation of subsumption of the property of not being produced, the property of being produced is subsumed. This twofold subsumption arises from the twofold <s>udāharaṇa</s>. And <s>upasaṃhāra</s> (subsumption) should be understood as that by which something is subsumed.
And when the <s>hetu</s> (reason) is twofold and the <s>udāharaṇa</s> (example) is twofold, the twofold subsumption is the same —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.39: The restatement of the <s>pratijñā</s> (thesis) after the statement of the <s>hetu</s> (reason) is <s>nigamana</s> (conclusion).

children.text:
sādharmyokte vā vaidharmyokte vā yathodāharaṇamupasaṃhriyate tasmādutpattidharmakatvādanityaḥ śabda iti nigamanam/
nigamyante aneneti pratijñāhetūdāharaṇopanayā ekatreti nigamanam|
nigamyante samarthyante saṃbadhyante|
tatra sādharmyokte tāvadvetau vākyam, anityaḥ śabda iti pratijñā|
utpattidharmakatvāditi hetuḥ|
utpattidharmakaṃ sthālyādi dravyamanityamityudāharaṇam|
tathā cotpattidharmakaḥ śabda ityupanayaḥ|
tasmādutpattidharmakatvādanityaḥ śabda iti nigamanam|
vaidharmyokte 'pi, anityaḥ śabdaḥ|
utpattidharmakatvāt, anatpattidharmakamātmādi dravyaṃ nityaṃ dṛṣṭam|
na ca tathānutpattidharmakaḥ śabdaḥ|
kiṃ tarhi? utpattidharmakaḥ|
tasmādutpattidharmakatvādanityaḥ śabda iti//
children.translated_text: Whether stated through <s>sādharmya</s> (positive analogy) or <s>vaidharmya</s> (negative analogy), when the subsumption is made in accordance with the <s>udāharaṇa</s>, the <s>nigamana</s> (conclusion) is: 'Therefore, because of possessing the property of being produced, sound is non-eternal.' <s>Nigamana</s> is that by which things are concluded — that is, the <s>pratijñā</s> (thesis), <s>hetu</s> (reason), <s>udāharaṇa</s> (example), and <s>upanaya</s> (application) are brought together into one. 'Concluded' means demonstrated, connected, related. In the case stated through <s>sādharmya</s>, the statement is as follows: 'Sound is non-eternal' — this is the <s>pratijñā</s>. 'Because of possessing the property of being produced' — this is the <s>hetu</s>. 'A substance such as a pot, which possesses the property of being produced, is non-eternal' — this is the <s>udāharaṇa</s>. 'And so too sound possesses the property of being produced' — this is the <s>upanaya</s>. 'Therefore, because of possessing the property of being produced, sound is non-eternal' — this is the <s>nigamana</s>. In the case stated through <s>vaidharmya</s> as well: 'Sound is non-eternal. Because of possessing the property of being produced. A substance such as the self, which does not possess the property of being produced, is seen to be eternal. And sound does not so lack the property of being produced. What then? It possesses the property of being produced. Therefore, because of possessing the property of being produced, sound is non-eternal.'

children.text:
avayavasamudāye ca vākye saṃbhūyetaretarābhisaṃbandhātpramāṇānyarthaṃ sādhayantīti|
saṃbhavastāvat, śabdaviṣayā pratijñā, āptopadeśasya pratyakṣānumānābhyāṃ pratisandhānādanṛṣeśca svātantryānupapatteḥ|
anumānaṃ hetuḥ, udāharaṇe saṃdṛśya pratipatteḥ|
taccodāharaṇabhāṣye vyākhyātam|
pratyakṣaviṣayamudāharaṇam, dṛṣṭenādṛṣṭasiddheḥ|
upamānamupanayaḥ, tathetyupasaṃhaarāt, na ca tatheti copamānadharmapratiṣedhe viparītadharmopasaṃhaarasiddheḥ|
sarveṣāmekārthapratipattau sāmarthyapradarśanaṃ nigamanamiti//
children.translated_text: And in a sentence consisting of the collection of <s>avayavas</s> (members of the syllogism), the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) establish the object through their mutual connection taken together. The correspondence is as follows: the <s>pratijñā</s> pertains to <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony), because of the connection of the instruction of a trustworthy person (<s>āptopadeśa</s>) with <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and <s>anumāna</s> (inference), and because independence is not possible for one who is not a seer. The <s>hetu</s> is <s>anumāna</s>, because of comprehension through seeing in the <s>udāharaṇa</s>. And that has been explained in the commentary on <s>udāharaṇa</s>. The <s>udāharaṇa</s> pertains to <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), because the unseen is established through the seen. The <s>upanaya</s> is <s>upamāna</s> (comparison), because of the subsumption 'it is so,' and because through the negation of the property of comparison by 'it is not so,' the subsumption of the opposite property is established. The <s>nigamana</s> is the demonstration of the combined capacity of all of them in apprehending a single object.

children.text:
itaretarābhisaṃbandho 'pi---asatyāṃ pratijñāyāmanāśrayā hetvādayo na pravartteran|
asati hetau kasya sādhanabhāvaḥ pradarśyeta? udāharaṇe sādhye ca kasyopasaṃhaaraḥ syāt? kasya cāpadeśātpratijñāyāḥ punarvacanaṃ nigamanaṃ syāt iti? asatyudāharaṇe kena sādharmyaṃ vaidharmyaṃ vā sādhyasādhanamupādīyeta? kasya vā sādharmyavaśādupasaṃhaaraḥ pravarteta? upanayaṃ cāntareṇa sādhye 'nupasaṃhṛtaḥ sādhako dharmo nārthaṃ sādhayet|
nigamanābhāve cānabhivyaktasaṃbandhānāṃ pratijñādīnāmekārthena pravartanaṃ tatheti pratipādanaṃ kasyeti//
children.translated_text: The mutual connection is also as follows — if the <s>pratijñā</s> were absent, the <s>hetu</s> and the rest, having no basis, would not operate. If the <s>hetu</s> were absent, whose character as a means of proof would be demonstrated? If the <s>udāharaṇa</s> and the <s>sādhya</s> were absent, what would be subsumed under what? And in the absence of what would the restatement of the <s>pratijñā</s> constitute the <s>nigamana</s>? If the <s>udāharaṇa</s> were absent, by what would the <s>sādharmya</s> (similarity) or <s>vaidharmya</s> (dissimilarity) with the <s>sādhya</s> (what is to be proved) and the <s>sādhana</s> (means of proof) be taken up? And by virtue of what similarity would the subsumption proceed? Without the <s>upanaya</s>, the proving property, not being subsumed under the <s>sādhya</s>, would not establish the object. And in the absence of the <s>nigamana</s>, when the connection of the <s>pratijñā</s> and the rest remains unexpressed, how would their operation toward a single object and its establishment as such be accomplished?

children.text:
athāvayavārthaḥ|
sādhyasya dharmasya dharmiṇā saṃbandhopapādanaṃ pratijñārthaḥ|
udāharaṇena samānasya viparītasya vā sādhyasya dharmasya sādhakabhāvavacanaṃ hetvarthaḥ|
dharmayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvapradarśanamekatrodāharaṇārthaḥ|
sādhanabhūtasya dharmasya sādhyena dharmeṇa sāmānādhikaraṇyopapādanamupanayārthaḥ|
udāharaṇasthayorddharmayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvopapattau sādhye viparītaprasaṅgapratiṣedhārthaṃ nigamanam//
children.translated_text: Now, the purpose of each <s>avayava</s> (member). The purpose of the <s>pratijñā</s> is to establish the connection of the property to be proved (<s>sādhya dharma</s>) with the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>). The purpose of the <s>hetu</s> is to state the proving capacity of the property that is the same as or opposite to the <s>sādhya</s> property, with reference to the <s>udāharaṇa</s>. The purpose of the <s>udāharaṇa</s> is to demonstrate in one place the relation of the <s>sādhya</s> (provable) and <s>sādhana</s> (proving) properties. The purpose of the <s>upanaya</s> is to establish the co-location (<s>sāmānādhikaraṇya</s>) of the proving property with the property to be proved. The purpose of the <s>nigamana</s> is to preclude the unwanted consequence of the opposite, once the relation of the <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> properties established in the <s>udāharaṇa</s> has been demonstrated.

children.text: na caitasyāṃ hetūdāharaṇapariśuddhau satyāṃ sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ pratyavasthānasya vikalpājjātinigrahasthānabahutvaṃ prakramate|
children.translated_text: And when the <s>hetu</s> and <s>udāharaṇa</s> have been thus purified through <s>sādharmya</s> (positive analogy) and <s>vaidharmya</s> (negative analogy), the multiplicity of <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinders) and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (points of defeat) does not proceed from the alternatives of counter-position.

children.text: avyavasthāpya khalu dharmayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvamudāharaṇe jātivādī pratyavatiṣṭhate|
children.translated_text: Indeed, it is without establishing the relation of <s>sādhya</s> (provable) and <s>sādhana</s> (proving) properties in the <s>udāharaṇa</s> that the <s>jāti</s>-disputant takes his counter-position.

children.text: vyavasthiteha khilu dharmayoḥ sādhyasādhanabhāve dṛṣṭāntasthe gṛhyamāṇe sādhanabhūtasya dharmasya hetutvena upādānaṃ na sādharmyamātrasya, na vairdharmyamātrasya veti //39//
children.translated_text: But when the relation of <s>sādhya</s> and <s>sādhana</s> properties is established and apprehended as residing in the <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (example), the adoption of the proving property as <s>hetu</s> is not merely on the basis of <s>sādharmya</s> (similarity) alone, nor merely on the basis of <s>vaidharmya</s> (dissimilarity) alone.

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ tarko lakṣaṇīya iti athedamucyate---
children.translated_text: Henceforth, <s>tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning) is to be defined — and so it is said:

<s>NyS</s> 1.1.40: With respect to an object whose true nature (<s>tattva</s>) is unknown, conjecture (<s>ūha</s>) through the fitness of cause (<s>kāraṇopapatti</s>), for the purpose of knowing the true nature, is <s>tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning).

children.text:
avijñāyamānatattve 'rthe jijñāsā tāvajjāyate jānīyemamarthamiti|
atha jijñāsitasya vastuno vyāhatau dharmauṃ vibhāgena vimṛśati, kiṃ svit ittthamāhosvinnetthamiti|
vimṛśyamānayordharmayorekataraṃ kāraṇopapattyā anujñānāti, sambhavatyasmin kāraṇaṃ pramāṇaṃ heturiti|
kāraṇopapattyā syādevametat netaraditi//
children.translated_text: When the true nature of an object is not known, first a desire to know arises: 'Let me know this object.' Then one deliberates upon the two mutually contradictory properties of the object under inquiry, distinguishing them: 'Is it this way, or is it not this way?' Upon deliberating on the two properties, one approves of one of them through the fitness of cause (<s>kāraṇopapatti</s>), thinking: 'A cause, a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), a reason is possible for this one.' Through the fitness of cause, one concludes: 'It must be thus, and not otherwise.'

children.text:
tatra nidarśanam, yo 'yaṃ jñātā jñātavyamarthaṃ jānīte, taṃ tattvato jānīyeti jijñāsā|
sa kimutpattidharmako 'nutpattidharmakaṃ iti vimarśaḥ|
vimṛśyamāne 'vijñātatattve 'rthe yasya dharmasyābhyanujñākāraṇamupapadyate, tamanujānāti|
yadyayamanutpattidharmakaḥ tataḥ svakṛtasya karmaṇaḥ phalamanubhavati jñātā|
duḥkhajanmapravṛttidoṣamithyājñānānāmuttaramuttaraṃ pūrvasya pūrvasya kāraṇam, uttarottarāpāye ca tadanantarābhāvādapavarga iti syātāṃ saṃsārāpavargauṃ|
utpattidharmake jñātari punarna syātām|
utpannaḥ khalu jñātā dehendriyaviṣayabuddhivedanābhiḥ saṃbadhyata iti nāsyedaṃ svakṛtasya karmaṇaḥ phalam|
utpannaśca bhūtvā na bhavatīti, tasyāvidyamānasya niruddhasya vā svakṛtakarmaṇaḥ phalopabhogo nāsti, tadevamekasyānekaśarīrayogaḥ śarīraviyogaścātyantaṃ na syāditi, yatra
kāraṇamanupapadyamānaṃ paśyati, tannānujānāti|
so 'yamevaṃlakṣaṇa ūhastarka ityucyate//
children.translated_text: An illustration of this: the knower who knows the object to be known — the desire to know is: 'Let me know him in his true nature.' The deliberation is: 'Is he one who possesses the property of being produced, or one who does not possess the property of being produced?' When the true nature of the object under deliberation is unknown, one approves of that property for which a cause of approval is available. If this [knower] does not possess the property of being produced, then the knower experiences the fruit of action performed by himself. Suffering, birth, activity, defects, and false knowledge — each succeeding one is the cause of the one preceding it, and with the removal of each succeeding one, the one immediately prior ceases — thus both <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of rebirth) and <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) would be possible. But if the knower possessed the property of being produced, they would not be possible. For a knower who has been produced is connected with body, sense organs, objects, cognition, and sensation — and so this [experience] would not be the fruit of action performed by himself. And what has been produced, having come into being, ceases to be — and for what is non-existent or has ceased, there is no experience of the fruit of self-performed action. Thus there would never be the connection of one [self] with many bodies nor separation from the body. Where one sees that the cause does not obtain, that one does not approve. This conjecture (<s>ūha</s>) of such a character is called <s>tarka</s>.

children.text:
kathaṃ punarayaṃ tattvajñānārtho na tattvajñānameveti? anavadhāraṇāt|
anujānātyayamekataraṃ dharmaṃ kāraṇopapattyā, na tvavadhārayati na vyavasyati na niścinoti evamevedamiti|
kathaṃ tattvajñānārtha iti? tattvajñānaviṣayābhyanujñālakṣaṇādūhād bhāvitātprasannādanantaraṃ pramāṇasāmarthyāt tattvajñānam utpadyata ityevaṃ tattvajñānārtha iti//
children.translated_text: But how is this 'for the purpose of knowing the true nature' and not itself knowledge of the true nature? Because there is no definitive determination. One approves of one property through the fitness of cause, but one does not definitively determine, does not decide, does not ascertain 'it is certainly just so.' How then is it 'for the purpose of knowing the true nature'? Because from the conjecture (<s>ūha</s>) — which has the character of approval regarding the subject matter of true knowledge — when it has been cultivated and becomes clear, immediately thereafter, through the capacity of the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), knowledge of the true nature arises. In this way it is 'for the purpose of knowing the true nature.'

children.text: so 'yaṃ tarkaḥ pramāṇāni pratisandadhānaḥ pramāṇābhyanujñānāt pramāṇasahito vāde 'padiṣṭa iti|
avijñātatattve 'rthe iti yathā so 'rtho bhavati tasya tathābhāvastattvamaviparyayo yāthātathyam //40//
children.translated_text: 'With respect to an object whose true nature is unknown' — the true nature (<s>tattva</s>) of that object is its being as it is, its non-deviation, its conformity to reality.

This <s>tarka</s>, connecting the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) and being approved by the <s>pramāṇas</s>, has been taught as accompanied by <s>pramāṇas</s> in the context of <s>vāda</s> (debate).
And regarding this subject matter of <s>tarka</s> —
<s>NyS</s> 1.1.41: The ascertainment of an object through deliberation upon <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) and <s>pratipakṣa</s> (counter-thesis) is <s>nirṇaya</s> (determination).

children.text:
sthāpanā sādhanam, pratiṣedha upālambhaḥ|
tau sādhanopālambhau pakṣapratipakṣāśrayau vyatiṣaktāvanubandhena pravarttamānau pakṣapratipakṣāvityucyete|
tayoranyatarasya nivṛttiḥ ekatarasyāvasthānamavarjanīyamavaśyambhāvitvāt|
yasyāvasthānaṃ tasyārthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇayaḥ//
children.translated_text: <s>Sthāpanā</s> (establishment) is <s>sādhana</s> (proof); <s>pratiṣedha</s> (refutation) is <s>upālambha</s> (censure). Those two — <s>sādhana</s> and <s>upālambha</s> — being based on the <s>pakṣa</s> and <s>pratipakṣa</s> respectively and operating in mutual entanglement through continuous connection, are called <s>pakṣa</s> and <s>pratipakṣa</s>. The cessation of one of them and the remaining of the other is inevitable, being necessarily so. The ascertainment of the object of that which remains is <s>nirṇaya</s> (determination).

children.text:
nedaṃ pakṣapratipakṣābhyāmarthāvadhāraṇaṃ sambhavatīti eko hi pratijñātamarthaṃ taṃ hetutaḥ sthāpayati pratiṣiddhaṃ coddharati dvitīyasya|
dvitīyena sthāpanāhetuśca pratiṣidhyate tasyaiva pratiṣedhahetuścoddhriyate|
sa nivarttate|
tasya nivṛttau yo 'vatiṣṭhate tenārthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇayaḥ//
children.translated_text: 'This ascertainment of the object through <s>pakṣa</s> and <s>pratipakṣa</s> is not possible' — [objection:] for one person establishes the proposed object through reasons and refutes what has been denied by the second. By the second, the reason for establishment is refuted, and the reason for his own refutation is challenged. He [the second] withdraws. Upon his withdrawal, the ascertainment of the object by the one who remains is <s>nirṇaya</s> (determination).

children.text:
ubhābhyāmevārthāvadhāraṇamityāha|
kayā yuktyā? ekasya saṃbhavo dvitīyasyāsambhavaḥ|
tāvetau sambhavāsambhavau vimarśaṃ saha nivarttayata ubhayasambhave|
ubhayāsambhave tvanivṛtto nimarśa iti|
vimṛśyeti vimarśaṃ kṛtvā|
so 'yaṃ vimarśaḥ pakṣapratipakṣāvavadyotya nyāyaṃ pravartayatītyupādīyata iti|
etacca viruddhayorekadharmisthayorbodhavyam|
yatra tu dharmisāmānyagatau viruddhau dharmauṃ hetutaḥ sambhavataḥ tatra samuccayaḥ, hetuto 'rthasya tathābhāvopapatteḥ|
yathā kriyāvad dravyamiti lakṣaṇavacane yasya dravyasya kriyāyogo hetutaḥ saṃbhavati tat kriyāvat, yasya na saṃbhavati tadakriyamiti|
ekadharmisthāyośca viruddhayoḥ dharmayorayugapadbhāvavinoḥ kālavikalpaḥ, yathā tadeva dravyaṃ kriyāyuktaṃ kriyāvat, anutpannoparatakriyaṃ punarakriyamiti//
children.translated_text: He says: the ascertainment of the object is indeed through both. By what reasoning? The possibility of one and the impossibility of the other. These two — possibility and impossibility — together terminate the deliberation when both are possible; but when both are impossible, the deliberation is not terminated. 'Having deliberated' means having performed deliberation. This deliberation, by illuminating the <s>pakṣa</s> and <s>pratipakṣa</s>, sets the method of reasoning in motion — and so it is adopted. And this should be understood with respect to two contradictory [properties] residing in a single <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer). But where two contradictory properties reside in the <s>dharmin</s> in general and both are possible on the basis of reasons, there is combination, because the object's being so is established through reasons. For example, in the definitional statement 'a substance possesses action,' that substance for which the connection with action is possible on the basis of reasons possesses action, and that for which it is not possible is without action. And for two contradictory properties residing in a single <s>dharmin</s> that do not exist simultaneously, there is a temporal distinction — for example, that very substance, when conjoined with action, possesses action, and when its action has not yet arisen or has ceased, it is without action.

children.text: na cāyaṃ nirṇaye niyamaḥ vimṛśyaiva pakṣapratipakṣābhyāmarthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇaya iti, kiṃ tarhi? bhavati khalvindriyārthasannikarṣādutpannapratyakṣe 'rthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇaya iti, parīkṣāviṣaye tu vimṛśya pakṣapratipakṣābhyāmarthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇayaḥ|

children.translated_text: and in <s>śāstra</s> (systematic treatise) and <s>vāda</s> (debate), [it is] without deliberation.

And there is no restriction regarding <s>nirṇaya</s> that ascertainment of the object must be only through deliberation upon <s>pakṣa</s> and <s>pratipakṣa</s>. Rather, there is indeed ascertainment of the object as <s>nirṇaya</s> when <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) arises from the contact of sense organ and object. But in the domain of inquiry, ascertainment of the object through deliberation upon <s>pakṣa</s> and <s>pratipakṣa</s> is <s>nirṇaya</s>,
Thus ends the first lesson of the first chapter in <s>Vātsyāyana</s>'s <s>Nyāyabhāṣya</s>.

children.text:
tisraḥ kathā bhavanti, vādo jalpo vitaṇḍā ceti|
tāsām---
children.translated_text: There are three kinds of discourse (<s>kathā</s>): <s>vāda</s> (debate), <s>jalpa</s> (disputation), and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil). Among these —

children.text: NyS_1,2.1: pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambhaḥ siddhāntāviruddhaḥ pañcāvayavopapannaḥ pakṣapratipakṣaparigraho vādaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 1.2.1: The adoption of <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) and <s>pratipakṣa</s> (counter-thesis), which employs <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), <s>tarka</s> (hypothetical reasoning), proof (<s>sādhana</s>) and censure (<s>upālambha</s>), which does not contradict established doctrine (<s>siddhānta</s>), and which is furnished with the five members (<s>pañcāvayava</s>), is <s>vāda</s> (debate).

children.text:
ekādhikaraṇasthau viruddhau dharmauṃ pakṣapratipakṣau pratyanīkabhāvāt, astyātmā nāstyātmeti|
nānādhikaraṇasthau viruddhāvapi na pakṣapratipakṣau, yathā nitya ātmā, anityā buddhiriti|
parigraho 'bhyupagamavyavasthā|
sodyayaṃ pakṣapratipakṣaparigraho vādaḥ|
tasya viśeṣaṇaṃ pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambhaḥ|
pramāṇatarkasādhanaḥ pramāṇatarkopālambhaśca|
pramāṇaistarkaṇa ca sādhanamupālambhaścāsmin kriyata iti|
sādhanaṃ sthāpanā|
upālambhaḥ pratiṣadhaḥ|
tau sādhanopālambhau ubhayorapi pakṣayorvyatiṣaktāvanubaddhau ca tāvad yāvadeko nivṛtta ekataro vyavasthita iti|
nivṛttasyopālambho vyavasthitasya sādhanamiti//
children.translated_text: Two contradictory properties residing in a single substratum are <s>pakṣa</s> (thesis) and <s>pratipakṣa</s> (counter-thesis), because they are mutually opposed — as in 'the self exists' and 'the self does not exist.' Two contradictory properties residing in different substrata are not <s>pakṣa</s> and <s>pratipakṣa</s> — as in 'the self is eternal' and 'cognition is non-eternal.' <s>Parigraha</s> (adoption) is the acceptance and commitment [to a position]. This adoption of <s>pakṣa</s> and <s>pratipakṣa</s> is <s>vāda</s>. Its qualifier is: 'which employs <s>pramāṇa</s>, <s>tarka</s>, proof, and censure.' That is, it employs <s>pramāṇas</s> and <s>tarka</s> for both proof and censure. By <s>pramāṇas</s> and by <s>tarka</s>, both proof and censure are carried out in it. <s>Sādhana</s> (proof) is <s>sthāpanā</s> (establishment). <s>Upālambha</s> (censure) is <s>pratiṣedha</s> (refutation). Those two — proof and censure — are mutually entangled and continuously connected with respect to both <s>pakṣas</s>, until one is defeated and the other is established. The censure belongs to the defeated, and the proof belongs to the established.

children.text:
jalpe nigrahasthānaviniyogādvāde tatpratiṣedhaḥ|
tatpratiṣedhe ca kasyacidabhyanujñānārthaṃ siddhāntāviruddha iti vacanam|
siddhāntamabhyupetya tadvirodhī viruddha iti viruddhasya hetvābhāsasya nigrahasthānasyābhyanujñā vāde|
pañcāvayavopapanna iti hīnamanyatamenāpyavayavena nyūnam hetudāharaṇādhikamadhikam iti caitayorabhyanujñānārthamiti//
children.translated_text: Since the application of points of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>) in <s>jalpa</s> (disputation) [implies their] prohibition in <s>vāda</s> (discussion), the statement '<s>siddhāntāviruddha</s>' (not contradicting the established doctrine) serves to approve [certain things] in <s>vāda</s>. Having accepted an established doctrine and [proposing something] contradicting it is <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory) — thus the approval in <s>vāda</s> of the contradictory [reason], which is a pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) and a point of defeat. '[Equipped with] five members' — [something] lacking even one member is deficient; having more than the reason and example is excessive — and the approval of both of these [is stated].

children.text: anyathobhāvapi pakṣau sthāpanāhetunā pravṛttau vāda iti syāt|
children.translated_text: Otherwise, even when both sides (<s>pakṣa</s>) are established merely by the reason for establishing [the thesis], it would [still] be <s>vāda</s>.

children.text: antareṇāpi cāvayavasaṃbandhaṃ pramāṇānyarthaṃ sādhayantīti dṛṣṭam, tenāpi kalpena sādhanopālambhau vāde bhavata iti jñāpayati|
children.translated_text: And it is observed that even without the connection of [formal syllogistic] members, the <s>pramāṇas</s> establish a meaning — he indicates that proof and refutation in <s>vāda</s> can also occur in that manner.

children.text: chalajātinigrahasthānasādhanopālambho jalpa iti vacanādvinigraho jalpa iti mā vijñāyi, chalajātinigrahasthānasādhanopālambha eva jalpaḥ, pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambho vāda eveti sa mā vijñāyītyevamartha pṛthak pramāṇatarkagrahaṇamiti //1//
children.translated_text: Lest it be understood from the statement 'proof and refutation through <s>chala</s> (quibble), <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinder), and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (point of defeat) is <s>jalpa</s>' that any refutation is <s>jalpa</s> — [the separate mention clarifies that] only proof and refutation through <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> is <s>jalpa</s>, while proof and refutation through <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s> is <s>vāda</s> alone — lest this be misunderstood, the separate mention of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s> serves this purpose. //1//

Since <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) and <s>tarka</s> (reasoning) are included within the members [of the syllogism], the separate mention of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s> is for the purpose of indicating that proof and refutation [can occur independently].

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.2: <s>Jalpa</s> (disputation) is proof and refutation as described above, [but also employing] <s>chala</s> (quibble), <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinder), and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (point of defeat). //

children.text:
yathoktopapanna iti, pramāṇatarkasādhanopālambhaḥ siddhāntāviruddhaḥ pañcāvayavopapannaḥ pakṣapratipakṣaparigrahaḥ|
chalajātinigrasthānasādhanopālambha iti, chalajātinigrahasthānaiḥ sādhanamupālambhaścāsmin kriyata iti evaṃviśeṣaṇo jalpaḥ//
children.translated_text: 'As described above' (<s>yathoktopapanna</s>) means: equipped with proof and refutation through <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>tarka</s>, not contradicting established doctrine, equipped with five members, and embracing both thesis and counter-thesis. 'Proof and refutation through <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s>' means: <s>jalpa</s> is so qualified because proof and refutation are accomplished in it through <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s>.

children.text:
na khalu vai chalajātinigrahasthānaiḥ sādhanaṃ kasyacidarthasya sambhavati, pratiṣedhārthataivaiṣāṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇe viśeṣalakṣaṇe ca śrūyate vacanavighāto 'rthavikalpopattyā chalam iti, sādharmyavaigharmyābhyāṃ pratyavasthānaṃ jātiḥ
vipratipattirapratipattiśca nigrahasthānam iti|
viśeṣalakṣaṇeṣvapi yathāsvamiti|
na caitadvijānīyātpratiṣedhārthatayaivārthaṃ sādhayantīti, chalajātinigrahasathānopālambho jalpa ityevamapyucyamāne vijñāyata etaditi//
children.translated_text: Indeed, the establishment of any object is not possible through <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> [alone]; their purpose of negation is heard in both the general definition and the specific definitions — 'the frustration of a statement through the supposition of an alternative meaning is <s>chala</s>,' 'counter-argument through similarity and dissimilarity is <s>jāti</s>,' 'misunderstanding and non-understanding are <s>nigrahasthāna</s>' — and likewise in the specific definitions, each respectively. And one should not think that they establish a meaning only through negation; even if stated as 'proof and refutation through <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> is <s>jalpa</s>,' this [subsidiary role] is understood.

children.text:
pramāṇaiḥ sādhanopālambheyīśchalajātinigrahasthānānāmaṅgabhāvaḥ svapakṣarakṣaṇārthatvāt, na svatantrāṇāṃ sādhanabhāvaḥ|
yattatpramāṇairarthasya sādhanaṃ tatra chalajātinigrasthānānāmaṅgābhāvo rakṣaṇārthatvāt|
tāni hi prayujyamānāni parapakṣavighāte svapakṣaṃ rakṣanti|
tathā coktaṃ tattvādhyavasāyasaṃrakṣaṇārthaṃ jalpavitaṇḍe bījaprarohasaṃharakṣaṇārthaṃ kaṇṭakaśākhāvaraṇavat iti|
yaścāsau pramāṇaiḥ pratipakṣasyopālambhastasya caitāni prayujyamānāni pratiṣedhabighātātsahakārīṇi bhavanti|
children.translated_text: And when refutation of the opponent is accomplished through <s>pramāṇas</s>, these [devices], when employed, become auxiliaries through the obstruction of [the opponent's] counter-refutation.

children.text: tadevamaṅgībhūtānāṃ chalādīnāmupādānaṃ jalpe, na svatantraṇāṃ sādhanabhāvaḥ|
children.translated_text: Thus, the employment of <s>chala</s> and the rest as subsidiaries [occurs] in <s>jalpa</s>; they do not independently function as proof.
But in refutation (<s>upālambha</s>), they also have independence. // 2 //

The subsidiary status (<s>aṅgabhāva</s>) of <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> to proof and refutation through <s>pramāṇas</s> is due to their being for the purpose of protecting one's own thesis; they do not independently function as proof. The establishment of a meaning through <s>pramāṇas</s> — therein <s>chala</s>, <s>jāti</s>, and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> have subsidiary status because they serve a protective function. For when employed, they protect one's own thesis through the obstruction of the opponent's thesis. As has been said: '<s>jalpa</s> and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> serve to protect the ascertainment of truth, like a fence of thorny branches protecting the growth of a seed.'
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.3: That [<s>jalpa</s>], devoid of the establishment of a counter-thesis, is <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavil). //

children.text:
sa jalpo vitaṇḍā bhavati|
kiṃ viśeṣaṇaḥ? pratipakṣasthāpanayā hīnaḥ|
yau tau samānādhikaraṇau viruddhau dharmauṃ pakṣapratipakṣāvityuktau tayorekataraṃ vaitaṇḍiko na sthāpayatīti parapakṣapratiṣedhenaiva pravarttata iti//
children.translated_text: That <s>jalpa</s> becomes <s>vitaṇḍā</s>. With what qualification? Devoid of the establishment of a counter-thesis. Of those two mutually opposed properties sharing the same substratum, called thesis and counter-thesis as stated [earlier], the caviler (<s>vaitaṇḍika</s>) does not establish either one — he proceeds solely by negating the opponent's thesis.

children.text: astu tarhi sa pratipakṣahīno vitaṇḍā? yadvai khalu tatparapratiṣedhalakṣaṇaṃ vākyaṃ sa vaitaṇḍikasya pakṣaḥ, na tvasau sādhyaṃ kaṃcidarthaṃ pratijñāya sthāpayatīti|

children.translated_text: Therefore, let the [sūtra] stand as it is. //3//

[Objection:] Then let <s>vitaṇḍā</s> be 'devoid of a counter-thesis'? [Reply:] That very statement whose character is the negation of the other's [thesis] is the caviler's thesis; but he does not propose any object to be proved and then establish it.

Due to the absence of the defining characteristic of a [valid] reason, [these are] non-reasons; but because of their resemblance to a reason through the general appearance of reasoning, they appear as reasons. They are as follows —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.4: The pseudo-reasons (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>) are: <s>savyabhicāra</s> (the deviating), <s>viruddha</s> (the contradictory), <s>prakaraṇasama</s> (the equivalent to the question), <s>sādhyasama</s> (the equivalent to what is to be proved), and <s>kālātīta</s> (the untimely). //
Of these —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.5: The inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>) is <s>savyabhicāra</s> (the deviating). //

children.text:
vyabhicāra ekatrāvyavasthitiḥ|
saha vyabhicāreṇa varttate iti savyabhicāraḥ|
nidarśanam---nityaḥ śabdo 'sparśatvāt|
sparśavān kuṃmoḥ anityo dṛṣṭaḥ|
na ca tathā sparśavān śabdaḥ|
tasmādasparśatvānnityaḥ śabda
iti|
dṛṣṭānte sparśavattvamanityatvaṃ ca dharmauṃ na sādhyasādhanabhūtau gṛhyate, sparśavāṃścāṇurnityaśceti|
ātmādau ca dṛṣṭānte udāharaṇasādharmyātsādhyasādhanaṃ hetuḥ iti asparśatvāditi heturnityatvaṃ vyabhicarati, asparśā ca buddhiranityā ceti|
evaṃ dvividhāpi dṛṣṭānte vyabhicārātsādhyasādhanabhāvo nāstīti lakṣaṇābhāvādaheturiti//
children.translated_text: Deviation (<s>vyabhicāra</s>) is non-fixation in one [conclusion]. That which occurs together with deviation is <s>savyabhicāra</s>. An illustration: 'Sound is eternal because it is intangible (<s>asparśatva</s>). A pot, which is tangible, is observed to be non-eternal. Sound is not tangible like that. Therefore, because of its intangibility, sound is eternal.' In the example, the two properties — tangibility and non-eternality — are not grasped as being in the relation of what is to be proved and the proving [reason], since an atom is both tangible and eternal. And in the example of the <s>ātman</s> (self) and the like, [where one argues] from the similarity of the example that what proves the probandum is the reason — the reason 'because of intangibility' deviates from eternality, since <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is both intangible and non-eternal. Thus, due to deviation in both types of examples, there is no relation of probandum and proof — due to the absence of the defining characteristic [of a valid reason], it is a non-reason.
Eternality is also one extreme.
Non-eternality is also one extreme.

children.text: ekasminnante vidyata iti aikāntiko viparyayādanaikānitakaḥ, ubhāyāntavyāpakatvāditi // 5//
children.translated_text: What is found in one extreme is <s>aikāntika</s> (conclusive); the opposite is <s>anaikāntika</s> (inconclusive) — because it pervades both extremes. // 5 //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.6: Having accepted an established doctrine and [proposing what] contradicts it is <s>viruddha</s> (the contradictory). //

children.text:
taṃ viruṇaddhīti tadvirodhī, abhyupetaṃ siddhāntaṃ vyāhantīti|
yathā so 'yaṃ vikāro vyakterapaiti nityatvapratiṣedhāt, na nityo vikāra upapadyate|
apeto 'pi vikāro 'sti vināśapratiṣedhāt|
so 'yaṃ nityatvapratiṣedhāditi heturvyakterapeto 'pi vikāro 'stītyanena svasiddhāntena virudhyate|
katham? vyaktirātmalābhaḥ|
upāyaḥ pracyutiḥ|
yadyātmalābhātpracyuto vikāro 'sti, nityatvapratiṣedhau nopapadyate|
yadvyakterapetasyāpi vikārasyāstitvam, tat khalu nityatvamiti|
nityatvapratiṣedho nāma vikārasyātmalābhātpracyuteḥ upapattiḥ|
yadātmalābhātpracyavate tadanityaṃ dṛṣṭam|

children.translated_text: What exists does not dissolve from its acquisition of nature.

children.text: astitvaṃ cātmalābhāpracyutiriti ca viruddhāvetau dhamau na saha sambhavata iti|
children.translated_text: Existence and non-dissolution from the acquisition of nature — these two properties are contradictory and cannot co-exist.

children.text: so 'yaṃ heturyaṃ siddhāntamāśritya pravarttate tameva vyāhantīti // 6//
children.translated_text: This reason, which contradicts the very established doctrine on which it relies, [is <s>viruddha</s>]. // 6 //

That which obstructs it is '<s>tadvirodhī</s>' (contradicting it) — it contradicts the accepted established doctrine. For example: 'This modification (<s>vikāra</s>) departs from its manifestation (<s>vyakti</s>) because of the negation of its eternality; a non-eternal modification is unjustifiable. Even though departed, the modification exists, because of the negation of its destruction.' This reason — 'because of the negation of eternality' — is contradicted by its own established doctrine that 'even though departed from manifestation, the modification exists.' How? Manifestation is the acquisition of [its own] nature (<s>ātmalābha</s>). Departure is dissolution. If the modification exists after having dissolved from its acquisition of nature, then the negation of eternality is unjustifiable. For if the modification exists even when departed from manifestation, that is indeed eternality. 'Negation of eternality' means the justification that the modification dissolves from its acquisition of nature. What dissolves from its acquisition of nature is observed to be non-eternal.

children.text: NyS_1,2.7: yasmāt prakaraṇacintā saḥ nirṇayārthamapadiṣṭaḥ prakaraṇasamaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.7: That which has been adduced for the purpose of deciding the very question (<s>prakaraṇa</s>) under inquiry is <s>prakaraṇasama</s> (equivalent to the question). //

children.text:
vimarśādhiṣṭhānau pakṣapratipakṣāvubhāvanavasitau prakaraṇam|
tasya cintā vimarśātprabhṛti prāṅnirṇayādyatsamīkṣaṇam,
sā jijñāsā yatkṛtā sa nirṇayārthaṃ prayukta ubhayapakṣasāmyāt prakaraṇamanativartamānaḥ prakaraṇasamo nirṇayāya na prakalpate|
prajñāpanaṃ tvanityaḥ śabdo nityadharmānupalabdherityanupalabhyamānanityadharmakamanityaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ sthālyādi//
children.translated_text: The thesis and counter-thesis, both unresolved, constituting the basis for deliberation, [form] the <s>prakaraṇa</s> (question at issue). Its inquiry (<s>cintā</s>) is the investigation from the beginning of deliberation until before the decision — that is the desire-to-know; the [reason] employed for the purpose of that [decision], because of its equality with both sides, does not go beyond the question and does not serve for a decision. It is the <s>prakaraṇasama</s>. An illustration: 'Sound is non-eternal because the property of eternality is not apprehended' — and [similarly] what is observed as having no apprehended eternal property is non-eternal, like a pot and the like.

children.text:
yantra samāno dharmaḥ saṃśayakāraṇaṃ hetutvenopādīyate, sa saṃśayasamaḥ savyabhicāra eva|
yā tu vimarśasya viśeṣāpekṣitā ubhayapakṣaviśeṣānupalabdhiśca sā prakaraṇaṃ pravartayati|
yathā śabde nityadharmo nopalabhyate evamanityadharmaḥ api|
seyamubhayapakṣaviśeṣānupalabdhiḥ prakaraṇacintāṃ pravartayati|
katham? viparyaye hi prakaraṇanivṛtteḥ|
yadi nityadharmaḥ śabde gṛhyeta, na syātprakaraṇam|
children.translated_text: If the eternal property were apprehended in sound, there would be no question.

children.text: yadi vā anityadharmo gṛhyeta, evamapi nivartteta prakaraṇam|
children.translated_text: Or if the non-eternal property were apprehended, then too the question would be resolved.

children.text: so 'yaṃ heturubhau pakṣau pravartayannanyatarasya nirṇayāya na prakalpate // 7//
children.translated_text: This reason, which activates both sides, does not serve for the decision of either one. // 7 //

When a common property that is the cause of doubt is employed as a reason, that is <s>saṃśayasama</s> (equivalent to doubt), which is indeed a case of <s>savyabhicāra</s> (deviation). But the expectation of a distinguishing feature in the deliberation, and the non-apprehension of a distinguishing feature for either side — that is what activates the <s>prakaraṇa</s> (question). Just as the eternal property is not apprehended in sound, so too the non-eternal property [is not apprehended]. This non-apprehension of a distinguishing feature for either side activates the investigation of the question. How? Because in the contrary case, the question would be resolved.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.8: What is not distinguished from the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) because it [itself] needs to be proved is <s>sādhyasama</s> (equivalent to what is to be proved). //

children.text:
dravyaṃ chāyeti sādhyam, gatimattvāditi hetuḥ|
sādhyenāviśiṣṭaḥ sādhanīyatvāt sādhyasamaḥ|
ayamapyasiddhatvātsādhayavatprajñāpayitavyaḥ|
sādhyaṃ tāvadetat---kiṃ puruṣavacchāyāpi gacchati āho svidāvarakadravye saṃsarpati āvaraṇasantānādasannidhisantāno 'yaṃ tejaso gṛhyata iti|
children.translated_text: First, this itself is what needs to be proved: does the shadow move like a person, or does [the shadow] spread over the obstructing substance — [is] this uninterrupted non-presence of light apprehended due to the continuity of obstruction?

children.text: sarpatā khalu dravyeṇa yo yastejobhāga āvriyate tasya tasyāsannidhirevāvicchinno gṛhyata iti|
children.translated_text: Indeed, whatever portion of light is obstructed by the moving substance — the uninterrupted non-presence of precisely that [light] is apprehended.
And obstruction is the prevention of arrival [of light]. // 8 //

[Thesis:] 'A shadow is a substance' — this is the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum). 'Because it has motion' — this is the reason. [This reason] is not distinguished from the probandum because it itself needs to be established; therefore it is <s>sādhyasama</s>. This too, being unestablished, must be demonstrated just like the probandum.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.9: That which is adduced when the time has passed is <s>kālātīta</s> (the untimely). //

children.text:
kālātyayena yukto yasyārthaikadeśo 'padiśyamānasya sa kālātyayāpadiṣṭaḥ kālātīta ityucyate|
nidarśanam nityaḥ śabdaḥ saṃyogavyaṅgyatvāda rūpavat|
prāgūrddhaṃ ca vyakteravasthitaṃ rūpaṃ pradīpaghaṭasaṃyogena vyajyate, tathā ca śabdo 'pyavasthito bherīdaṇḍasaṃyogena vyajyate, dāruparaśusaṃyogena vā|
tasmātsaṃyogavyaṅgyatvānnityaḥ śabda ityayamahetuḥ kālātyayāpadeśāt|
vyañjakasya saṃyogasya kālaṃ na vyaṅgyasya rūpasya vyaktiratyeti|
sati pradīpasaṃyoge rūpasya grahaṇaṃ bhavati, na nivṛtte saṃyoge rūpaṃ gṛhyate|
nivṛtte tu dāruparaśusaṃyoge dūrasthena śabdaḥ śrūyate vibhāgakāle|
seyaṃ śabdasya vyaktiḥ|
saṃyogakālam atyetīti na saṃyoganimittā bhavati|
kasmāt? kāraṇābhāvāddhi kāryābhāva iti|
evamudāharaṇasādharmyasyābhāvādasādhanamayaṃ heturhetvābhāsa iti/
avayavaviparyāsavacanaṃ na sūtrārthaḥ|
kasmāt?
yasya yenārthasambandho dūrasthasyāpi tasya saḥ/
arthato hyasamarthānāmānantaryamakāraṇam//
children.translated_text: That which, when a part of its meaning is being adduced, is combined with a temporal impropriety — that is called <s>kālātīta</s> (untimely), i.e., <s>kālātyayāpadiṣṭa</s> (adduced with temporal impropriety). An illustration: 'Sound is eternal because it is manifested through conjunction, like color. Prior to and after [its] manifestation, color subsists and is manifested through the conjunction of a lamp and a pot; so too, sound subsists and is manifested through the conjunction of a drumstick and a drum, or of an axe and wood. Therefore, because it is manifested through conjunction, sound is eternal.' This is a non-reason due to temporal impropriety. The manifestation of the color being manifested does not outlast the time of the manifesting conjunction. When the lamp-conjunction exists, the apprehension of color occurs; when the conjunction has ceased, color is not apprehended. But when the conjunction of wood and axe has ceased, sound is heard by a distant person at the time of separation. This manifestation of sound outlasts the time of conjunction; therefore, it is not caused by conjunction. Why? Because from the absence of a cause, there follows the absence of the effect. Thus, due to the absence of the similarity of the example, this reason is an unestablished proof — a pseudo-reason (<s>hetvābhāsa</s>). The statement of the members in reversed order is not the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. Why? 'For one who has a connection with a meaning, that connection exists even when [the parts are] far apart; for those that are meaningless, [mere] contiguity is not a cause.'

children.text:
ityetadvacanādviparyāsenokto heturudāharaṇasādharmyāttathā vaidharmyātsādhyasādhanaṃ hetulakṣaṇa na jahāti|
ajahaddhetulakṣaṇaṃ na hetvābhāso bhavatīti//
children.translated_text: From this statement, a reason stated in reversed order, [if it establishes] the probandum through the similarity or dissimilarity of the example, does not abandon the defining characteristic of a [valid] reason. And what does not abandon the defining characteristic of a reason is not a pseudo-reason.
That this very [point] is stated again [here] — therefore, that is not the meaning of the <s>sūtra</s>. //9//
The statement of members in reversed order as 'untimely' is stated [elsewhere] as a point of defeat (<s>nigrahasthāna</s>).
Now, <s>chala</s> (quibble) —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.10: The frustration of a statement through the supposition of an alternative meaning is <s>chala</s> (quibble). //

children.text: na sāmānyalakṣaṇe chalaṃ śakyamudāhartum, vibhāge tūdāharaṇāni // 10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Chala</s> cannot be illustrated through the general definition; but illustrations [will be given] in the classification. // 10 //
And the classification [is] —

children.text: NyS_1,2.11: tat trividhaṃ vākchalaṃ sāmānyacchalamupacāracchalaṃ ca //
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.11: That [<s>chala</s>] is threefold: <s>vākchala</s> (verbal quibble), <s>sāmānyacchala</s> (quibble based on generality), and <s>upacāracchala</s> (quibble based on figurative usage). //
Of these —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.12: When a meaning has been stated without specification, the attribution of an alternative meaning contrary to the speaker's intention is <s>vākchala</s> (verbal quibble). //

children.text:
navakambalo 'yaṃ māṇavaka iti prayogaḥ|
atra navaḥ kambalo 'syeti vakturābhiprāyaḥ|
vigrahe tu viśeṣo, na samāse|
tatrāyaṃ chalavādī vaktuḥ abhiprāyādavivakṣitamanyamarthaṃ nava kambalā asyeti tāvadabhihitaṃ bhavateti kalpayati|
kalpayitvā cāsambhavena pratiṣedhati, eko 'sya kambalaḥ kuto nava kambalā iti|
tadidaṃ sāmānyaśabde vāci nimitte chalaṃ vākchalamiti//
children.translated_text: The usage is: 'This young man is <s>navakambala</s> (new-blanketed).' Here the speaker's intention is: 'new is the blanket of his' (<s>navaḥ kambalo 'sya</s>). The distinction is in the analysis [of the compound], not in the compound [itself]. Therein the <s>chala</s>-disputant, from the speaker's intention, fabricates another meaning that was not intended — 'nine blankets are his' (<s>nava kambalā asya</s>) — and posits that this much has been stated. Having postulated this, he refutes it by [showing its] impossibility: 'He has [only] one blanket — whence nine blankets?' This is <s>chala</s> (quibbling) based on the equivocality of a common word in speech — [hence it is called] <s>vākchala</s> (verbal quibbling).

children.text:
asya pratyavasthānam---sāmānyaśabdasyānekārthatve 'nyatarābhidhānakalpanāyāṃ viśeṣavacanam|
navakambala ityanekārthābhidhānam, navaḥ kambalo 'syeti, nava kambalā asyeti ca|
etasminprayukte yeyaṃ kalpanā navakambalā asyetyetad bhavatābhihitam, tacca na sambhavatīti|
etasyāmanyatarābhidhānakalpanāyāṃ viśeṣo vaktavyaḥ,
yasmādviśeṣo 'rthaviśeṣeṣu vijñāyate 'yamartho 'nenābhihita iti|
sa ca viśeṣo nāsti, tasmānmithyābhiyogamātrametaditi//
children.translated_text: The counter to this is: when a common word has multiple meanings, and one of those meanings is being fabricated [as the intended one], the specific meaning [must be stated]. '<s>Navakambala</s>' is an expression with multiple meanings: 'new is his blanket' and 'nine blankets are his.' When this [expression] is used and the fabrication is made — 'you have stated that nine blankets are his, and that is impossible' — against this fabrication of one [particular] meaning, a distinction must be stated, because the distinction [of meaning] is recognized among the particular meanings — 'this meaning was stated by this [expression].'
