And that distinction is not [established]; therefore this is merely a false charge.

children.text:
prasaddhiśca loke śabdārthasambandho 'bhidhānābhidheyaniyamaniyogaḥ|
asyābhidhānasyāyamartho 'bhidhena iti samānaḥ sāmānyaśabdasya, viśeṣo viśiṣṭaśabdasya|
prayuktapūrvāśceme śabdā arthe prayujyante, nāprayuktapūrvāḥ|
prayogaścārthasampratyayārthaḥ|
arthapratyayācca vyavahāra iti|
tatraivamarthagatyarthe śabdaprayoge sāmarthyātsāmānyaśabdasya prayoganiyamaḥ|
ajāṃ grāmaṃ naya, sarpirādara, brāhmaṇaṃ bhojayeti sāmānyaśabdāḥ santo 'rthāvayaveṣu prayujyante, sāmarthyāt yatrārthakriyādeśanā sambhavati tatra pravartante nārthasāmānye, kriyādeśanāsambhavāt|
evamayaṃ sāmānyaśabdo navakambala iti yo 'rthaḥ sambhavati navaḥ kambalo 'syeti, tatra pravartate|
children.translated_text: Thus this common word '<s>navakambala</s>' — the meaning that is possible, 'new is his blanket,' functions there.

children.text: yasatu na sambhavati nava kambalā asyeti, tatra na pravartate|
children.translated_text: But the [meaning] that is not possible — 'nine blankets are his' — does not function there.
This censure of another's statement through the fabrication of an untenable meaning is not valid. //12//

And the established convention in the world is the relation between word and meaning — the fixed determination of designation and designated. 'This meaning is the designated of this designation' — this is the same for a common word, and a specific [meaning belongs to] a specific word. These words are used for meanings in which they have been previously used, not in those where they have not been previously used. And usage is for the purpose of communicating meaning. And from the apprehension of meaning, [comes] practical activity. Therein, when words are used for the purpose of communicating meaning, there is by capacity a fixed determination of the usage of common words. 'Lead the goat to the village,' 'bring the ghee,' 'feed the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>' — these common words, being [general], are used for particular objects; by capacity they function where the indication of a [particular] action is possible, not in the generality of meaning, because the indication of action is not possible [there].

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.13: The fabrication of an unreal meaning through the over-extension of a general [term], when the [intended] meaning is possible — that is <s>sāmānyachala</s> (quibbling based on generality).

children.text:
aho khalavasau brāhmaṇo vidyācaraṇasampanna ityukte kaścidāha sambhavati brāhmaṇe vidyācaraṇasampaditi|
asya vacanasya vidhāto 'rthavikalpopapattyā asambhūtārthakalpanayā kriyate yadi brāhmaṇe vidyācaraṇasampat sambhavati nanu vrātye 'pi sambhavet, vrātyo 'pi brāhmaṇaḥ, so 'pyastu vidyācaraṇasampannaḥ|
yadvivakṣitamarthamāpnoti cātyeti ca tadatisāmānyam|
yathā brāhmaṇatvaṃ vidyācaraṇasampadaṃ kvacidāpnoti kvacidatyetīti|
sāmānyanimittaṃ chalaṃ sāmānyacchalamiti/
asya ca pratyavasthānam---avivakṣitahetukasya viṣayānuvādaḥ praśaṃsārthatvād vākyasya|
tadatrāsaṃbhūtārthakalpanānupapattiḥ|
yathā sambhavantyasmin kṣetre śālaya iti|
anirākṛtamavivakṣitaṃ ca bījajanma|
pravṛttiviṣayastu kṣetraṃ praśasyate|
so 'yaṃ kṣetrānuvādo, nāsmin śālayo vidhīyanta iti|
bījātaṃ śālinirvṛttiḥ satī na vivakṣitā|
evaṃ sambhavati brāhmaṇe vidyācaraṇasampaditi sampadviṣayo brāhmaṇatvaṃ na sampaddhetuḥ|
na cātra heturvivakṣitaḥ|
viṣayānuvādastvayaṃ praśaṃsārthatvād vākyasya, sati brāhmaṇatve sampaddhetuḥ samartha iti|
children.translated_text: This is a restatement of the subject-matter, because the statement is for the purpose of praise — given that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-hood, when present, is a competent cause of [such] endowment.

children.text: viṣayaṃ ca praśaṃsatā vākyena yathāhetutaḥ phalanirvṛttirna pratyākhyāyate|
children.translated_text: And by a statement that praises the subject-matter, the production of the result from the [actual] cause is not being denied.
This being so, the fabrication of an unreal meaning through distortion of the statement is unjustified. //13//

When it is said, 'Oh, this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> is truly endowed with learning and conduct,' someone says: 'Learning and conduct are possible in a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>.' A distortion of the purport of this statement is made through the device of an alternative meaning-fabrication: 'If learning and conduct are possible in a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, would they not also be possible in a <s>vrātya</s> (uninitiated one)? For a <s>vrātya</s> is also a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>; let him too be endowed with learning and conduct.' That which reaches the intended meaning and also goes beyond it — that is <s>atisāmānya</s> (over-generalization). Just as <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-hood sometimes reaches and sometimes goes beyond the endowment of learning and conduct. <s>Chala</s> (quibbling) based on the general [term] is <s>sāmānyachala</s>. And the counter to this is: when the cause is not intended, a restatement of the subject-matter [suffices], because the statement is for the purpose of praise. Therefore, the fabrication of an unreal meaning is unjustified here. Just as [when one says] 'rice thrives in this field,' the production from seed is neither refuted nor intended [as the point]. Rather, the field is praised as the domain of activity. This is a restatement about the field — rice is not being prescribed in it. The production of rice from seed, though real, is not intended [as the topic].

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.14: The denial of the real existence of a meaning, when an expression involving a variant property is indicated — that is <s>upacārachala</s> (quibbling based on figurative usage).

children.text:
abhidhānasya dharmo yathārthaprayogaḥ|
dharmavikalpo 'nyatra dṛṣṭasyānyatra prayogaḥ|
tasya nirdeśe dharmavikalpanirdeśe|
yathā mañcāḥ krośantīti arthasadbhāvaneva pratiṣedhaḥ mañcasthāḥ puruṣāḥ krośanti, na tu mañcāḥ krośanti//
children.translated_text: The property of a designation is its literal usage. A variant property is the usage in another [context] of what was observed in one [context]. Its indication is the indication of a variant property. For example: 'The platforms are shouting' — the denial of the real existence of the meaning [means]: the people standing on the platforms are shouting, not the platforms themselves.

children.text:
kā punaratrārthavikalpopattiḥ? anyathā prayuktasyānyathārthakalpanaṃ, bhaktyā prayoge prādhānyena kalpanam upacāraviṣayaṃ chalamupacāracchalam|
upacāro nītārthaḥ sahacaraṇādinimittena, atadbhāve tadvadabhidhānamupacāra iti//
children.translated_text: But what is the device of alternative meaning here? The fabrication of another meaning for what was used in one way; when [a word is] used figuratively, postulating [it as used] literally — that is <s>chala</s> whose domain is figurative usage, i.e., <s>upacārachala</s>. Figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) is indirect meaning; [it occurs] due to association and the like — speaking as if something were what it is not, due to its absence, is <s>upacāra</s>.

children.text:
atra samādhiḥ---prasiddhe prayoge vakturyathābhiprāyaṃ śabdārthayorabhyanujñā pratiṣedho vā na cchandataḥ|
pradhānabhūtasya śabdasya bhāktasya ca guṇabhūtasya prayoga ubhayorloke siddhaḥ|
siddhe prayoge yathā vakturabhiprāyastathā śabdārthāvanujñeyau pratiṣedhyau vā na cchandataḥ|
yadi vaktā pradhānaśabdaṃ prayuṅkte, yathābhūtasyābhyanujñā pratiṣedho vā na nchandataḥ|
children.translated_text: If the speaker uses the word in its primary sense, acceptance or rejection is of what is literal, not arbitrary.
But if [the word is used] in its secondary sense? Then [acceptance or rejection is] of the secondary [sense].

children.text: yatra tu vaktā guṇabhūtaṃ śabdaṃ prayuṅkte pradhānabhūtamabhipretya paraḥ pratiṣedhati, svamanīṣayā pratiṣedho 'sau bhavati na paropālambha iti // 14 //
children.translated_text: But where the speaker uses a word in its secondary sense intending the primary sense, and the opponent refutes [only] the primary sense — that refutation is of his own devising, not a censure of the other. //14//

The resolution here is: in an established usage, the acceptance or rejection of word and meaning according to the speaker's intention is not arbitrary. The usage of both the primary word and the secondary (figurative) word is established in the world. In an established usage, word and meaning should be accepted or rejected as per the speaker's intention, not arbitrarily.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.15: <s>Upacārachala</s> (figurative quibbling) is indeed [the same as] <s>vākchala</s> (verbal quibbling), because there is no distinction.

children.text: ihāpi sthānyartho guṇaśabdaḥ, pradhānaśabdaḥ sathānārtha iti kalpayitvā pratiṣidhyata iti // 15 //
children.translated_text: Here too, the word in the secondary sense is [treated as if it is] in the primary sense, and the word in the primary sense is [treated as if it is] in the secondary sense — having fabricated [this], it is refuted. //15//
<s>Upacārachala</s> is not different from <s>vākchala</s>, because there is no distinction in fabricating another meaning in its case as well.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.16: No, because it is a different thing.
<s>Upacārachala</s> is not the same as <s>vākchala</s>, because that denial of the real existence of the meaning is a different thing.
How so? Because of the fabrication of a different meaning.
For the fabrication of another meaning is one thing; the denial of the real existence of the meaning is another. //16//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.17: Or, if there is no distinction, then because of some similarity, the consequence would be that there is only one [type of] <s>chala</s> (quibbling).
And just as this reasoning refutes the threefold [division], so too
it refutes the accepted twofold [division] as well.

children.text: vidyate hi kiṃcitsādharmyānna nivartate, tritvamapi na nivartsyatīti // 17//
children.translated_text: For the [argument based on] some similarity does not stop [at three]; the threefold [division] too will not be refuted [on that ground alone]. //17//
Having accepted the twofold [division] of <s>chala</s>, the threefold [division] is refuted on the ground of some similarity.
After this —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.18: A <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinder) is an objection based on similarity or dissimilarity.

children.text:
prayukte hi hetau yaḥ prasaṅgo jāyate sā jātiḥ|
sa ca prasaṅgaḥ sādharmyavaidharmyābhyā pratyavasthānamupālambhaḥ pratiṣedha iti|
udāharaṇasādharmyāt sādhyasādhanaṃ hetuḥ ityasyodāharaṇavaidharmyeṇa pratyavasthānam|
tathā udāharaṇavaidharmyātsādhyasādhanaṃ hetuḥ ityasyodāharaṇasādharmyeṇa pratyavasthānam|
pratyanīkabhāvājjāyamāno 'rtho jātirati// 17 //
children.translated_text: When a reason (<s>hetu</s>) has been employed, the objection that arises is a <s>jāti</s>. And that objection is a counter-argument, a censure, a refutation based on similarity or dissimilarity. An objection through dissimilarity with the example [counters] the reason that establishes the <s>sādhya</s> (probandum) through similarity with the example. Likewise, an objection through similarity with the example [counters] the reason that establishes the <s>sādhya</s> through dissimilarity with the example. A meaning arising from opposition is called <s>jāti</s>. //17//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.19: <s>Vipratipattiḥ</s> (wrong apprehension) and <s>apratipattiḥ</s> (non-apprehension) are <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (grounds of defeat).

children.text:
viparītā vā kutsitā vā pratipattirvipratipattiḥ|
vipratipadyamānaḥ parājayaṃ prāpnoti|
nigrahasthānaṃ khalu parājayaprāptiḥ|

children.translated_text: <s>Apratipattiḥ</s> is non-commencement even regarding the subject of commencement.

children.text: pareṇa sthāpitaṃ vā na pratiṣedhati, pratiṣedhaṃ vā noddharati|
children.translated_text: Either one does not refute what has been established by the opponent, or one does not remove the refutation.
And these are not the only grounds of defeat, since [the list is] not exhaustive. //19//
<s>Vipratipattiḥ</s> is apprehension that is reversed or debased. One who apprehends wrongly incurs defeat. A <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (ground of defeat) is indeed the incurrence of defeat.
Is there no distinction between <s>jāti</s> and <s>nigrahasthāna</s>, like the illustration, or is there a distinction, like the doctrine? To this he says —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 1.2.20: The multiplicity of <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinders) and <s>nigrahasthāna</s> (grounds of defeat) is due to the varieties of those [categories].

children.text:
tasya sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ pratyavasthānasya vikalpājjātibahutvam, tayośca vipratipattyapratipattyovikalpānnigrahasthānabahuttvam|
nānākalpo vikalpaḥ|
vividho vā kalpo vikalpaḥ/
tatrānanubhāṣaṇamajñānamapratibhā vikṣepo matānujñā paryanuyojyopekṣaṇamityapratipattirnigrahasthānam|
śeṣastu vipratipattiriti//
children.translated_text: The multiplicity of <s>jāti</s> is due to the varieties of that counter-argument based on similarity and dissimilarity; and the multiplicity of <s>nigrahasthāna</s> is due to the varieties of those two — wrong apprehension (<s>vipratipattiḥ</s>) and non-apprehension (<s>apratipattiḥ</s>). 'Variety' (<s>vikalpa</s>) means manifold division, or diverse division. Therein: non-response, ignorance, lack of readiness, distraction, assent [to the opponent's view], and ignoring what is objectionable — these constitute non-apprehension (<s>apratipattiḥ</s>) as a ground of defeat. The rest is wrong apprehension (<s>vipratipattiḥ</s>).

children.text: ta ime pramāṇādayaḥ padārthā uddiṣṭā yathoddeśaṃ ca lakṣitā yathālakṣaṇaṃ ca parīkṣiṣyanta iti trividhā cāsya

children.translated_text: <s>śāstra</s> (treatise) should be understood. //20//

These categories beginning with <s>pramāṇa</s> have been enumerated, and they have been defined according to their enumeration, and they will be examined according to their definitions. And the threefold procedure of this
// End of the second lesson of the first chapter of <s>Vātsyāyana's</s> <s>Nyāyabhāṣya</s> //
And this first chapter is complete.

children.text: śrī śrīnivāsa svāmi, śrī vināyaka svāmi, śrī sarasvatī devī,
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Śrīnivāsa Svāmī</s>, <s>Śrī Vināyaka Svāmī</s>, <s>Śrī Sarasvatī Devī</s>,
<s>Oṃ</s>
Now the first lesson of the second chapter of the <s>Nyāyabhāṣya</s> with sub-commentary.

children.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ pramāṇādiparīkṣā sā ca"vimṛśya pakṣapratipakṣābhyāmarthāvadhāraṇaṃ nirṇayaḥ 1-1-41"ityagre vimarśa eva parīkṣyate---
children.translated_text: After this [comes] the examination of <s>pramāṇa</s> and the rest; and that [examination], since '<s>nirṇaya</s> (ascertainment) is the determination of a matter through deliberation on the thesis and counter-thesis' [1.1.41], the deliberation itself is examined first —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.1: There is no <s>saṃśaya</s> (doubt) from the ascertainment of a property common [to several things], or from the ascertainment of the property of one of them.

children.text: samānasya dharmasyādhyavasāyāt saṃśayo na dharmamātrāt, atha vā 'samānamanayordharmamupalabhe' iti dharmadharmigrahaṇe saṃśayābhāva iti, atha vā samānadharmādhyavasāyādarthāntarabhūte dharmiṇi saṃśayo 'nupapannaḥ-- na jātu rūpāsayārthāntarabhūtasyādhyavasāyādarthāntarabhūte sparśe saṃśaya iti, atha vā nādhyavasāyāt = arthāvadhāraṇād anavadhāraṇajñānaṃ saṃśaya upapadyate--- kāryakāraṇayoḥ sārūpyābhavāditi|
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃśaya</s> does not [arise] from the ascertainment of a common property merely — not from the property alone. Or [alternatively]: when both the property and the property-bearer (<s>dharmin</s>) are apprehended — 'I apprehend a common property between them' — there is absence of <s>saṃśaya</s>. Or [alternatively]: from the ascertainment of a common property, <s>saṃśaya</s> is untenable regarding a property-bearer that is a different thing — for there is never <s>saṃśaya</s> about touch, which is a different thing, from the ascertainment of color, which is [also] a different thing. Or [alternatively]: not from ascertainment (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) — that is, from determination of meaning — does <s>saṃśaya</s>, which is cognition of non-determination, arise, because there is no resemblance between cause and effect.
By this, 'from the ascertainment of multiple properties' is also explained.

children.text: anyataradharmādhyavasāyācca saṃśayo na bhavati-- tato hyanyatarāvadhāraṇameveti // 1 //
children.translated_text: And from the ascertainment of the property of one of them, <s>saṃśaya</s> does not arise — for from that there is only the determination of one of them. //1//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.2: And [no doubt arises] from [mere] conflicting testimony or [mere] indeterminate status.

children.text: na vipratipattimātrādavyavasthāmātrādvā saṃśayaḥ, kiṃ tarhi ?. vipratipattimupalabhamānasya saṃśayaḥ, evamavyavasthāyāmapīti|
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃśaya</s> does not [arise] from mere conflicting testimony or mere indeterminate status. Rather, [it arises] for one who perceives the conflicting testimony — [then] there is <s>saṃśaya</s>. Likewise also in the case of indeterminate status.

children.text: atha vā 'astyātmā' ityeke 'nāstyātmā' ityapare manyante ityupalabdheḥ kathaṃ saṃśayaḥ syāt ? iti|
children.translated_text: Or [the objection runs]: 'The <s>ātman</s> exists' — some think; 'the <s>ātman</s> does not exist' — others think. From [such] perception, how could <s>saṃśaya</s> arise?

children.text: tathopalabdhiravyavasthitā anupalabdhiś cāvyavasthiteti vibhāgenādhyavasite saṃśayo nopapadyate iti // 2 //
children.translated_text: Similarly, perception is indeterminate and non-perception is indeterminate — when distinguished in this way and ascertained, <s>saṃśaya</s> is untenable. //2//
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.3: And because of agreement in the case of disagreement.

children.text: yāṃ va vipratipattiṃ bhavān saṃśayahetuṃ manyate sā saṃpratipattiḥ-- sā hi dvayoḥ pratyanīkadharmaviṣayā, tatra yadi viprattipatteḥ saṃśayaḥ ? saṃpratipattereva saṃśaya iti // 3 //
children.translated_text: The disagreement (<s>vipratipatti</s>) which you consider as the cause of doubt — that is [itself] an agreement (<s>saṃpratipatti</s>). For that [disagreement] has as its object the properties of two opposed [views]. If there is doubt from disagreement, [then there would be] doubt from agreement itself. [End of NyS 2.1.3]
[Section: NySBh 2.1.4]
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.4: And because indeterminacy is established in what is itself indeterminate.

children.text: na saṃśayaḥ, yadi tāvadiyamavyavasthā ātmanyeva vyavasthitā ? vyavasthānādavyavasthā na bhavatītyanupapannaḥ saṃśayaḥ, athāvyavasthātmani na vyavasthitā ? evamatādātmyādavyavasthā na bhavatīti saṃśayābhāva iti // 4 //
children.translated_text: There is no doubt — if this indeterminacy is established in [its own] nature? Then, because of being established, it is not indeterminacy — and thus doubt is unjustified. But if the indeterminacy is not established in its own nature? Then, because of not being of that nature, there is no indeterminacy — hence there is no doubt. [End of NyS 2.1.4]
[Section: NySBh 2.1.5]
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.5: Similarly, there would be perpetual doubt, because of the continuous presence of those properties.

children.text: yena kalpena bhavān samānadharmopapatteḥ saṃśaya iti manyate tena khalv atyantasaṃśayaḥ prasajyate-- samānadharmopapatteranucchedāt saṃśayānucchedaḥ-- nāyamataddharmā dharmī vimṛśyamāno gṛhyate satataṃ tu taddharmā bhavatīti // 5 //
children.translated_text: By the very reasoning by which you hold that doubt arises from the presence of common properties — by that, perpetual doubt would follow. Because the presence of common properties is not cut off, doubt would not be cut off — the object being examined is never grasped as lacking those properties, but is constantly possessed of those properties. [End of NyS 2.1.5]
[Section: NySBh 2.1.6]
A concise resolution of this elaborate refutation —

children.text: NyS_2,1.6: yathoktādhyavasāyādeva tadviśeṣāpekṣāt saṃśaye nāsaṃśayo nātyantasaṃśayo vā //
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 2.1.6: Because of the very determination as stated, which looks for a distinguishing feature — there is neither absence of doubt nor perpetual doubt.

children.text:
na saṃśayānutpattiḥ saṃśayānucchedaśca prasajyate, katham ?. yattāvat-- 'samānadharmādhyavasāyaḥ saṃśayahatuḥ na samānadharmamātramiti,' evametat|
kasmādevaṃ nocyate ? iti,"vaśeṣāpekṣiḥ"itivacanāt tatsiddheḥ. viśeṣasyāpekṣā = ākāṅkṣā sā cānupalabhyamāne vaśeṣe simarthā|
na coktam-- 'samānadharmāpekṣaḥ' iti|
samāne ca dharme kathamākāṅkṣā na bhaved yadyayamapratyakṣaḥ myāt, etena sāmarthyena vajñāyite-- 'samānadharmādhyavasāyāt' iti|
upapattivacanādvā. samānadharmopapatterityucyate. na cānyā sadbhāvasaṃvedanādṛte samānadharmopapattirasti, anupalabhyamānasadbhāvo hi samāno dharmo 'vadyimānavad bhavatīti|
vaṣiyaśabdena vā vaṣiyiṇaḥ pratyayasyābhidhānaṃ yathā loke 'dhūmenāgniranumīyate' ityukte 'dhūmadarśanenāgniranumīyate' itijñāyate, katham ?. dṛṣṭvā hi dhūmamathāgnimanuminoti nādṛṣṭe. na caṃ vākye darśanaśabdaḥ śrūyate. anujānāti ca vākyasyārthapratyāyakatvaṃ tena manyāmahe-- vaṣiyaśabdena vaṣiyiṇaḥ pratyayasyābhidhānaṃ boddhānujānāti. evamihāpi samānadharmaśabdena samānadharmādhyavasāyamāheti|
children.translated_text: Neither the non-arising of doubt nor the non-cessation of doubt follows. How? As for [the objection that] 'the determination of common properties is the cause of doubt, not merely common properties' — that is indeed so. Why is it not stated thus? Because it is already established by the statement 'looking for a distinguishing feature' (<s>viśeṣāpekṣa</s>). The expectation (<s>apekṣā</s>) of a distinguishing feature is the desire [to know it], and that is effective when the distinguishing feature is not apprehended. Nor was it said 'looking for a common property.' And how could there be a desire for what is common? If this [common property] were imperceptible, by this very implication, [the meaning] 'from the determination of common properties' is understood. Or from the statement about presence (<s>upapatti</s>) — 'because of the presence of common properties' is said. And there is no presence of common properties without the awareness of their existence; for a common property whose existence is not apprehended becomes like what is non-existent. Or, by the word 'distinguishing feature' (<s>viśeṣa</s>), the cognition of [seeking] a distinguishing feature is meant — just as in the world, when 'fire is inferred from smoke' is said, it is understood as 'fire is inferred from seeing smoke.' How? For one infers fire after seeing smoke, not when [smoke is] unseen. Yet the word 'seeing' does not occur in the sentence. One accepts the capacity of the sentence to convey meaning — thus we hold that by the word 'distinguishing feature,' the cognition of [seeking] a distinguishing feature is meant, [and] the knower accepts [this]. So here too, by the word 'common property,' the determination of common properties is meant.

children.text:
yaduktam-- 'samānamanayodharmamupalabhe iti dharmadharmigrahaṇe saṃśayābhāvaḥ' iti, pūrvadṛṣṭaviṣayametatuyāvahamarthau pūrvamadrākṣaṃ tayoḥ samānaṃ dharmamupalabhe viśeṣaṃ nopalabhe iti. kathaṃ nu viśeṣaṃ paśyeyaṃ yenānyataramavadhārayeyamiti, na caitat samānadharmopalabdhau dharmadharmigrahaṇamātreṇa nivartate iti|
yaccoktam-- nārthāntarādhyavasāyādanyatra saṃśaya iti. yo hyarthāntarādhyavasāyamātraṃ saṃśayahetumupādadīta sa evaṃ vācya iti|
yatpunaretat-- kāryakāraṇayoḥ sārūpyābhāvāditi, kāraṇasya bhāvābhāvayoḥ kāryasya bhāvābhāvau kāryakāraṇayoḥ sārūpyamuyasyotpādāt yadutpadyate yasya cānutpādād yannotpadyate tat kāraṇaṃ kāryamitarad ityetsārūpyam asti ca saṃśayakāraṇe saṃśaye caitaditi|
etena anekadharmādhyavasāyāditi pratiṣedhaḥ parihṛta iti|
yatpunaretaduktam-- vipratipattyavyavasthādhyavasāyācca na saṃśaya iti, pṛthakpravādayorvyāhatamarthamupalabhe viśeṣaṃ ca na jānāmiunopalabhe yenānyataramavadhārayeyaṃ tatkotra viśeṣaḥ syād yenaikataramavadhārayeyamiti saṃśayo vipratipattijanitoyaṃ na śakyo vipratipattisaṃpratipattimātreṇa nivartayitumiti|
evam upalabdhyanupalabdhyavyavasthākṛte saṃśaye veditavyamiti|
yatpunaretat--"vipratipattau ca saṃpratipatteḥ3"iti, vipratipattiśabdasya yorthaḥ tadadhyavasāyo viśeṣāpekṣaḥ saṃśayahetustasya ca samākhyāntareṇa na nivṛttiḥusamāne 'dhikaraṇe vyāhatārthau pravādau vipratipattiśabdasyārthaḥ tadadhyavasāyaśca viśeṣāpekṣaḥ saṃśayahetuḥ na cāsya saṃpratipattiśabde samākhyāntare yojyamāne saṃśayahetutvaṃ nivartate. tadidamakṛtabuddhisaṃmohanamiti|
yatpunaḥ"avyavasthātmani vyavasthitatvāccāvyavasthāyāḥ4"iti, saṃśayahetorarthasyāpratiṣedhāt avyavasthābhyanujñānācca nimittāntareṇa śabdāntarakalpanā vyarthā, śabdāntarakalpanā-- 'avyavasthā khalv avyavasthā na bhavati-- avyavasthātmani vyavasthitatvāditi' |
nānayorupalabdhyanupalabdhyoḥ sadasadviṣayatvaṃ viśeṣāpekṣaṃ saṃśayaheturna bhavatīti pratiṣidhyate|
yāvatā cāvyavasthātmani vyavasthitā na tāvatātmānaṃ jahāti tāvatā hyanujñātā bhavatyavyavasthā, evamiyaṃ kriyamāṇāpi śabdāntarakalpanā nārthāntaraṃ sādhayatīti|

children.translated_text: And as for this — 'Similarly, there would be perpetual doubt, because of the continuous presence of those properties' — doubt does not arise from common properties and the like alone.

children.text: kiṃ tarhi ?. tadviṣayādhyavasāyād viśeṣasmṛtisahitāt iti. ato nātyantasaṃśaya iti|
children.translated_text: From what then? From the determination regarding that object, accompanied by the memory of the distinguishing feature. Therefore, there is no perpetual doubt.

children.text: "anyataradharmādhyavasāyādvā na saṃśayaḥ"iti. tanna yuktam-- viśeṣāpekṣo vimarśaḥ saṃśayaḥ itivacanāt. viśeṣaścānyataradharmo na tasminn adhyavasīyamāne viśeṣāpekṣā saṃbhavatīti // 6 //
children.translated_text: 'Or there is no doubt from the determination of a property belonging to one [alternative]' — this is not valid, because of the statement that deliberation looking for a distinguishing feature is doubt. And the property belonging to one [alternative] is the distinguishing feature; when that is being determined, the expectation of a distinguishing feature is not possible [since it is already found]. [End of NyS 2.1.6]

As for what was said — 'In apprehending common properties of these two, since both property and property-bearer are grasped, there is no doubt' — this relates to a previously seen object: 'I previously saw both objects; I apprehend their common property but do not apprehend the distinguishing feature. How might I see the distinguishing feature by which I could ascertain either one?' And this is not eliminated merely by grasping property and property-bearer when common properties are apprehended. And as for what was said — 'There is no doubt except from the determination of something different' — whoever adduces mere determination of something different as the cause of doubt is to be refuted thus. And as for this — 'Because of the absence of similarity between cause and effect' — the existence and non-existence of the effect [follow] from the existence and non-existence of the cause; the similarity of cause and effect [means]: that from whose arising something arises, and from whose non-arising something does not arise — that is the cause, the other is the effect. And this [similarity] exists both in the cause of doubt and in doubt itself. By this, the objection 'from the determination of multiple properties' is also resolved. And as for what was said — 'There is no doubt from the determination of disagreement and indeterminacy' — apprehending contradictory meanings in separate assertions and not knowing, not apprehending, the distinguishing feature by which one could ascertain either one — 'Where would the distinguishing feature be by which I could ascertain either one?' — this doubt born of disagreement cannot be eliminated merely by disagreement or agreement. Similarly, one should understand regarding doubt arising from [the indeterminate status of] perception and non-perception. And as for this — 'Because of agreement in the case of disagreement' — the meaning of the word 'disagreement' (<s>vipratipatti</s>) is the determination of that [contradictory meaning], which looks for a distinguishing feature, [and] is the cause of doubt; and it is not eliminated by substituting another name. Contradictory assertions regarding the same subject are the meaning of the word 'disagreement'; the determination of that looks for a distinguishing feature and is the cause of doubt; and its status as the cause of doubt is not eliminated by applying the alternative name 'agreement.' This [objection] fails to produce confusion in the wise. And as for 'Because indeterminacy is established in what is itself indeterminate' — because the object that causes doubt is not refuted, and because indeterminacy is conceded, the fabrication of another word for another reason is pointless — the fabrication of another word: 'Indeterminacy is indeed not indeterminacy — because indeterminacy is established in its own nature.' The [doubt-causing] status of these — perception and non-perception — as being concerned with existing and non-existing objects, which looks for a distinguishing feature and is the cause of doubt, is not thereby refuted. And insofar as [indeterminacy] is established in its own nature, it does not abandon itself — to that extent, indeterminacy is conceded. Thus, even when this fabrication of another word is made, it does not establish a different meaning.
[Section: NySBh 2.1.7]
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.7: Wherever there is doubt, there [follows] this succession of further and further [debate].

children.text: yatra yatra saṃśayapūrvikā parīkṣā śāstre kathāyāṃ vā tatra tatraivaṃ saṃśaye pareṇa pratiṣiddhe samādhirvācya iti, ataḥ sarvaparīkṣāvyāpitvāt prathamaṃ saṃśayaḥ parīkṣita iti // 7 //
children.translated_text: Wherever in the treatise or in discussion there is examination preceded by doubt — there, when doubt is refuted by the opponent, a resolution must be stated. Therefore, because it pervades all examination, doubt has been examined first. [End of NyS 2.1.7]
[Section: NySBh 2.1.8] Now the examination of <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge) —
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.8: [Objection:] Perception and the other [means of valid knowledge] are not valid — because [their relation to objects of] the three times is not established.

Perception and the rest are not valid means of knowledge — because [their relation to objects of] the three times is not established, that is, because the relation of prior, posterior, and simultaneous [existence of means and object] is untenable. [End of NyS 2.1.8]
[Section: NySBh 2.1.9] Now the analysis of the meaning of the general statement —

children.text: NyS_2,1.9: pūrvaṃ hi pramāṇasiddhau nendriyārthasaṃnikarṣāt pratyakṣotpattiḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 2.1.9: For if the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) is established first, perception does not arise from the contact of sense-organ and object.

children.text: gandhādiviṣayaṃ jñānaṃ pratyakṣaṃ tad yadi pūrvaṃ paścād gandhādīnāṃ siddhiḥ ? nedaṃ gandhādi saṃnikarṣādutpadyate iti // 9 //
children.translated_text: The cognition having odor and the like as its object is perception. If that [perception] exists first and the objects — odor and the like — are established afterward? Then this [perception] does not arise from the contact with odor and the like. [End of NyS 2.1.9]
[Section: NySBh 2.1.10]
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.10: If [the <s>prameya</s>] is established afterward, the <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge) is not established through <s>pramāṇas</s>. [End of NyS 2.1.10]

children.text: asati pramāṇe kena pramīyamāṇo 'rthaḥ prameyaḥ syāt ?, pramāṇena khalu pramīyamāṇo 'rthaḥ prameyam ityetat sidhyati //
children.translated_text: In the absence of a <s>pramāṇa</s>, by what would the object being measured be a <s>prameya</s>? For it is established that an object is a <s>prameya</s> [only] when it is being measured by a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
[Section: NySBh 2.1.11]
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.11: If [they are] established simultaneously — because of cognitions being restricted to individual objects, there would be no successive functioning of cognitions.

children.text:
yadi pramāṇaṃ prameyaṃ ca yugapad bhavataḥ ? evamapi gandhādiṣvindriyārtheṣu jñānāni pratyarthaniyatāni yugapad saṃbhavantīti jñānānāṃ pratyarthaniyatatvāt kramavṛttitvābhāvaḥuyā imā buddhayaḥ krameṇārtheṣu vartante tāsāṃ kramavṛttitvaṃ na saṃbhavatīti|
vyāghātaśca-- "yugapad jñānānutpattirmanaso liṅgam 1-1-26"iti, etāvāṃśca pramāṇaprameyayoḥ sadbhāvaviṣayaḥ sa cānupapanna iti, tasmāt pratyakṣādīnāṃ pramāṇatvaṃ na saṃbhavatīti // 11 //
children.translated_text: If <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s> exist simultaneously? Even so, since cognitions of sense-objects like odor and the rest are restricted to individual objects and would [all] occur simultaneously — because of cognitions being restricted to individual objects, there would be no successive functioning. These cognitions that function successively with respect to objects — their successive functioning would not be possible. And there is a contradiction with [the sūtra]: 'The non-simultaneous arising of cognitions is the inferential mark of the mind (<s>manas</s>)' [NyS 1.1.16]. And this entire [argument] concerns the existence of <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s>, which is untenable — therefore the validity of perception and the rest is not possible. [End of NyS 2.1.11]

children.text:
asya samādhiḥ--- upalabdhihetorupalabdhiviṣayasya cārthasya pūrvāparasahabhāvā- 'niyamād yathādarśanaṃ vibhāgavacanam2. kvacidupalabdhihetuḥ pūrvaṃ paścādupalabdhiviṣayo yathādityasya prakāśaḥ, utpadyamānānāṃ kvacit pūrvamupalabdhiviṣayaḥ paścādupalabdhiheturyathāvasthitānāṃ pradīpaḥ, kvacidupalabdhiheturupalabdhiviṣayaśca saha bhavato yathā dhūmenāgnergrahaṇamiti/ upalabdhihetuśca pramāṇaṃ prameyaṃ tūpalabdhiviṣayaḥ/ evaṃ pramāṇaprameyayoḥ pūrvāparasahabhāve 'niyate yathārtho dṛśyate tathā vibhajya vacanīya iti, tatraikāntena pratiṣedhānupapattiḥ-- sāmānyena khalu vibhajya pratiṣedha ukta iti/ samākhyāhetosraikālyayogāt tathābhūtā samākhyā3. yatpunaridam-- 'paścātsiddhauuasati pramāṇe prameyaṃ na sidhyati-- pramāṇena pramīyamāṇo 'rthaḥ prameyamiti vijñāyate' iti, pramāṇamityetasyāḥ samākhyāyā upalabdhihetutvaṃ nimittaṃ tasya traikālyayogaḥ-- 'upalabdhimakārṣīt' 'upalabdhiṃ karoti' 'upalabdhiṃ kariṣyati' iti samākhyāhetoḥ traikālyayogāt samākhyā tathābhūtā, pramito 'nenārthaḥ pramīyate pramāsyate iti pramāṇam. pramitaṃ pramīyate pramāsyate iti ca prameyam, evaṃ sati bhaviṣyatyasmin hetuta upalabdhiḥupramāsyate 'yamarthaḥ prameyamidam ityetatsarvaṃ bhavatīti|
traikālyānabhyanujñāne ca vyavahārānupapa4ttiḥ. yaścaivaṃ nābhyanujānīyāt tasya 'pācakamānaya pakṣyati' 'lāvakamānaya laviṣyatītivyavahāro nopapadyate iti|
"pratyakṣādīnāmaprāmāṇyaṃ traikālyāsiddheḥ 2-1-8"ityevamādivākyaṃ pramāṇapratiṣedhaḥ. tatrāyaṃ praṣṭavyaḥ- athānena pratiṣedhena bhavatā kiṃ kriyate iti, kiṃ saṃbhavo nivartyate ? athāsaṃbhāvo jñāpyate ? iti, tad yadi saṃbhavo nivartyate ? sati saṃbhave pratyakṣādīnāṃ pratiṣedhānupapattiḥ, athāsaṃbhavo jñāpyate ? pramāṇalakṣaṇaṃ prāptastarhi pratiṣedhaḥ-- pramāṇāsaṃbhavasyopalabdhihetutvāditi // 11 //
children.translated_text: The resolution of this: Because there is no fixed rule of priority, posteriority, or simultaneity between the cause of apprehension and the object of apprehension, the division is stated according to what is observed. Sometimes the cause of apprehension is prior and the object of apprehension posterior — as the light of the sun [which exists before the objects it reveals]; sometimes the object of apprehension is prior and the cause of apprehension posterior — as a lamp [reveals] things already existing; sometimes the cause of apprehension and the object of apprehension exist together — as the apprehension of fire from smoke. The <s>pramāṇa</s> is the cause of apprehension, and the <s>prameya</s> is the object of apprehension. Thus, when there is no fixed rule of priority, posteriority, or simultaneity for <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s>, the division should be stated according to how the object is seen — therefore a blanket refutation is untenable, for the refutation was stated generally, by division. [The designation has] a three-time applicability because of the cause of designation. The designation 'that which is to be measured' — this designation 'pramāṇa' has apprehension-causality as its basis, and that has a three-time applicability: 'it caused apprehension,' 'it causes apprehension,' 'it will cause apprehension' — because the cause of designation has a three-time applicability, the designation is of such nature. '<s>Pramāṇa</s>' [means]: the object was measured by this, is measured, will be measured. '<s>Prameya</s>' [means]: [the object] was measured, is being measured, will be measured. This being so, when there is the future causal relation — 'this object will be measured, this is the <s>prameya</s>' — all of this is valid. And if the three-time [applicability] is not conceded, worldly transactions would be untenable. And one who does not concede this — for him the transaction 'bring the cook, he will cook' or 'bring the harvester, he will harvest' would be untenable. The statement 'Perception and the rest are not valid means — because [their relation to objects of] the three times is not established' [NyS 2.1.8] and so forth — this is a refutation of <s>pramāṇa</s>. Here he should be asked: What do you accomplish by this refutation? Is a possibility being negated? Or is an impossibility being made known? If a possibility is being negated? Then, given that the possibility [of pramāṇas] exists, the refutation is untenable. If an impossibility is being made known? Then the refutation itself has acquired the character of a <s>pramāṇa</s> — because the impossibility of <s>pramāṇa</s> is itself a cause of apprehension. [End of NyS 2.1.11]
[Section: NySBh 2.1.12] Moreover —
NyS_2,1.12: Because of non-establishment in the three times (<s>traikālyāsiddhi</s>), refutation is impossible.

children.text: asya tu vibhāgaḥ-- pūrvaṃ hi pratiṣedhasiddhāvasati pratiṣedhye kimanena pratiṣidhyate ?, paścāt siddhau pratiṣedhāsiddhiḥ- pratiṣedhābhāvāditi, yūgapatsiddhau pratiṣedhyasiddhyabhyanujñānādanarthakaḥ pratiṣedha iti, pratiṣedhalakṣaṇe ca vākye 'nupapadyamāne siddhaṃ pratyakṣādīnāṃ pramāṇatvamiti // 12 //
children.translated_text: The analysis of this is as follows: If the refutation is established prior [to the thing to be refuted], then when the object of refutation is already present, what is being refuted by it? If it is established afterwards, then the refutation is not established — because of the absence of the refutation [at the relevant time]. If both are established simultaneously, then since the establishment of the object of refutation is thereby conceded, the refutation is purposeless. And when the statement characterizing the refutation is itself untenable, the <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood (validity as means of knowledge) of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception) and the rest is established. // 12 //
NyS_2,1.13: And because of the refutation of all <s>pramāṇa</s>s, refutation is impossible.

children.text: katham ?. "traikālyāsiddheḥ"ityasya hetoryadyudāharaṇamupādīyate ? hetvarthasya sādhakatvaṃ dṛṣṭānte darśayitavyamiti. na ca tarhi pratyakṣādīnāmaprāmāṇyam, atha pratyakṣādīnāmaprāmāṇyam ?. upādīyamānamapyudāharaṇaṃ nārthaṃ sādhayiṣyatīti. soyaṃ sarvapramāṇairvyāhato heturahetuḥ-- "siddhāntamabhyupetya tadvirodhī viruddhaḥ 1-2-6"iti, vākyārtho hyasya siddhāntaḥ sa ca vākyārthaḥ-- 'pratyakṣādīni nārthaṃ sādhayanti' iti. idaṃ cāvayavānāmupādānamarthasya sādhanāyeti/ atha nopādīyate? apradarśitahetvarthasya dṛṣṭānte na sādhakatvamiti pratiṣedho nopapadyate-- hetutvāsiddheriti // 13 //
children.translated_text: How so? If an example (<s>udāharaṇa</s>) is adduced for the reason (<s>hetu</s>) stated as 'because of non-establishment in the three times' — since the probative force of the reason's meaning must be shown in the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) — then there is no invalidity of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest. But if <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest are invalid, then even an example, though adduced, will not establish the meaning. Thus this reason, which contradicts all <s>pramāṇa</s>s, is a non-reason — as stated: 'That which contradicts an accepted <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine) is <s>viruddha</s> (contradictory) [NyS 1.2.6].' For its <s>siddhānta</s> is the meaning of the statement, and that meaning of the statement is: '<s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest do not establish any object.' Yet this very employment of the members [of the syllogism] is for the purpose of establishing an object. Now, if no example is adduced, then since the meaning of the reason has not been demonstrated in the example, there is no probative force, and hence refutation is impossible — because the status of being a <s>hetu</s> is not established. // 13 //
NyS_2,1.14: Or, if the validity of that [refutation-statement] is granted, there is no contradiction of all <s>pramāṇa</s>s.

children.text: pratiṣedhalakṣaṇe svavākye teṣāmavayavāśritānāṃ pratyakṣādīnāṃ prāmāṇye 'bhyanujñāyamāne paravākyepyavayavāśritānāṃ prāmāṇyaṃ prasajyate-- aviśeṣāditi. evaṃ ca na sarvāṇi pramāṇāni pratiṣidhyante iti/"vipratiṣedhaḥ"iti vītyayamupasargaḥ saṃpratipattyarthe navyāghāte-- arthābhāvāditi // 14 //
children.translated_text: If the <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest — which are relied upon as members [of the syllogism] — is conceded in one's own statement that is of the nature of a refutation, then the <s>pramāṇa</s>-hood of those relied upon as members in the opponent's statement also follows — because there is no distinguishing difference. Thus, not all <s>pramāṇa</s>s are refuted. The prefix 'vi' in '<s>vipratiṣedha</s>' is used in the sense of agreement (<s>sampratipatti</s>), not in the sense of opposition — because that meaning [of opposition] is absent here. // 14 //
NyS_2,1.15: And [there is] non-refutation in all three times, as in the establishment [of a musical instrument] from sound — because of the establishment of that [<s>pramāṇa</s>].

children.text:
kimarthaṃ punaridamucyate ? pūrvoktanibandhanārtham. yattāvat pūrvoktam-- 'upalabdhihetorupalabdhiviṣayasya cārthasya pūrvāparasahabhāvāniyamād yathādarśanaṃ vibhāgavacanam' iti taditaḥ samuttthānaṃ yathā vijñāyeta|
aniyamadarśī khalvayaṃ krṛṣirniyamena pratiṣedhaṃ pratyācaṣṭe-- traikālyasya cāyuktaḥ pratiṣedha iti|

tatraikāṃ vidhāmudāharati-- śabdādātodyasiddhivaditi, yathā paścāt siddhena śabdane pūrvasiddhamātodyamanumīyate. sādhyaṃ cātodyaṃ sādhanaṃ ca śabdaḥ. antarhite hyātodye svanato 'numānaṃ bhavatīti-- vīṇā vādyate veṇuḥ pūryate iti svanaviśeṣeṇātodyaviśeṣaṃ pratipadyate. tathā pūrvasiddhamupalabdhiviṣayaṃ paścātsiddhenopalabdhihetunā pratipadyate iti. nidarśanārthatvāccāsya śeṣayorvidhayoryathoktamudāharaṇaṃ veditavyamiti|
children.translated_text: In that context, he illustrates one mode: 'as in the establishment of a musical instrument from sound' — just as a musical instrument (<s>ātodya</s>) established previously is inferred from the sound established subsequently. The <s>ātodya</s> is what is to be established (<s>sādhya</s>) and the sound (<s>śabda</s>) is the means of establishing it (<s>sādhana</s>). For when the instrument is hidden, inference arises from the sound — one ascertains the specific instrument from the specific sound: 'a <s>vīṇā</s> is being played,' 'a flute (<s>veṇu</s>) is being blown.' Similarly, one apprehends the previously established object of apprehension through the subsequently established means of apprehension. And since this [example] serves as an illustration, for the remaining two modes, the example should be understood as already stated.

children.text: kasmāt punariha tannocyate pūrvoktamupapādyate ? iti, sarvathā tāvadayamarthaḥ prakāśayitavyaḥ sa iha vā prakāśyeta tatra vā na kaścidviśeṣa iti|
children.translated_text: But why is it not stated here and instead what was said before is being corroborated? In any case, this meaning must be elucidated — whether it is elucidated here or there, there is no difference.

children.text: pramāṇaṃ prameyamiti ca samākhyā samāveśena vartate-- samākhyānimittavaśāt. samākhyānimittaṃ tūpalabdhisādhanaṃ pramāṇam upalabdhiviṣayaśca prameyamiti. yadā copalabdhiviṣayaḥ kvacidupalabdhisādhanaṃ bhavati tadā pramāṇaṃ prameyamiti caiko 'rtho 'bhidhīyate // 15 //
children.translated_text: The designations '<s>pramāṇa</s>' and '<s>prameya</s>' apply through inclusion (<s>samāveśa</s>) — in accordance with the ground for the designation. The ground for the designation is: that which is the means of apprehension is <s>pramāṇa</s>, and that which is the object of apprehension is <s>prameya</s>. And when the object of apprehension in some context becomes the means of apprehension, then a single entity is designated both as '<s>pramāṇa</s>' and as '<s>prameya</s>.' // 15 //

But for what purpose is this stated? It is for the purpose of grounding what was said before. What was previously stated — 'Because there is no fixed rule regarding the prior, posterior, or simultaneous occurrence of the means of apprehension and the object of apprehension, the distinction is stated as it is observed' — this is so that one may understand how this [topic] arises from that. This critic, who perceives the absence of a fixed rule, rejects the refutation on the grounds of a fixed rule — [arguing] that refutation in the three times is unjustified.
For the purpose of illuminating this meaning, the following is stated:
NyS_2,1.16: And [its] <s>prameyatā</s> (status as object of knowledge) is like the validity of a balance (<s>tulā</s>).

children.text: gurutvaparimāṇajñānasādhanaṃ tulā pramāṇam. jñānaviṣayo gurudravyaṃ suvarṇādi prameyam. yadā (ca) suvarṇādinā tulāntaraṃ vyavasthāpyate tadā tulāntarapratipattau suvarṇādi pramāṇaṃ tulāntaraṃ prameyamiti, evamanavayavena tantrārtha uddiṣṭo veditavyaḥ-- ātmā tāvadupalabidhaviṣayatvāt prameye paripaṭhitaḥ upalabdhau ca svātantryāt pramātā, buddhirupalabdhisādhanatvāt pramāṇam. upalabdhiviṣayatvāt prameyam. ubhayābhāvāt pramitiḥ evamarthaviśeṣe samākhyāsamāveśo yojyaḥ|

tathā ca kārakaśabdā nimittavaśāt samāveśena vartante iti. 'vṛkṣastiṣṭhatīti svasthitau svātantryāt kartā, 'vṛkṣaṃ paśyatītidarśanenāptumiṣyamāṇatvāt karma. 'vṛkṣeṇa candramasaṃ jñāpayatīti jñāpakasya sādhakatamatvāt karaṇam. 'vṛkṣāyodakamāsiñcatīti āsicyamānenodakena vṛkṣamabhipraitīti saṃpradānam. 'vṛkṣāt parṇaṃ patatīti "dhruvamapāye 'pādānam" ityapādānam. 'vṛkṣe vayāṃsi santīti "ādhāro 'dhikaraṇam" ityadhikaraṇam, evaṃ ca sati ca dravyamātraṃ kārakaṃ na vā kriyāmātram|
children.translated_text: Likewise, <s>kāraka</s> (syntactic-semantic role) terms apply through inclusion in accordance with the ground [for designation]. [For example:] 'The tree stands' — in standing by itself, due to its independence, it is the <s>kartā</s> (agent). 'He sees the tree' — because it is desired to be reached by the act of seeing, it is the <s>karma</s> (object). 'He indicates the moon by means of the tree' — because of being most effective as an indicator, it is the <s>karaṇa</s> (instrument). 'He pours water for the tree' — because the one pouring water aims at the tree, it is the <s>sampradāna</s> (recipient). 'A leaf falls from the tree' — 'the fixed point in departure is the <s>apādāna</s> (source).' 'Birds are on the tree' — 'the substratum is the <s>adhikaraṇa</s> (locus).' This being so, it is not mere substance that is the <s>kāraka</s>, nor mere action alone.

children.text: kiṃ tarhi ? kriyāsādhanaṃ kriyāviśeṣayuktaṃ kārakam--- yat kriyāsādhanaṃ svatantraḥ sa kartā. na dravyamātraṃ na kriyāmātram, kriyayā vyāptumiṣyamāṇatamaṃ karma. na dravyamātraṃ na kriyāmātram, evaṃ sādhakatamādiṣvapi, evaṃ ca kārakānvākhyānaṃ yathaivopapattita evaṃ lakṣaṇataḥ kārakānvākhyānamapi na dravyamātreṇa na kriyayā vā|
children.translated_text: What then? That which is an instrument of action and is associated with a specific action is a <s>kāraka</s>. That which is an instrument of action and is independent is the <s>kartā</s> (agent) — it is not mere substance nor mere action. That which is most desired to be pervaded by the action is the <s>karma</s> (object) — it is not mere substance nor mere action. The same applies to 'most effective' and the rest. Thus, the explanation of <s>kāraka</s>s, just as it is established through actual usage, so also through definitions — the explanation of <s>kāraka</s>s is not through mere substance nor through action alone.

children.text: kiṃ tarhi ?. kriyāsādhane kriyāviśeṣayukta iti, kāparakaśabdaścāyaṃ pramāṇaṃ prameyamiti sa ca kārakadharmaṃ na hātumarhati. asti bho kārakaśabdānāṃ nimittavaśāt samāveśaḥ pratyakṣādīni ca pramāṇāni-- upalabdhihetutvāt. prameyaṃ ca-- upalabdhiviṣayatvāt, saṃvedyāni pratyakṣādīni pramāṇāni ca-- 'pratyakṣeṇopalabhe anumānenopalabhe upamānenopalabhe āgamenopalabhe. pratyakṣaṃ me jñānam ānumānikaṃ me jñānam aupamānikaṃ me jñānam āgamikaṃ me jñānam' iti viśeṣā gṛhyante, lakṣaṇataśca jñāpyamānāni jñāyante viśeṣeṇa-- 'indriyārthasaṃnikarṣotpannaṃ jñānam' ityevamādinā // 16 //
children.translated_text: What then? It is through being an instrument of action associated with a specific action. And this term '<s>pramāṇa</s>' and '<s>prameya</s>' is also a <s>kāraka</s> term, and it should not abandon the character of <s>kāraka</s>s. Indeed, <s>kāraka</s> terms apply through inclusion based on the ground [for designation]. <s>Pratyakṣa</s> and the rest are <s>pramāṇa</s>s — because of being the causes of apprehension; and they are <s>prameya</s>s — because of being objects of apprehension. <s>Pratyakṣa</s> and the rest are knowable and are also <s>pramāṇa</s>s — [as when one says:] 'I apprehend through <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), I apprehend through <s>anumāna</s> (inference), I apprehend through <s>upamāna</s> (comparison), I apprehend through <s>āgama</s> (verbal testimony). My knowledge is perceptual, my knowledge is inferential, my knowledge is based on comparison, my knowledge is based on testimony' — thus the distinctions are grasped. And through their definitions they are known specifically — as in 'knowledge born from the contact of sense-organ and object' and so forth. // 16 //

A balance (<s>tulā</s>) is a <s>pramāṇa</s> as the means of knowing weight and measure. The heavy substance — gold and so forth — is the <s>prameya</s> as the object of knowledge. When another balance is calibrated by means of gold and so forth, then in the ascertainment of that other balance, the gold etc. is the <s>pramāṇa</s> and the other balance is the <s>prameya</s>. In this way, the meaning of the system should be understood as stated without omission: <s>ātman</s> (self), being an object of apprehension, is listed among the <s>prameya</s>s; and being independent in apprehension, it is the knower (<s>pramātā</s>). <s>Buddhi</s> (cognition), being the means of apprehension, is a <s>pramāṇa</s>; being an object of apprehension, it is a <s>prameya</s>. In the absence of both [means and object aspects], it is a <s>pramiti</s> (resultant cognition). Thus, the inclusion of designations should be applied to specific objects in this manner.

children.text: seyamupalabdhiḥ pratyakṣādiviṣayā kiṃ pramāṇāntarataḥ ? athāntareṇa pramāṇam = asādhanā ? iti, kaścātra viśeṣaḥ ?,
children.translated_text: Now, is this apprehension, which has <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest as its objects, [established] through another <s>pramāṇa</s>? Or is it without a <s>pramāṇa</s>, that is, without a means of establishment? And what difference does it make?
NyS_2,1.17: Because of establishment through a <s>pramāṇa</s>, there would be the absurd consequence of the <s>pramāṇa</s>s being established by another <s>pramāṇa</s>.

children.text: yadi pratyakṣādīni pramāṇenopalabhyante ? yena pramāṇenopalabhyante tat pramāṇāntaramastīni pramāṇāntarasadbhāvaḥ prasajyate ityanavasthāmāha-- tasyāpyanyena tasyāpyanyeneti, na cānavasthā śakyānujñātum-- anupapatteriti // 17 //
children.translated_text: If <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest are apprehended by a <s>pramāṇa</s>, then there must be another <s>pramāṇa</s> by which they are apprehended — thus the existence of another <s>pramāṇa</s> absurdly follows. This states an infinite regress (<s>anavasthā</s>): that too by yet another, and that too by yet another. And the infinite regress cannot be accepted — because it is untenable. // 17 //

NyS_2,1.18: Or, if that [regress] ceases, then just as the <s>pramāṇa</s>s are established [without further <s>pramāṇa</s>s], so too would the <s>prameya</s>s be established [without <s>pramāṇa</s>s].

children.text: yadi pratyakṣādyupalabdhau pramāṇāntaraṃ nivartate ? ātmetyupalabdhāvapi pramāṇāntaraṃ nivartsyati-- aviśeṣāt. evaṃ ca sarvapramāṇavilopa iti // 18 //
children.translated_text: If another <s>pramāṇa</s> is dispensed with in the apprehension of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest, then another <s>pramāṇa</s> would also be dispensed with in the apprehension of <s>ātman</s> (self) and the rest — because there is no distinguishing difference. And thus there would be the loss of all <s>pramāṇa</s>s. // 18 //
Therefore he says:
NyS_2,1.19: No, because of the establishment of that [<s>pramāṇa</s>], as in the establishment of the illumination of a lamp.

children.text: yathā pradīpaprakāśaḥ pratyakṣāṅgatvād dṛśyadarśane pramāṇaṃ sa ca pratyakṣāntareṇa

cakṣuṣaḥ saṃnikarṣeṇa gṛhyate, pradīpabhāvābhāvayordarśanasya tathābhāvād darśanaheturanumīyate. 'tamasi pradīpamupādadīthāḥ' ityāptopadeśenāpi pratipadyate, evaṃ pratyakṣādīnāṃ yathādarśanaṃ pratyakṣādibhirevopasabdhiḥ|
children.translated_text: through the contact of the eye — and because seeing is present or absent depending on the presence or absence of the lamp, [the lamp] is inferred as the cause of seeing. Through the instruction of a trustworthy person (<s>āpta</s>) also one understands: 'Take up a lamp in the darkness.' Similarly, the apprehension of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest is through <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest themselves, as is observed.

children.text: indriyāṇi tāvat svaviṣayagrahaṇenaivānumīyante. arthāḥ pratyakṣato gṛhyante. indriyārthasaṃnikarṣāstvāvaraṇena liṅgenānumīyante. indriyārthasaṃnikarṣotpannaṃ jñānamātmamanasoḥ saṃyogaviśeṣādātmasamavāyācca sukhādivad gṛhyate. evaṃ pramāṇaviśeṣo vibhajya vacanīyaḥ|
children.translated_text: The sense organs, to begin with, are inferred through the very grasping of their own objects. Objects are grasped through <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception). The contacts of sense-organ and object are inferred through the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of obstruction. The knowledge born from the contact of sense-organ and object is grasped — like pleasure and the like — through a particular conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> (mind), and through inherence (<s>samavāya</s>) in <s>ātman</s>. Thus, the specific <s>pramāṇa</s>s should be stated by distinguishing them in this way.

children.text: yathā ca dṛśyaḥ san pradīpaprakāśo dṛśyāntarāṇāṃ darśanaheturiti dṛśyadarśanavyavasthāṃ labhate evaṃ prameyaṃ sat kiñcidarthajātamupalabdhihetutvāt pramāṇaprameyavyavasthāṃ labhate, seyaṃ pratayakṣādibhireva pratyakṣādīnāṃ yathādarśanamupalabdhirna pramāṇāntarato na ca pramāṇamanteraṇa niḥsādhaneti //
children.translated_text: And just as the light of a lamp, while being visible itself, is the cause of seeing other visible things — and thus obtains the status of being both visible and the cause of seeing — so too, a certain class of objects, while being <s>prameya</s> (knowable), obtains the status of both <s>pramāṇa</s> and <s>prameya</s> because of being the cause of apprehension. This apprehension of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest is through <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest themselves as observed — it is neither from another <s>pramāṇa</s>, nor without a means of establishment.

Just as the light of a lamp, being a component of <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), is a <s>pramāṇa</s> for seeing what is visible, and that [light] is grasped through another instance of <s>pratyakṣa</s>,

children.text:
tanaiva tasyāgrahaṇamiti cet ? na-- arthabhedasya lakṣaṇasāmānyāt5|
pratyakṣādīnāṃ pratyakṣādibhireva grahaṇamityayuktam-- anyena hyanyasya grahaṇaṃ dṛṣṭamiti, na-- arthabhedasya lakṣaṇasāmānyātupratyakṣalakṣaṇenānekorthaḥ saṃgṛhītastatra kena cit kasyacid grahaṇamityadoṣaḥ, evamanumānādiṣvapīti, yathoddhṛtenodakenāśayasthasya grahaṇamiti //
children.translated_text: [Objection:] But then the same thing cannot grasp itself! No — because though the objects differ, the definition is general. The claim that <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest are grasped only by <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest themselves is objected to on the grounds that grasping of one thing by another is what is observed. The reply is: No [fault], because although the objects differ, the definition is general — by the definition of <s>pratyakṣa</s>, multiple objects are comprehended; among them, any one [instance of <s>pratyakṣa</s>] grasps any other, so there is no fault. The same applies to <s>anumāna</s> (inference) and the rest. It is like water drawn up [from a well] being used to ascertain [the level of] water remaining in the reservoir.

children.text: 'ahaṃ sukhī ahaṃ duḥkhī ca' iti tenaiva jñātrā tasyaiva grahaṇaṃ dṛśyate."
children.translated_text: 'I am happy, I am suffering' — here the very same knower is seen to grasp itself.
'The non-arising of simultaneous cognitions is the inferential mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of <s>manas</s> (mind).'

children.text: iti ca tenaiva manasā tasyaivānumānaṃ dṛśyate, jñāturjñeyasya cābhedo grahaṇasya grāhyasya cābheda iti //
children.translated_text: And thus the very same <s>manas</s> is seen to be inferred by itself. [One might object:] there is no difference between the knower and the known, or between the grasping and what is grasped.
And because the knower and the mind are seen [to grasp themselves].
[Objection:] But there is a difference in the ground (<s>nimitta</s>) here! [Reply:] It is the same [situation].

children.text: na nimittāntareṇa vinā jñātātmānaṃ jānīte. na ca nimittāntareṇa vinā manasā mano gṛhyate iti, samānametat |
children.translated_text: The knower does not know itself without a different ground, and the mind is not grasped by itself without a different ground — this is the same [as our case].

children.text: pratyakṣādibhiḥ pratyakṣādīnāṃ grahaṇam ityatrāpyarthabhedo na gṛhyate iti //
children.translated_text: Even in the grasping of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest by <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest, the difference of objects is not [to be denied] — [the difference is indeed present].

children.text:
pratyakṣādīnāṃ cāviṣayasyānupapatteḥ8|
yadi syāt kiñcidarthajātaṃ pratyakṣādīnāmaviṣayaḥ yat pratyakṣādibhirna śakyaṃ grahītuṃ tasya grahaṇāya pramāṇāntaramupādīyeta tattu na śakyaṃ kenacidupapādayatumiti, pratayakṣādīnāṃ yathādarśanamevedaṃ saccāsacca sarvaṃ viṣaya iti //
children.translated_text: And because it is impossible for <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest to have no object: If there were some class of objects that were not objects of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest — which could not be grasped by <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest — then another <s>pramāṇa</s> would need to be posited for grasping it. But no one can establish such [a class of objects]. Therefore, everything — both existent and non-existent — is indeed the object of <s>pratyakṣa</s> and the rest, as observed.

children.text: viśeṣahetumantareṇa sādhyasādhanāyopādadate yathā pradīpaprakāśaḥ pradīpāntaraprakāśamantareṇa gṛhyate tathā pramāṇāni pramāṇāntaramantareṇa gṛhyante iti. sa cāyam--- kva cinnivṛttidarśanādanivṛttidarśanācca kva cidanekāntaḥ9|
children.translated_text: Without a specific reason, they adduce [the example] for proving what is to be proved: just as the light of a lamp is grasped without the light of another lamp, so too <s>pramāṇa</s>s are grasped without another <s>pramāṇa</s>. But this is inconclusive (<s>anekānta</s>) — because in some cases cessation is observed, and in other cases non-cessation is observed.

children.text: yathāyaṃ prasaṅgo nivṛttidarśanāt pramāṇasādhanāyopādīyate evaṃ prameyasādhanāyāpyupādeyaḥ-- aviśeṣahetutvāt, yathā sthālyādirūpagrahaṇe pradīpaprakāśaḥ prameyasādhanāyopādīyate evaṃ pramāṇa sādhanāyāpyupādeyaḥ-- viśeṣahetvabhāvāt, soyaṃ viśeṣahetuparigrahamantareṇa dṛṣṭānta ekasmin pakṣe upādeyo na pratipakṣe ityanekāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as this [logical] consequence is employed for the purpose of establishing the <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge) from the observation of [its] reversal, so too it should be employed for establishing the <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge) — because the reason is not specific. Just as the light of a lamp is employed for establishing the <s>prameya</s> in the perception of color of a pot and the like, so too it should be employed for establishing the <s>pramāṇa</s> — because there is no specific reason [for distinguishing the two cases]. Thus, without accepting a specific reason, this example is inconclusive (<s>anekānta</s>) — employable in one thesis but not in the counter-thesis.
And being an example in only one thesis is inconclusive — because there is no specific reason.
But some accept the example as unsubstantiated by the reason.

children.text: viśeṣahetuparigṛhītastu dṛṣṭānta ekasmin pakṣe upasaṃhiyamāṇo na śakyo 'nanujñātum evaṃ ca sati 'anekāntaḥ' ityayaṃ pratiṣedho na bhavati|
children.translated_text: But when an example supported by a specific reason is applied to one thesis, it cannot be left unapproved; and this being so, the refutation 'it is inconclusive' does not hold.

children.text: pratyakṣādīnāṃ pratyakṣādibhirupalabdhāv anavastheticet ? na-- saṃvidviṣaya- nimittānāmupalabdhyā vyavahāropapa11tteḥ|
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If the apprehension of perception and the rest [requires] perception and the rest, there would be infinite regress? [Reply:] No — because practical activity is justified by the apprehension of the objects, causes, and conditions of awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>).

children.text: pratyakṣeṇārthamupalabhe anumānenārthamupalabhe upamānenārthamupalabhe āgamenārthamupalabhe iti. pratyakṣaṃ me jñānam ānumānikaṃ me jñānam aupamānikaṃ me jñānam āgamikaṃ me jñānamiti saṃvidviṣayaṃ saṃvinnimittaṃ copalabhamānasya dharmārthasukhāpavargaprayojanaḥ tatpratyanīkaparivarjanaprayojananaśca vyavahāra upapadyate soyaṃ tāvatyaiva nirvartate. na cāsti vyavahārāntaramanavasthāsādhanīyaṃ yena prayukto 'navasthāmupādadīteti // 19 //
children.translated_text: When an object is apprehended through perception, when an object is apprehended through inference, when an object is apprehended through analogy, when an object is apprehended through testimony — 'my knowledge is perceptual,' 'my knowledge is inferential,' 'my knowledge is analogical,' 'my knowledge is testimonial' — for one who apprehends the object of awareness and the condition of awareness, practical activity whose purpose is <s>dharma</s> (merit), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>sukha</s> (pleasure), and <s>apavarga</s> (liberation), as well as the avoidance of their opposites, is justified; and this [justification] is accomplished with just this much. And there is no further practical activity that would need to be established [by an infinite regress] and for the sake of which one would have to take up an infinite regress. // 19 //
When a specific reason is accepted, the counter-argument (<s>upasaṃhāra</s>) cannot be rejected, so there is no refutation.

children.text: sāmānyena pramāṇāni parīkṣya viśeṣeṇa parīkṣyante, tatra---
children.translated_text: Having examined the <s>pramāṇas</s> in general, they are now examined in particular. In that regard —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.20: [Objection:] The definition of perception is unjustifiable because of the incomplete statement. //

children.text: ātmamanaḥsaṃnikarṣo hi kāraṇāntaraṃ noktamiti, na cāsaṃyukte dravye saṃyogajanyasya guṇasyotpattiriti. jñānotpattidarśanādātmamanaḥsaṃnikarṣaḥ kāraṇam|
manaḥsaṃnikarṣānapekṣasya cendrinayārthasaṃnikarṣasya jñānakāraṇatve yugapadutpadyeran buddhaya iti manaḥsaṃnikarṣopi kāraṇam // 20 //
children.translated_text: And if the contact of sense-organ and object, independent of the conjunction with <s>manas</s>, were the cause of cognition, then cognitions would arise simultaneously — therefore the conjunction with <s>manas</s> is also a cause. // 20 //

For the conjunction of the <s>ātman</s> (self) and the <s>manas</s> (mind), which is an additional cause, has not been stated; and a quality born of conjunction does not arise in a substance not conjoined. From the observation of the arising of cognition, the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> is a cause.
This <s>sūtra</s> has already been commented upon earlier —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.21: In the absence of the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s>, perception does not arise. //

children.text: ātmamanasoḥ saṃnikarṣābhāve notpadyate pratyakṣam indriyārthasaṃnikarṣābhāvavaditi, sati cendriyārthasaṃnikarṣe jñānotpattidarśanāt kāraṇabhāvaṃ bruvate // 21 //
children.translated_text: In the absence of the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s>, perception does not arise — just as [it does not arise] in the absence of the contact of sense-organ and object. And since the arising of cognition is observed when there is contact of sense-organ and object, they assert [its] causal status. // 21 //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.22: [Objection:] The same consequence applies to direction, place, time, and space (<s>ākāśa</s>). //

children.text: digādiṣu satsu jñānabhāvāt tānyapi kāraṇānīti. akāraṇabhāvepi jñānotpatterdigādisaṃnidheravarjanīyatvāt |
yadāpyakāraṇaṃ digādīni jñānotpattau tadāpi satsu digādiṣu jñānena bhavitavyaṃ na hi digādīnāṃ saṃnidhiḥ śakyaḥ parivarjayitumiti|
children.translated_text: Even when direction and the rest are not causes of the arising of cognition, cognition must occur when direction and the rest are present, for the presence of direction and the rest cannot be eliminated.

children.text: tatra kāraṇabhāve hetuvacanam-- etasmād hetordigādīni jñānakāraṇānīti|
children.translated_text: There, the statement of reason for their being causes: 'Direction and the rest are causes of cognition because of this reason.'
Then the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> should be counted [as an additional cause]. // 22 //

[Objection:] Since cognition occurs when direction and the rest are present, they too are causes. [Reply:] Even without being causes, the presence of direction and the rest cannot be avoided when cognition arises.
To this, the following is said —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.23: Because cognition is a mark (<s>liṅga</s>) of the <s>ātman</s>, there is no exclusion [of the <s>ātman</s>-<s>manas</s> conjunction]. //

children.text: jñānamātmaliṅgam-- tadguṇatavāt. na cāsaṃyukte dravye saṃyogajasya guṇasyotpattirastīti // 23 //
children.translated_text: Cognition is a mark of the <s>ātman</s> — because it is a quality of [the <s>ātman</s>]. And a quality born of conjunction does not arise in a substance not conjoined. // 23 //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.24: And because of [cognition's] non-simultaneity being a mark of [the <s>manas</s>], there is no [exclusion] of the <s>manas</s> [either]. //
'No exclusion' — this continues [from the previous <s>sūtra</s>].
'The non-simultaneous arising of cognitions is the inferential mark of the <s>manas</s>' [NyS 1.1.16]
— when this is stated, it is indeed established that the contact of sense-organ and object, as dependent on the conjunction with <s>manas</s>, is the cause of cognition. // 24 //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.25: Because the contact of sense-organ and object is the specific cause of perception, it is stated with its own word. //

children.text: pratyakṣānumānopamānaśabdānāṃ nimittamātmamanaḥsaṃnikarṣaḥ pratyakṣasyaivendriyārthasaṃnikarṣa ity asamāno 'samānatvāt tasya grahaṇam // 25 //
children.translated_text: The conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> is the cause of perception, inference, analogy, and verbal testimony [alike]; only the contact of sense-organ and object is specific to perception — because it is not common [to the others], it is mentioned [in the definition]. // 25 //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.26: And because the contact of sense-organ and object is the cause [of cognition] even for those who are asleep and those whose mind is absorbed [elsewhere]. //

children.text: indriyārthasaṃnikarṣasya grahaṇaṃ nātmamanasoḥ saṃnikarṣasyeti, ekadā khalvayaṃ prabodhakālaṃ praṇidhāya suptaḥ praṇidhānavaśāt prabudhyate, yadā tu tīvrau dhvanisparśauṃ prabodhakāraṇaṃ bhavatastadāprasuptasyendriyārthasaṃnikarṣanimittaṃ prabodhajñānamutpadyate tatra na jñāturmanasaś ca saṃnikarṣasya prādhānyaṃ bhavati, kiṃ tarhi ?. indriyārthayoḥ saṃnikarṣasya--nahyatmā jijñāsamānaḥ prayatnena manastadā prerayatīti|
children.translated_text: The mention of the contact of sense-organ and object [in the definition], not of the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> — [is justified as follows:] At some time, a person falls asleep having resolved to wake at a [certain] time; he wakes up due to the force of that resolution. But when intense sounds and touches become the cause of waking, then for the one not [consciously] sleeping, the waking cognition arises from the contact of sense-organ and object; there, the primacy does not belong to the conjunction of the knower and mind. Rather, [it belongs] to the contact of sense-organ and object — for the self, not being desirous of knowing, does not then impel the mind by effort.

children.text: ekadā khalvayaṃ viṣāyāntarāvyāsaktamanāḥ saṃkalpavaśād viṣayāntaraṃ jijñāsamānaḥ prayatnapreritena manasā indriyaṃ saṃyojya yad viṣayāntaraṃ jānīte, yadā tu khalvasya niḥsaṃkalpasya nirjijñāsasya ca vyāsaktamanaso bāhyaviṣayopanipātanād jñānamutpadyate tadendriyārthasaṃnikarṣasya prādhānyam-- na hyatrāsau jijñāsamānaḥ prayatnena manaḥ prerayatīti|
children.translated_text: At another time, a person whose mind is absorbed in one object, desiring to know another object through the force of intention, joins the mind impelled by effort with a sense-organ and thereby knows the other object. But when, for one who has no intention and no desire to know, whose mind is absorbed, cognition arises from the impact of an external object — then the primacy belongs to the contact of sense-organ and object, for here too, not being desirous of knowing, he does not impel the mind by effort.

Therefore, the contact of sense-organ and object should be mentioned because of its primacy; the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> should not [be mentioned] because of its subsidiary status. // 26 //
And there is another reason for [its] primacy —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.27: And specific cognitions are designated by those [sense-organs and objects]. //
By those —

children.text: indriyairarthaiśca vyapadiśyante jñānaviśeṣāḥ, katham ?. 'ghrāṇena jighrati' 'cakṣuṣā paśyati' 'rasanayā rasayatīti. 'ghrāṇavijñānaṃ cakṣurvijñānaṃ rasanavijñānam' 'gandhavijñānaṃ rūpavijñānaṃ rasavijñānam' iti ca, indriyaviṣayaviśeṣācca pañcadhābuddhirbhavati ataḥ prādhanyamindriyārthasaṃnikarṣasyeti // 27 //
children.translated_text: specific cognitions are designated by [their respective] sense-organs and objects. How? 'He smells with the nose,' 'he sees with the eye,' 'he tastes with the tongue.' [And:] 'Olfactory cognition, visual cognition, gustatory cognition'; 'cognition of odor, cognition of color, cognition of taste.' And because of the specificity of sense-organ and object, cognition is fivefold. Therefore, the contact of sense-organ and object has primacy. // 27 //

children.text: yaduktam-- 'indriyārthasaṃnikarṣagrahaṇaṃ kāryaṃ nātmamanasoḥ saṃnikarṣasyeti. kasyāt ?. suptavyāsaktamanasāmindriyārthayoḥ saṃnikarṣasya jñānanimittatvāt' iti. soyam---
children.translated_text: [Regarding] what was said: 'The contact of sense-organ and object should be mentioned, not the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s>. Why? Because the contact of sense-organ and object is the cause of cognition for those who are asleep and those whose mind is absorbed' — this [argument] is —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.28: [Objection:] It is a non-reason because of self-contradiction (<s>vyāghāta</s>). //

children.text: yadi tāvat kvacidātmamanasoḥ sanikarṣasya jñānakāraṇatvaṃ neṣyate ? tadā
children.translated_text: If the causal status of the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> for cognition is denied in any case whatsoever, then
'the non-simultaneous arising of cognitions is the inferential mark of the <s>manas</s>' [NyS 1.1.16]

children.text: iti vyāhanyeta. nedānīṃ manasaḥ saṃnikarṣamindriyārthasaṃnikarṣo 'pekṣate. manaḥsaṃyogānapekṣāyāṃ ca yugapajjñānotpattiprasaṅgaḥ|
children.translated_text: — this would be contradicted. [For] the contact of sense-organ and object would [then] not depend on the conjunction with <s>manas</s>. And if the conjunction with <s>manas</s> is not required, the simultaneous arising of cognitions would follow.

children.text: atha mā bhūd vyāghāta iti sarvavijñānānāmātmamanasoḥ saṃnikarṣaḥ kāraṇamiṣyate ? tadavasthamevedaṃ bhavati-- 'jñānakāraṇatvādātmamanasoḥ saṃnikarṣasya grahaṇaṃ kāryam' iti // 28 //
children.translated_text: [Reply:] Or, lest there be contradiction, if the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> is accepted as a cause of all cognitions, then the situation remains the same — 'the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> should be mentioned because of its being a cause of cognition.' // 28 //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.29: [Reply:] No, because of the preponderance of the specific object. //

children.text: nāsti vyāghātaḥ- na hyātmamanaḥsaṃnikarṣasya jñānakāraṇatvaṃ vyabhicarati. indriyārthasaṃnikarṣasya prādhānyamupādīyate-- arthaviśeṣaprābalyāddhi suptavyāsaktamanasāṃ jñānotpattirekadā bhavati|
children.translated_text: There is no contradiction — for the causal status of the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> for cognition is not deviated from. The primacy of the contact of sense-organ and object is what is being stated — for it is due to the preponderance of a specific object that cognition arises at certain times for those who are asleep and those whose mind is absorbed.

children.text: arthaviśeṣaḥ kaścidevendriyārthastasya prābalyaṃ tīvratāpaṭute, taccārthaviśeṣaprābalyāmindriyārthasaṃnikarṣaviṣayaṃ nātmamanasoḥ saṃnikarṣaviṣayaṃ tasmādindriyārthasaṃnikarṣaḥ pradhānamiti|
children.translated_text: A specific object is a certain sense-object; its preponderance is its intensity and acuteness; and that preponderance of the specific object pertains to the domain of the contact of sense-organ and object, not to the domain of the conjunction of <s>ātman</s> and <s>manas</s> — therefore the contact of sense-organ and object has primacy.

children.text: asati praṇidhāne saṃkalpe cāsati suptavyāsaktamanasāṃ yad indriyārthasaṃnikarṣādutpadyate jñānaṃ tatra manaḥsaṃyogopi kāraṇamiti manasi kriyākāraṇaṃ vācyamiti, yathaiva jñātuḥ khalvayamicchājanitaḥ prayatno manasaḥ preraka ātmaguṇa evamātmani guṇāntaraṃ sarvasya sādhakaṃ pravṛttidoṣajanitamasti yena preritaṃ mana indriyeṇa saṃbadhyate. tena hy apreryamāṇe manasi saṃyogābhāvāt jñānātutpattau sarvārthatāsya nivartate. eṣitavyaṃ cāsaya guṇāntarasya dravyaguṇakarmakārakatvam anyathā hi caturvidhānāmaṇūnāṃ bhūtasūkṣmāṇāṃ manasāṃ ca tato 'nyasya kriyāhetorasaṃbhavāt śarīrendriyaviṣayāṇāmanutpattiprasaṅgaḥ // 29 //
children.translated_text: In the absence of [prior] resolution and intention, the cognition that arises for those who are asleep and those whose mind is absorbed from the contact of sense-organ and object — therein the conjunction with <s>manas</s> is also a cause; thus, the efficient cause (<s>kriyākāraṇa</s>) for the mind must be stated. Just as the knower's effort born of desire is a quality of the <s>ātman</s> that impels the mind, so too there is another quality of the <s>ātman</s>, born of activity and faults, that accomplishes all things, by which the mind when impelled conjoins with the sense-organ. For when the mind is not impelled, from the absence of conjunction, cognition does not arise, and its omnipresence [as a cause] would cease. And one should seek the nature of this other quality as being a producer of substance, quality, and action — for otherwise, since there is no other cause of activity for the four types of atoms, the subtle elements (<s>bhūtasūkṣma</s>), and the minds, there would be the undesirable consequence of the non-arising of bodies, sense-organs, and objects. // 29 //
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.30: [Objection:] Perception is [really] inference, because apprehension is from the grasping of one part. //

children.text:
yadidamindriyārthasaṃnikarṣādutpadyate jñānam 'vṛkṣaḥ' iti etat kila pratyakṣaṃ tatkhalvanumānameva, kasmāt ?. ekadeśagrahaṇād vṛkṣasyopalabdheḥ |
arvāgbhāgamayaṃ gṛhītvā vṛkṣamupalabhate na caikadeśo vṛkṣaḥ, tatra yathā dhūmaṃ gṛhītvā vahnimanuminoti tādṛgeva tad bhavati|
kiṃ punargṛhyamāṇādekadeśād arthāntaramanumeyaṃ manyase ?, avayavasamūhapakṣe avayavāntarāṇi dravyotpattipakṣe tāni cāvayavī ceti|
avayavasamūhapakṣe tāvadekadeśagrahaṇād vṛkṣabuddherabhāvaḥ-- na hy agṛhyamāṇamekadeśāntaraṃ vṛkṣo gṛhyamāṇaikadeśavaditi|
children.translated_text: On the theory of an aggregate of parts, there would be no cognition of a tree from the grasping of one part — for another part not being grasped is not [cognized] like the part being grasped as being a tree.

children.text: atha ekadeśagrahaṇādekadeśāntarānumāne samudāyapratisaṃdhānāt tatra vṛkṣabuddhiḥ ?, na tarhi vṛkṣabuddhiranumānamevaṃ sati bhavitumarhatīti|
children.translated_text: [Objection:] From the grasping of one part, by inferring the other parts, from the synthesis of the aggregate, the cognition of a tree [arises]? [Reply:] Then the cognition of a tree, this being so, would deserve to be inference itself.

children.text: dravyāntarotpattipakṣe nāvayavy anumeyaḥ-- asyaikadeśasaṃbaddhasyāgrahaṇād grahaṇe cāviśeṣādanamumeyatvābhāvaḥ, tasmād vṛkṣabuddhiranumānaṃ na bhavati // 30 //
children.translated_text: On the theory of the production of a different substance [i.e., a whole from parts], the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) is not to be inferred — because of the non-grasping of [something] connected to [only] one part, and because if [the whole] were grasped there would be no difference, and hence no inferability. Therefore, the cognition of a tree is not inference. // 30 //

The cognition that arises from the contact of sense-organ and object — 'it is a tree' — this, it is claimed, is perception; but that is indeed only inference. Why? Because the apprehension of the tree is from the grasping of one part. Having grasped the front part, one apprehends the tree — but a part is not the tree. Therefore, just as one infers fire from grasping smoke, exactly so is this [case]. What do you think is to be inferred as something other than the part being grasped? On the theory that [a whole is] an aggregate of parts — the other parts; on the theory that [a whole is] a substance produced [from parts] — both the other parts and the whole (<s>avayavin</s>).
Relying on the grasping of one part, the inferentiality of perception is being argued. And that [argument] —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.31: [Reply:] No, because apprehension is through perception itself to the full extent. //

children.text: yat tadekadeśagrahaṇamāśrīyate pratyakṣeṇāsāvupalambhaḥ, na copalambho nirviṣayosti yāvaccārthajātaṃ tasya viṣayastāvadabhyanujñāyamānaṃ pratyakṣavyavasthāpakaṃ bhavati|
children.translated_text: That grasping of one part which is relied upon — that apprehension is through perception.
