And apprehension is not without an object; and to the extent that the totality of objects is its domain, to that extent, when conceded, it serves to establish [the cognition as] perception.
What, then, is that totality of objects other [than the part]? The whole (<s>avayavin</s>) or the aggregate.

children.text: na caivadeśagrahaṇam anumānaṃ bhāvayituṃ śakyam-- hetvabhāvāditi //
children.translated_text: And the grasping of one part cannot be made into inference — because of the absence of a [valid] reason.
Perception is not inference. Why? Because the apprehension is through perception itself.

children.text: pratyakṣapūrvakamanumānam-- saṃbaddhāvagnidhūmau pratyakṣato dṛṣṭavato dhūmapratyakṣadarśanād agnāvanumānaṃ bhavati. yacca saṃbaddhayorliṅgaliṅganoḥ pratyakṣaṃ yacca liṅmātrapratyakṣagrahaṇaṃ naitadantareṇānumānasya pravṛttirasti na tvetadanumānam-- indriyārthasaṃnikarṣajatvāt. na cānumeyasyendriyeṇa saṃnikarṣādanumānaṃ bhavati, soyaṃ pratkṣānumānayorlakṣaṇabhedo mahānāśrayitavya iti // 31 //
children.translated_text: Inference is preceded by perception — for one who has perceived through direct perception fire and smoke in connection, from the direct perception of smoke [alone], an inference of fire arises. The perception of the connected mark (<s>liṅga</s>) and the marked (<s>liṅgin</s>), and the perceptual apprehension of the mark alone — without these, there is no functioning of inference; yet this [perception] is not itself inference, because it arises from the contact of sense-organ and object. And inference does not arise from the contact of the sense-organ with the inferred [object]. This great distinction in the defining characteristics of perception and inference should be relied upon. //31//
And for another reason too, there is no consequence of perception being inference — because [inference] is preceded by [perception].
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.32: And the perception of a part [alone] is not [sufficient], because the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) exists.

children.text: na caikadeśopalabdhimātram, kiṃ tarhi ?. ekadeśopalabdhiḥ tatsahacaritāvayavyupalabdhiśca, kasmāt ?. avayavisadbhāvāt |
children.translated_text: Not merely the perception of a part; rather, the perception of a part and the perception of the whole accompanying it. Why? Because the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) exists.

For this whole is distinct from its parts. Since [the whole], being in the location of its parts, is such that perception of it is warranted by its causes, its non-perception when a part is perceived is untenable.

children.text:
akṛtsnagrahaṇāditicet ? na-- kāraṇato 'nyasyaikadeśasyābhāvāt13|
na cāvayavāḥ kṛtsnā gṛhyante-- avayavairevāvayavāntaravyavadhānāt. nāvayavī kṛtsno gṛhyate iti-- nāyaṃ gṛhyamāṇeṣvavayaveṣu parisamāpta iti, seyamekadeśopalabdhiranivṛttaiveti|
kṛtsnamiti vai khalvaśeṣatayāṃ satyāṃ bhavati. akṛtsnamiti śeṣe sati. taccaitad avayaveṣu bahuṣvasti-- avyavadhāne grahaṇād vyavadhāne cāgrahaṇāditi|
aṅgaṃ tu bhavān pṛṣṭo vyācaṣṭām-- gṛhyamāṇasyāvayavinaḥ kimagṛhītaṃ manyase ? yenaikadeśopalabdhiḥ syāditi, na hyasya kāraṇebhyo 'nye ekadeśā bhavantīti, tatrāvayavavṛttaṃ nopapadyate iti|
idaṃ tasya vṛttam-- yeṣāmindriyasaṃnikarṣād grahaṇamavayavānāṃ taiḥ saha gṛhyateyeṣāmavayavānāṃ vyavadhānādagrahaṇaṃ taiḥ saha na gṛhyate|

children.translated_text: And this does not create a difference [in the whole's existence].

children.text: samudāyopyaśeṣatā vā samudāyo vṛkṣaḥ syāt ? tatprāptirvā ? ubhayathā grahaṇābhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Would the aggregate — the exhaustive collection — be the tree? Or would it be the conjunction [of parts]? Either way, there is absence of apprehension.

children.text: mūlaskandhaśākhāpalāśādīnāmaśeṣatā vā samudāyo vṛkṣa iti syāt ? prāptirvā samudānayināmiti ? ubhayathā (api) samudāyabhūtasya vṛkṣasya grahaṇaṃ nopapadyate iti |
children.translated_text: Would the tree be the aggregate — the exhaustive collection — of root, trunk, branches, leaves, and the rest? Or the conjunction of those that come together? Either way, the apprehension of the tree as an aggregate is untenable.

children.text: avayavaistāvadavayavāntarasya vyavadhānādaśeṣagrahaṇaṃ nopapadyate prāptigrahaṇamapi nopapadyate-- prāptimatāmagrahaṇāt, seyamekadeśagrahaṇasahacaritā vṛkṣabuddhirdravyāntarotpattau kalpate na samudāyamātre iti // 32 //
children.translated_text: First, the exhaustive apprehension through parts is untenable because other parts intervene. The apprehension through conjunction is also untenable — because those possessing the conjunction are not apprehended. Thus, this cognition of a tree, accompanied by the perception of a part, is suitable [only] if a different substance is produced, not for a mere aggregate. //32//

[Objection:] Because the whole is not grasped entirely? No — because there is no other part beyond the causes. The parts themselves are not grasped entirely — because other parts intervene between [perceived] parts. The whole is not grasped entirely — meaning it is not exhausted in the perceived parts. This is just the perception of a part, which has not ceased. 'Entire' (<s>kṛtsna</s>) applies when there is no remainder; 'not entire' (<s>akṛtsna</s>) when there is a remainder. And this applies to many of the parts — because of grasping where there is no obstruction and non-grasping where there is obstruction. But the gentleman, when asked, should explain — what does he consider as ungrasped in the whole that is being grasped? By which there would be 'perception of a part,' for this [whole] has no parts other than its causes. Hence, the behavior [described] regarding the parts is untenable. This is its behavior: together with those parts whose apprehension [results] from sense-organ contact, it is grasped; together with those parts whose non-apprehension [results] from obstruction, it is not grasped.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.33: Because [the existence of] the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) is what is to be proved, there is doubt.
'Because the whole exists' —
this is a non-valid reason, because [the whole's existence] is what is to be proved.

children.text: sādhyaṃ tāvadetat-- kāraṇebhyo dravyāntaramutpadyate iti. anupapāditametat, evaṃ ca sati vipratipattimātraṃ bhavati vipratipatteścāvayavini saṃśaya iti // 33 //
children.translated_text: This indeed is what needs to be proved — that a different substance arises from [its] causes. This has not been established, and this being so, there is merely a disagreement; and from the disagreement, doubt about the whole. //33//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.34: [If the whole does not exist,] the apprehension of everything [would be impossible], because the whole is not established.
If the whole does not exist? The apprehension of everything is untenable.
What is that 'everything'? Substance, quality, action, universal, particular, and inherence.

children.text: kathaṃ kṛtvā ?, paramāṇusamavasthānaṃ tāvad darśanaviṣayo na bhavati-- atīndriyatvādaṇūnām. dravyāntaraṃ cāvayavibhūtaṃ darśanaviṣayo nāsti. darśanaviṣayāśceme dravyādayo gṛhyante te niradhiṣṭhānā na gṛhyeranu gṛhyante tu-- 'kumbhoyaṃ śyāma eko mahān saṃyuktaḥ spandate asti mṛnmayaśca' iti. santi ceme guṇādayo dharmā iti. tena sarvasya grahaṇāt paśyāmo 'sti dravyāntarabhūto 'vayavīti // 34 //
children.translated_text: How so? First, the configuration of atoms is not an object of visual perception — because atoms are supersensible. And a different substance, being a whole, is not an object of visual perception [on the opponent's view]. These objects of visual perception — substance and the rest — are apprehended; they would not be apprehended without a substrate, yet they are apprehended: 'This is a pot, dark-colored, one, large, conjoined, moving, existing, and made of clay.' And there exist these properties — qualities and the rest. Therefore, from the apprehension of everything, we see that the whole exists as a different substance. //34//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.35: And because of the justification of holding and pulling.

children.text: avayavyarthāntarabhūta iti, saṃgrahakārite vai dhāraṇākarṣaṇe, saṃgraho nāma saṃyogasahacaritaṃ guṇāntaraṃ snehadravatvakāritam apāṃ saṃyogādāme kumbhe agnisaṃyogāt pakve|
yadi tvavayavakārite abhaviṣyatām ? pāṃśurāśiprabhṛtiṣvapyajñāsyetām, dravyāntarānutpattau ca tṛṇopalakāṣṭhādiṣu jatusaṃgṛhīteṣvapi nābhaviṣyatāmiti|
children.translated_text: But if [holding and pulling] were produced by [mere] parts? They would be known also in heaps of sand and the like; and if no different substance were produced, they would not exist even in straw, stones, wood, and the like bound together with lac.

children.text: athāvayavinaṃ pratyācakṣāṇakaḥ 'mā bhūt pratyakṣalopaḥ' ityaṇusañcayaṃ darśanaviṣayaṃ pratijānānaḥ kimanuyoktavyaḥ ? iti, 'ekamidaṃ dravyam' ityekabuddherviṣayaṃ paryanuyojyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, one who denies the whole, saying 'let there be no loss of perception,' [and instead] claims that a collection of atoms is the object of visual perception — what should he be challenged on? He should be challenged regarding the object of the unitary cognition: 'this is one substance.'

children.text: kimekabuddhirabhinnārthaviṣayā ? aho bhinnārthaviṣayā ? iti, abhinnārthaviṣayeticet ? arthāntarānujñānādavayavisiddhiḥ, nānārthaviṣayeti cet ? bhinneṣvekadarśanānupapattiḥ |
children.translated_text: Is the unitary cognition directed at an undifferentiated object? Or at a differentiated object? If directed at an undifferentiated object? Then, by the acknowledgment of a different thing, the whole is established. If directed at a differentiated object? Then a unitary perception of differentiated [objects] is untenable.

children.text: anekasmin eka iti vyāhatā buddhirna dṛśyate iti // 35 //
children.translated_text: 'One' regarding what is many — a contradictory cognition is not observed. //35//

The whole is a different thing — for holding and pulling are produced by cohesion (<s>saṃgraha</s>). Cohesion is a quality other [than conjunction], accompanied by conjunction, produced by viscosity and fluidity — [as in] water, from conjunction in an unfired pot, [and] from conjunction with fire in a fired [pot].
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.36: [Objection:] If [it is argued that] apprehension is like an army or a forest? No — because atoms are supersensible.

children.text: yathā senāṅgeṣu vanāṅgeṣu ca dūrādagṛhyamāṇapṛthaktveṣu 'ekam' ityupapadyate buddhiḥ evamaṇuṣu saṃciteṣvagṛhyamāṇapṛthaktveṣu 'ekam' ityupapadyate buddhiriti |
children.translated_text: Just as regarding the members of an army or a forest, whose separateness is not grasped from a distance, the cognition 'one' arises — so too regarding atoms collected together, whose separateness is not grasped, the cognition 'one' arises.

children.text: yathāgṛhyamāṇapṛthaktvānāṃ senāvanāṅgānām ārāt kāraṇāntarataḥ pṛthaktvasyāgrahaṇaṃ yathāgṛhyamāṇajātīnāṃ palāśa iti vā khadira iti vā nārāj jātigrahaṇaṃ bhavati yathāgṛhyamāṇapraspandānāṃ nārāt spandagrahaṇam. gṛhyamāṇe cārthajāte pṛthaktvasyāgrahaṇāt 'ekam' iti bhāktaḥ pratyayo bhavati. na tvaṇūnāṃ gṛhyamāṇapṛthaktvānāṃ kāraṇataḥ pṛthaktvasyāgrahaṇād bhākta ekapratyayaḥ-- atīndriyatvādaṇṛnāmiti |
children.translated_text: Just as the separateness of the members of an army or forest, whose separateness is not being grasped, is not grasped from a distance due to another cause — just as the species of [trees] whose species is being grasped [only nearby], such as '<s>palāśa</s>' or '<s>khadira</s>,' is not grasped from a distance — just as the movement of those whose movement is being grasped is not grasped from a distance. And when a group of objects is being grasped, from the non-apprehension of separateness, the cognition 'one' arises figuratively (<s>bhākta</s>). But regarding atoms, whose separateness is being grasped, it is not the case that a figurative cognition of unity arises from the non-apprehension of separateness due to a cause — because atoms are supersensible.

children.text: idameva parīkṣyate-- kimekapratyayo 'ṇusaṃcayaviṣayaḥ ? āho svinna ? iti, aṇusaṃcaya eva senāvanāṅgāni, na ca parīkṣyamāṇamudāharaṇamiti yuktam-- sādhyatvāditi //
children.translated_text: This very point is being examined: is the cognition of unity directed at a collection of atoms? Or is it not? The collection of atoms would be just like the members of an army or forest. But it is not proper to use what is being examined as an illustration — because it is what is to be proved.
[Objection:] Because it is observed? No — because the examination of that subject is justified. //14//

children.text:
yadapi manyeta-- dṛṣṭamidaṃ senāvanāṅgānāṃ pṛthaktvasyāgrahaṇādabhedena 'ekam' itigrahaṇaṃ na ca dṛṣṭaṃ śakyaṃ pratyākhyātumiti|
tacca naivam-- tadviṣayasya parīkṣopapatteḥ
children.translated_text: And if one were to think — it is observed that from the non-apprehension of the separateness of the members of an army or forest, there is a unitary apprehension, and what is observed cannot be denied — that is not so, because the examination of that subject is justified.

children.text:
darśanaviṣaya evāyaṃ parīkṣyate yoyamekamiti pratyayo dṛśyate sa parīkṣyate-- kiṃ dravyāntaraviṣayo vā ? athāṇusaṃcayaviṣayaḥ ? iti, atra darśanamanyatarasya sādhakaṃ na bhavati|
nānābhāve cāṇūnāṃ pṛthaktvasyāgrahaṇādabhedena 'ekam' itigrahaṇam atasmiṃstaditipratyayo yathā sthāṇau puruṣa iti|
tataḥ kim ?. atasmiṃstaditipratyayasya pradhānāpekṣitvāt pradhānasiddhiḥ|
sthāṇau puruṣa iti pratyayasya kiṃ pradhānam ?. yo 'sau puruṣe puruṣapratyayaḥ tasmin sati puruṣasāmānyagrahaṇāt sthāṇau puruṣoyamiti, evaṃ nānābhūteṣu 'ekam' iti sāmānyagrahaṇāt pradhāne sati bhavitumarhati pradhānaṃ ca sarvasyāgrahaṇād nopapadyate iti. tasmādabhinne evāyamabhedapratyayaḥ-- 'ekam' iti//
children.translated_text: This very thing, which is the subject of observation, is being examined — the cognition 'one' that is observed is being examined: is it directed at a different substance? Or at a collection of atoms? Herein, observation does not establish either one. And when atoms are [in fact] diverse, from the non-apprehension of separateness, the unitary cognition 'one' would be a superimposition — like the cognition of a person on a post. What follows from that? Because the cognition of superimposition depends on a primary [referent], the primary [referent] is established. What is the primary [referent] of the cognition 'this is a person' regarding a post? Because the cognition of a person [arises] from the apprehension of the universal 'person-ness' when a [real] person exists — [one thinks] 'this is a person' regarding the post. Similarly, because of the apprehension of the universal 'one-ness' when there are diverse [atoms], [this cognition] is justified when a primary [referent] exists. But the primary [referent] is untenable if everything [i.e., the whole] is not apprehended. Therefore this cognition of non-difference regarding what is non-different — 'one' — [is justified].

[Objection:] The unitary cognition regarding the objects of other senses is the primary [referent]? No — because in the absence of a reason for distinction, the illustration would be indeterminate. //15//

children.text: śrotrādiviṣayeṣu śabdādiṣvabhinneṣu ekapratyayaḥ pradhānam anekasminn ekapratyayasyeti|

evaṃ ca sati dṛṣṭāntopādānaṃ na vyavatiṣṭhate-- viśeṣahetvabhāvāt, aṇuṣu saṃciteṣvekapratyayaḥ kimatasmiṃstaditipratyayaḥ sthāṇau puruṣapratyayavat ? athārthasya tathābhāvāt tasmiṃstaditipratyayo yathā śabdasyaikatvādekaḥ śabda iti ?, viśeṣahetuparigrahamantareṇa dṛṣṭāntau saṃśayamāpādayata iti|
children.translated_text: This being so, the use of an illustration does not stand — because of the absence of a reason for distinction. Is the unitary cognition regarding collected atoms a superimposition, like the cognition of a person on a post? Or is it because the object is actually thus, a cognition of what is [truly] present, as [the cognition] 'one sound' [arises] because of the unity of sound? Without establishing a distinguishing reason, the two illustrations [merely] produce doubt.
'Like a pot, the aggregate alone [has] odor and the rest' — the odor and the rest are the counter-illustration.
Similarly, he should be challenged regarding the cognitions of magnitude, conjunction, movement, universal, and particular — and in those too, the same consequence [applies].
Regarding the objects of hearing and the rest — sounds and the like, which are undifferentiated — the unitary cognition is the primary [referent for] the cognition of unity regarding what is many.

children.text: ekatvabuddhistasmiṃstaditipratyaya iti viśeṣahetuḥ-- mahaditi- pratyena sāmānādhikaraṇyāt | 16 |
children.translated_text: The distinguishing reason [showing] that the unitary cognition is a superimposition is: the co-referentiality with the cognition 'large.' //16//

children.text:
'ekamidaṃ mahacca' ityekaviṣayau pratyayau samānādhikaraṇau bhavatastena vijñāyate-- yanmahat tadekamiti|
aṇusamūhātiśayagrahaṇaṃ mahatpratyaya iticet ? so 'yam amahatsvaṇuṣu mahatpratyayo 'tasmiṃstaditipratyayo bhavatīti|
kiṃ cātaḥ ? atasmiṃstaditipratyayasya pradhānāpekṣitvāt pradhānasiddhiriti ubhavitavyaṃ mahatyeva mahatpratyayeneti|
children.translated_text: 'This is one and large' — these two cognitions with the same object are co-referential. From this it is known: what is large is one. [Objection:] If the cognition 'large' is the apprehension of an excess of the collection of atoms? Then this cognition 'large' regarding atoms, which are not large, would be a superimposition. What follows? Because the cognition of superimposition depends on a primary [referent], the primary [referent] is established — there must be a cognition 'large' regarding what is [actually] large.

children.text: aṇuḥ śabdo mahāniti ca vyavasāyāt pradhānasiddhiriticet ? na-- mandatīvratāgrahaṇamiyattānavadhāraṇād yathā dravye | 17 |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Because of the certain judgment 'a small sound, a large [sound],' the primary [referent] is established? No — the apprehension of faint and intense [sounds] is [merely] the non-determination of quantity, as in the case of substance. //17//

children.text:
'aṇuḥ śabdo 'lpo mandaḥ' ityetasya grahaṇam 'mahān śabdaḥ paṭustīvraḥ' ityetasya grahaṇam, kasmāt ? iyattānavadhāraṇātuna hyayam 'mahān śabdaḥ' itivyavasyan 'iyānayam' ityavadhārayati yathā badarāmalakabilvādīni|
'saṃyukte ime' iti ca dvitvasamānāśrayaprāptigrahaṇam //
children.translated_text: The apprehension of 'a small sound, slight, faint' and the apprehension of 'a large sound, sharp, intense' — why [does this not establish 'large']? Because of the non-determination of quantity — for one making the certain judgment 'this is a large sound' does not determine 'it is of this magnitude,' as [one does] with berries, <s>āmalaka</s> fruits, <s>bilva</s> fruits, and the like. And 'these are conjoined' — this is the apprehension of duality having a common substrate with conjunction.
[Objection:] Two aggregates are the substrate of conjunction? //18//

children.text: koyaṃ samudāyaḥ ? prāptiranekasya ? anekā vā prāptirekasya samudāya iticet ? prāpteragrahaṇaṃ prāptyāśritāyā | 19 |
children.translated_text: What is this aggregate? Is the conjunction of many [things] [the aggregate]? Or is the many conjunctions of one [thing the aggregate]? [Objection:] If so — the conjunction is not apprehended, since it depends on conjunction. //19//

children.text: 'saṃyukte ime vastunī' iti nātra dve prāptī saṃyukte gṛhyete //
children.translated_text: 'These two things are conjoined' — here, two conjunctions that are conjoined are not apprehended.

children.text: anekasamūhaḥ sudāya iticet ? na-- dvitvena sāmānādhikaraṇyasya grahaṇāt | 20 |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] The aggregate of many [atoms] is [the substrate]? No — because duality is apprehended as co-referential [with the conjoined]. //20//

children.text: 'dvāvimau saṃyuktāvarthauṃ' iti grahaṇe sati nānekasamūhāśrayaḥ saṃyogo gṛhyate na ca dvayoraṇvorgrahaṇamasti tasmānmahatī dvitvāśrayabhūte dravye saṃyogasya sthānamiti//
children.translated_text: When it is apprehended that 'these two conjoined objects' — [the cognition] is not that conjunction resides in an aggregate of many [atoms]; nor is there apprehension of two atoms. Therefore, the great substance — being the substrate of duality — is the locus of conjunction.

children.text: pratyāsattiḥ pratīghātāvasānā saṃyogo nārthāntaramiticet ? na-- arthāntarahetutvāt saṃyogāsya | 21 |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] Proximity, ending in impact, is conjunction — not a different thing? No — because conjunction is a cause of different things. //21//

children.text: śabdarūpādispandānāṃ hetuḥ saṃyogaḥ-- na ca dravyayorguṇāntaropajananamantareṇa śabde rūpādiṣu spande ca kāraṇatvaṃ gṛhyate tasmād guṇāntaram|

children.translated_text: And [conjunction] is the object of a cognition, being a different thing — or [it is the object of] the negation of that. //22//

children.text: 'kuṇḍalī guruḥ akuṇḍalaśchātraḥ' iti saṃyogabuddheśca yadyarthāntaraṃpa na viṣayaḥ ? arthāntarapratiṣedhastarhi viṣayastatra--- pratiṣidhyamānavacanam | 23 |
children.translated_text: 'The one with earrings is the teacher; the one without earrings is the student' — if the cognition of conjunction has no different object? Then the negation of a different thing is its object — the statement negating [conjunction as a different thing]. //23//

children.text:
'saṃyukte dravye' iti yadarthāntaramanyatra dṛṣṭamiha pratiṣidhyate tad vaktavyamiti|
dvayormahatorāśritasya grahaṇād nāṇvāśraya iti //
children.translated_text: That different thing, observed elsewhere, which is denied here [in the case of] 'conjoined substances' — that must be stated. From the apprehension of [conjunction] residing in two large [substances], it does not reside in atoms.

Conjunction is the cause of sound, color, and movement. And one does not apprehend causality regarding sound, color, and the rest, and movement, without the production of a different quality in the two substances. Therefore [conjunction] is a different quality.
[NyS 2.1.25:] The statement about the substrate is [needed] because what is in a different substrate is not manifest. [End of NyS 2.1.25]
[Objection:] If the atomic configuration is the object? — [NyS 2.1.26:] The statement about the capacity of what is reached and what is not reached. [End of NyS 2.1.26]

children.text:
kimaprāpte aṇusamavasthāne tadāśrayo jātiviśeṣo gṛhyate ? atha prāpte ? iti|
aprāpte grahaṇamiticet ? vyavahitasyāṇusamavasthānasyāpyupalabdhiprasaṅgaḥuvyavahite 'ṇusamavasthāne tadāśrayo jātiviśeṣo gṛhyeta|
prāpte grahaṇamiticet ? madhyaparabhāgayoraprāptau anabhivyaktiḥ|
children.translated_text: Is the particular universal (<s>jātiviśeṣa</s>) dependent on that [atomic configuration] grasped when the atomic configuration has not been reached? Or when it has been reached? If it is grasped when not reached? Then even an obstructed atomic configuration would be apprehended — the particular universal dependent on it would be grasped even when the atomic configuration is obstructed. If it is grasped when reached? Then when [the sense-organ] has not reached the middle and far parts, there is no manifestation.

children.text: yāvat prāptaṃ bhavati tāvatyabhivyaktiriticet ? tāvato 'dhikaraṇatvamaṇusamavasthānasyauyāvati prāpte jātiviśeṣo gṛhyate tāvadasyādhikaraṇamiti prāptaṃ bhavati tatra--- ekasamudāye pratīyamāne 'rthabhede | 26 |
children.translated_text: [Objection:] If there is manifestation to the extent that [the atomic configuration] is reached? Then the atomic configuration has substrate-hood to just that extent — the particular universal is grasped to the extent that [the configuration] is reached, and to that extent it is its substrate. This being established, it follows — [NyS 2.1.26:] When a single aggregate is cognized, there would be a difference of objects.

children.text: evaṃ ca sati yo 'ṇusamudāyo vṛkṣa iti pratīyate tatra vṛkṣabahutvaṃ pratīyetauyatra yatra hyaṇusamudāyasya bhāge vṛkṣatvaṃ gṛhyate sa sa vṛkṣa iti, tasmāt samuditāṇusamavasthānasyārthāntarasya jātiviśeṣābhivyaktiviṣayatvād avayavyarthāntarabhūta iti // 36 //
children.translated_text: And this being so, the aggregate of atoms that is cognized as a tree would [have to] be cognized as many trees — for wherever a part of the atomic aggregate has tree-nature grasped, that is a tree. Therefore, since the atomic configuration, which is a different object from the whole (<s>avayavin</s>), is the object of the manifestation of the particular universal, the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) exists as a different entity. [End of NyS 2.1.36]

The non-rejection of the particular universal (<s>jātiviśeṣa</s>) that is the sign of the continuity of cognition. Or if it is rejected, the orderly arrangement of cognitions would be untenable. [End of NyS 2.1.24]
[Section: NySBh 2.1.37]
Perception has been examined. Now inference (<s>anumāna</s>) is examined —
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.37: [Objection:] Inference (<s>anumāna</s>) is not a valid means of knowledge, because of deviation [from truth] due to obstruction, disturbance, and similarity.
It is not a valid means of knowledge —
meaning it does not establish its object even once.

children.text: rodhādapi nadī pūrṇā gṛhyate tadā ca 'upariṣṭhād vṛṣṭo devaḥ' iti mithyānumānam. nīḍopaghātādapi pipīlikāṇḍasaṃcāro bhavati tadā ca 'bhaviṣyati vṛṣṭiḥ' iti mithyānumānamiti, puruṣopi mayūravāśitamanukaroti tadāpi śabdasādṛśyād mithyānumānaṃ bhavati // 37 //
children.translated_text: Even from a dam, a river is seen to be full, and then the false inference 'the god has rained upstream' [is made]. Even from the disturbance of nests, there is movement of ant-eggs, and then the false inference 'there will be rain' [is made]. A person also imitates the cry of a peacock, and then too, from the similarity of sound, a false inference occurs. [End of NyS 2.1.37]
[Section: NySBh 2.1.38]
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.38: [Reply:] No, because these are cases of something different [from valid inference], due to [mere partial] similarity and partial [features].

children.text:
nāyamanumānavyabhicāraḥ ananumāne tu khalvayamanumānābhimānaḥ|
katham ?. nāviśiṣṭo liṅgaṃ bhavitumarhati, pūrvodakaviśiṣṭaṃ khalu varṣodakaṃ śīghrataratvaṃ srotaso bahutaraphenaphalaparṇakāṣṭhādivahanaṃ copalabhamānaḥ pūrṇatvena nadyāḥ 'upari vṛṣṭo devaḥ' ityanuminoti nodakavṛddhimātreṇa|
pipīlikāprāyasyāṇḍasaṃcāre 'bhaviṣyati vṛṣṭiḥ' ityanumīyate na kāsāṃ ciditi|
children.translated_text: When ant-eggs of the majority [species] of ants are being transported, 'there will be rain' is inferred — not [from the movement] of just any [ants].

children.text: 'nedaṃ mayūravāśitaṃ tatsadṛśoyaṃ śabdaḥ' itiviśeṣāparijñānād mithyānumānamiti, yastu viśiṣṭācchabdād viśiṣṭamayūravāśitaṃ gṛhṇati tasya viśiṣṭo 'rtho gṛhyamāṇo liṅgaṃ yathā sarpādīnāmiti|
children.translated_text: 'This is not a peacock's cry; this sound resembles it' — from the failure to discern the distinguishing feature, a false inference [results]. But one who grasps a distinguished peacock's cry from a distinguished sound — for him, a distinguished object being grasped is the inferential sign, just as with serpents and the like.

This is the fault of the inferrer, not of inference [itself] — [the fault of] one who, through a distinguishable object that should be inferred, seeks to know it through the perception of an undistinguished object. [End of NyS 2.1.38]

This is not a deviation of inference; rather, this is a false presumption of inference where there is no [actual] inference. How? An undistinguished [mark] cannot be an inferential sign (<s>liṅga</s>). One who observes rain-water distinguished from prior water — by the greater swiftness of the current and the greater carrying of foam, fruits, leaves, wood, and the like — infers from the fullness of the river 'the god has rained upstream,' not merely from the rise of water.
[Section: NySBh 2.1.39]
Inference has the three times as its object — 'because of apprehending the three times,' it was said. And here —
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.39: [Objection:] The present does not exist, because the times of 'having fallen' and 'about to fall' are possible for what is falling.

children.text: vṛntāt pracyutasya phalasya bhūmau pratyāsīdato yad ūrdhvaṃ sa patito 'dhvā tatsaṃyuktaḥ patitakālaḥ, yo 'dhasyāt sa patitavyo 'dhvā tatsaṃyuktaḥ kālaḥ patitavyakālaḥ, nedānīṃ tṛtīyo 'dhvā vidyate yatra patatīti vartamānaḥ kālo gṛhyeta. tasmād vartamānaḥ kālo na vidyate iti // 39 //
children.translated_text: For a fruit that has detached from its stalk and is approaching the ground: what is above is the path already fallen, and the time associated with it is the 'having-fallen' time; what is below is the path yet to be fallen, and the time associated with it is the 'about-to-fall' time. There is now no third path where it is falling, such that the present time could be grasped. Therefore, the present time does not exist. [End of NyS 2.1.39]
[Section: NySBh 2.1.40]
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.40: [Reply:] And in the absence of the present, those [past and future] too would be absent, because they depend on it.
Time is not manifested by spatial path; rather, it is manifested by action (<s>kriyā</s>).

children.text: patatīti yadā patanakriyā vyuparatā bhavati sa kālaḥ patitakālaḥ, yadotpatsyate sa patitavyakālaḥ, yadā dravye vartamānā kriyā gṛhyate sa vartamānaḥ kālaḥ, yadi cāyaṃ dravye vartamānaṃ patanaṃ na gṛhṇāti kasya uparamam utpatsyamānatāṃ vā prativadyate ?|
children.translated_text: When the action of falling has ceased — that time is the 'having-fallen' time. When [the action] will arise — that is the 'about-to-fall' time. When the action present in the substance is grasped — that is the present time. And if one does not grasp the falling as present in the substance, whose cessation or future arising is being stated?

children.text: patitaḥ kāla iti bhūtā kriyā, patitavyaḥ kāla iti cotpatsyamānā kriyā, ubhayoḥ kālayoḥ kriyāhīnaṃ dravyam, adhaḥ pratatīti kriyāsaṃbaddham, soyaṃ kriyādravyayoḥ saṃbandhaṃ gṛhṇāti vartamānaḥ kālaḥ tadāśrayau cetarau kālau tadabhāve na syātāmiti // 40 //
children.translated_text: 'Having-fallen' time — that is past action; 'about-to-fall' time — that is future action. In both times, the substance is devoid of action; 'it extends downward' — [this shows it is] connected with action. This [one who grasps] the connection of action and substance grasps the present time; the other two times depend on it, and in its absence, they would not exist. [End of NyS 2.1.40]
[Section: NySBh 2.1.41]
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.41: The establishment of the past and the future is not through mutual dependence.

children.text:
yady atītānāgatau itaretarāpekṣau sidhyetām ? pratipadyemahi vartamānavilopam. nātītāpekṣānāgatasiddhiḥ nāpyanāgatāpekṣātītasiddhiḥ|
kayā yuktyā |
kena kalpena atītaḥ. kathamatītāpekṣānāgatasiddhiḥ ? kena ca kalpenānāgataḥ ? iti. naitacchakyaṃ nirvaktum |
avyākaraṇīyametad vartamānalope iti|
yacca manyeta-- hrasvadīrghayoḥ sthalanimnayoḥ chāyātapayośca yathetaretarāpekṣayā siddhirevam atītānāgatayoriti, tannopapadyate-- viśeṣahetvabhāvāt. dṛṣṭāntavat pratidṛṣṭāntopi prasajyate-- yathā rūpasparśauṃ gandharasau netaretarāpekṣau sidhyataḥ evamatītānāgatāviti netaretarāpekṣā kasya cit siddhiriti|

children.translated_text: Because in the absence of one, the absence of the other [entails] the absence of both. [End of NyS 2.1.27]

children.text: yadyekasyānyatarāpekṣā siddhiḥ ? anyatarasyedānīṃ kimapekṣā ?. yadyanyatarasyaikāpekṣā siddhiḥ ? ekasyedānīṃ kimapekṣā ?, evamekasyābhāve anyataranna sidhyatīti ubhayābhāvaḥ prasajyate|
children.translated_text: If one is established through dependence on the other? Then what does the other depend on? If the other is established through dependence on the one? Then what does the one depend on? Thus, in the absence of one, the other is not established — and the absence of both follows.

children.text: arthasadbhāvavyaṅgyaścāyaṃ vartamānaḥ kālaḥ-- 'vidyate dravyam' 'vidyate guṇaḥ' 'vidyate karma' iti // 41 //
children.translated_text: And this present time is manifested by the existence of things — 'substance exists,' 'quality exists,' 'action exists.' [End of NyS 2.1.41]

If the past and the future were established through mutual dependence? We would accept the elimination of the present. But the future is not established through dependence on the past, nor the past through dependence on the future. By what reasoning [could this be]? By what consideration is [something] past? How is the future established through dependence on the past? And by what consideration is [something] future? This cannot be stated. This is inexplicable if the present is eliminated. And should one think — 'Just as short and long, high and low, shadow and sunlight are established through mutual dependence, so too the past and the future' — that is untenable, because there is no distinguishing reason. A counter-example follows the example — just as form and touch, odor and flavor are not established through mutual dependence, so too the past and the future — nothing is established through mutual dependence.
[Section: NySBh 2.1.42]
And for that which does not exist —
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.42: In the absence of the present, there would be non-apprehension of everything, because perception would be untenable.

children.text:
pratyakṣam indriyārthasaṃnikarṣajaṃ. na cāvidyamānam |
asad indriyeṇa saṃnikṛṣyate, na cāyaṃ vidyamānam |

sat kiñcidanujānātīti pratyakṣanimittaṃ pratyakṣaviṣayaḥ pratyakṣajñānaṃ sarvaṃ nopapadyate, pratyakṣānupapattau tatpūrvakatvād anumānāgamayoranupapattiḥ sarvapramāṇavilope sarvagrahaṇaṃ na bhavatīti|
children.translated_text: exists — [therefore] perception's basis, perception's object, perceptual cognition — none of these would be tenable. If perception is untenable, since inference and scriptural testimony are preceded by it, they too would be untenable; with the collapse of all <s>pramāṇas</s>, there would be no apprehension of anything.

children.text: ubhayathā ca vartamānaḥ kālo gṛhyate-- kvacidarthasadbhāvavyaṅgyo yathā 'asti dravyam' iti. kvacit kriyāsaṃtānavyaṅgyo yathā 'pacati chinattīti. nānāvidhā caikārthā kriyā kriyāsaṃtānaḥ kriyābhyāsaśca, nānāvidhā caikārthā kriyā 'pacatīti |
children.translated_text: And the present time is grasped in two ways — sometimes manifested by the existence of things, as 'substance exists'; sometimes manifested by the continuity of action and associated with the three times, as 'he cooks,' 'he cuts.' A series of diverse, unified actions is an action-continuum, and also action-repetition. Diverse unified action [is illustrated by] 'he cooks' —

children.text: sthālyadhiśrayaṇam udakāsecanaṃ taṇḍulāvapanamedhopasarpaṇam agnyabhijvālanaṃ darvīghaṭṭanaṃ maṇḍasrāvaṇam adhovatāraṇamiti. chinattīti kriyābhyāsaḥ-- udyabhyodyamya paraśuṃ dāruṇi nipātayan chinattītyucyate // 42 //
children.translated_text: Setting the pot on [the fire], pouring water, adding grain-husks, approaching the fuel, kindling the fire, stirring with the ladle, draining the liquid, taking it down. 'He cuts' is an action-repetition — raising the axe again and again and bringing it down upon the wood, one is said to be 'cutting.' [End of NyS 2.1.42]
Perception arises from the contact of sense-organ and object. And what is non-existent — what is unreal cannot be contacted by a sense-organ. And this one does not concede that anything existent
[Section: NySBh 2.1.43]

children.text: yaccedaṃ pacyamānaṃ chidyamānaṃ ca tat kriyamāṇaṃ tasmin kriyamāṇe---
children.translated_text: And that which is being cooked and being cut — that is being acted upon — and when it is being acted upon —
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.43: But because of the tenability of 'done-ness' and 'to-be-done-ness,' apprehension [of the present] is of both kinds.

children.text: kriyāsaṃtāno 'nārabdhaścikīrpito 'nāgataḥ kālaḥ 'pakṣyatīti. prayojanāvasānaḥ kriyāsaṃtānoparamo 'tītaḥ kālaḥ 'apākṣīt' iti. ārabdhakriyāsaṃtāno vartamānaḥ kālaḥ 'pacatīti, tatra yā uparatā sā kṛtatā yā cikīrṣitā sā kartavyatā yā vidyamānā sā kriyamāṇatā. tadevaṃ kriyāsaṃtānasthaḥ traikālyasamāhāraḥ 'pacati pacyate' iti vartamānagrahaṇena gṛhyate-- kriyāsaṃtānasya hyatrāvicchedo vidhīyate nārambho noparam iti|
children.translated_text: An action-continuum that has not begun [and] is intended — that is the future time: 'he will cook.' An action-continuum that has reached its purpose and ceased — that is the past time: 'he cooked.' An action-continuum that has begun — that is the present time: 'he cooks.' Therein, what has ceased is the 'done-ness'; what is intended is the 'to-be-done-ness'; what is [currently] existing is the 'being-done-ness.' Thus, the aggregate of the three times situated in the action-continuum is grasped by the present-tense apprehension 'he cooks, it is being cooked' — for here the non-interruption of the action-continuum is what is expressed, not the beginning nor the cessation.

children.text: soyamubhayathā vartamānāṃ gṛhyate-- apavṛkto vyapavṛktaśca atītānāgatābhyām. sthitivyaṅgyaḥ-- 'vidyate dravyam' iti. kriyāsaṃtānāvicchedābhidhāyī ca traikālyānvitaḥ-- 'pacati chinattīti|
children.translated_text: This present is grasped in both ways — distinguished and separated from the past and the future. Manifested by [continued] existence: 'substance exists.' And expressing the non-interruption of the action-continuum, associated with the three times: 'he cooks, he cuts.'

children.text: anyaśca pratyāsattiprabhṛterrathasya vivakṣāyāṃ tadabhidhāyī bahuprakāro lokeṣūtprekṣitavyaḥ, tasmādasti vartamānaḥ kāla iti // 43 //
children.translated_text: And other [uses] in the world — from proximity onward, when one wishes to speak of a chariot, the many kinds of expressions that denote it are to be observed. Therefore, the present time exists. [End of NyS 2.1.43]
[Section: NySBh 2.1.44]
(Now the examination of <s>upamāna</s>, comparison)
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.44: [Objection:] <s>Upamāna</s> (comparison) is not established, because of complete similarity, predominant similarity, or partial similarity.

children.text: atyantasādharmyādupāmanaṃ na sidhyati-- na caivaṃ bhavati 'yathā gaurevaṃ gauḥ' iti, prāyaḥsādharmyādupamānaṃ na sidhyati-- na hi bhavati 'yathānaḍvānevaṃ mahiṣaḥ' iti, ekadeśasādharmyādupamānaṃ na sidhyati-- na hi sarveṇa sarvamupamīyate iti // 44 //
children.translated_text: <s>Upamāna</s> is not established from complete similarity — for it never happens that 'a cow is like a cow.' <s>Upamāna</s> is not established from predominant similarity — for it does not happen that 'a buffalo is like a bull.' <s>Upamāna</s> is not established from partial similarity — for everything is not compared with everything [on the basis of any shared feature]. [End of NyS 2.1.44]
[Section: NySBh 2.1.45]
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.45: [Reply:] Because <s>upamāna</s> is established through well-known similarity, the stated defects do not apply.

children.text: na sādharmyasya kṛtsnaprāyālpabhāvamāśrityopamānaṃ pravartate, kiṃ tarhi ?. prasiddhasādharmyāt sādhyasādhanabhāvamāśritya pravartate. yatra caitadasti na tatropamānaṃ pratiṣeddhuṃ śakyaṃ tasmād yathoktadoṣo nopapadyate iti// 45 //
children.translated_text: <s>Upamāna</s> does not operate by relying on the complete, predominant, or partial nature of similarity. What then? It operates by relying on the relation of means and end (<s>sādhyasādhanabhāva</s>) through well-known similarity. And where this [relation] exists, <s>upamāna</s> cannot be refuted — therefore the stated defect does not apply. [End of NyS 2.1.45]
[Section: NySBh 2.1.46]
Then let <s>upamāna</s> be [just a form of] inference —
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.46: [Objection:] Because the imperceptible is established through the perceptible.

children.text: yathā dhūmena pratyakṣeṇāpratyakṣasya vahnergrahaṇamanumānam evaṃ gavā pratyakṣeṇāpratyakṣasya gavayasya grahaṇamiti nedamanumānād viśiṣyate // 46 //
children.translated_text: Just as the apprehension of imperceptible fire through perceptible smoke is inference, so too the apprehension of the imperceptible <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox) through the perceptible cow — this is not different from inference. [End of NyS 2.1.46]
[Reply:] It is different, he says. By what reasoning? —
[Section: NySBh 2.1.47]

children.text: NyS_2,1.47: nāpratyakṣe gavaye pramāṇārthamupamānasya paśyāma iti //
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 2.1.47: [Reply:] We do not see the purpose of <s>upamāna</s> as a means of knowledge regarding the imperceptible <s>gavaya</s>.

children.text:
yadā hyayamupayuktopamāno godarśī gavā samānamarthaṃ paśyati tadā ayaṃ gavaya ityasya saṃjñāśabdasya vyavasthāṃ pratipadyate na caivamanumānamiti|
parārthaṃ copamānam-- yasya hyupameyamaprasiddhaṃ tadarthaṃ prasiddhopameyena kriyate iti|
parārthamupamānamiticet ? na-- svayamadhyavasāyāt |
bhavati ca bhoḥ svayamadhyavasāyaḥ- yathā gaurevaṃ gavaya iti|
nādhyavasāyaḥ
children.translated_text: For when this person, having employed the <s>upamāna</s> and seeing a cow, perceives an object similar to a cow — then he cognizes the conventional relation of the designating word '<s>gavaya</s>' [to its referent]; and this is not inference. And <s>upamāna</s> is for the sake of another — for one to whom the object of comparison is unknown, [the comparison] is made through a well-known object of comparison. [Objection:] If <s>upamāna</s> is for the sake of another? [Reply:] No — because of one's own determination. Indeed, sir, there is one's own determination: 'as a cow, so a <s>gavaya</s>.' [Objection:] The determination

children.text: pratiṣidhyate upamānaṃ tu tanna bhavati--"prasiddhasādharmyāt sādhyasādhanamupamānam 1-1-6"na ca yasyopameyaṃ prasiddhaṃ taṃ prati sādhyasādhanabhāvo vidyate iti // 47 //
children.translated_text: is not refuted, but that [determination] is not <s>upamāna</s> — '<s>upamāna</s> is the means of establishing what is to be proved through well-known similarity' [NyS 1.1.6]. And for one to whom the object of comparison is well-known, there is no relation of means and end [to be established]. [End of NyS 2.1.47]
And moreover—
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.48: Because <s>upamāna</s> (comparison) is established through the application 'thus,' there is no non-distinction [from <s>anumāna</s> (inference)].

children.text: tathetisamānadharmopasaṃhārādupamānaṃ sidhyati nānumānam-- ayaṃ cānayorviśeṣa iti // 48 //
children.translated_text: Through the application of similar properties as 'thus,' <s>upamāna</s> (comparison) is established, not <s>anumāna</s> (inference)—and this is the distinction between the two. // 48 //
(Now, the examination of <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) as a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge)—)
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.49: <s>Śabda</s> (verbal testimony) is <s>anumāna</s> (inference)—because the object, not being apprehended [directly], is to be inferred.

children.text: śabdo 'numānaṃ na pramāṇāntaram, kasmāt ?. śabdārthasyānumeyatvāt, kathamanumeyatvam ? pratyakṣato 'nupalabdheḥ, yathānupalabhyamāno liṅgī mitena liṅgena paścād mīyate ityanumānam evaṃ mitena śabdena paścād mīyate 'rtho 'nupalabhyamāna ityanumānaṃ śabdaḥ // 49 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śabda</s> (verbal testimony) is <s>anumāna</s> (inference), not a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge). Why? Because the object of <s>śabda</s> is to be inferred. How is it to be inferred? Because it is not apprehended through <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception). Just as the <s>liṅgin</s> (the thing characterized by the mark), not being [directly] apprehended, is subsequently measured by the apprehended <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark)—that is <s>anumāna</s>—so too the object, not being [directly] apprehended, is subsequently measured by the apprehended <s>śabda</s> (word)—thus <s>śabda</s> is <s>anumāna</s>. // 49 //
And for this further reason, <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) is <s>anumāna</s> (inference)—
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.50: Because cognition does not function in two [different] ways.

children.text: pramāṇāntarabhāve dvipravṛttirupalabdhiḥ = anyathā hyupalabdhiranumāne anyathopamāne tad vyākhyātam, śabdānumānayostūpalabdhiradvipravṛttiḥ yathānumāne pravartate tathā śabdepi, viśeṣābhāvādanumānaṃ śabda iti // 50 //
children.translated_text: When there is a separate <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), cognition functions in two ways—it operates one way in <s>anumāna</s> (inference) and another way in <s>upamāna</s> (comparison); that has been explained. But in the case of <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) and <s>anumāna</s>, cognition does not function in two ways—as it operates in <s>anumāna</s>, so also in <s>śabda</s>. Because there is no distinction, <s>śabda</s> is <s>anumāna</s>. // 50 //
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.51: And because of the relation [between word and meaning].

children.text: "śabdonumānam"iti vartate, saṃbaddhayośca śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandhaprasiddhau śabdopalabdherarthagrahaṇaṃ yathā saṃbaddhayorliṅgaliṅginoḥ saṃbandhapratītau liṅgopalabdhau liṅgigrahaṇamiti // 51 //
children.translated_text: The statement '<s>śabda</s> is <s>anumāna</s>' is continued here. When the relation between <s>śabda</s> (word) and <s>artha</s> (meaning), which are related, is well-known, there is grasp of the meaning from the apprehension of the word—just as when the relation between <s>liṅga</s> (inferential mark) and <s>liṅgin</s> (the thing marked), which are related, is recognized, there is grasp of the <s>liṅgin</s> from the apprehension of the <s>liṅga</s>. // 51 //
As for the [objection] 'because the object is to be inferred'—that is not so—
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.52: The cognition of the object from <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) arises from the authority of <s>āptopadeśa</s> (reliable testimony).

children.text:
'svargaḥ apsarasaḥ uttarāḥ kuravaḥ sapta dvīpāḥ samudro lokasaṃniveśaḥ' ityevamāderapratyakṣasyārthasya na śabdamātrāt pratyayaḥ, kiṃ tarhi ? 'āptairayamuktaḥ śabdaḥ' ityataḥ saṃpratyayaḥ-- viparyayeṇa saṃpratyayābhāvāt na tvevamanumānamiti|
yat punaḥ--
"upalabdheradvipravṛttitvāt 2-1-50" iti.
ayameva śabdānumānayorupalabdheḥ pravṛttibhedaḥ tatra viśeṣe satyahetuḥ-- 'viśeṣābhāvāt' iti|

yat punaridam--"saṃbandhācca"iti, asti ca śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandho 'nujñātaḥ asti ca pratiṣiddhaḥu 'asyedam' itiṣaṣṭhīviśiṣṭasya vākyasyārthaviśeṣo 'nujñātaḥ prāptilakṣaṇastu śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandhaḥ pratiṣiddhaḥ|
children.translated_text: Why? Because it is not apprehended by any <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge). Through <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception), first of all, there is no apprehension of physical contact between word and meaning—because [the meaning] is beyond the senses. The meaning, having gone beyond the range of that sense-organ by which the word is grasped, is not grasped [by it]; and the meaning, even though it exists as an object beyond the senses, [cannot be reached by them]; and <s>prāpti</s> (contact) is grasped only when both are grasped by the same sense-organ.

children.text: kasmāt ?, pramāṇatonupalabdheḥupratyakṣatastāvat śabdārthaprāpternopalabdhiḥ-- atīndriyatvātuyenendriyeṇa gṛhyate śabdastasya viṣayabhāvamativṛtto 'rtho na gṛhyate, asti cātīndriyaviṣayabhūtopyarthaḥ, samānena cendriyeṇa gṛhyamāṇayoḥ prāptirgṛhyate iti|
children.translated_text: And if the relation characterized by <s>prāpti</s> (physical contact) between word and meaning were grasped, then either the meaning would be near the word, or the word would be near the meaning, or both would be in both places. // 52 //

children.text: prāptilakṣaṇe ca gṛhyamāṇe saṃbandhe śabdārthayoḥ śabdāntike vārthaḥ syāt arthāntike vā śabdaḥ syāt ubhayaṃ vobhayatra // 52 //

children.translated_text:
With regard to objects beyond perception such as '<s>svarga</s> (heaven), <s>Apsarases</s>, <s>Uttarakurus</s>, the seven continents, the ocean, the arrangement of the worlds'—the cognition does not arise from <s>śabda</s> (word) alone. What then? The cognition arises from the fact that 'this word was uttered by an <s>āpta</s> (reliable authority)'—because in the contrary case there would be no cognition. Therefore it is not <s>anumāna</s> (inference) in this way.
As for the [objection]—
'Because cognition does not function in two ways' (2.1.50):
This very difference in the functioning of cognition between <s>śabda</s> and <s>anumāna</s>, when this distinction exists, is groundless—the claim 'because there is no distinction.'
As for the [objection] 'And because of the relation'—there is indeed a relation between <s>śabda</s> (word) and <s>artha</s> (meaning) that is accepted, and there is one that is rejected. The meaning of the sentence qualified by the sixth case-ending (genitive) 'of this, that' is accepted; but the relation between word and meaning characterized by <s>prāpti</s> (physical contact) is rejected.
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.53: And because filling, burning, and cutting are not apprehended, there is absence of [physical] relation.

The meaning is also: because there is absence of <s>sthāna</s> (place of articulation) and <s>karaṇa</s> (instrument of articulation).
Nor is this apprehended even through <s>anumāna</s> (inference)—that the meaning is near the word.
Even on this view, the word, which is to be uttered through the <s>sthāna</s> (place of articulation) and <s>karaṇa</s> (instrument of articulation) in the mouth—if the meaning were near it, then upon the utterance of the words for food, fire, and sword, filling, burning, and cutting should be apprehended. But they are not apprehended. Because they are not apprehended, the relation characterized by <s>prāpti</s> (physical contact) is not to be inferred.

children.text:
sthānakaraṇābhāvāditi cārthaḥ|
na cāyamanumānatopyupalabhyate-- śabdāntike 'rtha iti|
etasmin pakṣe 'py āsyasthānakaraṇoccāraṇīyaḥ śabdastadantike 'rtha iti annāgnyasiśabdoccāraṇe pūraṇapradāhapāṭanāni gṛhyeran. na ca gṛhyante, agrahaṇānnānumeyaḥ prāptilakṣaṇḥ saṃbandhaḥ|
arthāntike śabdaṃ iti-- sthānakaraṇāsaṃbhavād anuccāraṇam, sthānaṃ kaṇṭhādayaḥ karaṇaṃ prayatnaviśeṣaḥ tasyārthāntike 'nupapattiriti|
children.translated_text: And because both are negated, neither [alternative holds].
Therefore, the meaning is not in physical contact with the word. // 53 //

As for 'the word being near the meaning'—because the <s>sthāna</s> (place of articulation) and <s>karaṇa</s> (instrument of articulation) cannot exist [there], there would be no utterance. The <s>sthāna</s> is the throat and other [places of articulation]; the <s>karaṇa</s> is the specific effort [of articulation]. Their impossibility near the meaning [follows].
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.54: Because of the fixed correlation of word and meaning, [the relation] is not negated.

From observing the fixed correlation of the cognition of meaning from words, it is inferred: there exists a relation between word and meaning that is the cause of this fixed correlation. For in the absence of a relation, there would be the unwanted consequence that cognition of any meaning would arise from any word whatsoever. Therefore, the relation is not negated. // 54 //

children.text: śabdārthapratyayasya vyavasthādarśanād anumīyate-- asti śabdārthasaṃbandho vyavasthākāraṇam, asaṃbandhe hi śabdamātrādarthamātre pratyayaprasaṅgaḥ tasmādapratiṣedhaḥ saṃbandhasyeti // 54 //

children.translated_text: Here is the resolution—
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.55: No, because the cognition of meaning from words is <s>sāmayika</s> (conventional).

The fixed correlation of word and meaning is not produced by [physical] relation. What then? It is produced by <s>samaya</s> (convention). That is what we stated: 'The meaning of the sentence qualified by the genitive "of this, that" is accepted as the relation between word and meaning'—that is what we called <s>samaya</s> (convention).

children.text: na saṃbandhakāritaṃ śabdārthavyavasthānam. kiṃ tarhi ?. samayakāritaṃ yattadavocāma-- 'asyedamiti ṣaṣṭhīviśiṣṭasya vākyasyārthaviśeṣo 'nujñātaḥ śabdārthayoḥ saṃbandhaḥ' iti samayaṃ tamavocāma iti|

kaḥ punarayaṃ samayaḥ ?, 'asya śabdasyedamarthajātamabhidheyam' ityabhidhānābhidhaiyaniyamaniyogaḥ, tasminnupayukte śabdādarthasaṃpratyayo bhavati, viparyaye hi śabdaśravaṇepi pratyayābhāvaḥ, saṃbandhavādināpi cāyamavarjanīya iti|
children.translated_text: And because ordinary people grasp [meaning] from [words as they are] being used; and grammar is the explanation of speech characterized by word-forms, for the purpose of preserving convention; the definition of explained speech is the definition of meaning; a sentence is a collection of words upon the completion of meaning.

children.text: prayujyamānagrahaṇācca laukikānām, samayapālanārthaṃ cedaṃ padalakṣaṇāyā vāco 'nvākhyānaṃ vyākaraṇam, vyākyalakṣaṇāyā vāco 'rthalakṣaṇam, padasamūho vākyam arthaparisamāptāviti|
children.translated_text: Thus, the relation between word and meaning characterized by <s>prāpti</s> (physical contact), even if it were to exist in the meaning, would not serve as a reason for <s>anumāna</s> (inference). // 55 //

children.text: tadevaṃ prāptilakṣaṇasya śabdārthasaṃbandhasyārthajuṣo 'py anumānahetur na bhavatīti // 55 //

children.translated_text: What then is this <s>samaya</s> (convention)? It is the binding regulation of designation and designatum: 'of this word, this class of meanings is to be denoted.' When that [convention] is employed, cognition of the meaning arises from the word. In the contrary case, even upon hearing the word, there is no cognition. And this [convention] cannot be avoided even by the proponent of [physical] relation.
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.56: And because there is no restriction [of word-use] across different communities.

The cognition of meaning from words is <s>sāmayika</s> (conventional), not natural. <s>Ṛṣis</s> (sages), <s>āryas</s> (cultured people), and <s>mlecchas</s> (foreigners) employ words as they wish for conveying meaning. If the capacity of words to convey meaning were natural, such arbitrary usage would not be possible—just as the capacity of luminous light to produce cognition of form does not vary across different communities. // 56 //

children.text: sāmayikaḥ śabdārthasaṃpratyayo na svābhāvikaḥ-- ṛṣyāryamlecchānāṃ yathākāmaṃ śabdaprayogo 'rthapratyāyanāya pravartate, svābhāvike hi śabdasyārthapratyāyakatve yathākāmaṃ na syāt, yathā taijasasya prakāśasya rūpapratyayahetutvaṃ na jātiviśeṣaṃ vyabhicaratīti // 56 //

children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 2.1.57: That [<s>śabda</s>] is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge)—because of the defects of <s>anṛta</s> (falsehood), <s>vyāghāta</s> (contradiction), and <s>punarukta</s> (repetition).

Regarding the <s>putrakāmeṣṭi</s> (sacrifice for obtaining a son), the oblation, and repetition—the revered <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) subjects to examination this very specific <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony).

children.text: śabdasya pramāṇatvaṃ na saṃbhavati, kasmāt ?. anṛtadoṣāt-- putrakāmeṣṭau--"putrakāmaḥ putreṣṭyā yajeta"iti. neṣṭau saṃsthitāyāṃ putrajanma dṛśyate, dṛṣṭārthasya vākyasyānṛtatvāt adṛṣṭārthamapi vākyam--"agnihotraṃ juhuyāt svargakāmaḥ"ityādyanṛtamiti jñāyate|
children.translated_text: And because of the defect of contradicting what has been enjoined—regarding the oblation, having enjoined 'one should offer when [the sun] has risen,' 'one should offer when [the sun] has not risen,' 'one should offer when [the sun] is about to rise,' it then contradicts what was enjoined: 'The dark one devours his oblation, he who offers when [the sun] has risen'; 'The spotted one devours his oblation, he who offers when [the sun] has not risen'; 'The dark and spotted ones devour his oblation, he who offers when [the sun] is about to rise.' Because of the contradiction, one or the other must be false.

children.text: vihitavyāghātadoṣācca-- havane"udite hotavyam" "anudite hotavyam" "samayādhyuṣite hotavyam"iti vidhāya vihitaṃ vyāhanti--"śyāvo 'syāhutimabhyavaharati ya udite juhoti" "śabalo 'syāhutimabhyavaharati yo 'nudite juhoti" "śyāvaśavalau vāsyāhutimabhyavaharato yaḥ samayādhyuṣite juhoti" (iti) vyāghātāccānyatarad mithyeti|
children.translated_text: And because of the defect of <s>punarukta</s> (repetition)—when repetition is being taught, 'He recites the first [<s>sāmidhenī</s> verse] three times and the last three times'—there is the defect of repetition. And repetition is the speech of the inattentive. Therefore, <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) is not a <s>pramāṇa</s>—because of the defects of falsehood, contradiction, and repetition. // 57 //

children.text: punaruktadoṣācca-- abhyāse deśyamāne"triḥ prathamāmanvāha triruttamām"iti punaruktadoṣo bhavati. punarukta ca pramattavākyamiti. tasmādapramāṇaṃ śabdaḥ-- anṛtavyāghātapunaruktadoṣebhya iti // 57 //

children.translated_text: The <s>pramāṇa</s>-status (validity) of <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) is not possible. Why? Because of the defect of <s>anṛta</s> (falsehood)—in the <s>putrakāmeṣṭi</s>: 'He who desires a son should sacrifice with the <s>putreṣṭi</s> (son-producing sacrifice).' But upon the completion of the sacrifice, no birth of a son is seen. Since a statement whose visible result [fails] is false, the statement concerning an unseen result—'He who desires <s>svarga</s> (heaven) should offer the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-oblation)'—is also known to be false.
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.58: No, because of deficiency in <s>karma</s> (action), <s>kartṛ</s> (agent), and <s>sādhana</s> (instrument).

There is no defect of <s>anṛta</s> (falsehood) in the <s>putrakāmeṣṭi</s> (sacrifice for obtaining a son). Why? Because of <s>vaiguṇya</s> (deficiency) in <s>karma</s> (action), <s>kartṛ</s> (agent), and <s>sādhana</s> (instrument). The parents, being joined through the <s>iṣṭi</s> (sacrifice), produce a son. The <s>iṣṭi</s> is the <s>karaṇa</s> (instrument), the <s>sādhana</s>. The parents are the <s>kartṛs</s> (agents). The conjunction is the <s>karma</s> (action). From the proper qualification of all three, a son is born. From <s>vaiguṇya</s> (deficiency), the opposite [results]. As for deficiency dependent on the sacrifice: deficiency of <s>karma</s> is failure in proper performance; deficiency of <s>kartṛ</s> is an ignorant performer or one of impure conduct; deficiency of <s>sādhana</s> is that the oblation-material is unrefined or spoiled; the <s>mantras</s> are deficient or excessive, lacking in proper accent or phoneme; the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee) is ill-gotten, deficient, or condemned.

children.text: nānṛtadoṣaḥ putrakāmeṣṭau, kasmāt ?, karmakartṛsādhanavaiguṇyāt, iṣṭyā pitarau saṃyujyamānau putraṃ janayata iti, iṣṭiḥ karaṇam sādhanaṃ. pitarau kartārau. saṃyogaḥ karma. trayāṇāṃ guṇayogāt putrajanma. vaiguṇyād viparyayaḥ, iṣṭyāśrayaṃ tāvat karmavaiguṇyaṃ samīhābhreṣaḥ, kartṛvaiguṇyam avidvān prayoktā kapūyācaraṇaśca, sādhanavaiguṇyaṃ havirasaṃskṛtam upahatamiti. mantrā nyūnādhikāḥ svaravarṇahīnā iti. dakṣiṇā durāgatā hīnā ninditā ceti|
children.translated_text: Furthermore, deficiency dependent on the birth [of the child]: deficiency of <s>karma</s> is improper sexual union; deficiency of <s>kartṛ</s> is disorder of the womb or damage to the seed; deficiency of <s>sādhana</s> has been stated [above] with reference to the sacrifice.

children.text: athopajanāśrayaṃ karmavaiguṇyaṃ mithyāsaṃprayogaḥ, kartṛvaiguṇyaṃ yonivyāpādo bījopaghātaśceti, sādhanavaiguṇyam iṣṭāvabhihitam|
children.translated_text: And in the world too, 'He who desires fire should churn the fire-stick'—this is an injunctive statement. There, deficiency of <s>karma</s> is churning improperly; deficiency of <s>kartṛ</s> is inattention with respect to knowledge and effort; deficiency of <s>sādhana</s> is wet or hollow wood. There the result is not produced, yet there is no defect of <s>anṛta</s> (falsehood), because the production of the result is seen when [all] qualifications are properly present. And this [Vedic injunction] does not differ from the worldly [example]: 'He who desires a son should sacrifice with the <s>putreṣṭi</s>.' // 58 //

children.text: loke ca 'agnikāmo dāruṇī mathnīyāt' iti vidhivākyam tatra karmavaiguṇyaṃ mithyābhimanthānam. kartṛvaiguṇyaṃ prajñāprayatnagataḥ pramādaḥ. sādhanavaiguṇyam ārdraṃ suṣiraṃ dāru iti. tatra phalaṃ na niṣpadyate iti nānṛtadoṣaḥ, guṇayogena phalaniṣpattidarśanāt, na cedaṃ laukikād bhidyate--"putrakāmaḥ putreṣṭyā yajeta"iti // 58 //

children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 2.1.59: Because, having accepted [a particular time], it is a statement of fault regarding deviation from the [accepted] time.

'There is no <s>vyāghāta</s> (contradiction) in the oblation'—this is continued. He who breaks the accepted time of oblation and offers at some other time—regarding him, this fault of deviating from the accepted time is stated: 'The dark one devours his oblation, he who offers when [the sun] has risen.' This is a <s>nindāvacana</s> (statement of censure) regarding deviation from the injunction. // 59 //

children.text: 'na vyāghāto havane' ityanuvartate, yo 'bhyupagataṃ havanakālaṃ bhinatti tato 'nyatra juhoti tatrāyamabhyupagatakālabhedo doṣa ucyate--"śyāvo 'syāhutimabhyavaharati ca udite juhoti"tadidaṃ vidhibhreṣe nindāvacanamiti // 59 //

children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 2.1.60: And because <s>anuvāda</s> (restatement) is appropriate.

'The defect of <s>punarukta</s> (repetition) through recurrence'—this is the topic under discussion. Purposeless recurrence is <s>punarukta</s> (mere repetition). Purposeful recurrence is <s>anuvāda</s> (meaningful restatement). The recurrence that is—

'He recites the first [<s>sāmidhenī</s> verse] three times and the last three times'—this is appropriately an <s>anuvāda</s> (meaningful restatement)—because it has a purpose. For through the threefold recitation of the first and last [verses], the <s>sāmidhenīs</s> become fifteen in number, and accordingly the <s>mantra</s> declares: 'With this fifteen-spoked thunderbolt of speech I strike the rival—him who hates us and whom we hate.' The <s>mantra</s> declares [a weapon of] fifteen <s>sāmidhenīs</s> as a thunderbolt, which would not be possible without the repetition. // 60 //

children.text: "triḥ prathamāmanvāha triruttamām"iti anuvāda upapadyate-- arthavattvāt, trirvacanena hi prathamottamayoḥ pañcadaśatvaṃ sāmadhenīnāṃ bhavati tathā ca mantrābhivādaḥ--"idamahaṃ bhrātṛvyaṃ pañcadaśāreṇa vāgvajreṇa bādhe yo 'smān dveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmaḥ"iti pañcadaśasāmidhenīvajraṃ mantro 'bhivadati tadabhyāsamantareṇa na syāditi // 60 //

children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 2.1.61: And because the meaning is grasped from the division of sentences.
<s>Śabda</s> (verbal testimony) is a <s>pramāṇa</s> (means of valid knowledge), just as in the world. // 61 //
And the division of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> (exegetical) sentences is threefold—
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.62: Because of the distribution into <s>vidhi</s> (injunction), <s>arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage), and <s>anuvāda</s> (restatement) sentences.

Indeed, <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> sentences are distributed in three ways: <s>vidhi</s>-sentences (injunctions), <s>arthavāda</s>-sentences (explanatory passages), and <s>anuvāda</s>-sentences (restatements). // 62 //

children.text: tridhā khalu brāhmaṇavākyāni viniyuktāni-- vidhivacanāni arthavādavacanāni anuvādavacanānīti // 62 //

children.translated_text: Among these—
<s>NyS</s> 2.1.63: <s>Vidhi</s> (injunction) is that which enjoins.
That sentence which enjoins,

which impels—that is <s>vidhi</s> (injunction). And <s>vidhi</s> is either <s>niyoga</s> (binding obligation) or <s>anujñā</s> (permission), as in: 'He who desires <s>svarga</s> (heaven) should offer the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-oblation)'—and so forth. // 63 //

children.text: codakaṃ sa vidhiḥ, vidhistu niyogo 'nujñā vā yathā --"agnihotraṃ juhuyāt svargakāmaḥ" ityādi // 63 //

children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.64: <s>Arthavāda</s> (explanatory passage) consists of praise (<s>stuti</s>), blame (<s>nindā</s>), <s>parakṛti</s> (the practice of another), and <s>purākalpa</s> (ancient precedent). //

children.text:
vidheḥ phalavādalakṣaṇā yā praśaṃsā sā stutiḥ saṃpratyayārthā-- stūyamānaṃ śraddadhīteti, pravartikā ca-- phalaśravaṇāt pravartate--"
sarvajito vai devāḥ sarvamajayan sarvasyāptyai sarvasya jityai sarvameva tenāpnoti sarvaṃ jayati"
ityevamādi|
aniṣṭaphalavādo nindā varjanārthā-- ninditaṃ na samācarediti"
sa eṣa vā va prathamo yajño yajñānāṃ yajjyotiṣṭomo ya etenāniṣṭvānyena yajate garte patati |
ayamevaitad jīryate vā pramīyate vā"
ityevamādi|
anyakartṛkasya vyāhatasya vidhervādaḥ parakṛtiḥ--"
hutvā vapāmevāgre 'bhidhārayanti atha pṛṣadājyaṃ taduha carakādhvaryavaḥ pṛṣadājyamevāgre 'bhidhārayanti 'agneḥ prāṇāḥ pṛṣadājyaṃ stomam' ityevamabhidadhati"
ityevamādi|
aitihyasamācarito vidhiḥ purākalpa iti--"
tasmādvā etena brāhmaṇā bahiṣpavamānaṃ sāmastomamastauṣan-- yone yajñaṃ pratanavāmahe"
children.translated_text: 'Therefore indeed the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> praised the <s>Bahiṣpavamāna</s> <s>Sāma</s> <s>Stoma</s> by this [formula]: "We spread the sacrifice for the singer"'
— and so forth.

children.text: kathaṃ parakṛtipurākalpau arthavādāviti ?, stutinindāvākyenābhisaṃbandhād vidhyāśrayasya kasyacidarthasya dyotanādarthavāda iti // 64 //
children.translated_text: How are <s>parakṛti</s> and <s>purākalpa</s> classified as <s>arthavāda</s>? Because, through their connection with statements of praise or blame, they illuminate some meaning that serves as a basis for an injunction — [therefore they are] <s>arthavāda</s>. // 64 //

Praise (<s>stuti</s>) is commendation characterized by stating the result of an injunction; its purpose is to inspire conviction — 'one should believe what is praised'; and it is motivating — because of hearing the result, one is motivated [to act]. [Example:] 'The <s>Sarvajit</s> [sacrifice] is indeed [for] the gods; by the <s>Sarvajit</s> they conquered everything — for the attainment of everything, for the conquest of everything; by it one indeed attains everything, conquers everything' — and so forth. Blame (<s>nindā</s>) is the statement of an undesirable result, for the purpose of avoidance — 'one should not practice what is blamed.' [Example:] 'This is indeed the first sacrifice among sacrifices, namely the <s>Jyotiṣṭoma</s>; whoever, without having performed this, sacrifices with another, falls into a pit. This one indeed grows old or dies' — and so forth. <s>Parakṛti</s> (the practice of another) is the statement of an injunction performed by another [authority] that contradicts [the standard practice]. [Example:] 'Having offered the omentum first, they then offer the curds-and-ghee (<s>pṛṣadājya</s>). But the <s>Caraka</s> <s>Adhvaryus</s> offer the curds-and-ghee first, saying: "The vital breaths of <s>Agni</s> are the curds-and-ghee, the <s>stoma</s>"' — and so forth. <s>Purākalpa</s> (ancient precedent) is an injunction established by traditional report and practice. [Example:]
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.65: The repetition of what has been enjoined by an injunction is <s>anuvāda</s> (reiteration). //

children.text:
vidhyanuvacanaṃ cānuvādo vihitānuvacanaṃ ca |
pūrvaḥ śabdānuvādo 'paro 'rthānuvādaḥ, yathā punaruktaṃ dvividham evamanuvādopi|
kimarthaṃ punarvihitamanūdyate ?, adhikārārtham |
vihitamadhikṛtya stutirbodhyate nindā vā vidhiśeṣo vābhidhiyate, vihitānantarārtho 'pi cānuvādo bhavati, evamanyadapyutprekṣaṇīyam|
children.translated_text: Taking what has been enjoined as the context, praise or blame or a supplementary injunction is stated. And <s>anuvāda</s> also serves as a prelude to what immediately follows the injunction. Other [functions] should be similarly understood.

children.text: lokepi ca vidhirarthavādo 'nuvāda iti ca trividhaṃ vākyam-- 'odanaṃ pacet' iti vidhivākyam, arthavādavākyam-- 'āyurvarco balaṃ sukhaṃ pratibhānaṃ cānne pratiṣṭhitam', anuvādaḥ-- 'pacatu pacatu bhavān' ityabhyāsaḥ, 'kṣipraṃ pacyatām' iti vā 'aṅga pacyatām' iti (vā) adhyeṣaṇārtham, 'pacyatāmeva' iti cāvadhāraṇārtham|
children.translated_text: In the world too, there is a threefold [classification of] statements: injunction, <s>arthavāda</s>, and <s>anuvāda</s>. 'He should cook rice' is an injunctive statement. An <s>arthavāda</s> statement: 'Life-span, splendor, strength, happiness, and intelligence are established in food.' <s>Anuvāda</s>: 'Let him cook, let him cook!' — this is repetition; or 'Let it be cooked quickly!' or 'Please let it be cooked!' — for the purpose of urging; 'Let it indeed be cooked!' — for the purpose of emphasis.

children.text: yathā laukike vākye vibhāgenārthagrahaṇāt pramāṇatvam evaṃ vedavākyānāmapi vibhāgenārthagrahaṇāt pramāṇatvaṃ bhavitumarhatīti // 65 //
children.translated_text: Just as in worldly statements, validity (<s>prāmāṇya</s>) arises from grasping the meaning through analysis, so too for Vedic statements, validity should arise from grasping the meaning through analysis. // 65 //

<s>Anuvāda</s> is both the reiteration of an injunction and the reiteration of what has been enjoined. The former is verbal reiteration (<s>śabdānuvāda</s>), the latter is reiteration of meaning (<s>arthānuvāda</s>) — just as repetition (<s>punaruktam</s>) is twofold, so too is <s>anuvāda</s>. For what purpose is what has been enjoined reiterated? For the purpose of [providing] a context (<s>adhikāra</s>).

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.66: [Objection:] There is no distinction between <s>anuvāda</s> (reiteration) and <s>punarukta</s> (redundant repetition), since the occurrence of verbal repetition is possible [in both]. //

children.text: kasmāt ?. ubhayatra hi pratītārthaḥ śabdo 'bhyastate. caritārthasya śabdasyābhyāsādubhayamasādhviti // 66 //
children.translated_text: Why? Because in both cases, a word whose meaning has already been understood is repeated. Since a word that has served its purpose is repeated — both [cases] are faulty. // 66 //
'Redundant repetition is faulty; reiteration is proper' — this distinction is not justifiable.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.67: [Reply:] There is no non-distinction [between the two], just as in the instruction to go faster and faster — because of the [different function of] repetition. //

children.text: kasmāt ?, arthavato 'bhyāsasyānuvādabhāvāt, samāne 'bhyāse punaruktam anarthakam arthavānabhyāso 'nuvādaḥ-- śīghrataragamanopadeśavat 'śīghraṃ śīghraṃ gamyatām' iti kriyātiśayo 'bhyāsenaivocyate. udāharaṇārthaṃ cedam, evamanyopyabhyāsaḥ-- 'pacati pacatīti kriyānuparamaḥ, 'grāmo grāmo ramaṇīyaḥ' iti vyāptiḥ, 'pari pari trigartebhyo vṛṣṭo devaḥ' iti parivarjanam, 'adhyadhimaṇḍaṃ niṣaṇṇam, iti sāmīpyam, 'tiktaṃ tiktam' iti prakāraḥ, evamanuvādasya stutinindāśeṣavidhiṣu adhikārārthatāvihitānantarārthatā ceti // 67 //
children.translated_text: Why? Because meaningful repetition has the nature of <s>anuvāda</s>. When the repetition is the same [in form], redundant repetition is meaningless, [but] meaningful repetition is <s>anuvāda</s> — like the instruction to go faster and faster: 'Go quickly! quickly!' — by the repetition itself, an intensification of the action is expressed. This is [given] for the sake of illustration; thus too with other [types of] repetition: '<s>pacati pacati</s>' ('he cooks and cooks') [indicates] non-cessation of the action; '<s>grāmo grāmo ramaṇīyaḥ</s>' ('every village is delightful') [indicates] universality; '<s>pari pari trigartebhyo vṛṣṭo devaḥ</s>' ('the god rained all around except for the <s>Trigarta</s> people') [indicates] exclusion; '<s>adhyadhimaṇḍaṃ niṣaṇṇam</s>' ('seated right on the platform') [indicates] proximity; '<s>tiktaṃ tiktam</s>' ('bitter, bitter') [indicates] degree. Thus, <s>anuvāda</s> serves the function of providing context for praise, blame, and supplementary injunctions, as well as being a prelude to what immediately follows [the injunction]. // 67 //
There is no non-distinction between <s>anuvāda</s> and <s>punarukta</s>.

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ pratiṣedhahetūddhārādeva śabdasya pramāṇatvaṃ sidhyati ?. na, ataśca---
children.translated_text: [Question:] Is the validity of <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony) established merely by refuting the counter-arguments? No; and therefore —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.1.68: Just like the validity of <s>mantras</s> and <s>Āyurveda</s>, the validity [of the <s>Veda</s>] is due to the validity of reliable persons (<s>āpta</s>). //

children.text:
kiṃ punarāyurvedasya prāmāṇyam ?, yattadāyurvedenopadiśyate-- 'idaṃ kṛtveṣṭamadhigacchati idaṃ varjayitvāniṣṭaṃ jahāti' (iti) tasyānuṣṭhīyamānasya tathābhāvaḥ |

aviparyayaḥ, mantrapadānāṃ ca viṣabhūtāśanipratiṣedhārthānāṃ prayoge 'rthasya tathābhāvaḥ. etat prāmānaṇyam|

loke ca bhūyānupadeśāśrayo vyavahāraḥ, laukikasyāpyupadeṣṭurupadeṣṭavyāthejñānena parānujighṛkṣayā yathābhūtārthacikhyāpayiṣayā ca prāmāṇyam tatparigrahādāptopadeśaḥ pramāṇamiti|
