anityaḥ sa iti cet ? aviśeṣavacanam |
anāptopadeśo laikiko na nitya iti kāraṇaṃ vācyamiti|
children.translated_text: A reason should be stated [for why] worldly instruction by non-<s>āptas</s> is not eternal.

children.text: yathāniyogaṃ cārthasya pratyāyanād nāmadheyaśabdānāṃ loke prāmāṇyam. nityatvāt prāmāṇyānupapattiḥ |
children.translated_text: The validity of name-words in the world [arises] from their being conveyed according to convention (<s>niyoga</s>) with respect to [their] meaning. [If it arose] from eternality, validity would be unjustifiable.

children.text: yatrārthe nāmadheyaśabdo niyujyate loke tasya niyogasāmarthyāt pratyāyako bhavati na nityatvāt|
children.translated_text: The name-word that is conventionally applied to a meaning in the world — by the force of that convention it becomes a means of conveying [meaning], not because of eternality.

children.text: manvantarayugāntareṣu cātītānāgateṣu saṃpradāyābhyāsaprayogāviccheda iti vedānāṃ nityatvam. āptaprāmāṇyācca prāmāṇyam, laukikeṣu śabdeṣu caitat samānamiti // 68 //
children.translated_text: And in [the succession of] <s>Manvantaras</s> and <s>Yugas</s> past and future, the unbroken continuity of tradition, repetition, and usage — this is the eternality of the <s>Vedas</s>. And [their] validity is from the validity of <s>āptas</s>; and this is the same in worldly words as well. // 68 //

What is the validity of <s>Āyurveda</s>? That which is taught by <s>Āyurveda</s> — 'by doing this one attains what is desired; by avoiding this one abandons what is undesired' — when practiced, it is found to be so. It has truthful content. It is non-erroneous. And when <s>mantra</s>-words whose purpose is to counteract poison, spirits, and lightning are employed, the meaning is found to be as [stated]. This is [their] validity. What produces this? The validity of reliable persons (<s>āpta</s>). And what is the validity of <s>āptas</s>? [It consists of] having directly realized <s>dharma</s>, compassion for beings, and the desire to communicate things as they truly are. The <s>āptas</s> indeed, having directly realized <s>dharma</s>, out of compassion for beings [think]: 'This is to be abandoned; this is its cause of abandonment. This is to be attained; this is its cause of attainment' — and thus they instruct. For those living beings who do not understand on their own, there is no other cause of understanding than instruction; and without understanding, there is neither purposeful action nor avoidance; and without acting, there is no well-being; nor is there any other benefactor for them. 'Come, let us instruct them as we have seen, as things truly are; they, hearing and understanding, will abandon what is to be abandoned and will attain what is to be attained' — thus is the instruction of <s>āptas</s>. When embraced through this threefold validity of <s>āptas</s> and practiced, it becomes the means of establishing the meaning. Thus, the instruction of <s>āptas</s> is a <s>pramāṇa</s>; thus, <s>āptas</s> are a <s>pramāṇa</s>. By the instruction of <s>āptas</s> whose object is seen — by <s>Āyurveda</s> — the portion of the <s>Veda</s> whose object is unseen should be inferred to be a <s>pramāṇa</s>, because the reason — the validity of <s>āptas</s> — is the same. And a portion of this [<s>Veda</s>] too — 'One who desires a village should sacrifice' and the like — has a seen object; by that too it should be inferred [to be valid]. And in the world, the greater part of practical activity relies on instruction; the validity of even a worldly instructor [derives from his] knowledge of what is to be taught, his desire to benefit others, and his desire to communicate things as they truly are — and from the acceptance of that [validity], the instruction of <s>āptas</s> is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. And by inference from the commonality of seer and proclaimer — those very <s>āptas</s> who are the seers and proclaimers of the Vedic meanings are [also the seers and proclaimers] of <s>Āyurveda</s> and the rest — so the validity of the <s>Veda</s> should be inferred like the validity of <s>Āyurveda</s>. [Objection:] Because of the eternality of Vedic statements, [grounding] validity on the validity of <s>āptas</s> is inappropriate. [Reply:] <s>Śabda</s> (word) has validity as a <s>pramāṇa</s> for the apprehension of meaning because of its expressive capacity (<s>vācakatva</s>); for if [words were] eternal, since everything would be said by everything, the fixed correspondence of word and meaning would be unjustifiable. [Objection:] 'There is no expressive capacity if [words are] non-eternal'? [Reply:] No — because meaning is observed in worldly [words]. [Objection:] 'Those too are eternal'? [Reply:] No — because the miscommunication of meaning from the instruction of unreliable persons would be unjustifiable [if words were inherently valid due to eternality]. For [on that view], since <s>śabda</s> is a <s>pramāṇa</s> because of eternality [alone, there could be no error]. [Objection:] 'It is non-eternal'? [Reply:] That is a statement without specification.
// End of the first lesson of the second chapter of <s>Vātsyāyana's</s> <s>Nyāyabhāṣya</s> //
Now the second lesson of the second chapter of the <s>Nyāyabhāṣya</s>. //
Thinking that the enumeration of <s>pramāṇas</s> is not accurate, he says —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.1: [Objection:] There are not [only] four [<s>pramāṇas</s>], because of the validity of <s>aitihya</s> (tradition), <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), <s>saṃbhava</s> (inclusion), and <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence). //

children.text:
na catvāryeva pramāṇāni|
kiṃ tarhi ?. aitihyamarthāpattiḥ saṃbhavo 'bhāva ityetānyapi pramāṇāni tāni kasmānnoktāni ?|
'iti hocuḥ' ity anirdiṣṭapravaktṛkaṃ pravādapāramparyam aitihyam|
arthādā pattiḥ arthāpattiḥ. āpattiḥ |
prāptiḥ |
prasaṅgaḥ, yatrābhidhīyamāne 'rthe yo 'nyo 'rthaḥ prasajyate so 'rthāpattiḥ yathā-- 'megheṣv asatsu vṛṣṭirna bhavatīti, kimatra prasajyate ? 'tatsu bhavatīti|
children.translated_text: consequence: when a certain meaning is stated, another meaning that necessarily follows is <s>arthāpatti</s>. For example: 'When there are no clouds, rain does not occur' — what follows here? 'When there are [clouds], it does occur.'

children.text: saṃbhavo nāma avinābhāvino 'rthasya sattāgrahaṇādanyasya sattagrahaṇaṃ yathā-- droṇasya sattāgrahaṇā-- dāḍhakasya sattāgrahaṇam. āḍhakasya grahaṇāt prasthasyeti|
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃbhava</s> (inclusion) is the grasping of the existence of one thing from the grasping of the existence of another thing that cannot exist without it. For example: from the grasping of the existence of a <s>droṇa</s> [measure], the grasping of the existence of an <s>āḍhaka</s> [measure]; from the grasping of an <s>āḍhaka</s>, [the grasping of] a <s>prastha</s>.

children.text: abhāvaḥ-- virodhī abhūtaṃ bhūtasya. avidyamānaṃ varṣakarma vidyamānasya vāyvabhrasaṃyogasya pratipādakam-- vidhārake hi vāyvabhrasaṃyoge gurutvādapāṃ patanakarma na bhavatīti // 1 //
children.translated_text: <s>Abhāva</s> (non-existence) — [is] the contradictory; the non-existent [demonstrates] the existent. The non-existing action of rain demonstrates the existing conjunction of wind and clouds — for when the obstructing conjunction of wind and clouds [exists], the action of falling of water does not occur because of [its] heaviness. // 1 //

There are not only four <s>pramāṇas</s>. What then? <s>Aitihya</s> (tradition), <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption), <s>saṃbhava</s> (inclusion), and <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence) — these too are <s>pramāṇas</s>; why were they not stated? 'Thus they spoke' — a succession of reports without a specified originator is <s>aitihya</s> (tradition). <s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is the arrival (<s>āpatti</s>) of a meaning from [another] meaning — arrival means attainment,

children.text: satyam etāni pramāṇāni na tu pramāṇāntarāṇi. pramāṇāntaraṃ ca manyamānena pratiṣedha ucyate so 'yam--
children.translated_text: These are indeed <s>pramāṇas</s>, but not additional <s>pramāṇas</s> [beyond the four]. The refutation directed to one who considers them additional <s>pramāṇas</s> is this —

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.2: [Reply:] There is no refutation [of the fourfold classification], because <s>aitihya</s> is not a meaning different from <s>śabda</s> (verbal testimony), and because <s>arthāpatti</s>, <s>saṃbhava</s>, and <s>abhāva</s> are not meanings different from <s>anumāna</s> (inference). //

children.text: katham?, 'āptopadeśaḥ śabdaḥ' iti. na ca śabdalakṣaṇam aitihyād vyāvartate. soyaṃ bhedaḥ sāmānyāt saṃgṛhyate iti|
children.translated_text: How? '<s>Śabda</s> is the instruction of a reliable person (<s>āpta</s>).' And the definition of <s>śabda</s> does not exclude <s>aitihya</s>. This specific [case] is subsumed under the general [category].

children.text: pratyakṣeṇāpratyakṣasya saṃbaddhasya prapittiranumānaṃ tathā cārthāpattisaṃbhavābhāvāḥ, vākyārthasaṃpratyayenānabhihitasyārthasya pratyakanīkabhāvād grahaṇam arthāpattiranumānameva, avinābhāvavṛttyā ca saṃbaddhayoḥ samudāyasamudāyinoḥ samudāyenetarasya grahaṇaṃ saṃbhavaḥ tadapyanumānameva, 'asmin satīdaṃ nopapadyate' iti virodhitve prasiddhe kāryānutpattyā kāraṇasya pratibandhakamanumīyate|
children.translated_text: The apprehension of something imperceptible that is connected with something perceptible through perception is <s>anumāna</s> (inference); and so too are <s>arthāpatti</s>, <s>saṃbhava</s>, and <s>abhāva</s>. <s>Arthāpatti</s> — the grasping, through the comprehension of the meaning of a sentence, of an unstated meaning that is the counterpart [of the stated meaning] — is indeed just inference. <s>Saṃbhava</s> — the grasping of one [measure] from the whole and the parts that are inseparably related through invariable concomitance — is also indeed just inference. [<s>Abhāva</s>:] 'When this exists, this other is unjustifiable' — when the contradiction is established, the obstruction of the cause is inferred from the non-production of the effect.

children.text: soyaṃ yathārtha eva pramāṇoddeśa iti 'satyametāni pramāṇāni na tu pramāṇāntarāṇītyuktam // 2 //
children.translated_text: Thus, the enumeration of <s>pramāṇas</s> is indeed accurate — [hence] it was said 'These are indeed <s>pramāṇas</s>, but not additional <s>pramāṇas</s>.' // 2 //
The refutation is unjustifiable.
Here, the approval of <s>arthāpatti</s> as a <s>pramāṇa</s> is unjustifiable, for thus —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.3: [Objection:] <s>Arthāpatti</s> (presumption) is not a [valid] <s>pramāṇa</s>, because of its inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntikatva</s>). //

children.text: asatsu megheṣu vṛṣṭirna bhavatīti satsu bhavati ityetadārthādāpadyate. satsvapi caikadā na bhavati. seyamarthāpattirapramāṇamiti // 3 //
children.translated_text: 'When there are no clouds, rain does not occur' — from this, the meaning 'when there are [clouds], it does occur' is presumed. But even when they are present, sometimes it does not occur. Thus, this <s>arthāpatti</s> is not a [valid] <s>pramāṇa</s>. // 3 //
<s>Arthāpatti</s> is not inconclusive —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.4: [Reply:] Because of the false presumption of <s>arthāpatti</s> where there is no [genuine] <s>arthāpatti</s>. //

children.text:
'asati kāraṇe kāryaṃ notpadyate' itivākyāt pratyanīkabhūto 'rthaḥ-- 'sati kāraṇe kāryamutpadyate' ityarthādāpadyate. abhāvasya hi bhāvaḥ pratyanīka iti. soyaṃ kāryotpādaḥ sati kāraṇe 'rthādāpadyamāno na kāraṇasya sattāṃ vyabhicarati-- na khalv asati kāraṇe kāryamutpadyate tasmād nānaikāntikī|
yattu 'sati kāraṇe nimittapratibandhāt kāryaṃ notpadyate' iti ?. kāraṇadharmo 'sau na tvarthāpatteḥ prameyam|
kiṃ tarhyasyāḥ prameyam ?, sati kāraṇe kāryamupadyate iti |
yo 'sau kāryotpādaḥ kāraṇasattāṃ na vyabhicarati tadasyāḥ prameyam|
evaṃ tu sati anarthāpattau arthāpattyabhimānaṃ kṛtvā pratiṣedha ucyate iti, dṛṣṭaśca kāraṇadharmo na śakyaḥ pratyākhyātumiti // 4 1/
children.translated_text: This being so, [when the opponent argues] that <s>arthāpatti</s> is not [valid] — pretending there is <s>arthāpatti</s> [and then] stating a refutation — the observed property of the cause cannot be denied. //4//

From the statement 'when the cause is absent, the effect does not arise,' the opposite meaning follows by implication — 'when the cause is present, the effect arises.' For existence (<s>bhāva</s>) is the opposite of non-existence (<s>abhāva</s>). This arising of the effect, following by implication from the presence of the cause, does not deviate from the existence of the cause — for indeed, the effect does not arise when the cause is absent; therefore, [<s>arthāpatti</s>] is not inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>). As for [the objection] 'when the cause is present, the effect does not arise due to the obstruction of a cooperating cause' — that is a property of the cause, not the object of <s>arthāpatti</s> as a <s>pramāṇa</s>. What then is its object as a <s>pramāṇa</s>? 'When the cause is present, the effect arises.' The arising of the effect does not deviate from the existence of the cause — that is its object as a <s>pramāṇa</s>.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.5: And the invalidity of the refutation [itself follows] from [its] inconclusiveness.

children.text: 'arthāpattir na pramāṇam-- anaikāntikatvāt' iti vākyaṃ pratiṣedhaḥ tenānena arthāpatteḥ pramāṇatvaṃ pratiṣidhyate na sadbhāvaḥ, evamanaikāntiko bhavati. anaikāntikatvādapramāṇenānena na kaścidarthaḥ pratiṣidhyate iti // 5 //
children.translated_text: The statement '<s>arthāpatti</s> is not a <s>pramāṇa</s> — because of inconclusiveness' is the refutation. By this, the validity of <s>arthāpatti</s> as a <s>pramāṇa</s> is being denied, not its existence. [But] it is thus itself inconclusive. Because of its inconclusiveness, no purpose is denied by this invalid [argument]. //5//

children.text: artha manyase niyataviṣayeṣvartheṣu svaviṣaye vyabhicāro bhavati. na ca pratiṣedhasya sadbhāvo viṣayaḥ ?, evaṃ tarhi---
children.translated_text: You think [each <s>pramāṇa</s>] has its own restricted domain and deviation occurs in [another's] domain. And the existence [of <s>arthāpatti</s>] is not the subject of the refutation? If so, then —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.6: Or, if that [refutation] is valid, then the invalidity of <s>arthāpatti</s> [does not follow].

children.text: athāṅpatterapi kāryotpādane kāraṇasattāyā avyabhicāro viṣayaḥ na ca kāraṇadharmo nimittapratibandhāt kāyāṅnutpādakatvamiti // 6 //
children.translated_text: If the non-deviation of <s>arthāpatti</s> too — the non-deviation of the cause's existence from the arising of the effect — is its domain, and the property of the cause — the non-production [of the effect] due to obstruction of a cooperating cause — [is not its domain], then [<s>arthāpatti</s> is valid]. //6//
The acceptance of <s>abhāva</s> (non-existence) as a <s>pramāṇa</s> is untenable. How?
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.7: <s>Abhāva</s> (non-existence) is not a [valid] <s>pramāṇa</s>, because its <s>prameya</s> (object of knowledge) is not established.
Regarding <s>abhāva</s> — the majority of objects of knowledge being well-known in the world — it is said by way of distinction:
'<s>Abhāva</s> is not a [valid] <s>pramāṇa</s> — because its <s>prameya</s> is not established.'
Now, since the subject has many aspects, a partial example is given —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.8: The <s>prameya</s> of that [<s>abhāva</s>] is established for the unmarked, because [they are] recognized by the absence of marks in [contrast with] the marked.

children.text: katham ?. lakṣiteṣu vāsaḥsu anupādeyeṣu, upādeyānāmalakṣitānām alakṣaṇalakṣitatvāt = lakṣaṇābhāvena lakṣitatvāditi, ubhayasaṃnidhau' alakṣitāni vāsāṃsyānaya' iti prayukto yeṣu vāsaḥsatu lakṣaṇāni na bhavanti tāni lakṣaṇābhāvena pratipadyate pratipadya cānayati pratipattihetuśca pramāṇamiti // 8 //
children.translated_text: How? Regarding marked garments that are not to be taken, the unmarked ones that are to be taken [are recognized] because of being recognized by the absence of marks — that is, by [their] being recognized through the non-existence of marks. In the presence of both, when directed 'bring the unmarked garments,' one understands those garments in which marks do not exist by the absence of marks, and having understood, brings them. And the means of understanding is a <s>pramāṇa</s>. //8//
The <s>prameya</s> of that <s>abhāva</s> is established.

children.text: NyS_2,2.9: asatyarthe nābhāva iti cen nānyalakṣaṇopapatteḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.9: [Objection:] If [<s>abhāva</s> is argued as invalid] because [the marks] have never existed in the [unmarked] object? No — because of the justification from other [objects having] marks.

children.text: yatra bhūtvā kiñcinna bhavati tatra tasyābhāva upapadyate. na cālakṣiteṣu vāsaḥsu lakṣaṇāni bhūtvā na bhavanti. tasmātteṣu lakṣaṇābhāvo 'nupapanna iti, na-- anyalakṣaṇopapatteḥ |
children.translated_text: Where something, having existed, ceases to exist — there, the absence of that is justified. But in the unmarked garments, marks have not existed and then ceased to exist. Therefore the absence of marks in them is untenable. [Reply:] No — because of the justification from other [objects having] marks.

children.text: yathāyamanyeṣu vāsaḥsu lakṣaṇānāmupapattiṃ paśyati naivamalakṣiteṣu soyaṃ lakṣaṇābhāvaṃ paśyan abhāvenārthaṃ pratipadyate iti // 9 //
children.translated_text: Just as one sees the presence of marks in other garments but not in the unmarked ones — seeing the absence of marks, one understands the object by [its] non-existence. //9//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.10: Because of their [marks'] existence in the marked [garments], [the argument] is a non-reason for the unmarked.
The marks exist in those [marked] garments.

children.text: vidyamānatā yeṣāṃ bhavati na teṣāmabhāvo lakṣaṇānām |
children.translated_text: Those marks whose existence obtains — there is no absence of them.

children.text: yāni ca lakṣiteṣu vidyante lakṣaṇāni teṣāmalakṣiteṣvabhāva ity ahetuḥ-- yāni khalu bhavanti teṣāmabhāvo vyāhata iti // 10 //
children.translated_text: And the marks that exist in the marked — that their absence [exists] in the unmarked is a non-reason — for the absence of those that exist is contradictory. //10//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.11: No — because of the establishment of the expectation regarding the [marks'] being situated [in some garments but not others].

children.text: na brūmo yāni lakṣaṇāni bhavanti teṣāmabhāva iti kiṃ tu keṣu cillakṣaṇānyavasthitāni, anavasthitāni keṣucit. apekṣamāṇo yeṣu lakṣaṇānāṃ bhāvaṃ na paśyati tāni lakṣaṇābhāvena prapidyate iti // 11 //
children.translated_text: We do not say that there is absence of those marks that exist. Rather, marks are situated in some [garments], and not situated in others. When one, expecting [marks], does not see the existence of marks in some [garments], one understands those by the absence of marks. //11//
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.12: And because <s>abhāva</s> (absence) before origination is justified.

children.text: abhāvadvaitaṃ khalu bhavati-- prāk cotpatteravidyamānatā. utpannasya cātmano hānādavidyamānatā. tatrālakṣiteṣu vāsaḥsu prāgutpatteravidyamānatālakṣaṇo lakṣaṇānāmabhāvo netara iti // 12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Abhāva</s> is indeed twofold — prior non-existence before origination, and non-existence due to the destruction of what has originated. Among these, in the unmarked garments, the absence of marks is of the nature of prior non-existence — non-existence before origination — not the other [type]. //12//

children.text:
"āptopadeśaḥ śabdaḥ 1-1-7"
iti pramāṇabhāve viśeṣaṇaṃ bruvatā 'nānāprakāraḥ śabdaḥ' iti jñāpyate. tasmin sāmānyena vicāraḥ-- kiṃ nityo 'thānityaḥ ? iti, vimarśahetvanuyoge ca vipratipatteḥ saṃśayaḥ, 'ākāśaguṇaḥ śabdo vibhurnityo 'bhivyaktidharmakaḥ' ityeke, gandhādisahavṛttirdravyeṣu saṃniviṣṭo gandhādivadavasthito 'bhivyaktidharmakaḥ' ityapare, 'ākāśaguṇaḥ śabda utpattinirodhadharmako buddhivat' ityapare, 'mahābhūtasaṃkṣobhajaḥ śabdo 'nāśrita utpattidharmako nirodhadharmakaḥ' ityanye. ataḥ saṃśayaḥ-- kimatra tattvam ? iti, 'anityaḥ śabdaḥ' ityuttaram |
children.translated_text: '<s>Āptopadeśa</s> (reliable testimony) is <s>śabda</s>' [NyS 1.1.7] — by stating a qualification for its being a <s>pramāṇa</s>, it is indicated that '<s>śabda</s> is of many kinds.' Regarding it, a general inquiry [arises]: is it permanent or impermanent? And when the reason for deliberation is demanded, [there is] doubt from disagreement. Some [say]: '<s>Śabda</s> is a quality of <s>ākāśa</s> (space), all-pervading, permanent, subject to manifestation.' Others [say]: '<s>Śabda</s> co-exists with odor and the rest, is situated in substances, is fixed like odor and the rest, subject to manifestation.' Others [say]: '<s>Śabda</s> is a quality of <s>ākāśa</s>, subject to origination and cessation, like <s>buddhi</s> (cognition).' Still others [say]: '<s>Śabda</s> is born from the agitation of the great elements, is unsupported, subject to origination and cessation.' Hence the doubt: what is the truth here? The answer: '<s>Śabda</s> is impermanent.'
How?
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.13: Because [<s>śabda</s>] has a beginning, because it is sensory, and because of figurative usage as with produced things.

children.text:
ādiḥuyoniḥukāraṇam-- ādīyate 'smāditi. kāraṇavad anityaṃ dṛṣṭam. saṃyogavibhāgajaśca śabdaḥ kāraṇavattvādanitya iti|
kā punariyam arthadeśānā-- 'kāraṇavattvāt' iti ?, utpattidharmakattvādanityaḥ śabda iti = bhūtvā na bhavati = vināśadharmaka iti|
sāṃśayikametat-- kimutpattikāraṇaṃ saṃyogavibhāgau śabdasya ? āhosvidabhivyaktikāraṇam?. ityata āha-- aindriyakatvāt (iti) indriyapratyāsattigrāhya aindriyakaḥ|
kimayaṃ vyañjakena samānadeśo 'bhivyajyate rūpādivat ? atha saṃyogajācchabdācchabdasaṃtāne sati śrotrapratyāsanno gṛhyate ? iti--- saṃyoganivṛttau śabdagrahaṇānna vyañjakena samānadeśasya grahaṇam1|
dāruvraścane dāruparaśusaṃyoganivṛttau dūrasthena śabdo gṛhyate. na ca vyañjakābhāve vyaṅgyagrahaṇaṃ bhavati tasmānna vyañjakaḥ saṃyogaḥ, utpādake tu saṃyoge saṃyogajācchabdācchabdasantāne sati śrotrapratyāsannasya grahaṇamiti yuktaṃ saṃyoganivṛttau śabdasya grahaṇamiti|
itaścaśabda utpadyate nābhivyajyate-- kṛtakavadupacārātu 'tīvraṃ mandam' iti kṛtakamupacaryate-- 'tīvraṃ sukhaṃ mandaṃ sukham. tīvraṃ duḥkhaṃ mandaṃ duḥkham' iti. upacaryate ca-- 'tīvraḥ śabdo mandaḥ śabdaḥ' iti|
vyañjakasya tathābhāvād grahaṇasya tīvramandatā rūpavaditi cet ? na-- abhibhavopapatteḥ|
saṃyogasya vyañjakasya tīvramandatayā śabdagrahaṇasya tīvramandatā bhavati na tu śabdo bhidyate yathā prakāśasya tīvramandatayā rūpagrahaṇasyeti, tacca naivam-- abhibhavopapatteḥu tīvro bherīśabdo mandaṃ tantrīśabdam abhibhavati na mandaḥ, na ca śabdagrahaṇamabhibhāvakaṃ śabdaśca na bhidyate (iti), śabde tu bhidyamāne yukto 'bhibhavaḥ tasmādutpadyate śabdo nābhivyajyate iti|
abhibhavānupapattiśyaca-- vyañjakasamānadeśasyābhivyaktau prāptyabhāvāt3|
'vyañjakena samānadeśo 'bhivyajyate śabdaḥ' ityetasmin pakṣe nopapadyate 'bhibhavaḥ-- na hi bherīśabdena tantrīsvanaḥ prāpta iti|
aprāpte 'bhibhava iticet ? śabdamātrābhibhavaprasaṅgaḥ4|

artha manyeta 'asatyāṃ prāptāvabhibhavo bhavatīti, evaṃ sati yathā bherīśabdaḥ kañcit tantrīsvanamabhibhavati evamantikasthopādānāniva davīyaḥsthopādānānapi tantrīsvanānabhibhavet-- aprāpteraviśeṣāt. tatra kvacideva bheryā praṇāditāyāṃ sarvalokeṣu samānakālāstantrīsvanā na śrūyeran iti|
children.translated_text: One might think 'overriding occurs without conjunction.' If so, just as a drum-sound overrides some string-sound, it would also override string-sounds produced at a great distance, just as those produced nearby — because there is no distinction in the absence of conjunction. Then, whenever a drum is sounded, all string-sounds in all regions at the same time would not be heard.

children.text: nānābhūteṣu śabdasantāneṣu satsu śrotrapratyāsattibhāvena kasyacicchabdasyautīvreṇa mandasyābhibhavo yukta iti|
children.translated_text: When sound-series are diverse [and existing separately], overriding of a faint sound by an intense one near the ear is justified, because of [their] proximity to the ear.

children.text: kaḥ punarayamabhibhavo nāma ?, grāhyasamānajātīyagrahaṇakṛtamagrahaṇam abhibhavaḥ yatholkāprakāśasya grahaṇārhasyādityaprakāśeneti // 13 //
children.translated_text: What indeed is this overriding? Non-apprehension caused by the apprehension of something of the same kind as the apprehensible — that is overriding; as, for example, the light of a torch, though fit to be apprehended, [is overridden] by sunlight. //13//

'Beginning' (<s>ādi</s>) means source, cause — 'it is begun from this.' What has a cause is observed to be impermanent. And <s>śabda</s>, born from conjunction and disjunction, is impermanent because of having a cause. But what is this specificity of meaning — 'because of having a cause'? <s>Śabda</s> is impermanent because of being subject to origination — it comes into being and then ceases to be — it is subject to destruction. [Objection:] This is doubtful — are conjunction and disjunction the cause of origination of <s>śabda</s>? Or the cause of its manifestation? Therefore he says: because it is sensory (<s>aindriyaka</s>) — that which is grasped by proximity to the sense-organ is <s>aindriyaka</s>. Is this [<s>śabda</s>] manifested in the same location as the manifester, like color and the rest? Or, in a series of sounds arising from the initial sound born of conjunction, is [<s>śabda</s>] grasped when it comes near the ear? [Answer:] From the grasping of <s>śabda</s> when the conjunction ceases, [it follows that] grasping is not of something in the same location as the manifester. When wood is being split, at the cessation of the conjunction of wood and axe, a distant person grasps the <s>śabda</s>. And in the absence of a manifester, there is no grasping of the manifestable; therefore conjunction is not a manifester. But with conjunction as the producer, in a series of sounds [produced] from the initial sound born of conjunction, the grasping of what is near the ear is justified — [thus] the grasping of <s>śabda</s> upon the cessation of conjunction [is explained]. And furthermore, <s>śabda</s> is produced, not manifested — because of figurative usage as with produced things: 'intense, faint' is figuratively applied to produced things — 'intense pleasure, faint pleasure; intense pain, faint pain.' And the figurative usage: 'intense sound, faint sound.' [Objection:] Because the manifester is [intense or faint], the grasping is intense or faint, as with color? No — because overriding (<s>abhibhava</s>) is justified. Because of the intensity and faintness of conjunction as the manifester, the grasping of <s>śabda</s> would be intense or faint — but the <s>śabda</s> itself is not differentiated — just as by the intensity and faintness of light, the grasping of color [varies]. But that is not so — because overriding is justified: an intense drum-sound overrides a faint string-sound, not the faint [overriding the intense]. And it is not the case that the grasping of <s>śabda</s> overrides while the <s>śabda</s> itself is not differentiated. Rather, when <s>śabda</s> is differentiated, overriding is justified. Therefore <s>śabda</s> is produced, not manifested. And overriding would be unjustified [on the manifestation view] — because of the impossibility of conjunction when manifestation is in the same location as the manifester.

<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.14: [Objection:] No — because of the permanence of pot-absence, which is like a universal; and because of figurative usage regarding permanent things as if they were impermanent.

children.text:
na khalvādimattvādanityaḥ śabdaḥ|
kasmāt ?, vyabhicārāt = ādimataḥ khalu ghaṭābhāvasya dṛṣṭaṃ nityatvam|
kathamādimān ?, kāraṇavibhāgebhyo hi ghaṭo na bhavati|
kathamasya nityatvam ? yo 'sau kāraṇavibhāgebhyo na bhavati na tasyābhāvo bhāvena kadācid nirvartyate iti|
children.translated_text: How is it permanent? That which does not exist due to the disjunction of its causes — its absence is never brought to an end by existence.

children.text: yadapi aindriyakatvāt. (iti) tadapi vyabhicarati = aindriyakaṃ ca sāmānyaṃ nityaṃ ceti|
children.translated_text: As for 'because it is sensory' — that too deviates: the universal is sensory and yet permanent.

children.text: yadapi kṛtakavadupacārāditi. etadapi vyabhicarati nityeṣvanityavadupacāro dṛṣṭo yathā hi bhavati-- 'vṛkṣasya pradeśaḥ kambalasya pradeśaḥ' evam-- 'ākāśasya pradeśa ātmanaḥ pradeśaḥ' iti bhavatīti // 14 //
children.translated_text: As for 'because of figurative usage as with produced things' — that too deviates: figurative usage regarding permanent things as if impermanent is observed — just as 'a part of the tree, a part of the blanket,' so too 'a part of space, a part of the self' is [said]. //14//

<s>Śabda</s> is not impermanent because of having a beginning. Why? Because of deviation — for the permanence of pot-absence, which has a beginning, is observed. How does it have a beginning? From the disjunction of its causes, the pot ceases to exist.
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.15: Because of the distinction between the literal and the figurative, there is no deviation.

children.text: nityamityatra kiṃ tāvat tattvam ?, arthāntarasyānutpattidharmakasyātmahānānupapattirnityatvaṃ taccābhāve nopapadyate, bhāktaṃ tu bhavati-- yattatrātmānamahāsītuyad bhūtvā na bhavati na jātu tat punarbhavati. tatra nitya iva nityo ghaṭābhāva ityayaṃ padārtha iti|
tatra yathājātīyakaḥ śabdo na tathājātīyakaṃ kāryaṃ kiñcid nityaṃ dṛśyate ity avyabhicāraḥ // 15 //
children.translated_text: Therein, no produced thing of the same kind as <s>śabda</s> is seen to be permanent — hence there is no deviation. //15//

Regarding 'permanent' — what is the literal [meaning] here? The impossibility of self-destruction for a different thing that is not subject to origination — that is permanence, and that is not justified for <s>abhāva</s> (absence). But the figurative [usage] applies — when that which had its own existence, having existed, ceases to exist, it never comes into being again. So pot-absence is 'permanent as it were' — this is [merely] a verbal convention.
As for 'because of the permanence of the universal' — since what is grasped by proximity to the sense-organ is sensory —
<s>Nyāyasūtra</s> 2.2.16: Because [<s>śabda</s> is] qualified by inference from a series (<s>saṃtāna</s>).
What then? From being graspable by proximity to the sense-organ, a series (<s>saṃtāna</s>) is inferred — and from that, impermanence. //16//

'There is no deviation regarding permanent [things]' — this is the topic under discussion. [The argument:] the impermanence of <s>śabda</s> does not [follow merely] from the capacity of sense-organ grasping.
[Section: NySBh 2.2.17]
And as for [the objection] 'Even in eternal [substances], because of metaphorical usage as with non-eternal [ones]' — no —
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.17: Because the causal substance is designated by the word 'part' (<s>pradeśa</s>), there is no deviation even in eternal [substances].

children.text:
'evamākāśapradeśaḥ ātmapradeśaḥ' iti. nātrākāśātmanoḥ kāraṇadravyamabhidhīyate yathā kṛtakasya|
kathaṃ hyavidyamānamabhidhīyate, avidyamānatā ca pramāṇato 'nupalabdheḥ|
kiṃ tarhi tatrābhidhīyate ?, saṃyogasyāvyāpyavṛttitvamuparicchinnena dravyeṇākāśasvaya saṃyogo nākāśaṃ vyāpnoti = avyāpya vartate iti. tadasya kṛtakena dravyeṇa sāmānyam, na hyāmalakayoḥ saṃyogāśrayaṃ vyāpnoti, sāmānyakṛtā ca bhaktiḥ-- 'ākāśasya pradeśaḥ' iti, anenātmapradeśo vyākhyātaḥ|

children.translated_text: And like conjunction, the non-pervading existence of <s>śabda</s> (sound), <s>buddhi</s> (cognition), and the like [is also accounted for].

children.text: parīkṣitā ca tīvramandatā śabdatattvaṃ na bhaktikṛteti|
children.translated_text: And intensity and mildness have been examined — [they constitute] the true nature of <s>śabda</s>, not a metaphorical usage.

children.text: kasmāt punaḥ sūtrakārasyāsminnarthe sūtraṃ na śrūyate iti ?, śīlamidaṃ bhagavataḥ sūtrakārasya bahuṣvadhikaraṇeṣu dvau pakṣau na vyavasthāpayati, tatra śāstrasiddhāntāt tattvāvadhāraṇaṃ pratipattumarhatīti manyate, śāstrasiddhāntastu nyāyasamākhyātamanumataṃ bahuśākhamanumānamiti // 17 //
children.translated_text: Why then is a <s>sūtra</s> of the <s>sūtrakāra</s> (author of the aphorisms) not heard on this matter? It is the manner of the venerable <s>sūtrakāra</s> that in many topics he does not establish both sides [of the argument]; he considers that the truth should be ascertained from the established doctrine of the <s>śāstra</s>. And the established doctrine of the <s>śāstra</s> is the inference designated by the name <s>Nyāya</s>, which is accepted [and] has many branches. [End of NyS 2.2.17]

'Thus, a part of <s>ākāśa</s> (space), a part of <s>ātman</s> (self)' — here, a causal substance of <s>ākāśa</s> and <s>ātman</s> is not being denoted, as [it is] for a produced [substance]. For how can what is non-existent be denoted? And it is non-existent because it is not apprehended by any <s>pramāṇa</s>. What then is denoted there? The non-pervading nature of <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) — the conjunction of a limited substance with <s>ākāśa</s> does not pervade <s>ākāśa</s>, i.e., it exists without pervading. This [non-pervading nature] is its commonality with a produced substance — for the conjunction-substrate does not pervade even two <s>āmalakas</s> (gooseberries). And the metaphorical expression is based on this commonality — 'a part of <s>ākāśa</s>.' By this, 'a part of <s>ātman</s>' is also explained.
[Section: NySBh 2.2.18]

children.text: athāpi khalu 'idamasti idaṃ nāstīti kuta etat pratipattavyamiti ?, pramāṇata upalabdheranupalabdheśceti, avidyamānastarhi śabdaḥ---
children.translated_text: Now then — 'How is it to be known that this exists and this does not exist? From a <s>pramāṇa</s> — from apprehension and non-apprehension.' Then <s>śabda</s> is non-existent —
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.18: [Objection:] Because of non-apprehension prior to utterance, and because of non-apprehension [not being due] to obstruction and the like.

children.text:
prāguccāraṇānnasti śabdaḥ|
kasmāt ? anupalabdheḥ, sato 'nupalabdhirāvaraṇādibhya etannopapadyate|
kasmāt ?. āvaraṇādīnāmanupalabdhikāraṇānāmagrahaṇāt = anenāvṛtaḥ śabdo nopalabhyate asaṃnikṛṣṭaścendriyavyavadhānād ityevamādi anupalabdhikāraṇaṃ na gṛhyate iti. so 'yamanuccārito nāstīti|
uccāraṇamasya vyañjakaṃ tadabhāvāt prāguccāraṇādanupalabdhiriti|
kimidamuccāraṇaṃ nāmeti ?, vivakṣājanitena prayatnena koṣṭhyasya vāyoḥ preritasya kaṇṭhatālvādipratighātād varṇābhivyaktiriti|
children.translated_text: What is this utterance? Through effort generated by the desire to speak, the internal air (<s>vāyu</s>) is propelled, and from its striking against the throat, palate, and so forth, the phonemes (<s>varṇas</s>) are manifested.

children.text: saṃyogaviśeṣo vai pratighātaḥ pratiṣiddhaṃ ca saṃyogasya vyañjakatvaṃ tasmānna vyañjakābhāvādagrahaṇam api tvabhāvādeveti. soyamuccāryamāṇaḥ śrūyate śrūyamāṇaścābhūtvā bhavati ityanumīyate. ūrdhvañcoccāraṇānna śrūyate sa bhūtvā na bhavati = abhāvānna śrūyate iti|
children.translated_text: A particular conjunction is indeed the striking; and conjunction's [capacity as] a manifester has been refuted. Therefore, non-apprehension is not due to the absence of a manifester, but rather due to [the śabda's] non-existence itself. This [śabda], being uttered, is heard; and being heard, it is inferred as 'it comes into being, not having been before.' And after utterance it is not heard — it ceases to be, having existed; it is not heard because of its non-existence.
How [is this known]? Because 'non-apprehension due to obstruction and the like' has been stated. Therefore <s>śabda</s> has the nature of arising and disappearing. [End of NyS 2.2.18]

<s>Śabda</s> does not exist before utterance. Why? Because of non-apprehension. The non-apprehension of an existing thing [might be] due to obstruction and the like — but this is untenable. Why? Because the causes of non-apprehension, such as obstruction, are not grasped — [one cannot say] 'the <s>śabda</s>, obstructed by this, is not apprehended' or 'it is not in contact [with the sense-organ] because of the interposition of the sense-organ' — such a cause of non-apprehension is not grasped. Therefore, this unuttered [śabda] does not exist. Utterance is its manifester (<s>vyañjaka</s>); due to its absence, there is non-apprehension before utterance.
[Section: NySBh 2.2.19]
And this being so, [the eternalist], burying the truth as if with dust, states this —
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.19: [Reply:] Because of the non-apprehension of the non-apprehension of that [obstruction], obstruction is tenable.

children.text: yadyanupalambhādāvaraṇaṃ nāsti ?. āvaraṇānupalabdhirapi tarhyanupalambhānnāstīti. tasyā abhāvādapratiṣiddhamāvaraṇamiti|

children.translated_text: But how does the gentleman know that the non-apprehension of obstruction is not apprehended?
What is to be known here, since it is self-evident (<s>pratyātmavedanīya</s>)?

children.text: samānam = ayaṃ khalvāvaraṇamanupalabhamānaḥ pratyātmameva saṃvedayate-- 'nāvaraṇamupalabhe' iti, yathā kuḍyenāvṛtasyāvaraṇamupalabhamānaḥ pratyātmameva saṃvedayate, seyamāvaraṇopalabdhivad āvaraṇānupalabdhirapi saṃvedyaiveti, evaṃ ca satyapahṛtaviṣayamuttaravākyamastīti // 19 //
children.translated_text: [Reply:] The same [applies to you] — this one, not apprehending obstruction, is self-evidently aware: 'I do not apprehend the obstruction.' Just as one whose [view is] obstructed by a wall, apprehending the obstruction, is self-evidently aware [of it] — so this non-apprehension of obstruction is equally self-evident, just like the apprehension of obstruction. And this being so, the rejoinder [in the next sūtra] has had its subject-matter removed. [End of NyS 2.2.19]
If obstruction does not exist because of non-apprehension? Then the non-apprehension of obstruction also does not exist because of non-apprehension. Due to its absence, obstruction is not refuted.
[Section: NySBh 2.2.20]
But the eternalist (<s>jātivādin</s>) speaks as if making a concession —
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.20: Just as the non-apprehension [of obstruction] exists despite being unapprehended, so too obstruction is not untenable because of non-apprehension.

children.text: yadyabhyanujānāti bhavān-- 'nānupalīyamānāvaraṇānupalabdhirastīti. abhyanujñāvaya ca vadati-- 'nāstyāvaraṇamanupalambhāt' ityetat. etasminnapyabhyanujñāvāde pratipattiniyamo nopapadyate iti // 20 //
children.translated_text: If the gentleman concedes — 'the non-apprehension of obstruction that is not apprehended exists' — then he is speaking on the basis of [his own] concession. He says 'obstruction does not exist because of non-apprehension' [precisely on this basis]. Even in this concession-based argument, a determinate conclusion is not tenable. [End of NyS 2.2.20]
Just as the non-apprehension of obstruction exists even though it is not apprehended, so too obstruction exists even though it is not apprehended.
[Section: NySBh 2.2.21]
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.21: [Counter-reply:] Non-apprehension, being of the nature of non-apprehension, is not a valid reason.

children.text: yudapalabhyate tadasti. yannopalabhyate tannāstīti anupalambhātmakam asaditi vyavasthitam, upalabdhyabhāvaścānupalabdhiriti seyamabhāvatvānnopalabhyate sacaca khalvāvaraṇaṃ tasyopalabdhyā bhavitavyaṃ na nopalabhyate tasmānnāstīti|

children.translated_text: Therefore, what was said — 'obstruction is not untenable because of non-apprehension' — is unjustified. [End of NyS 2.2.21]

What is apprehended exists; what is not apprehended does not exist — thus, non-existence is established as being of the nature of non-apprehension. And non-apprehension is the absence of apprehension — this, being of the nature of absence, is not apprehended. But obstruction, if it exists, should be apprehended — it is not apprehended, therefore it does not exist.
[Section: NySBh 2.2.22]

children.text: atha śabdasya nityatvaṃ pratijānānaḥ kasmād hetoḥ pratijānīte ?---
children.translated_text: Now, one who claims the eternality of <s>śabda</s> — for what reason does he claim it? —
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.22: [Claim:] Because of being intangible (<s>asparśatva</s>).

children.text: asparśamākāśaṃ nityaṃ dṛṣṭamiti tathā ca śabda iti // 22 //
children.translated_text: The intangible <s>ākāśa</s> (space) is seen to be eternal — and similarly <s>śabda</s>. [End of NyS 2.2.22]

children.text:
so 'yamubhayataḥ savyabhicāraḥ-- sparśavāṃścāṇurnityaḥ. asparśaṃ ca karmānityaṃ dṛṣṭam|
"asparśatvāt" ityetasya sādhyasādharmyeṇodāharaṇam---
children.translated_text: This [argument] deviates in both directions — the tangible atom is [also] eternal; and intangible action (<s>karma</s>) is seen to be non-eternal. For 'because of being intangible' — the example conforming to the thesis (<s>sādhyasādharmya</s>) —
[Section: NySBh 2.2.23]
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.23: [Counter-example:] No, because action (<s>karma</s>) is non-eternal [though intangible].
The example differing from the thesis (<s>sādhyavaidharmya</s>) —
[Section: NySBh 2.2.24]
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.24: [Counter-example:] No, because the atom is eternal [though tangible].
In both examples, because of deviation [of the mark from the thesis], [intangibility] is not a valid reason. [End of NyS 2.2.24]
[Section: NySBh 2.2.25]
Then this is the reason —
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.25: [Claim:] Because of being handed down (<s>saṃpradāna</s>).

children.text: saṃpradīyamānamavasthitaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ saṃpradīyate ca śabda ācāryeṇāntevāsine tasmādavasthita iti // 25 //
children.translated_text: What is handed down is seen to be enduring; and <s>śabda</s> is handed down by the teacher to the student — therefore it is enduring. [End of NyS 2.2.25]
[Section: NySBh 2.2.26]
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.26: [Reply:] This is not a valid reason, because of the non-apprehension [of śabda] in the interval between them.

children.text: yena saṃpradīyate yasmai ca tayorantarāle 'vasthānamasya kena liṅgenopalabhyate ?, sapradīyamāno hyavasthitaḥ saṃprādāturapaiti saṃpradānaṃ ca prāpnoti ityavarjanīyametat // 26 //
children.translated_text: Between the one who hands down and the one to whom it is handed down — by what inferential mark is its endurance in the interval apprehended? For what is being handed down, being enduring, would depart from the giver and arrive at the recipient — this is unavoidable. [End of NyS 2.2.26]
[Section: NySBh 2.2.27]
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.27: [Counter-reply:] Not refuted, because of the fact of teaching.

children.text: adhyāpanaṃ liṅgam-- asati saṃpradāne 'dhyāpanaṃ na syāditi // 27 //
children.translated_text: Teaching is the inferential mark — in the absence of handing down, teaching would not exist. [End of NyS 2.2.27]
[Section: NySBh 2.2.28]
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.28: [Reply:] Not refuted, because teaching [is possible] on either thesis.

children.text: samānamadhyāpanamubhayoḥ pakṣayoḥ-- saṃśayānivṛtteḥ-- kimācāryasthaḥ śabdo 'stevāsinamāpadyate tadadhyāpanam ? āho svit nṛtyopadeśavad gṛhītasyānukaraṇam adhyāpanam ? iti,

children.translated_text: Thus, teaching is not an inferential mark of handing down. [End of NyS 2.2.28]

Teaching is common to both theses — because the doubt is not resolved: Is the <s>śabda</s> existing in the teacher transmitted to the student — is that teaching? Or is it imitation of what is grasped, like instruction in dancing — is that teaching?
[Section: NySBh 2.2.29]
Then this is the reason —
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.29: [Claim:] Because of repetition (<s>abhyāsa</s>).

children.text: abhyasyamānamavasthitaṃ dṛṣṭam-- 'pañcakṛtvaḥ paśyatīti rūpamavasthitaṃ punaḥ punardṛśyate, bhavati ca śabde 'bhyāsaḥ-- 'daśakṛtvo 'dhīto 'nuvākaḥ viṃśatikṛtvo 'dhītaḥ' iti, tasmādavasthitasya punaḥ punaruccāraṇam abhyāsa iti // 29 //
children.translated_text: What is repeated is seen to be enduring — 'one sees five times' means the enduring form is seen again and again. And there is repetition in the case of <s>śabda</s> — 'the lesson has been recited ten times, twenty times.' Therefore, the repeated utterance of what is enduring is repetition. [End of NyS 2.2.29]
[Section: NySBh 2.2.30]
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.30: [Reply:] No, because the expression 'repetition' is [also] used metaphorically even when [the objects are] different.

children.text: anavasthānepyabhyāsasyābhidhānaṃ bhavati-- 'dvirnṛtyatu bhavān trirnṛtyatu bhavān' iti 'dviranṛtyat triranṛtyat' 'dviragnihotraṃ juhoti' 'dvirbhuṅkte' (iti) // 30 //
children.translated_text: Even when [the objects] are not enduring, the expression 'repetition' is used — 'Sir, please dance twice, dance three times'; 'he danced twice, he danced three times'; 'he offers the <s>agnihotra</s> twice'; 'he eats twice.' [End of NyS 2.2.30]
[Section: NySBh 2.2.31]

children.text: evaṃ vyabhicārāt pratiṣiddhahetau anyaśabdasya prayogaḥ pratiṣidhyate---
children.translated_text: Thus, when the reason has been refuted due to deviation, the use of the word 'other' (<s>anya</s>) is refuted —
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.31: [Counter-reply:] Since something different from something else is non-different from itself, it is not different — therefore otherness does not exist.

children.text: yadidam 'anyat' iti manyase tat svātmano 'nanyatvādanyanna bhavati evamanyatāyā abhāvaḥ, tatra yaduktam-- 'anyatvepyabhyāsopacārāt' iti etadayuktamiti // 31 //
children.translated_text: What you consider 'other' — that, being non-different from itself, is not other. Thus otherness does not exist. Therefore, what was said — 'even when [the objects are] different, [the expression] repetition is metaphorical' — is unjustified. [End of NyS 2.2.31]
[Section: NySBh 2.2.32]

children.text:
śabdaprayogaṃ pratiṣedhataḥ śabdāntaraprayogaḥ pratiṣidhyate---
  NyS_2,2.32: tadabhāve nāstyananyatā tayoritaretarāpekṣasiddheḥ //
children.translated_text: For one who refutes the use of a word, the use of another word is refuted — <s>NyS</s> 2.2.32: In its absence, there is no non-otherness either, because each is established in dependence on the other.

children.text: anyasmād anyatāmupapādayati bhavān upapādya ca anyat pratyācaṣṭe, 'ananyat' iti ca śabdamanujānāti. prayuṅkte ca 'ananyat' iti etat samāsapadam. anyaśabdoyaṃ pratiṣedhena saha samasyate. yadi cātrottaraṃ padaṃ nāsti kasyāyaṃ pratiṣedhenana saha samāsaḥ ?, tasmāt tayoranyānanyaśabdayoritaro 'nanyaśabda itaramanyaśabdamapekṣamāṇaḥ sidhyatīti tatra yaduktam-- 'anyatāyā abhāvaḥ' iti etadayuktamiti // 32 //
children.translated_text: The gentleman establishes otherness from something else, and having established it, denies 'other' and concedes the word 'non-other.' And he uses the compound word 'non-other' (<s>ananyat</s>). This word 'other' (<s>anya</s>) is compounded with the negation. If the latter word [anya] does not exist here, with what is this negation compounded? Therefore, of these two words — 'other' and 'non-other' — the word 'non-other' is established in dependence on the word 'other' as its counterpart. Therefore, what was said — 'otherness does not exist' — is unjustified. [End of NyS 2.2.32]
[Section: NySBh 2.2.33]
Let <s>śabda</s> then be eternal —
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.33: [Claim:] Because of the non-apprehension of a cause of destruction.

children.text: yadanityaṃ tasya vināśaḥ kāraṇād bhavati yathā loṣṭasya kāraṇadravyavibhāgāt, śabdaścedanityastasya vināśo yasmātkāraṇād bhavati tadupalabhyeta na copalabhyate tasmānnitya iti // 33 //
children.translated_text: What is non-eternal — its destruction occurs from a cause, as a clod [is destroyed] from the disjunction of its causal substance. If <s>śabda</s> is non-eternal, the cause from which its destruction occurs should be apprehended — but it is not apprehended. Therefore, [śabda] is eternal. [End of NyS 2.2.33]
[Section: NySBh 2.2.34]
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.34: [Reply:] Because of the non-apprehension of a cause of non-hearing, there would follow perpetual hearing.
[Counter-reply:] If [non-hearing is due to] the absence of a manifester? [Reply:] The manifester has been refuted.

children.text: atha vidyamānasya nirnimittam aśravaṇamiti ?. vidyamānasya nirnimitto vināśa iti|
children.translated_text: [Counter-reply:] If the non-hearing of what exists is without a cause? [Reply:] Then the destruction of what exists is also without a cause.

children.text: samānaśca dṛṣṭavirodho nimittamantareṇa vināśe cāśrivaṇe ceti // 34 //
children.translated_text: And the opposition with observation is the same — whether regarding causeless destruction or causeless non-hearing. [End of NyS 2.2.34]
Just as from the non-apprehension of a cause of destruction, there follows indestructibility, so from the non-apprehension of a cause of non-hearing, there follows perpetual hearing.
[Section: NySBh 2.2.35]

<s>NyS</s> 2.2.35: And when [the cause of destruction] is apprehended, [the argument] 'because of the non-apprehension of [a cause of destruction]' is without basis, since [the cause] is non-existent [as claimed].

children.text: anumānāccopalabhyamāne śabdasya vināśakaraṇe 'bavanāśakāraṇānupalabdheḥ = asattvāt' ityanapadeśaḥ yathā 'yasmādviṣāṇī tasmādaśvaḥ' iti|

kimanumānamiticet ?. saṃtānopapattiḥ, upapāditaḥ śabdasaṃtānaḥ-- saṃyogavibhāgajāt śabdācchabdāntaraṃ tatopyanyat tatopyanyaditi, tatra kāryaḥ śabdaḥ kāraṇaśabdaṃ viruṇaddhi. pratighātidravyasaṃyogastu antyasya śabdasya nirodhakaḥ, dṛṣṭaṃ hi tiraḥpratikuḍyamantikasthenāpyaśravaṇaṃ śabdasya śravaṇaṃ dūrasthenāpyasati vyavadhāne iti|
children.translated_text: If it is asked, 'Is this an inference?' — the succession theory is established. The succession of <s>śabda</s> (sound) has been demonstrated: from a sound born of <s>saṃyoga</s> (conjunction) and <s>vibhāga</s> (disjunction) arises another sound, from that yet another, and from that still another. In this process, the effect-sound obstructs the cause-sound. The conjunction with a <s>pratighāti-dravya</s> (blocking substance) is what arrests the final sound in the series. For it is observed that sound is not heard even by one standing nearby when there is a wall in between, while it is heard even by one standing far away when there is no obstruction.

children.text: ghaṇṭāyāmabhihanyamānāyāṃ tārastārataro mando mandatara iti śrutibhedād nānāśabdasaṃtāno 'vicchedena śrūyate, tatra nitye śabde ghaṇṭāsthamanyagataṃ vāvasthitaṃ saṃtānavṛtti vā abhivyaktikāraṇaṃ vācyaṃ yena śrutisaṃtāno bhavatīti, śabdabhede cāsati śrutibheda upapādayitavya iti|
children.translated_text: When a <s>ghaṇṭā</s> (bell) is struck, a succession of different sounds is heard without interruption — high-pitched, then higher-pitched, soft, then softer — due to the difference in pitch. In this case, if <s>śabda</s> (sound) were <s>nitya</s> (eternal), one would have to specify the cause of manifestation — whether it resides in the bell, or has gone elsewhere, or operates through succession — by which the continuity of hearing occurs. And if there is no difference in sound, the difference in hearing would have to be explained.

children.text: anitye tu śabde ghaṇṭāsthaṃ saṃtānavṛtti saṃyogasahakāri nimittāntaraṃ saṃskārabhūtaṃ paṭumandamanuvartate tasyānuvṛttyā śabdasaṃtānānuvṛttiḥ paṭumandabhāvācca tīvramandatā śabdasya. tatkṛtaśca śrutibheda iti // 35 //
children.translated_text: But if <s>śabda</s> (sound) is <s>anitya</s> (non-eternal), then the additional cause residing in the bell, operating through succession, cooperating with conjunction, being in the nature of <s>saṃskāra</s> (residual impression), follows the pattern of sharp and soft. Through its continuation, there is continuation of the sound-succession, and through its sharp-and-soft character, there is the intensity and softness of sound. The difference in hearing is caused by that. // 35 //

When the cause of the destruction of <s>śabda</s> is apprehended through inference, [the argument] 'because of the non-apprehension of a cause of destruction — [therefore] because of its non-existence' is without basis — just as [the fallacious inference] 'because it has horns, therefore it is a horse.'

children.text: na vai nirnimittāntaraṃ saṃskāra upalabhyate anupalabdhernāstīti---
children.translated_text: Surely no <s>saṃskāra</s> (residual impression) is perceived without an additional cause. From non-perception, it does not follow that it does not exist —
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.36: Because of the cessation of sound upon contact caused by the hand, non-perception is not [a valid objection]. //

children.text: pāṇikarmaṇā pāṇighaṇṭāpraśleṣo bhavati tasmiṃśca sati śabdasaṃtāno nopalabhyate ataḥ śravaṇānupapattiḥ, tatra pratighātidravyasaṃyogaḥ śabdasya nimittāntaraṃ saṃskārabhūtaṃ niruṇaddhītyanumīyate. tasya ca nirodhāt śabdasaṃtāno notpadyate anutpanne ca śrutivicchedaḥ, yathā pratighātidravyasaṃyogādiṣoḥ kriyāhetau saṃskāre niruddhe gamanābhāva iti|
kampasaṃtānasya sparśanendriyagrāhyasya coparamaḥ kāṃsyapātrādiṣu pāṇisaṃśleṣo liṅgaṃ saṃskārasaṃtānasyeti, tasmānnimittāntarasya saṃskārabhūtasya nānupalabdhiriti // 36 //
children.translated_text: The cessation of the succession of vibration, which is perceptible by the sense of touch, in bronze vessels and the like upon contact with the hand, is the inferential mark of the succession of <s>saṃskāra</s> (residual impression). Therefore, there is no non-perception of the additional cause that is in the nature of <s>saṃskāra</s>. // 36 //

By the action of the hand, contact between hand and bell occurs, and when that happens, the succession of sound is no longer perceived — hence the impossibility of hearing. From this it is inferred that the conjunction with a <s>pratighāti-dravya</s> (blocking substance) arrests the additional cause that is in the nature of <s>saṃskāra</s> (residual impression). And from its arrest, the sound-succession is not produced, and when it is not produced, there is cessation of hearing. Just as when the <s>saṃskāra</s> that is the cause of motion in an arrow is arrested by conjunction with a blocking substance, there is absence of movement.
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.37: And if, from non-perception of a cause of destruction, something persists, there would be the undesirable consequence of its eternality. //

children.text: yadi yasya vināśakāraṇaṃ nopalabhyate tadavatiṣṭhate avasthānācca tasya nityatvaṃ prasajyate ? evaṃ yāni khalpimāni śabdaśravaṇāni śabdābhivyaktaya iti mataṃ na teṣāṃ vināśakāraṇaṃ bhavatopapādyate anupapādanādavasthānam avasthānāt teṣāṃ nityatvaṃ prasajyate iti, atha naivam ?ḥ na tarhi vināśakāraṇānupalabdheḥ śabdasyāvasthānānnityatvamiti // 37 //
children.translated_text: If that whose cause of destruction is not perceived persists, and from its persistence its eternality follows — then those perceptions of sound which are considered to be manifestations of <s>śabda</s> (sound), their cause of destruction is not established by you. From non-establishment comes persistence, and from persistence follows the undesirable consequence of their eternality. But if this is not so, then one cannot argue that sound is eternal on the ground that it persists due to non-perception of its cause of destruction. // 37 //

children.text: kampasamānāśrayasya cānunādasya pāṇipraśleṣāt kāraṇoparamādabhāvaḥ, vaiyadhikaraṇye hi pratighātidravyāpraśleṣāt samānādhikaraṇasyaivoparamaḥ syāditi|
children.translated_text: And the absence of <s>anunāda</s> (resonance), which shares the same substrate as vibration, upon hand-contact is due to the cessation of its cause. For when the substrates are different, from the non-contact with the blocking substance, only that which shares the same substrate would cease.
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.38: Because of intangibility, the denial is not established. //

children.text: yadidam 'nākāśaguṇaḥ śabdaḥ' iti pratiṣidhyate. ayamanupapannaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ-- asparśatvāt śabdāśrayasya, rūpādisamānadeśasyāgrahaṇe śabdasaṃtānopapatterasparśavyāpidravyāśrayaḥ śabdaḥ iti jñāyate na ca kampasamānāśraya iti // 38 //
children.translated_text: Regarding the denial that '<s>śabda</s> (sound) is not a <s>guṇa</s> (quality) of <s>ākāśa</s> (space)' — this denial is untenable, because the substrate of sound is <s>asparśa</s> (intangible). When <s>rūpa</s> (form) and other qualities co-located with it are not perceived, yet the succession of sound is established, it is known that <s>śabda</s> resides in a substance that is pervaded by the intangible — and it does not share the same substrate as vibration. // 38 //

children.text:
pratidravyaṃ rūpādibhiḥ saha saṃniviṣṭaḥ śabdaḥ samānadeśo vyajyate iti nopapadyate|
katham ?
children.translated_text:
The claim that sound, being co-located with <s>rūpa</s> (form) and other qualities in each substance, is manifested, is not tenable.
How so?
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.39: And because of the occurrence of different forms in aggregation. //
The word 'ca' (and) means 'and because of the establishment of succession' — that has been explained.

children.text: yadi rūpādayaḥ śabdaśca pratidravyaṃ samastāḥusamuditāstasmin samāsasamudāye yo yathājātīyakaḥ saṃniviṣṭastasya tathājātīyasyaiva grahaṇena bhavitavyaṃ śabdasya rūpādivat, tatra yo 'yaṃ vibhāgaḥ eka dravye nānārūpā bhinnaśrutayo vidharmāṇaḥ śabdaḥ abhivyajyamānāḥ yacca vibhāgāntaraṃ sarūpāḥ samānaśrutayaḥ sadharmāṇaḥ śabdāḥ tīvramandadharmatayā bhinnāḥ śrūyante. tadubhayaṃ nopapadyate-- nānābhūtānāmutpadyamānānāmayaṃ dharmo naikasya vyajyamānasyeti|
children.translated_text: If <s>rūpa</s> (form) and other qualities together with <s>śabda</s> (sound) are aggregated in each substance, then in that aggregate, whatever is of a particular kind that is co-located, only that of the same kind should be perceived — sound should be like form and the rest. But here there is this differentiation: in a single substance, sounds of different forms, different pitches, and different properties are manifested. And there is another kind of differentiation: sounds of the same form, same pitch, and same properties are heard as differing in intensity and softness. Neither of these is tenable — this is a property of multiple things being produced, not of a single thing being manifested.

children.text: asti cāyaṃ vibhāgo vibhāgāntaraṃ ca tena vibhāgopapattermanyāmahe-- na pratidravyaṃ rūpādibhiḥ saha śabdaḥ saṃniviṣṭo vyajyate iti // 39 //
children.translated_text: And this differentiation and the other differentiation do exist. Therefore, from the establishment of such differentiation, we hold that sound is not manifested as co-located with <s>rūpa</s> and other qualities in each substance. // 39 //

children.text: dvividhaścāyaṃ śabdaḥ-- varṇātmako dhvanimātraśca tatra varṇātmani tāvat---
children.translated_text: And this <s>śabda</s> (sound) is of two kinds: that whose nature is <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme) and that which is mere <s>dhvani</s> (inarticulate sound). Regarding the one whose nature is <s>varṇa</s> —
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.40: There is doubt because of the teaching of both <s>vikāra</s> (modification) and <s>ādeśa</s> (substitution). //

children.text: 'dadhyatra' iti kecid ikāraḥ itvaṃ hitvā yatvamāpadyate iti vikāraṃ manyante, kecid ikārasya prayoge viṣayakṛte yad ikāraḥ sthānaṃ jahāti tatra yakārasya prayogaṃ bruvate, saṃhitāyāṃ viṣaye ikāro na prayujyate tasya sthāne yakāraḥ prayujyate sa ādeśa iti, ubhayamidamupadiśyate tatra na jñāyate kiṃ tattvamiti //
children.translated_text: In 'dadhyatra,' some hold that <s>ikāra</s> undergoes <s>vikāra</s> (modification) — abandoning its i-nature, it assumes ya-nature. Others state the use of <s>yakāra</s> in the place of <s>ikāra</s> when, in the domain created by the context, <s>ikāra</s> vacates its position: in <s>saṃhitā</s> (connected speech), in that domain, <s>ikāra</s> is not employed; in its place <s>yakāra</s> is employed — that is <s>ādeśa</s> (substitution). Both are taught. In this matter, the true nature is not known. //

children.text:
ādeśopadeśastattvam--- vikāropadeśe hyanvayasyāgrahaṇād vikārānanumānamiti5|
satyanvaye kiñcid nivartate kiñcidupajāyate iti śakyeta vikāro 'numātuṃ na cānvayo gṛhyate tasmād vikāro nāstīti//
children.translated_text:
The teaching of <s>ādeśa</s> (substitution) represents the truth — for in the teaching of <s>vikāra</s> (modification), since <s>anvaya</s> (continuity of substrate) is not apprehended, <s>vikāra</s> cannot be inferred.
If there were continuity, one could infer modification on the ground that something is removed and something arises. But continuity is not apprehended; therefore, <s>vikāra</s> does not exist. //

children.text:
bhinnakaraṇayośca varṇayoraprayoge prayogopapattiḥ|
vivṛtakaraṇa ikāraḥ īṣatspṛṣṭakaraṇo yakāraḥ tāvimau pṛthak karaṇākhyena prayatnenoccāraṇīyau tayorekasyāprayoge 'nyasya prayoga upapanna iti//
children.translated_text:
And for two <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) with different <s>karaṇa</s> (articulatory effort), the occurrence of one upon the non-occurrence of the other is established.
<s>Ikāra</s> has <s>vivṛta-karaṇa</s> (open articulation); <s>yakāra</s> has <s>īṣat-spṛṣṭa-karaṇa</s> (slight contact articulation). These two are to be pronounced with separately designated articulatory effort. When one of them is not employed, the employment of the other is established. //

children.text:
avikāre cāviśeṣaḥ7|
yatremau ikārayakārau na vikārabhūtau-- 'yatate. cachati. prāyaṃmta' iti. 'ikāraḥ idam' iti ca, yatra ca vikārabhūtau-- 'dṛṣṭyā' 'dadhyāhara' iti ubhayatra prayokturaviśeṣo yatnaḥ śrotuśca śrutiratyādeśopipattiḥ //
children.translated_text:
And in the absence of <s>vikāra</s> (modification), there is no difference.
Where these <s>ikāra</s> and <s>yakāra</s> are not in a modification relationship — as in 'yatate,' 'cachati,' 'prāyaṃta,' and '<s>ikāra</s>' in 'idam' — and where they are in a modification relationship — as in 'dṛṣṭyā,' 'dadhyāhara' — in both cases, there is no difference in the effort of the speaker, nor in the hearing of the listener. Therefore, <s>ādeśa</s> (substitution) is established. //

children.text:
prayujyamānāgrahaṇācca8|
na khalu ikāraḥ prayujyamāno yakāratāmāpadyamāno gṛhyate, kiṃ tarhi ?. ikārasya prayoge yakāraḥ prayujyate. tasmādavikāra iti //
children.translated_text:
And because the transforming entity is not perceived.
Indeed, <s>ikāra</s> is not perceived as being employed while transforming into <s>yakāra</s>-nature. Rather, in the domain of <s>ikāra</s>'s employment, <s>yakāra</s> is employed. Therefore, it is not <s>vikāra</s> (modification). //

children.text:
avikāre ca na śabdānvākhyānalopa9ḥ|
na vikriyante vaṇā iti|
na caitasmin pakṣe śabdānvākhyānasyāsaṃbhavo yena varṇavikāraṃ pratipadyemahīti|
children.translated_text: And in this position, there is no impossibility of the explanation of words, such that we would have to accept phoneme-modification.

children.text: na khalu varṇasya varṇāntaraṃ kāryam-- na hi ikārād yakāra utpadyate yakārādvā ikāraḥ, pṛthaksthānaprayatnotpādyā hīme varṇāsteṣāmanyo 'nyasya sthāne prayujyate iti yuktam|
children.translated_text: Indeed, one <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme) is not the effect of another — for <s>yakāra</s> is not produced from <s>ikāra</s>, nor <s>ikāra</s> from <s>yakāra</s>. These phonemes are produced by different <s>sthāna</s> (place) and <s>prayatna</s> (effort), and it is fitting that one is employed in the place of the other.

children.text: etāvaccaitat paraṇāmo vikāraḥ syāt kāryakāraṇabhāvo vā, ubhayaṃ ca nāsti tasmānna santi varṇavikāraḥ //
children.translated_text: This much could constitute <s>vikāra</s>: either transformation or a cause-effect relationship. But neither exists. Therefore, there are no phoneme-modifications. //

And in the absence of <s>vikāra</s> (modification), there is no loss of the explanation of words.
Phonemes are not modified.

children.text: "asterbhūḥ" "bruvo vaciḥ"iti yathā varṇasamudāyasya dhātulakṣaṇasya kvacidviṣaye varṇāntarasamudāyo na paraṇāmo ni kāryaṃ śabdāntarasya sthāne śabdāntaraṃ prayujyate tathā varṇasya varṇāntaramiti // 40 //
children.translated_text: Just as in 'asterbhūḥ' and 'bruvo vaciḥ,' a different phoneme-aggregate is not a transformation of the <s>dhātu</s> (verbal root) — which is a phoneme-aggregate — in a certain domain, nor is it an effect; rather, one word is employed in the place of another — so too, one phoneme in place of another. // 40 //
And just as modification of a phoneme-aggregate is not established, so too modification of individual <s>varṇas</s> (phonemes) is not established.
And for this further reason, modifications do not exist —
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.41: Because of the growth of the modification following the <s>prakṛti</s> (base form) and its growth. //

children.text: prakṛtyanuvidhānaṃ vikāreṣu dṛṣṭaṃ yakāre hasvadīrghānuvidhānaṃ nāsti yena vikāratvamanumīyata iti // 41 //
children.translated_text: Conformity to the <s>prakṛti</s> (base form) is observed in modifications. But in <s>yakāra</s>, there is no conformity to the short and long forms [of <s>ikāra</s>], by which its being a modification could be inferred. // 41 //
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.42: Since modifications are perceived as lesser, equal, or greater, the [argument for vikāra] is without valid reason. //

children.text:
davyavikārā nyūnāḥ samā adhikāśca gṛhyante. tadvadayaṃ vikāro nyūnaḥ syāditi|
dvividhasyāpi hetor abhāvād asādhanaṃ dṛṣṭāntaḥ-- atra nodāharaṇasādharmyād heturasti na vaidharmyāt. anupasaṃhṛtaśca hetunā dṛṣṭānto na sādhaka iti //
children.translated_text:
Modifications of <s>dravya</s> (substance) are perceived as lesser, equal, or greater. Accordingly, this modification should be lesser.
But since neither type of reason exists, the example fails to prove the point — here there is no reason by way of similarity with the example, nor by way of dissimilarity. And an example to which the reason has not been applied is not probative. //
And in the counter-example, there would be the undesirable consequence of non-restriction.

children.text: yathānaḍuhaḥ sthāne 'śvo voḍuṃ niyukto na tadvikāro bhavati. evamivarṇasya sthāne yakāraḥ prayukto na vikāra iti|
children.translated_text: Just as a horse yoked in the place of a bull to draw [a cart] is not a modification of it, so too <s>yakāra</s> employed in the place of <s>ikāra</s> is not a modification.

children.text: na cātra niyamaheturasti-- dṛṣṭāntaḥ sādhako na pratidṛṣṭānta iti // 42 //
children.translated_text: And here there is no reason for restriction — the example is probative, not the counter-example. // 42 //
And regarding the example of substance-modification —
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.43: Because there is no modification of things whose base-natures are not alike. //

children.text: atulyānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ prakṛtibhāvo vikalpane vikāraśca prakṛtīranuvidhīyate, na tvivarṇamanuvidhīyate yakāraḥ tasmādanudāharaṇam-- 'dravyavikāraḥ' iti // 43 //
children.translated_text: Dissimilar substances serve as the base, and in the alternative, modification conforms to its base. But <s>yakāra</s> does not conform to <s>ikāra</s>. Therefore, the example — 'substance-modification' — is inapplicable. // 43 //
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.44: Just as there is inequality in substance-modification, so there is an alternative regarding phoneme-modification. //

children.text: yathā dravyabhāvena tulyāyāḥ prakṛtervikāravaiṣamyam evaṃ varṇabhāvena tulyāyāḥ prakṛtervikāravikalpa iti // 44 //
children.translated_text: Just as there is inequality of modification for a base that is alike in substance-nature, so too there is an alternative of modification for a base that is alike in phoneme-nature. // 44 //
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.45: No, because the properties of modification do not apply. //

children.text: ayaṃ vikāradharmaḥ-- dravyasāmānye yadātmakaṃ dravyaṃ mṛdvā suvarṇaṃ vā tasyātmano 'nvaye pūrvo vyūho nivartate vyūhāntaraṃ copajāyate taṃ vikāramācakṣate, na varṇasāmānye kaścid śabdātmānvayī ya itvaṃ jahāti yatvaṃ cāpadyate, tatra yathā sati dravyabhāve vikāravaiṣamye nānaḍuho 'śvo vikāraḥ-- vikāradharmānupapatteḥ, evamivarṇasya na yakāro vikāraḥ-- vikāradharmānupapatteriti // 45 //
children.translated_text: This is the property of <s>vikāra</s> (modification): in the generality of <s>dravya</s> (substance), whatever is the nature of the substance — whether clay or <s>suvarṇa</s> (gold) — when that essential nature continues, the former configuration ceases and a new configuration arises; that is called modification. But in the generality of <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme), there is no continuing phonemic essence that abandons i-nature and assumes ya-nature. Therefore, just as when substance-nature is present but there is inequality of modification — a horse is not a modification of a bull — because the properties of modification do not apply, so too <s>yakāra</s> is not a modification of <s>ikāra</s>, because the properties of modification do not apply. // 45 //
And for this further reason, phoneme-modifications do not exist —
<s>NyS</s> 2.2.46: Because those that have undergone modification do not recur. //
How so? Because there is no inference from recurrence.
<s>Ikāra</s>, having assumed <s>yakāra</s>-nature, becomes <s>ikāra</s> again.

children.translated_text: The individual (<s>vyakti</s>) is the word-meaning. Why? Because of the application to the individual of [expressions beginning with] the word '<s>yā</s>' and the rest. Application means usage: '<s>yā gaus tiṣṭhati yā gaur niṣaṇṇā</s>' ('which cow stands, which cow is seated'). The word '<s>yā</s>' would [not be] an expression designating the universal — because [the universal is] undifferentiated. But because of differentiation, it designates a substance. '<s>Gavāṃ samūhaḥ</s>' ('a herd of cows') — because of differentiation, [this is] designation of substance, not of the universal — because [the universal is] undifferentiated. Relinquishing — '<s>vaidyāya gāṃ dadāti</s>' ('he gives a cow to the physician') is the relinquishing of a substance, not of the universal — because [the universal] is formless and because going and coming are untenable [for it]. Possession — connection as one's own: '<s>Kauṇḍinyasya gauḥ</s>' ('Kauṇḍinya's cow'), '<s>brāhmaṇasya gauḥ</s>' ('the brāhmaṇa's cow') — this is designation of substance, not [universal]: because of the differentiation of substances, the differentiation of possession is justified, whereas the universal is undifferentiated. Number — '<s>daśa gāvo viṃśatir gāvaḥ</s>' ('ten cows, twenty cows') — differentiated substances are counted, not the universal — because it is undifferentiated. Growth — the increase of parts of a substance that has causes: '<s>avardhata gauḥ</s>' ('the cow grew') — but the universal is partless. By this, diminution is [also] explained. Color �� '<s>śuklā gauḥ kapilā gauḥ</s>' ('a white cow, a brown cow') — the conjunction of quality [belongs to] substance, not to the universal. Compound — '<s>gohitaṃ gosukham</s>' ('cow-welfare, cow-happiness') — the conjunction with pleasure and the rest [belongs to] substance, not to the universal. Continuity — a series of reproduction of similar [offspring]: '<s>gaur gāṃ janayati</s>' ('a cow gives birth to a cow') — because of being subject to origination, this is justified for substance, not for the universal — because of the contrary. And substance is the individual (<s>vyakti</s>) — this is no different thing. //61//
