If [one argues that] because of non-apprehension upon awakening, the objects in a dream do not exist — then those objects that are apprehended by one who is awake, they exist because of apprehension — for the force of a reason operates through the contrary [case]. When apprehension is absent, non-existence is established from non-apprehension; but when there is absence in both ways, non-apprehension has no force. Just as from the absence of a lamp, there is the non-seeing of form — there, the existence [of form] is supported by the presence [of the lamp]. And regarding the distinction in the content of a dream — one who says 'like the notion of dream-objects' must state a reason for the distinction in the content of a dream. Some dreams are attended by fear, some by joy,
[Section: NySBh 4.2.34]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.34: The notion of dream-objects is like memory and imagination.

children.text:
pūrvopalabdhaviṣayaḥ, yathā smṛtiśca
saṃkalpaśca pūrvopalabdhaviṣayau na tasya pratyākhyānāya
kalpete. tathā svapne viṣayagrahaṇaṃ pūrvopalabdhaviṣayaṃ
na tasya pratyākhyānāvaya kalpate iti. evaṃ dṛṣṭaviṣayaśca
svapnānto jāgaritāntena|
yaḥ suptaḥ svapnaṃ paśyati sa eva jāgrat svapnadarśanāni pratisaṃdhatte--
'idamadrākṣam' iti. tatra jāgradbuddhivṛttivaśāt
svapnaviṣayābhimāno mithyeti vyavasāyaḥ
usati ca pratisaṃdhāne yā jāgrato buddhivṛttistadvaśādayaṃ
vyavasāyaḥ-- svapnaviṣayābhimāno mithyeti/
ubhayāviśeṣe tu sādhanānarthakyam|
yasya svapnāntajāgaritāntayoraviśeṣastasya
"svapnaviṣayābhimānavat"
iti sādhanamanarthakam-- tadāśrayapratayākhyānāt |
atasmiṃstaditi ca vyavasāyaḥ pradhānāśrayaḥ |
apuruṣe sthāṇau puruṣa iti (yaḥ) vyavasāyaḥ
sa pradhānāśrayaḥ-- na khalu puruṣe 'nupalabdhe
puruṣa ity apuruṣe vyavasāyo bhavati,
evaṃ svapnaviṣayasya vyavasāyaḥ-- 'hastinamadrākṣam'
'parvatamadrākṣam' iti pradhānāśrayo bhavitumarhati
// 34 //
children.translated_text: [It has] previously apprehended objects as its content. Just as memory and imagination have previously apprehended objects as their content and are not suited for the denial of that [object] — so too the apprehension of objects in a dream has previously apprehended objects as its content and is not suited for the denial of that [object]. Thus, the content of a dream is [based on] seen objects, and [it is connected] with the waking state. The very person who, while sleeping, sees a dream — that same person, while awake, connects the dream-visions — 'I saw this.' There, because of the force of the waking cognitive activity, the determination is that the notion of dream-objects is false. And when there is such connecting, it is because of the force of the waking cognitive activity that this determination [arises] — the notion of dream-objects is false. But if there is no distinction between dream and waking, the argument is purposeless. For one who [holds that] there is no distinction between dream and waking, the argument 'like the notion of dream-objects' is purposeless — because the basis of that [argument] is denied. And the determination 'this for that' has a primary referent as its basis. The determination 'this is a person' regarding a post, which is not a person — that has a primary referent as its basis — for surely the determination 'this is a person' regarding a non-person does not occur unless a [real] person has been apprehended. Similarly, the determination regarding dream-objects — 'I saw an elephant,' 'I saw a mountain' — should have a primary referent as its basis. [End of NyS 4.2.34]
[Section: NySBh 4.2.35]
And this being so —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.35: The destruction of false apprehension through knowledge of the truth, like the destruction of the notion of dream-objects upon awakening.

children.text:
sthāṇau 'puruṣoyam' itivyavasāyo mithyopalabdhiḥ |
atasmiṃstaditijñānam, sthāṇau 'sthāṇuḥ' itivyavasāyastattvajñānam,
tattvajñānena ca mithyopalabdhirnivartyate-- nārthaḥ
sthāṇupuruṣasāmānyalakṣaṇaḥ, yathā pratibodhe
yā jñānavṛttistayā svapnaviṣayābhimāno
nivartyate-- nārtho viṣayasāmānyalakṣaṇaḥ,
tathā māyagandharvanagaramṛgatṛṣṇikāṇāmapi
yā buddhayaḥ (tāḥ) etasmiṃstaditivyavasāyāstatrāpyanenaiva
kalpena mityopalabdhivināśastattvajñānād.
nārthapratiṣedha iti|
upādānavacca māyādiṣu mithyājñānam. prajñāpanīyasarūpaṃ ca dravyamupādāvaya
sādhanavān parasya mithyādhyavasāyaṃ karoti
sā māyā, nīhāraprabhatīnāṃ nagarasarūpasaṃniveśe
dūrād nagarabuddhirutpadyate viparyaye tadabhāvāt,
sūryamarīciṣu bhaumenoṣmaṇā
saṃsṛṣṭeṣu spandamāneṣūdakabuddhirbhavati--
sāmānyagrahaṇāt. antikasthasya viparyaye
tadabhāvāt, kvacit kadācit kasyacicca
bhāvād nānimittaṃ mithyājñānam|

children.translated_text: And the duality of cognition is observed — in illusion, for the performer and the other; in gandharva-city and mirage, for one far and near;
and in dream-objects, for the sleeping and the awake. All this, if everything were non-existent,
if there were utter namelessness,
if there were no selfhood — would be untenable. [End of NyS 4.2.35]

The determination 'this is a person' regarding a post is a false apprehension — a cognition of 'this for that.' The determination 'this is a post' regarding a post is knowledge of the truth. And by knowledge of the truth, false apprehension is dispelled — not the [real] object characterized by the commonality of post and person. Just as upon awakening, the notion of dream-objects is dispelled by the cognitive activity of knowledge — not the [real] object characterized by the commonality of [dream and real] objects. Similarly, the cognitions of illusion, gandharva-city, and mirage are determinations of 'this for that' — and in those too, by this very reasoning, the destruction of false apprehension is through knowledge of the truth, not the denial of the [real] object. And false cognition regarding illusion and the rest is caused by a material substrate. A substance resembling what is to be represented [is used as] material — one possessing the means produces a false determination in another; that is illusion. When there is a configuration resembling a city among mist and the like, the cognition of a city arises from a distance; in the contrary [situation], that [cognition] is absent. Regarding the sun's rays, mixed with terrestrial heat and trembling, there arises the cognition of water — because of the grasping of the general [resemblance]. For one standing nearby, in the contrary case, that [cognition] is absent. Because of the occurrence [of false cognition] in some [cases], sometimes, for some [persons], false cognition is not without a cause.
[Section: NySBh 4.2.36]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.36: And because of the apprehension of the cause and the existence of cognition itself.
The cause of false cognition is apprehended, and false cognition itself
is grasped as arisen in one's own self — because it is experienced. Therefore,
even false cognition exists. [End of NyS 4.2.36]
Even false cognition, like [valid cognition of] an object, is not to be denied. Why? Because of the apprehension of its cause and the apprehension of its existence.
[Section: NySBh 4.2.36]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.37: And because of the distinction based on truth and predominance, the twofold nature of false cognition is tenable.

children.text:
tattvaṃ sthāṇuriti. pradhānaṃ puruṣa iti.
tattvapradhānayoralopāt |
bhedāt sthāṇau puruṣa iti mithyābuddhirutpadyate--
sāmānyagrahaṇāt, evaṃ patākāyāṃ balāketi
loṣṭe kapota iti, na tv asamāne
viṣaye mithyābuddhīnāṃ samāveśaḥ--
sāmānyagrahaṇavyavasthānāt|
yasya tu nirātmakam |
nirupākhyaṃ sarva tasya samāveśaḥ prasajyate/
gandhādau ca prameye gandhādibuddhayo mithyābhimatāstattvapradhānayoḥ

children.translated_text: because of the absence of the apprehension of a common feature, are cognitions of truth alone,
not false. Therefore this is unjustified — 'the cognitions that are the means of valid knowledge
are false.' [End of NyS 4.2.37]

The truth is a post — the principal [category] is a person. By the elision of 'truth' and 'principal.' Because of difference, the false cognition 'a person' arises regarding a post — because of the apprehension of a common feature. Similarly, [the false cognition] 'a crane' regarding a flag, 'a pigeon' regarding a clod of earth. But there is no intermingling of false cognitions regarding dissimilar objects — because of the determination of the apprehension of common features. But for one who holds that everything is without self, without designation — for such a person, intermingling [of false cognitions] would follow. And regarding smell and the rest as objects of valid knowledge, the cognitions of smell and the rest, [even if] regarded as false regarding 'truth' and 'principal,'
[Section: NySBh 4.2.38]

children.text:
"doṣanimittānāṃ tattvajñānādahaṅkāranivṛttiḥ 4-2-1"
ityuktam. atha kathaṃ tattva jñānamutpadyate ? iti---
children.translated_text: It was stated — 'From the knowledge of truth regarding the causes of faults, the cessation of <s>ahaṃkāra</s> (ego-sense) [occurs]' (4.2.1). Now, how does the knowledge of truth arise? —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.38: From the repeated practice of a particular <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration).

children.text:
sa tu pratyāhṛtasyendriyārthebhyo
manaso dhārakeṇa prayatnena dhāryamāṇasyātmanā

children.translated_text: qualified by the desire for the knowledge of truth. When that [conjunction] obtains,
cognitions regarding sense-objects do not arise.
Through the power of repeated practice of that, the knowledge of truth arises. [End of NyS 4.2.38]
That [samādhi] is the conjunction of <s>manas</s>, withdrawn from sense-objects by a sustaining effort that holds it, with <s>ātman</s>,
[Section: NySBh 4.2.39]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.39: No, because of the predominance of specific objects.
Why? Because of the predominance of specific objects — even for one who does not desire [it],
the arising of cognition is observed, as in the case of thunder and the like.
In that case, a particular <s>samādhi</s> is untenable. [End of NyS 4.2.39]
This is not justified, because cognition arises even for one who does not wish it.
[Section: NySBh 4.2.40]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.40: And because of the impulsion by hunger and the like.
By hunger, thirst, cold, heat, and diseases, cognitions arise even for one who does not wish it. Therefore single-pointed concentration (<s>aikāgrya</s>) is untenable. [End of NyS 4.2.40]
[Section: NySBh 4.2.41]

children.text: astvetat samādhivyutthānanimittaṃ samādhipratyanīkaṃ ca. sati tvetasmin---
children.translated_text: Let these be the causes of disturbance from <s>samādhi</s> and obstacles to <s>samādhi</s>. But when this [samādhi] obtains —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.41: Its arising is due to the connection with the fruit of what was previously done.

children.text:
pūrvakṛtaḥ |
janmāntaropacitastattvajñānaheturdharmapravivekaḥ.
phalānubandhaḥ |
yogābhyāsamāmarthya, niṣphale hyabhyāse nābhyāsamādriyeran.
dṛṣṭaṃ hi laukikeṣu karmasv abhyāsasāmarthyam
// 41 //
children.translated_text: 'What was previously done' — the discrimination of <s>dharma</s> (merit), which is the cause of the knowledge of truth, accumulated in a previous birth. 'The connection with the fruit' — the efficacy of <s>yoga</s> practice; for if practice were fruitless, one would not undertake practice. For the efficacy of practice is observed in worldly activities. [End of NyS 4.2.41]
[Section: NySBh 4.2.42]
And for the purpose of removing obstacles —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.42: The instruction to practice <s>yoga</s> in forests, caves, riverbanks, and the like.

children.text:
yogābhyāsajanito dharmo janmāntare ḥpyanuvartate,
pracayakāṣṭhāgate tattvajñānahetau dharme prakṛṣṭāyāṃ
samādhibhāvanāyāṃ tattvajñānamutpadyate iti,
dṛṣṭaśca samādhinārthaviśeṣaprābalyābhibhavaḥ--
'nāhametadaśrauṣam nāhametadajñāsiṣam--
anyatra me mano 'bhūt' ityāha laukika iti
// 42 //
children.translated_text: The <s>dharma</s> produced by the practice of <s>yoga</s> continues even in a subsequent birth. When the <s>dharma</s> that is the cause of the knowledge of truth has reached the point of culmination, and when the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> is advanced, the knowledge of truth arises. And it is observed that <s>samādhi</s> overcomes the predominance of specific objects — 'I did not hear that, I did not know that — my mind was elsewhere,' thus says the ordinary person. [End of NyS 4.2.42]
[Section: NySBh 4.2.43]
If the arising of cognition even for one who does not wish it is accepted because of the predominance of specific objects —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.43: The same absurdity would apply in the case of <s>apavarga</s> (liberation) as well.
Even for the liberated one, cognitions would arise because of the power of external objects. [End of NyS 4.2.43]
[Section: NySBh 4.2.44]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.44: No, because [the arising of cognition] is inevitable when a body has been produced.

children.text:
karmavaśānniṣpanne śarīre ceṣṭendriyārthāśraye nimittabhāvādavaśyambhāvī
buddhīnāmutpādaḥ, na ca prabalopi san bāhyo 'rtha
ātmano buddhyutpāde samartho bhavati-- tasyendriyeṇa
saṃyogād buddhyutpāde sāmarthyaṃ dṛṣṭamiti
// 44 //
children.translated_text: When a body, which is the substrate of effort, sense-organs, and objects, has been produced through the force of <s>karma</s>, the arising of cognitions is inevitable because of the condition of being a cause. But even a powerful external object is not capable of producing cognition for <s>ātman</s> [without the body] — for the capacity to produce cognition is observed [only] from the conjunction with a sense-organ. [End of NyS 4.2.44]
[Section: NySBh 4.2.45]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.45: And its [i.e., the body's] absence [obtains] in <s>apavarga</s> (liberation).

children.text:
tasya |
buddhinimittāśrayasya śarīrendriyasya dharmādharmābhāvādabhāvo 'pavarge.
tatra yaduktam--
"aṇvargepyevaṃ prasaṅgaḥ 43"
iti tadayuktam, tasmāt sarvaduḥkhavimokṣopavargaḥ/
yasmāt sarvaduḥkhabījaṃ sarvaduḥkhāyatanaṃ

children.translated_text: are severed, therefore release from all suffering
is <s>apavarga</s>. Suffering that is without seed and without substrate
does not arise. [End of NyS 4.2.45]

The absence of the body and sense-organs, which are the substrate and cause of cognition, [obtains] in <s>apavarga</s>, because of the absence of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit). Regarding what was stated — 'The same absurdity would apply in the case of <s>apavarga</s> as well' (4.2.43) — that is unjustified. Therefore, <s>apavarga</s> is the complete release from all suffering. Because in <s>apavarga</s>, the seed of all suffering and the substrate of all suffering
[Section: NySBh 4.2.46]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.46: For that purpose, the refinement of <s>ātman</s> through <s>yama</s> (restraints) and <s>niyama</s> (observances), and through the methods of inner discipline from <s>yoga</s>.

children.text:
tasya |
apavargasyādhigamāya yamaniyamābhyāmātmasaṃskāraḥ,
yamaḥ
usamānamāśramiṇāṃ dharmasādhanam, niyamastu viśiṣṭamdva ātmasaṃskāraḥ
punaradharmahānaṃ dharmopacayaśca, yogaśāstrāccādhyātmavidhiḥ
pratipattavyaḥ sa punaḥ-- tapaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ pratyāhāro
dhyānaṃ dhāraṇeti, indriyaviṣayeṣu prasaṃkhyānābhyāso
rāgadveṣaprahāṇārthaḥ, upāyastu yogācāravidhānamiti
// 36 //
children.translated_text: For the attainment of <s>apavarga</s> (liberation), the refinement of <s>ātman</s> [is achieved] through <s>yama</s> and <s>niyama</s>. <s>Yama</s> is the common means of <s>dharma</s> for all <s>āśramins</s> (those in the stages of life); <s>niyama</s> is the specific one. The refinement of <s>ātman</s> consists in the abandonment of <s>adharma</s> (demerit) and the accumulation of <s>dharma</s> (merit). And from the <s>yoga</s> treatise, the method of inner discipline is to be understood — namely: <s>tapas</s> (austerity), <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of senses), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), and <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration). The practice of discernment regarding sense-objects is for the purpose of abandoning attachment and aversion. And the method is the prescribed conduct of <s>yoga</s> practice. [End of NyS 4.2.46]
[Section: NySBh 4.2.47]
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.47: The study and retention of knowledge, and discourse with those learned in it.

children.text:
"tadartham" itiprakṛtam|
jñāyate 'neneti jñānam = ātmavidyāśāstraṃ tasya grahaṇam = adhyayanadhāraṇe, abhyāsaḥ |
satatakriyā |
adhyayanaśravaṇacintanāni, tadvidyaiśca saha saṃvāda

children.translated_text: is for the purpose of the maturation of wisdom. And maturation means the resolution of doubt,
the understanding of what was not understood, and the confirmation of what was ascertained.
Concordant discussion is 'discourse.' [End of NyS 4.2.47]

'For that purpose' — this is the continuing subject. Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) means the treatise on the knowledge of <s>ātman</s>; 'its study' means learning and retention; 'practice' means constant application — study, listening, and reflection. 'And discourse with those learned in it'
[Section: NySBh 4.2.48]
'And discourse with those learned in it' — this statement with undistributed meaning is distributed —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.48: One should approach that with pupils, teachers, fellow students, and distinguished seekers of the highest good who are free from envy.
This is explained by its very recitation. [End of NyS 4.2.48]
[Section: NySBh 4.2.49]
If one should think — the adoption of thesis and counter-thesis is unfavorable to the other party —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.49: Or [one should approach] even one who lacks a counter-thesis, for the purpose of [establishing] one's objective, when there is a purpose.

'One should approach' — this continues. Seeking to acquire wisdom from another, by manifesting one's desire to know the truth, without establishing one's own thesis, one should purify one's own doctrine. [End of NyS 4.2.49]
[Section: NySBh 4.2.50]

children.text:
anyonyapratyanīkāni ca prāvādukānāṃ darśanāni svapakṣarāgeṇa
caike nyāyamativartante. tatra--
children.translated_text: The doctrines of debaters are mutually opposed, and some transgress proper reasoning out of attachment to their own thesis. In that case —

<s>NyS</s> 4.2.50: <s>Jalpa</s> (wrangling) and <s>vitaṇḍā</s> (cavilling) are for the protection of the ascertainment of truth, like the enclosure of thorny branches for the protection of the sprouting of a seed.
and who are striving for that purpose — this [is the teaching]. [End of NyS 4.2.50]
For those whose knowledge of truth has not yet arisen, whose faults have not yet been abandoned,
[Section: NySBh 4.2.51]
And for one who is being slighted by the other through contempt born of learning and the like —
<s>NyS</s> 4.2.51: With those two [jalpa and vitaṇḍā], contentious debate [is conducted].
'Contentiously' means with the desire to win, not with the desire to know the truth. This is for the protection of learning, not for the sake of gain, honor, or fame. [End of NyS 4.2.51]
Thus ends the fourth chapter of the <s>Nyāyabhāṣya</s> composed by the venerable <s>Vātsyāyana</s>.
Now [begins] the first section of the fifth chapter of the <s>Nyāyabhāṣya</s> with commentary.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.1]

children.text: sādharmyavaidharmyābhyāṃ pratyavasthānasya vikalpājjātibahutvamiti saṃkṣepeṇoktaṃ tadvistareṇa vibhajate, tāḥ khalvimā jātayaḥ sthāpanāhetau prayukte caturviṃśatiḥ pratiṣedhahetavaḥ |
children.translated_text: It was briefly stated that the multiplicity of <s>jāti</s> (futile rejoinders) arises from the varieties of counter-argument through similarity and dissimilarity — that is now distributed in detail. These <s>jātis</s> are indeed twenty-four counter-reasons against the establishing reason —

<s>NyS</s> 5.1.1: [The futile rejoinders are:] based on similarity, dissimilarity, excess, deficiency, the stated, the unstated, alternative, the accomplishment of the provable, attainment, non-attainment, consequence, counter-example, non-origination, doubt, petitio principii, the irrelevant, implication, non-distinction, tenability, perception, non-perception, permanence, impermanence, and effect.

children.text: sādharmyeṇa pratyavasthān aviśiṣyamāṇaṃ syāpanāhetutaḥ sādharmyasamaḥ, viśeṣaṃ tatra tatrodāhariṣyāmyaḥ, evaṃ vaidharmyasamaprabhṛtayopi nirvaktavyāḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: A counter-argument through similarity that is indistinguishable from the establishing reason is <s>sādharmyasama</s> (the futile rejoinder based on similarity). We shall illustrate the distinction in each case. Similarly, <s>vaidharmyasama</s> and the rest are also to be explained. [End of NyS 5.1.1]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.2]
The definition, however —

<s>NyS</s> 5.1.2: Because of the tenability of the opposite of that property when subsuming through similarity and dissimilarity, [these are called] the <s>sādharmyasama</s> and <s>vaidharmyasama</s> [futile rejoinders].

children.text: sādharmyeṇopasaṃkāre sādhyadharmviparyayopapatteḥ sādharmyeṇaiva pratyavasthānam aviśiṣyamāṇaṃ sthāpanāhetutaḥ sādharmyasamaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ, nidarśanam-- 'kriyāvānātmā-- dravyasya kriyaḥhetuguṇayogāt. dravyaṃ loṣṭaḥ kriyāhetuguṇayukta kriyāvān tathā cātmā tasamāt kriyāvān' iti, evamupasaṃhṛte paraḥ sādharmyeṇaiva pratyavatiṣṭhate-- 'niṣkriya ātmā-- vibhuno dravyasya niṣkriyatvāt. vibhu cākāśaṃ niṣkriyaṃ ca tathā cātmā tasmāt niṣkriyaḥ' iti, na cāsti viśeṣahetuḥ-- kriyāvatsādharmyāt kriyāvatā bhavitavyaṃ na purakriyasādharmyād niṣkriyeṇeti, viśeṣahetvabhāvān sādharmyasamāḥ pratiṣedho bhavati|

atha vaidharmyasamaḥ-- 'kriyāhetuguṇayukto loṣṭaḥ paricchinno dṛṣṭo na tathātmā tasmānna loṣṭavat kriyāvān' iti. na nāsti viśeṣahetuḥ-- kriyāvatsādharmyāt kriyāvatā bhavitavyaṃ na punaḥ kriyāvadvaidharmyādkiyeṇeti. viśeṣahetvabhāvād vaidharmyasamaḥ|
children.translated_text: Now the <s>vaidharmyasama</s>: 'The clod of earth, possessing the cause and quality of action, is observed to be limited [in size] — but <s>ātman</s> is not so; therefore it does not possess action like a clod.' There is no distinguishing reason — [to say] 'because of similarity with what possesses action, it must possess action, but not because of dissimilarity from what possesses action must it lack action.' Because of the absence of a distinguishing reason, [this is] the <s>vaidharmyasama</s>.

children.text: vaidharmyeṇa copasaṃhāre-- 'niṣkriya ātmā-- vibhutvāt. kriyāvad dravyamavibhu dṛṣṭaṃ yathā loṣṭaḥ na ca tathātmā tasmād niṣkriyaḥ' iti, vaidharmyeṇa pratyavasthānam-- 'niṣkriyaṃ dravyamākāśaṃ kriyāhetuguṇarahitaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ na tathātmā tasmānna niṣkriyaḥ' iti. ni cāsti viśeṣahetuḥ-- kriyāvadvaidharmyād niṣkriyeṇa bhavitavyaṃ na punarakriyavaidharmyāt kriyāvateti. viśeṣahetvabhāvād vaidharmyasamaḥ|
children.translated_text: And when subsumption is through dissimilarity: '<s>Ātman</s> is without action — because of being pervasive. A substance possessing action is observed to be non-pervasive, like a clod of earth, but <s>ātman</s> is not so; therefore it is without action.' The counter-argument through dissimilarity: 'The substance <s>ākāśa</s>, which is without action, is observed to lack the cause and quality of action, but <s>ātman</s> is not so; therefore it is not without action.' And there is no distinguishing reason — [to say] 'because of dissimilarity from what possesses action, it must be without action, but not because of dissimilarity from what lacks action must it possess action.' Because of the absence of a distinguishing reason, [this is] the <s>vaidharmyasama</s>.

children.text: atha ( punaḥ ) sādharmyasamaḥ-- 'kriyāvān loṣṭaḥ kriyāhetuguṇayukto dṛṣṭaḥ tathā cātmā tasmātpava kriyāvān' iti. na cāsti viśeṣahetuḥ-- kriyāvadvaidharmyād niṣkriyo na punaḥ kriyāvatsādharmyāt kriyāvāniti. viśeṣahetvabhāvāt sādharmyasamaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: And then the <s>sādharmyasama</s>: 'The clod of earth possesses action and is observed to possess the cause and quality of action; so too <s>ātman</s>; therefore it too possesses action.' And there is no distinguishing reason — [to say] 'because of dissimilarity from what possesses action, it lacks action, but not because of similarity with what possesses action does it possess action.' Because of the absence of a distinguishing reason, [this is] the <s>sādharmyasama</s>. [End of NyS 5.1.2]

When subsumption is through similarity, because of the tenability of the opposite of the provable property, a counter-argument through similarity alone that is indistinguishable from the establishing reason is the <s>sādharmyasama</s> refutation. An illustration: '<s>Ātman</s> possesses action — because a substance has conjunction with the cause and quality of action. The substance — a clod of earth — is observed to possess the cause and quality of action and to possess action; so too <s>ātman</s>; therefore it possesses action.' When thus subsumed, the opponent counter-argues through similarity alone: '<s>Ātman</s> is without action — because a pervasive substance is without action. <s>Ākāśa</s> (space) is pervasive and without action; so too <s>ātman</s>; therefore it is without action.' And there is no distinguishing reason — [to say] 'because of similarity with what possesses action, it must possess action, but not because of similarity with what lacks action must it lack action.' Because of the absence of a distinguishing reason, the <s>sādharmyasama</s> refutation obtains.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.3]
The answer to both of these —
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.3: Its establishment is like the establishment of 'cow' from 'cowness.'

children.text: sādharmyamātreṇa vaidharmyamātreṇa ca sādhyasādhane pratijñāyamāne syādavyavasthā sā tu dharmaviśeṣe nopapadyate, gosādharmyād gotvājjātiviśeṣād gauḥ sidhyati na tu sāsnādisaṃbandhāt. aśvādivaidharmyād gotvādeva gauḥ sidhyati na guṇādibhedāt, taccaitat kṛtavyākhyānamavayavaprakaraṇe, pramāṇānāmabhisaṃbandhāccaikārthakāritvaṃ samānaṃ vākye iti, hetvābhāsāśrayā khalv iyam avyavastheti // 3 //
children.translated_text: When proof and what is to be proved are asserted through mere similarity or mere dissimilarity, there would be indeterminacy. But that is not tenable with respect to a specific property. A cow is established through similarity with a cow — through cow-ness (<s>gotva</s>), the specific universal — not through connection with dewlap and the like. Through dissimilarity with a horse and the rest, a cow is established through cow-ness alone, not through difference in qualities and the like. And this has been explained in the section on the members [of a syllogism]. The co-operation of the means of valid knowledge toward a single purpose is the same as in a sentence. This indeterminacy is based on fallacious reasons. [End of NyS 5.1.3]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.4]

<s>NyS</s> 5.1.4: Because of the alternative properties of what is to be proved and the illustration, and because both [can be made] what is to be proved — the [futile rejoinders of] excess (<s>utkarṣa</s>), deficiency (<s>apakarṣa</s>), commendable (<s>varṇya</s>), censurable (<s>avarṇya</s>), alternative (<s>vikalpa</s>), and equal-to-what-is-to-be-proved (<s>sādhyasama</s>).

children.text:
dṛṣṭāntadharma sādhye samāsajata utkarṣasamaḥ-- yadi kriyāhetuguṇayogalloṣṭavat kriyāvānātmā ( tadā ) loṣṭavadeva sparśavānapi prāpnoti. atha na sparśavān loṣṭavat kriyāvānapi na prāpnoti, viparyaye vā viśeṣo vaktavya iti|
sādhye dharmābhāvaṃ dṛṣṭāntāt prasajato 'pakarṣasamaḥ-- loṣṭaḥ khalu kriyāvān avibhurdṛṣṭaḥ kāmamātmāpi kriyāvānavibhurastu. viparyaye vā viśeṣo vaktavya iti|
khyāpanīyo varṇyo viparyayādavarṇyaḥ tāvetau sādhyadṛṣṭāntadharmauṃ viparyasyato varṇyāvarṇyasamau bhavataḥ|
children.translated_text: What is to be made known is commendable (<s>varṇya</s>); the contrary is censurable (<s>avarṇya</s>). These two, by reversing the properties of what is to be proved and the illustration, become the commendable-censurable-equal (<s>varṇyāvarṇyasama</s>).

children.text: sādhanadharmayukte dṛṣṭānte dharmāntaravikalpāt sādhyadharmavikalpaṃ prasajato vikalpasamaḥ-- kriyāguṇahetuyuktaṃ kiñcid guru yathā loṣṭaḥ kiñcicca laghu yathā vāyurevaṃ kriyāhetuguṇayuktaṃ kiñcat kriyāvat syād yathā loṣṭaḥ kiñcidakriyaṃ yathātmā. viśeṣo vā vācya iti|
children.translated_text: When an alternative regarding the property of what is to be proved is derived from the illustration that possesses the properties of the proof, and an alternative property [is posited] — [it is] the alternative-equal (<s>vikalpasama</s>) — 'something possessing a quality that is the cause of action is heavy, like a clod; and something [possessing the same quality] is light, like wind. Similarly, something possessing a quality that is the cause of action may have action, like a clod; and something may be without action, like the self.' Or the distinction must be stated.

children.text: hetvādyivayavasāmarthyayogī dharmaḥ sādhyastaṃ dṛṣṭānte prasajataḥ sādhyasamaḥ-- yadi 'yathā loṣṭastathātmā ?' prāptastarhi 'yathātmā tathā loṣṭaḥ' iti. sādhyaścāyamātmā kriyāvāniti kāmaṃ loṣṭopi sādhyaḥ, atha naivam ? na tarhi 'yathā loṣṭastathātmā' (iti ) // 4 //
children.translated_text: A property that is to be proved, possessing the power of the members [of a syllogism] beginning with the reason — when that is applied to the illustration, [it is] the equal-to-what-is-to-be-proved (<s>sādhyasama</s>) — 'if as a clod, so the self' — then 'as the self, so too the clod' is also reached. And this self is to be proved as having action; very well, the clod too is to be proved [likewise]. Or if not so, then 'as a clod, so the self' does not hold. [End of NyS 5.1.4]

When a property of the illustration is applied to what is to be proved, [it is] the excess-equal (<s>utkarṣasama</s>) — 'if the self has action because of possessing a quality that is the cause of action, like a clod of earth, then it should also have touch like a clod.' Or if it does not have touch, then like a clod it should also not have action; or the distinction must be stated in the contrary case. When the absence of a property in what is to be proved is derived from the illustration, [it is] the deficiency-equal (<s>apakarṣasama</s>) — 'a clod is observed to have action and to be non-pervasive; very well, let the self too have action and be non-pervasive.' Or the distinction must be stated in the contrary case.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.5]
The reply to these —
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.5: Because establishment [occurs] through subsumption of partial similarity, there is no refutation through dissimilarity.

children.text: alabhyaḥ siddhasya nihnavaḥ, siddhaṃ ca kiñcitsādharmyādupamānam-- 'yathā gaustathā gavayaḥ' iti, tatra na labhyo gogavayayordharmavikalpaścodayitum, evaṃ sādhake dharme dṛṣṭāntādisāmarthyayukte na labhyaḥ sādhyadṛṣṭāntayordharmavikalpāt

children.translated_text: to state a refutation based on dissimilarity and difference of properties between what is to be proved and the illustration. [End of NyS 5.1.5]

The denial of what is established is not possible. And comparison is established through partial similarity — 'as a cow, so a <s>gavaya</s> (wild ox).' There, one cannot raise the objection of the difference of properties between a cow and a <s>gavaya</s>. Similarly, when the proving property is endowed with the power of the illustration and the rest, it is not possible
[Section: NySBh 5.1.6]
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.6: And because the illustration is tenable through the transfer of what is to be proved.

children.text: yatra laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ buddhisāmyaṃ tenāviparīto 'rtho 'tidiśyate prajñāpanārtham. evaṃ sādhyātideśād dṛṣṭānte upapadyamāne sādhyatvamanupapannamiti // 6 //
children.translated_text: Where there is equality of understanding among ordinary people and examiners, the uncontroverted meaning is transferred for the purpose of making known. Thus, when the illustration is tenable through the transfer of what is to be proved, [the claim that] it is [itself] something to be proved is untenable. [End of NyS 5.1.6]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.7]

children.text: NyS_5,1.7: prāpya sādhyamaprāpya vā hetoḥ prāptyāviśiṣṭatvād aprāptyāsādhakatvācca prāptyaprāptisamau //
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 5.1.7: Because the reason is undifferentiated whether it reaches or does not reach what is to be proved, and because without reaching it cannot prove — the [futile rejoinders of] reaching-equal and not-reaching-equal.

children.text: hetuḥ prāpya vā sādhyaṃ sādhayedaprāpya vā ?, na tāvat prāpya-- prāptyāmaviśiṣṭatvād asādhakaḥu dvayorvidyamānayoḥ prāptau satyāṃ kiṃ kasya sādhakaṃ sādhyaṃ vā ?|
children.translated_text: Does the reason prove what is to be proved by reaching it or without reaching it? Not by reaching — because when both [reason and what is to be proved] are present, reaching being undifferentiated, it does not prove. When both exist and reaching obtains, what proves what, and what is to be proved?

children.text: aprāpya sādhakaṃ na bhavati-- nāprāptaḥ pradīpaḥ prakāśayatīti|
children.translated_text: Without reaching, it cannot prove — a lamp that has not reached [an object] does not illuminate it.

children.text: prāptyā pratyavasthānaṃ prāptisamaḥ, aprāptyā pratyavasthānam aprāptisamaḥ // 7 //
children.translated_text: Objecting by [the impossibility of] reaching is the reaching-equal; objecting by [the impossibility of] not-reaching is the not-reaching-equal. [End of NyS 5.1.7]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.8]
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.8: Because of the observation that pots and the like are produced [through reaching], and because of affliction [i.e., influence at a distance], there is no refutation.

children.text: ubhayathā khalvayuktaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ-- kartṛkaraṇādhikaraṇāni prāpya mṛdaṃ ghaṭādikāryaṃ viṣpādayanti, abhicārācca pīḍane sati dṛṣṭam aprāpya sādhakatvamiti // 8 //
children.translated_text: In both ways, the refutation is unjustified. The agent, instrument, and substrate, by reaching the clay, produce the pot and other effects. And through affliction (<s>abhicāra</s>, i.e., sorcery), when there is affliction, the proving without reaching is observed. [End of NyS 5.1.8]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.9]

children.text: NyS_5,1.9: dṛṣṭāntasya kāraṇānapadeśāt pratyavasthānācca pratidṛṣṭāntena prasaṅgapratidṛṣṭāntasamau //
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 5.1.9: Because of not adducing a reason for the illustration and because of objecting with a counter-example — the [futile rejoinders of] implication-equal and counter-example-equal.

children.text: sādhanasyāpi sādhanaṃ vaktavyamiti prasaṅgena pratyavasthānaṃ prasaṅgasamaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ-- kriyāhetuguṇayogī kriyāvān loṣṭa itiheturnāpadiśyate na ca hetumantareṇa siddhirastīti|

pratidṛṣṭāntena pratyavasthānaṃ pratidṛṣṭāntasamaḥ-- 'kriyāvānātmā kriyāhetuguṇayogāt loṣṭavat' ityukte pratidṛṣṭānta upādīyate-- 'kriyāhetuguṇayuktamākāśaṃ niṣkriyaṃ dṛṣṭam' iti, kaḥ punarākāśasya kriyāheturguṇaḥ ? vāyunā saṃyogaḥ saṃskārāpekṣaḥ vāyuvanaspatisaṃyogavaditi // 9 //
children.translated_text: Objecting with a counter-example is the counter-example-equal (<s>pratidṛṣṭāntasama</s>) — when it is said 'the self has action because of possessing a quality that is the cause of action, like a clod,' a counter-example is adduced: 'space, possessing a quality that is the cause of action, is observed to be without action.' What then is the quality that causes action in space? Conjunction with wind, which depends on momentum (<s>saṃskāra</s>), like the conjunction of wind and trees. [End of NyS 5.1.9]

Objecting by implication that 'a proof for the proof too must be stated' is the implication-equal (<s>prasaṅgasama</s>) — [the objector says:] 'A clod has action because of possessing a quality that is the cause of action' — a reason is not adduced [for this], and without a reason there is no establishment.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.10]
The reply to these two —
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.10: Like the cessation of the implication of taking up a lamp, that [objection] is refuted.

children.text:
idaṃ tāvadayaṃ pṛṣṭo vaktumarhati-- atha ke pradīpamupādadate kimarthaṃ ceti ?, didṛkṣamāṇā dṛśyadarśanārthamiti / atha pradīpaṃ didṛkṣamāṇāḥ pradīpāntaraṃ kasmānnopādadate ?, antareṇāpi pradīpāntaraṃ dṛśyate pradīpastatra pradīpadarśanārthaṃ pradīpopādānaṃ nirarthakam|
atha dṛṣṭāntaḥ kimarthamucyate iti ?. aprajñātasya jñāpanārthamiti|
atha dṛṣṭānte kāraṇādeśaḥ kimarthaṃ mṛgyate ?, yadi prajñāpanārtham ?, prajñāto dṛṣṭāntaḥ sa khalu--"laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ yasminnarthe buddhisāmyaṃ sa dṛṣṭāntaḥ 1-1-25"iti tatprajñāpanārthaḥkāraṇāpadeśo nirarthaka iti prasaṅgasamasyottaram // 10 //
children.translated_text: Firstly, one being questioned should be asked — who then takes up a lamp, and for what purpose? Those who wish to see, for the purpose of seeing visible things. Why then do those who wish to see a lamp not take up another lamp? Because even without another lamp, the [first] lamp is seen — therefore, taking up a lamp for the purpose of seeing a lamp is pointless. Then, for what purpose is an illustration stated? For the purpose of making known what is not understood. Then, for what purpose is a reason sought for the illustration? If for the purpose of making known — the illustration is [already] well-known — for 'an illustration is that regarding which there is equality of understanding among ordinary people and examiners' [NyS 1.1.25]. Therefore, seeking a reason for the purpose of making that known is pointless. This is the reply to the implication-equal. [End of NyS 5.1.10]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.11]
Now the reply to the counter-example-equal —
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.11: And if the counter-example [were to serve as] a reason, the illustration is not a non-reason.

children.text: pratidṛṣṭāntaṃ bruvatā na viśeṣaheturapadiśyate-- anena prakāreṇa pratidṛṣṭāntaḥ sādhako na dṛṣṭānta iti, evaṃ pratidṛṣṭāntahetutve nāheturdṛṣṭānta ityupapadyate. sa ca kathaṃ heturnasyād yadyapratiṣiddhaḥ sādhakaḥ syāditi // 11 //
children.translated_text: One who adduces a counter-example does not adduce a reason for the distinction — [specifying] the manner in which the counter-example proves but not the illustration. Thus, when the counter-example [is claimed to] serve as reason, 'the illustration is not a non-reason' is tenable. And how would it not be a reason, if, being unrefuted, it would be probative? [End of NyS 5.1.11]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.12]
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.12: The non-arising-equal (<s>anutpattisama</s>): because of the absence of a cause prior to production.

children.text: anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvād ghaṭavadityukte apara āha-- prāgutpatteranutpanne śabde prayatnānantarīyakatvamanityatvakāraṇaṃ nāsti tadabhāvād nityatvaṃ prāptaṃ nityasya cotpattirnāsti|

children.translated_text: Objecting by [the impossibility of] non-arising is the non-arising-equal. [End of NyS 5.1.12]

When it is said 'sound is non-eternal because of being invariably preceded by effort, like a pot' — another says: 'Prior to production, in the unarisen sound, the property of being invariably preceded by effort, which is the cause of non-eternality, does not exist. Because of its absence, eternality is reached. And what is eternal does not have arising.'
[Section: NySBh 5.1.13]
The reply to this — <s>NyS</s> 5.1.13: Because the reason is tenable for what has arisen as being of such a nature, there is no negation of the cause.

children.text: tathābhāvādutpannasyeti-- utpannaḥ khalvayaṃ śabda iti bhavati. prāgutpatteḥ śabda eva nāsti-- utpannasya śabdabhāvāt. śabdasya sataḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvam anityatvakāraṇamupapadyate. kāraṇopapatterayuktoyaṃ doṣaḥ--

children.translated_text: 'because of the absence of a cause prior to production.' [End of NyS 5.1.13]

'Because of being of such a nature, [the reason applies] to what has arisen' — this sound has indeed arisen; this is the case. Prior to production, the sound simply does not exist — because of the arisen nature of the sound. For the existent sound, the property of being invariably preceded by effort as the cause of non-eternality is tenable. Because of the tenability of the cause, this objection is unjustified —
[Section: NySBh 5.1.14]

<s>NyS</s> 5.1.14: The doubt-equal (<s>saṃśayasama</s>): because of the common imperceptibility of the universal and the illustration, and because of similarity with both the eternal and the non-eternal.

children.text: anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvād ghaṭavadityukte hetau. saṃśayena pratyavatiṣṭhate-- sati prayatnānāntarīyakatve astyevāsya nityena sāmānyena sādharmyam- aindriyakatvam. asti ca ghaṭenānityena. ato nityānityasādharmyādanivṛttaḥ saṃśaya iti // 14 //
children.translated_text: When it is said 'sound is non-eternal because of being invariably preceded by effort, like a pot' — one objects with doubt: 'given the property of being invariably preceded by effort, there is indeed similarity with the eternal universal through its imperceptibility; and there is also [similarity] with the non-eternal pot. Therefore, because of similarity with both the eternal and the non-eternal, the doubt is not resolved.' [End of NyS 5.1.14]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.15]
The reply to this —

children.text: NyS_5,1.15: sādharmyātsaṃśaye na saṃśayo vaidharmyād ubhayathā vā saṃśaye 'tyantasaṃśayaprasaṅgo nityatvānabhyupagamācca sāmānyasyāpratiṣedhaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 5.1.15: When doubt [might arise] from similarity, there is no doubt [when there is] dissimilarity; or when doubt [arises] from both, the consequence of perpetual doubt; and because eternality [of the universal] is not accepted, there is no refutation of the universal.

children.text: viśeṣād vaidharmyādavadhāryamāṇe 'rthe 'puruṣaḥ' iti na sthāṇupuruṣasādharmyāt saṃśayo 'vakāśaṃ labhate, evaṃ vaidharmyād viśeṣāt prayatnānantarīyakatvādavadhāryamāṇe śabdasyānityatve nityānityasādharmyāt saṃśayo 'vakāśaṃ na labhate. yadi vai labheta ? tataḥ sthāṇupuruṣasādharmyānucchedādatyantaṃ saṃśayaḥ syāt, gṛhyamāṇe ca viśeṣe nityasādharmyaṃ saṃśayaheturiti nābhyupagamyate-- nahi gṛhyamāṇe puruṣasya viśeṣe sthāṇupuruṣasādharmyaṃ saṃśayaheturbhavati // 15 //
children.translated_text: When an object is being determined through a distinguishing feature, i.e., dissimilarity — [as when one determines] 'this is a person' — doubt based on the similarity of post and person does not find scope. Similarly, when the non-eternality of sound is being determined through a distinguishing feature — being invariably preceded by effort — doubt based on similarity with both eternal and non-eternal does not find scope. For if it did find scope, then because the similarity of post and person is never cut off, there would be perpetual doubt. And when a distinguishing feature is grasped, the similarity with the eternal as a cause of doubt is not accepted — for when a distinguishing feature of a person is grasped, the similarity of post and person does not become a cause of doubt. [End of NyS 5.1.15]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.16]
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.16: The topic-equal (<s>prakaraṇasama</s>): because of the establishment of [both sides of] the topic through similarity with both.

children.text: ubhayenaunityena cānityena sādharmyāt pakṣapratipakṣayoḥ pravṛttiḥ prakriyā, 'anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvād ghaṭavat' ityekaḥ pakṣaṃ pravartayati. dvitīyaśca nityasādharmyāt. evaṃ ca sati 'prayatnānantarīyakatvāt' itiheturanityasādharmyeṇocyamāno na prakaraṇamativartate. prakaraṇānativṛtternirṇayānanivartanam, samānaṃ caitannityasādharmyeṇocyamāne hetau, tadidaṃ prakaraṇānativṛttyā pratyavasthānaṃ prakaraṇasamaḥ|
samānaṃ caitadvaidharmye 'pi = ubhayavaidharmyāt prakriyāsiddheḥ prakaraṇasama iti // 16 //
children.translated_text: And this is the same with respect to dissimilarity too — the topic-equal is because of the establishment of the topic through dissimilarity with both. [End of NyS 5.1.16]

Because of similarity with both — the eternal and the non-eternal — there is the operation of the thesis and the counter-thesis, [which is] the topic (<s>prakriyā</s>). 'Sound is non-eternal because of being invariably preceded by effort, like a pot' — one advances this thesis. And the second, because of similarity with the eternal. And this being so, the reason 'because of being invariably preceded by effort,' when stated with similarity to the non-eternal, does not transcend the topic. Because of not transcending the topic, there is no bringing about of a conclusion. And this is the same when the reason is stated with similarity to the eternal. This is the topic-equal — objecting by not transcending the topic.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.17]
The reply to this —
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.17: Because of the establishment of the topic from the counter-thesis, refutation is untenable because of the tenability of the counter-thesis.

children.text: ubhayasādharmyāt prakriyāsiddhiṃ bruvatā pratipakṣāt prakriyāsiddhiruktā bhavati, yadyubhyasādharmyaṃ tatraikataraḥ pratipakṣa ityevaṃ satyupapannaḥ pratipakṣo bhavati. pratipakṣopapatteranupapannaḥ pratiṣedhaḥ-- yataḥ pratipakṣopapattiḥ pratiṣedhopapattiśceti vipratiṣiddhamiti|
tattvānavadhāraṇācca prakriyāsiddhiḥ-- viparyaye prakaraṇāvasānātu tattvāvadhāraṇe hyavasitaṃ prakaraṇaṃ bhavatīti // 17 //
children.translated_text: And the establishment of the topic is because of the non-determination of truth — in the contrary case, because of the conclusion of the topic, for when the truth is determined, the topic has been concluded. [End of NyS 5.1.17]

One who says 'the establishment of the topic is from similarity with both' has [thereby] stated the establishment of the topic from the counter-thesis. If there is similarity with both, then one of the two is a counter-thesis — this being so, the counter-thesis is tenable. Because of the tenability of the counter-thesis, the refutation is untenable — because the tenability of the counter-thesis and the tenability of refutation are contradictory.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.18]
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.18: The non-reason-equal (<s>ahetusama</s>): because of the non-establishment of the reason in the three times.

children.text: hetuḥusādhanaṃ tat sādhyāt pūrvaṃ paścāt saha vā bhavet. yadi pūrvaṃ sādhanam ? asati sādhye kasya sādhanam, atha paścāt ? asati sādhane kasyedaṃ sādhyam, atha yugapat sādhyasādhate ? dvayorvidyamānayoḥ kiṃ kasya sādhanaṃ kiṃ kasya sādhyam. iti heturahetunā na viśiṣyate|

children.translated_text: The objection based on the similarity to a non-reason, due to the commonality with a non-reason, is the <s>ahetusama</s> (fallacy of the equal non-reason). [End of NyS 5.1.18]

The reason, i.e., the means of establishing — that may be prior to, subsequent to, or simultaneous with what is to be established. If the means of establishing is prior — in the absence of what is to be established, what is it a means of establishing? If subsequent — in the absence of the means of establishing, what is this that is to be established? If the object to be established and the means of establishing are simultaneous — when both are [already] present, what is the means of establishing what, and what is to be established by what? Thus the reason is not distinguished from a non-reason.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.19]
The reply to this —
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.19: Not [so], because the establishment of what is to be established from a reason is not [dependent on] the three times.

children.text: na traikālyāsiddhiḥ, kasmāt ? hetutaḥ sādhyasiddheḥ, nirvatainīyasya nirvṛttiḥ vijñeyasya vijñānam ubhayaṃ kāraṇato dṛśyate. soyaṃ mahān pratyakṣaviṣaya udāharaṇamiti|
yattu khalūktam-- asati sādhye kasya sādhanamiti ? yattu nirvartyate yacca vijñāpyate tasyeti // 19 //
children.translated_text: As for what was said — 'in the absence of what is to be established, what is it a means of establishing?' — [the answer is:] it is the means of establishing that which is to be produced and that which is to be made known. [End of NyS 5.1.19]

It is not [dependent on] the non-establishment through the three times. Why? Because what is to be established is established from the reason. The production of what is to be produced and the knowledge of what is to be known — both are seen [to proceed] from a cause. This great [fact], being an object of perception, is the example.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.20]
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.20: And because of the inapplicability of the denial, [there is] no denial of what is to be denied.

children.text: 'pūrvaṃ paścād yugapadvā' pratiṣedha iti nopapadyate. pratiṣedhānupapatteḥ sthāpanāhetuḥ siddha iti // 20 //
children.translated_text: '[The reason is] prior to, subsequent to, or simultaneous with' — this denial is untenable. Because of the inapplicability of the denial, the reason for the establishment [of the thesis] is proven. [End of NyS 5.1.20]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.21]
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.21: The <s>arthāpattisama</s> (fallacy of presumption-parity) [is the objection that] establishes a counter-thesis through presumption.

children.text: 'anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvād ghaṭavat' iti sthāpite pakṣe arthāpattyā pratipakṣaṃ sādhayato 'rthāpattisamaḥ, yadi prayatnānantarīyakatvādanityasādharmyādanityaḥ śabda iti ? ( tadā ) arthādāpadyate-- nityasādharmyānnitya iti, asti tvasya nityena sādharmyam asparśatvamiti // 21 //
children.translated_text: When the thesis 'sound is non-eternal, because of being produced immediately after effort, like a pot' has been established, one who establishes a counter-thesis through <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) commits the <s>arthāpattisama</s>: if sound is non-eternal because of the similarity with non-eternal [things] due to being produced immediately after effort, then it is presumed from this that [sound is] eternal due to similarity with eternal [things]. And it does have a similarity with the eternal — namely, intangibility. [End of NyS 5.1.21]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.22]
The reply to this —

<s>NyS</s> 5.1.22: The tenability of the abandonment of the thesis [follows] from the presumption of what is unstated; because of the unstatedness and because of the non-conclusiveness of the presumption.

children.text: anupapādya sāmarthyam anuktamarthādāpadyate itibruvataḥ pakṣahānerupapattiḥ-- anuktatvāt = anityapakṣasiddhau arthādāpannam-- nityapakṣasya hāniriti|

anekāntikatvāccārthāpatteḥ = ubhayapakṣasamā ceyamarthāpattiḥ-- yadi nityasādharmyādasparśatvādākāśavacca nityaḥ śabdaḥ ? ( tadā ) arthādāpannam-- anityasādharmyāt prayatnānantarīyakatvādanitya iti, na ceyaṃ viparyayamātrādekāntenārthāpattiḥ. na khalu vai dhanasya grāvṇaḥ patanamiti arthādāpadyate-- dravāṇāmapāṃ patanābhāva iti // 22 //
children.translated_text: And because of the non-conclusiveness of the presumption — this presumption applies equally to both theses. If sound is eternal because of the similarity with eternal [things] due to intangibility, like <s>ākāśa</s> (space), then it is presumed from that — [sound is] non-eternal because of the similarity with non-eternal [things] due to being produced immediately after effort. And this presumption does not [operate] conclusively from mere reversal alone. For surely the falling of a stone that is heavy — from this it is not presumed that there is no falling of water, which is fluid. [End of NyS 5.1.22]

Without demonstrating the capacity [of the argument], one who says 'it is presumed from the meaning without being stated' — for him, the tenability of the abandonment of the thesis [follows] — because of unstatedness. That is: once the thesis of non-eternality is established, it is presumed from that — the abandonment of the thesis of eternality.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.23]

<s>NyS</s> 5.1.23: The <s>aviśeṣasama</s> (fallacy of non-distinction) [is the objection that], because of the applicability of one property, in the non-distinction [between the two], the consequence of universal non-distinction [follows] from the applicability of existence.

children.text: eko dharmaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvaṃ śabdaghaṭayorupapadyate ityaviśeṣe ubhayoranitayatve sarvasyāviśeṣaḥ prasajyate|
children.translated_text: One property — being produced immediately after effort — applies to both sound and pot; in the non-distinction [between them], the non-distinction of everything regarding non-eternality would follow.

children.text: katham ? sadbhāvopapatteḥ = eko dharmaḥ sadbhāvaḥ sarvasyopapadyate|
children.translated_text: How? Because of the applicability of existence — one property, existence, applies to everything.
Because of the applicability of existence and the consequence of universal non-distinction, the objection [is called] the <s>aviśeṣasama</s>. [End of NyS 5.1.23]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.24]
The reply to this —
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.24: Because of the inapplicability of the property in some cases and its applicability in others, there is no refutation.

children.text: yathā sādhyadṛṣṭāntayorekadharmasya prayatnānantarīyakatvasyopapatteranityatvaṃ dharmāntaram aviśeṣo naivaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ sadbhāvopapattinimittaṃ dharmāntaramasti yenāviśeṣaḥ syāt|
children.translated_text: Just as the non-eternality, which is a further property, [arises] from the applicability of one property — being produced immediately after effort — to the object to be established and the example, so it is not [the case] that for all things, through the applicability of existence, there is another property by which there would be non-distinction.

children.text: atha matam-- anityatvameva dharmāntaraṃ sadbhāvopapattinimittaṃ bhāvānāṃ sarvatra syāditi ?, evaṃ khalu vai kalpyamāne-- 'anityāḥ sarve bhāvāḥ sadbhāvopapatteḥ' itipakṣaḥ prāpnoti, tatra pratijñārthavyatiriktamanyadudāharaṇaṃ nāsti. anudāharaṇaśca heturnāstīti, pratijñaikadeśasya codāharaṇatvamanupapannam-- na hi sādhyamudāharaṇaṃ bhavati, sataśca nityānityabhāvādanityatvānupapattistasmāt 'sadbhāvopapatteḥ sarvāviśeṣaprasaṅgaḥ' iti nirabhidheyametadvākyamiti|
children.translated_text: And if one thinks — non-eternality itself is the further property which, due to the applicability of existence, would apply to things universally — indeed, when such is supposed, the thesis 'all things are non-eternal because of the applicability of existence' is reached. In that case, there is no example other than the content of the thesis. And a reason without an example does not exist. And it is untenable that part of the thesis serves as the example — for what is to be established cannot be the example. And because of the fact that what exists is [sometimes] eternal and [sometimes] non-eternal, the non-eternality [of everything] is untenable. Therefore, the statement 'the consequence of universal non-distinction because of the applicability of existence' is meaningless.

children.text: 'sarvabhāvānāṃ sadbhāvopapatteranityatvam' iti bruvatānujñātaṃ śabdasyānityatvaṃ tatrānupapannaḥ pratiṣedha iti // 24 //
children.translated_text: By one who says 'all things are non-eternal because of the applicability of existence,' the non-eternality of sound is accepted; regarding that, the refutation is untenable. [End of NyS 5.1.24]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.25]
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.25: The <s>upapattisama</s> (fallacy of tenability-parity) [is the objection based on] the applicability of reasons for both.

children.text: yady anityatvakāraṇamupapadyate śabdasya ity anityaḥ śabdaḥ ? nityatvakāraṇamapyupapadyate 'syāsparśatvamiti nityatvamapyupapadyate|
ubhayasya = anityatvasya nityatvasya ca kāraṇopapattyā pratyavasthānamupapattisamaḥ // 25 //
children.translated_text: The objection based on the applicability of reasons for both — non-eternality and eternality — is the <s>upapattisama</s>. [End of NyS 5.1.25]

If the reason for non-eternality applies to sound — namely, that sound is non-eternal because of being produced immediately after effort — the reason for eternality also applies to it, namely its intangibility; therefore eternality is also tenable.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.26]
The reply to this —
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.26: Because of the acceptance of the applicability of a reason, there is no refutation.

children.text: "ubhayakāraṇopapatteḥ"itibruvatā nānityatvakāraṇopapatteranityatvaṃ pratiṣidhyate, yadi pratiṣidhyate ? nobhayakāraṇopapattiḥ syāt|

children.translated_text: From the statement of the applicability of reasons for both, the applicability of the reason for non-eternality is accepted; from the acceptance, the refutation is untenable.
[Objection:] The refutation is from the contradiction? [Reply:] The contradiction is equal [for both sides].

children.text: ekasya nityatvānityatvaprasaṅgaṃ vyāhataṃ bruvatā uktaḥ pratiṣedha iticet ? spapakṣaparapakṣayoḥ samāno vyāghātaḥ sa ca naikatarasya sādhaka iti // 26 //
children.translated_text: If one says the refutation is because one who states the consequence of both eternality and non-eternality of a single [thing] contradicts himself — the contradiction is equal for one's own thesis and the opponent's thesis, and it does not establish either one. [End of NyS 5.1.26]

By one who says 'because of the applicability of reasons for both,' the applicability of the reason for non-eternality is not denied. If it were denied, there would not be the applicability of reasons for both.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.27]
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.27: The <s>upalabdhisama</s> (fallacy of apprehension-parity) [is the objection that], even in the absence of the stated reason, [the property is] apprehended.
The objection based on the apprehension of the property to be established even in the absence of the stated means of establishing — is the <s>upalabdhisama</s>. [End of NyS 5.1.27]

Even in the absence of the stated reason for non-eternality — being produced immediately after effort — the non-eternality of the sound produced from the breaking of a tree-branch by the force of wind is apprehended.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.28]
The reply to this —
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.28: Because the property is also tenable from another cause, there is no refutation.

children.text: prayatnānantarīyakatvāditi bruvatā kāraṇata utpattirabhidhīyate. na ( tu ) kāryasya kāraṇaniyamaḥ, yida ca kāraṇāntarādapyupapadyamānasya śabdasya tad anityatvamupapadyate ? kimatrapratiṣidhyate ? iti // 28 //
children.translated_text: By saying 'because of being produced immediately after effort,' production from a cause is stated. There is no restriction of the effect to [one particular] cause. And if the non-eternality of sound, which is tenable from another cause as well, is [thereby] tenable — what is refuted here? [End of NyS 5.1.28]

children.text: na prāguccāraṇād vidyamānasya śabdasyānupalabdhiḥ, kasmāt ? āvaraṇādyanupalabdheḥuyathā vidyamānasyodakāderarthasyāvāraṇāderanupalabdhirnaivaṃ śabdasyāgrahaṇakāraṇenāvaraṇādinānupalabdhiḥugṛhyeta caitadasyāgrahaṇakāraṇamudakādivad na ( ca ) gṛhyate tasmādudakādiviparītaḥ śabdo 'nupalabhyamāna iti---
children.translated_text: [It is objected:] sound, which exists prior to utterance, is not non-apprehended. Why? Because of the non-apprehension of obstructions and the like — just as for an existing object such as water, there is non-apprehension because of obstructions and the like, so too the non-apprehension of sound is due to a cause of non-grasping such as obstructions. And this cause of non-grasping would be grasped like [the obstruction of] water and the like — but it is not grasped. Therefore, sound, being non-apprehended, is the opposite of water and the like —
[Section: NySBh 5.1.29]

<s>NyS</s> 5.1.29: The <s>anupalabdhisama</s> (fallacy of non-apprehension-parity) [is the objection that], because the non-apprehension of the non-apprehension of that [obstruction] establishes the absence, [and] because of the tenability of the contrary, [there is parity].

children.text: teṣām āvaraṇādīnāmanupalabdhirnopalabhyate anupalambhānnāstīty abhāvo 'syāḥ sidhyati. abhāvasiddhau hetvabhāvāt tadviparītam astitvamāvaraṇādīnāmavadhāryate. tadviparītopapatteryat pratijñātam-- 'na prāguccāraṇādvidyamānasya śabdasyānupalabdhiḥ' ityetanna sidhyati. so 'yaṃ hetuḥ-- āvaraṇādyanupalabdheriti āvaraṇādiṣu cāvaraṇādyanupalabdhau ca samatayānupaladhyā pratyavasthito 'nupalabdhisamo bhavati // 29 //
children.translated_text: The non-apprehension of those obstructions and the like is not apprehended; from the non-apprehension, 'it does not exist' — thus its absence is established. When the absence is established, because of the absence of a reason, the contrary — namely the existence of obstructions and the like — is determined. Because of the tenability of the contrary, what was asserted — 'the non-apprehension of sound existing prior to utterance' — is not established. This reason — 'because of the non-apprehension of obstructions and the like' — being countered by the equal [treatment] of the non-apprehension in obstructions and the like and the non-apprehension of the non-apprehension, constitutes the <s>anupalabdhisama</s>. [End of NyS 5.1.29]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.30]
The reply to this —
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.30: Because non-apprehension has the nature of non-apprehension, [it is] not a [valid] reason.

children.text: 'āvaraṇādyanupalabdhirnāsti-- anupalambhāt' ityahetuḥ, kasmāt ?, anupalambhātmakatvādanupalabdheḥ = upalambhābhāvamātratvādanupalabdheḥ yadasti tadupalabdherviṣayaḥ = upalabdhyā tadastīti pratijñāyate. yannāsti tadanupalabdherviṣayaḥ = anupalabhyamānaṃ nāstīti pratijñāyate, soyamāvaraṇādyanupalabdheranupalambho 'nupalabdhau svaviṣaye pravartamāno na svaviṣayaṃ pratiṣedhati, apratiṣiddhā cāvaraṇādyanupalabdhirhetutvāya kalpayate|

āvaraṇādīni tu vidyamānatvādupalabdherviṣayāḥ teṣāmupalabdhyā bhavitavyaṃ yattāni nopalabhyante tad upalabdheḥ svaviṣayapratipādikāyā abhāvād = anuṣalambhādanupalabdherviṣayo gamyate-- 'na santyāvaraṇādīni śabdasyāgrahaṇakāraṇānīti, anupalambhādanupalabdhiḥ sidhyati-- viṣayaḥ sa tasyeti // 30 //
children.translated_text: But obstructions and the like, if they existed, would be objects of apprehension. They should be apprehended. That they are not apprehended is because of the absence of apprehension, which would indicate its own domain — from the non-apprehension, the domain of non-apprehension is understood: 'the obstructions and the like, which are causes of the non-grasping of sound, do not exist.' From the non-apprehension, non-apprehension is established — that is its domain. [End of NyS 5.1.30]

'The non-apprehension of obstructions and the like does not exist — because of non-apprehension' — this is not a [valid] reason. Why? Because non-apprehension has the nature of non-apprehension — that is, because non-apprehension is merely the absence of apprehension. What exists is the object of apprehension — by apprehension it is asserted 'this exists.' What does not exist is the object of non-apprehension — what is not apprehended is asserted 'this does not exist.' This non-apprehension of the non-apprehension of obstructions and the like, operating in its own domain — namely non-apprehension — does not deny its own domain. And the non-apprehension of obstructions and the like, being undenied, serves as a reason.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.31]
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.31: And because of the experience of the presence and absence of the varieties of knowledge in one's own self, [it is] not a [valid] reason.
'Not a [valid] reason' — this continues.

children.text: śarīre śarīriṇāṃ jñānavikalpānāṃ bhāvābhāvau saṃvedanīyau-- 'asti me saṃśayajñānam nāsti me saṃśayajñānam' iti. evaṃ pratyakṣānumānāgamasmṛtijñāneṣu. seyamāvaraṇādy anupalabdhiḥ |
children.translated_text: In the body, for embodied beings, the presence and absence of the varieties of knowledge are to be experienced — 'I have a cognition of doubt,' 'I do not have a cognition of doubt.' Similarly for perceptual, inferential, scriptural, and memorial cognitions. This non-apprehension of obstructions and the like

children.text: upalabdhyabhāvaḥ svasaṃvedyaḥ-- nāsti me śabdasyāvaraṇādyupalabdhiḥ iti = '
children.translated_text: is an absence of apprehension that is self-experienced — 'I do not have an apprehension of obstructions and the like regarding sound' —

children.text: nopalabhyante śabdasyāgrahaṇakāraṇānyāvaraṇādīnīti, tatra yaduktam-- 'tadanupalabdheranupalambhādabhāvasiddhiḥ' iti etannopapadyate // 31 //
children.translated_text: 'The causes of non-grasping of sound, such as obstructions and the like, are not apprehended.' Regarding that, what was said — 'from the non-apprehension of the non-apprehension of that, the absence is established' — that is untenable. [End of NyS 5.1.31]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.32]

<s>NyS</s> 5.1.32: The <s>anityasama</s> (fallacy of non-eternality-parity) [is the objection that], because of the similarity [of everything to what is non-eternal], due to the applicability of a common property, the consequence of universal non-eternality [follows].
By one who says 'sound is non-eternal because of similarity with a non-eternal pot' —
'there is a similarity of all things with the non-eternal pot' —

children.text: iti sarvasyānityatvamaniṣṭaṃ saṃpadyate, soyamanityatvena pratyavasthānādanityasama iti // 32 //
children.translated_text: the undesirable consequence that everything is non-eternal follows. This [objection], based on non-eternality, is the <s>anityasama</s>. [End of NyS 5.1.32]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.33]
The reply to this —
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.33: Because of the non-establishment from similarity, the non-establishment of the refutation [follows] from the similarity with what is to be refuted.

children.text: pratijñādyavayavayuktaṃ vākyaṃ pakṣanivartakaṃ pratipakṣalakṣaṇaṃ pratiṣedhaḥ, tasya pakṣeṇa pratiṣedhyena sādharmyaṃ pratijñādiyogaḥ, tad yadyanityasādharmyādanityatvasyāsiddhiḥ ?-- sādharmyādasiddheḥ, pratiṣedhasyāpyasiddhiḥ-- pratiṣedhyena sādharmyāditi // 33 //
children.translated_text: A statement equipped with the members of thesis and the rest, that overturns the thesis, is the counter-thesis, which is the refutation. Its similarity with the thesis that is to be refuted is its possession of thesis and the rest. If the non-eternality is not established because of the similarity — then because of the non-establishment from similarity, the refutation too is not established — because of similarity with what is to be refuted. [End of NyS 5.1.33]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.34]

children.text: NyS_5,1.34: dṛṣṭānte ca sādhyasādhanabhāvena prajñātasya dharmasya hetutvāttasya cobhayathā bhāvānnāviśeṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 5.1.34: Because in the example (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) the property known through the relation of what is to be proved and the means of proof is the reason, and because that [property] exists in both ways, there is no non-distinction.

children.text: dṛṣṭānte yaḥ khalu dharmaḥ sādhyasādhanabhāvena prajñāyate sa hetutvenābhidhīyate. sa cobhayathā bhavati-- kena citsamānaḥ kutaścidviśiṣṭaḥ. sāmānyāt sādharmya viśeṣācca vaidharmyam. ekaṃ sādharmyaviśeṣo hetuḥ nāviśeṣeṇa sādharmyamātraṃ vaidharmyamātraṃ vā. sādharmyamātraṃ vaidharmyamātraṃ cāśrityabhāvānāha--

children.translated_text: 'Because of the tenability of having equal properties from similarity, since universal impermanence would follow, [this is] equal to the impermanent [NyS 5.1.32].'
This is unjustified.
And what was said in the refutation of the non-distinction [objection] should also be understood [here]. [End of NyS 5.1.34]

In the example, the property that is known through the relation of what is to be proved and the means of proof — that is stated as the reason. And that exists in both ways — similar to something in one respect, different from something in another. From commonality [comes] similarity (<s>sādharmya</s>), and from difference [comes] dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmya</s>). The reason is a single [property combining] similarity and difference — not indiscriminately mere similarity or mere dissimilarity. And relying on mere similarity and mere dissimilarity, [the opponent] said —
[Section: NySBh 5.1.35]

<s>NyS</s> 5.1.35: Because impermanence is [either] permanent or impermanent in the impermanent [thing] — [and if permanent,] because permanence would be tenable for the impermanent — [this is] equal to the permanent (<s>nityasama</s>).

children.text: 'anityaḥ śabdaḥ' iti pratijñāyate. tadanityatvaṃ kiṃ śabde nityam ? athānityam ?. yadi tāvat sarvadā bhavati ? dharmasya sadā bhāvād dharmiṇopi sadā bhāva iti 'nityaḥ śabdaḥ' iti, atha na sarvadā bhavati ? anityatvasyābhāvād nityaḥ śabdaḥ, evaṃ nityatvena pratyavasthrānāt nityasamaḥ // 35 //
children.translated_text: 'Sound is impermanent' is the thesis. Is that impermanence permanent in sound, or impermanent? If it always exists — because of the perpetual existence of the property, the property-bearer too always exists — thus 'sound is permanent.' But if it does not always exist — because of the absence of impermanence, sound is permanent. Thus, because of the counter-establishment through permanence, [this is] equal to the permanent. [End of NyS 5.1.35]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.36]
The reply to this —
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.36: Because impermanence is [either] permanent or impermanent in what is to be negated — [and if impermanent,] because impermanence would be tenable — there is no refutation.

children.text:
pratiṣedhye śabde 'nityamanityatvasya bhāvāt' ityucyamāne 'nujñātaṃ śabdasyānityatvam. anityatvopapatteśca 'nānityaḥ śabdaḥ' iti pratiṣedho nopapadyate, atha nābhyupagamyate ? 'nityamanityatvasya bhāvāt' itiheturna bhavatīti hetvabhāvāt pratiṣedhānupapattiriti|
utpannasya nirodhād abhāvaḥ śabdasyānityatvaṃ tatra paripraśnānupapattiḥ |

soyaṃ praśnaḥ-- 'tadanityatvaṃ kiṃ śabde sarvadā bhavati ? atha na ?' ityanupapannaḥ, kasmāt ? utpannasyayo nirodhād abhāvaḥ śabdasya tad anityatvam. evaṃ ca saty adhikaraṇādheyavibhāgo vyāghātānnāstīti|
children.translated_text: This question — 'Does that impermanence always exist in sound, or not?' — is inapplicable. Why? Because the impermanence of sound is the cessation, the non-existence, of what has arisen. This being so, the distinction between substrate and what depends on the substrate does not exist, because of self-contradiction.

children.text: nityānityatvavirodhācca nityatvamanityatvaṃ caikasya dharmiṇo dharmāviti virudhyete |
children.translated_text: And because of the contradiction between permanence and impermanence — permanence and impermanence as properties of a single property-bearer are contradictory.

children.text: na saṃbhavataḥ, tatra yaduktam-- 'nityamanityatvasya bhāvād nitya eva' tad avartamānārthamuktamiti // 36 //
children.translated_text: They cannot coexist. Regarding that, what was said — 'because of the permanence of impermanence, [sound] is indeed permanent' — that was said about something that does not obtain. [End of NyS 5.1.36]

When it is said 'because of the permanence of impermanence' regarding the sound that is to be negated [i.e., refuted as permanent], the impermanence of sound has been conceded. And because of the tenability of impermanence, the negation 'sound is not impermanent' is untenable. But if [the permanence of impermanence] is not accepted, then 'because of the permanence of impermanence' is not a valid reason — and because of the absence of a reason, the negation is untenable. The impermanence of sound is the cessation of what has arisen — its non-existence; regarding that, the question is inapplicable.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.37]
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.37: Because of the multiplicity of the products of effort, [this is] equal to the effect (<s>kāryasama</s>).

children.text: 'prayatnānantarīyakatavādanityaḥ śabdaḥ' iti, yasya prayatnānantaramātmalābhaḥ tatkhalu abhūtvā bhavati yathā ghaṭādi kāryam. anityamiti ca 'bhūtvā na bhavatītyetadvijñāyate, evamavasthite

children.translated_text: 'because of the multiplicity of the products of effort'
— this refutation is stated.

children.text: prayatnānantaramātmalābhaśca dṛṣṭo ghaṭādīnām. vyavadhānāpohāccābhivyaktirvyavahitānām, tat kiṃ prayatnānantaramātmālābhaḥ śabdasya ? āho abhivyaktiḥ ? iti viśeṣo nāsti|
children.translated_text: The attainment of existence immediately after effort is observed in pots and the like. And the manifestation (<s>abhivyakti</s>) of concealed [things] is due to the removal of obstruction. So is it the attainment of existence immediately after effort for sound? Or is it manifestation? There is no distinction.
The counter-establishment through non-distinction of effects is [what is called] equal to the effect. [End of NyS 5.1.37]

'Sound is impermanent because it arises immediately after effort' — whatever attains its existence immediately after effort, that indeed comes into being having not existed [before], like an effect such as a pot. And 'impermanent' means 'having existed, it ceases to exist.' This being the case,
[Section: NySBh 5.1.38]
The reply to this —
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.38: If the effect is different [from manifestation], effort is not the cause — because of the tenability of the cause of non-apprehension.
If the effect is different [from manifestation], because of the tenability of the cause of non-apprehension, effort is not the cause of the manifestation of sound.

children.text: yatra prayatnānantaramabhivyaktistatrānupalabdhikāraṇaṃ vyavadhānamupapadyate. vyavadhānāpohācca prayatnānantarabhāvino 'rthasayopalabdhilakṣaṇābhivyaktirbhavatīti. na tu śabdasyānupalabdhikāraṇaṃ kiṃ cidupapadyate yasya prayatnānantaramapohāt śabdasyopalabdhilakṣaṇābhivyaktirbhavatīti. tasmādutpadyate śabdo nābhivyajyate iti // 38 //
children.translated_text: Where manifestation occurs immediately after effort, there obstruction is tenable as the cause of non-apprehension. And from the removal of obstruction, the manifestation characterized by the apprehension of an object that exists immediately [after effort] occurs. But for sound, no cause of non-apprehension is tenable, by the removal of which, immediately after effort, the manifestation characterized by the apprehension of sound would occur. Therefore, sound is produced, not manifested. [End of NyS 5.1.38]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.39]
If the non-conclusiveness of the reason is established — [the objection being that] because of non-conclusiveness it would be non-probative — and if non-conclusiveness [implies] non-probativeness —
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.39: In the refutation too, the same fault [applies].

children.text: pratiṣedhopyanaikāntikaḥ-- kiñcit pratiṣedhati kiñcinneti. anaikāntikatvād asādhaka iti|

atha vā śabdasyānityatvapekṣe prayatnānantaramutpādo nābhivyaktiriti viśeṣahetvabhāvaḥ, nityatvapakṣepi prayatnānantaramabhivyaktirnotpāda iti viśeṣahetvabhāvaḥ, soyamubhayapakṣasamoviśeṣahetvabhāva ityubhayamapyanaikāntikamiti // 39 //
children.translated_text: Or, regarding the impermanence of sound — the specific reason for [saying] that it is production immediately after effort, not manifestation, is absent; and in the thesis of permanence too — the specific reason for [saying] that it is manifestation immediately after effort, not production, is absent. This absence of a specific reason is equal to both positions — thus both are non-conclusive. [End of NyS 5.1.39]
The refutation too is non-conclusive — it refutes some things but not others. Because of non-conclusiveness, it is non-probative.
[Section: NySBh 5.1.40]
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.40: [This applies] everywhere in this way.

children.text: sarveṣu sādharmyaprabhatiṣu pratiṣedhahetuṣu yatra yatrāviśeṣo dṛśyate tatrobhayoḥ pakṣayoḥ samaḥ prasajyate iti // 40 //
children.translated_text: In all refutation-reasons beginning with similarity, wherever non-distinction is seen, the same [fault] applies to both positions. [End of NyS 5.1.40]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.41]
<s>NyS</s> 5.1.41: In the counter-refutation of a refutation, the fault is like the fault of the refutation.

children.text: yo 'yaṃ pratiṣedhepi samāno doṣaḥ anaikāntikatvamāpādyate so 'yaṃ pratiṣedhasya pratiṣedhepi samānaḥ, na 'anityaḥ śabdaḥ prayatnānantarīyakatvāt' iti sādhanavādinaḥ sthāpanā prathamaḥ pakṣaḥ,
children.translated_text: This same fault — the charge of non-conclusiveness that is brought even against the refutation — is the same even in the counter-refutation of the refutation. 'Sound is impermanent because of arising immediately after effort' — this is the establishment by the proponent, the first position.
'Because of the multiplicity of the products of effort, [this is] equal to the effect [NyS 5.1.37]'

children.text: iti dūṣaṇavādinaḥ pratiṣedhahetunā dvitīyaḥ pakṣaḥ sa ca pratiṣedha ityucyate, tasyāsya pratiṣedhepi samāno doṣa iti tṛtīyaḥ pakṣaḥ ( sa ca ) vipratiṣedha ucyate, tasmin pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhepi samāno doṣaḥ anaikāntikatvaṃ caturthaḥ pakṣaḥ // 4 //
children.translated_text: — this is the second position, by the refutation-reason of the objector, and that is called the refutation. In the [counter-]refutation of that refutation too, the same fault — this is the third position. And that is called the counter-refutation. In that counter-refutation of the refutation too, the same fault — non-conclusiveness — is the fourth position. [End of NyS 5.1.41]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.42]

children.text: NyS_5,1.42: pratiṣedhaṃ sadoṣamabhyupetya pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhe samāno doṣaprasaṅgo matānujñā //
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 5.1.42: Having accepted the refutation as faulty, in the counter-refutation, the implication of the same fault is a concession of [the opponent's] position (<s>matānujñā</s>).
Having accepted the refutation —
the second position — as faulty,
without extracting and [explicitly] addressing its [fault], having [merely] conceded [it], in the counter-refutation —

children.text: tṛtīyapakṣe samānam anaikāntikatvamiti samānaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ prasajato dūṣaṇavādino matānujñā prasajyate iti pañcamaḥ pakṣaḥ // 42 //
children.translated_text: in the third position, the same [fault of] non-conclusiveness — for one who implies the same objection, the concession of [the opponent's] position follows — this is the fifth position. [End of NyS 5.1.42]
[Section: NySBh 5.1.43]

children.text: NyS_5,1.43: svapakṣalakṣaṇāpekṣopapattyupasaṃhāre hetunirdeśe parapakṣadoṣābhyupagamāt samāno doṣaḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>NyS</s> 5.1.43: When the indication of the reason in the summation of the applicable fault, which depends on the characteristic of one's own position, involves the acceptance of the opposing position — the same fault [applies].

children.text:
sthāpanāpekṣe "prayatnakāryānekatvāt"
itidoṣaḥ pratiṣedhahetuvādinaḥ svapakṣalakṣaṇo bhavati, kasmāt ?, svapakṣasamutthatvāt, soyaṃ svapakṣalakṣaṇaṃ doṣamapekṣamāṇo 'nuddhṛtya |
anujñāya "pratiṣedhepi samāno doṣaḥ 39"
ityupapadyamānaṃ doṣaṃ parapakṣe upasaṃharati,itthaṃ cānaikāntikaḥ pratiṣedha iti hetuṃ nirdiśati, tatra svapakṣalakṣaṇāpekṣayopapadyamānadoṣopasaṃhāre hetunirdeśe ca sati anena parapakṣo 'bhyupagato bhavati|
kathaṃ kṛtvā ?, yaḥ pareṇa "prayatnakāryānekatvāt"
ityādinānaikāntikatvadoṣa uktastam anuddhṛtya
"pratiṣedhepi samāno doṣaḥ 39"
ityāha, evaṃ sthāpanāṃ sadoṣāmabhyupetya pratiṣedhepi samānaṃ doṣaṃ prasajataḥ parapakṣābhyupagamāt samāno doṣo bhavati. yathā parasya pratiṣedhaṃ sadoṣamabhyupetya pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhepi samāno doṣaprasaṅgo matānujñā prasajyate iti tathāsyāpi sthāpanāṃ sadoṣāmabhyupetya pratiṣedhepi samānaṃ doṣaṃ prasajato matānujñā prasajyate iti, sa khalvayaṃ ṣaṣṭhaḥ pakṣaḥ|
tatra khalu sthāpanāhetuvādinaḥ prathamatṛtīyapañcamapakṣāḥ, pratiṣedhahetuvādinaḥ dvitīyacaturthaṣaṣṭhapakṣāḥ, teṣāṃ sādhv asādhutāyāṃ mīmāṃsyamānāyāṃ caturthaṣaṣṭhayoraviśeṣāt punaruktadoṣaprasaṅgaḥ |
caturthapakṣe samānadoṣatvaṃ parasyocyate--
"pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhe pratiṣedhadoṣavad doṣaḥ 41"
iti,
ṣaṣṭhepi "parapakṣābhyupagamāt samāno doṣaḥ"
itisamānadoṣatvamevocyate nārthaviśeṣaḥ kaścidasti|
samānastṛtīyapañcamayoḥ punaruktadoṣaprasaṅga |
tṛtīyapakṣepi "pratiṣedhepi samāno doṣaḥ 39"
iti samānatvamabhyupagamyate. pañcamapakṣepi pratiṣedhavipratiṣedhe samāno doṣaprasaṅgo 'bhyupagamyate nārthaviśeṣaḥ kaściducyate iti|
tatra pañcamaṣaṣṭhapakṣayorarthāviśeṣāt punaruktadoṣaḥ, tṛtīyacaturthayormatānujñā, prathamadvitīyayorviśeṣahetvabhāva iti ṣaṭpakṣyāmubhayorasiddhiḥ|
kadā ṣaṭpakṣī ?, yadā "pratiṣedhepi sāmāno doṣaḥ"
ityevaṃ pravartate tadobhayoḥ pakṣayorasiddhiḥ, yadā tu
children.translated_text: [the argument] proceeds as 'in the refutation too, the same fault' — then there is non-establishment for both positions. But when
'if the effect is different [from manifestation], effort is not the cause — because of the tenability of the cause of non-apprehension [NyS 5.1.38]'
